title: Great concept, serious flaws
text:
First of all, the concept for this game is great. Having extended workout routines with the ability to monitor your form (at least a little) is a big step up from the individual exercises that come with the Wii Fit disc. It packs a lot more exercise into a half hour session, and really gets your heart rate up and your muscles sore. The variety of exercises is great, too. Most of them are fun.

But there are some significant problems.

The neoprene rubber backing on both of the leg bands I own is tearing along the seam at the end of the velcro strap. Each leg band has been used for approximately 24 workouts (equivalent to being worn for 12 hours). I contacted customer support and was told that EA's official policy was that the bands would only be replaced under warranty within 90 days of purchase, no matter how little they were used before the damage was discovered. The customer support representative commented that this has been a very common failure and that the warranty department has been absolutely inflexible on the expiration of the warranty period. The flaw in the design is obvious. The line of stitches places holes (which concentrate stress) along the edge of where the inflexible velcro strap meets the flexible neoprene backing. That promotes formation of rips starting at those holes. Replacements can only be obtained by purchasing another "accessory pack" for $20.

The resistance band is very soft and does not provide nearly enough resistance for most adults. I purchased a 3-pack of light/medium/heavy resistance bands from sporting goods store, and even the light band was significantly stiffer than the EA Sports band.

Some of the exercises have sensing problems:
Running registers best when you stomp, which is not good for your knees. When I run with a lighter step, the avatar slows down and I am required to run for a longer time than scheduled.
Jumping exercises (jump squats and side-to-side jumps) are weird. The trainer gives us a hard time for "slacking off" even though the actions are scored as correct.
Lunges register more quickly when the right leg is forward than when the left leg is forward. This makes for a lopsided workout.

I have brought up the sensing problems on the EA "support and feedback forum" for EA Sports Active, but no one from EA seems to monitor that forum any more. It is full of spam and unanswered questions.

This could be a truly great game if EA tried just a little harder.

title: I Resign!
text:
As a very casual chess player, I decided to give Fritz 12 a try. The program is smart enough to obliterate just about anyone, but you can play the game at several different difficulty levels. It even has a friend mode where the computer determines how strong a chess player you are and plays at close to your level. This is one tough opponent - even in the friend mode. There are also several "personalities" you can play against. Each personality has preprogrammed strengths and weaknesses (including how badly it blunders). You can also change several of their attributes to make them a stronger or weaker player.

Fritz 12 is packed with training tools. You can set the game up so it suggests opening moves; warns you if a square you are about to move to is under attack; give you hints or suggested moves; tell you what your opponent is planning to do; and much more.

The free beginner training videos are good. There are also several sample videos for other topics included, in hopes you decide to purchase additional training videos.

Even at full price this is a terrific training tool and should certainly help you improve your game, even though you may get a bit frustrated if you like to win.

title: Minor gripes but otherwise Fantastic.
text:
Works great so far. It has a decent look to it, as there really isn't much else they could have done to make it look better. The HD fits in easily, the product sits on top of the Xbox pretty nice, and the cord for the USB to Xbox is nice how its cut and grooved to fit around to the back of the Xbox. I installed a Seagate 2TB SSHD and games and apps load up just as quick, if not quicker than they would have on the console's internal HD. So there really isn't much of an issue as to what games should get preference on the internal HD or the external, except maybe if you wanted to go to a friend's house and didn't want to wait to download the game.

I would have given this five stars but there are very minor things that take away from the overall experience of this HD enclosure:
1) It doesn't make up for the use of one of the USB slots. Other enclosure's have made up for taking up a USB slot by adding extra USB slots to the front or sides which is really nice since there wasn't too many to begin with. Although a lot of those only take 2.5" HD's it was just a nice thing that this company could have added to the enclosure that would really set it up in comparison with those.
2)It needs its own power source as it doesn't use power from the Xbox to run the HD. This isn't a major issue, as generally there are plenty of available power outlets around a TV or gaming area, but it would have been nice if everything was less cluttered. The plug is also a little bigger than a normal plug, so it might overlap onto outlets as well. This isn't a reason not to get it, as its not a huge issue, but its worth noting that other enclosures don't need an external power source. But again, many of those also don't support 3.5" drives either.. so its something to keep in mind.
3) It makes a verrrryyy slight noise. This is expected. In fact, this isn't even a problem on the enclosure's part. The SSHD I installed obviously has moving parts and that's the source of the noise. And this might just be me being really picky, and asking for too much, but it would've been nice to add sound insulation to the insides of the enclosure to nearly eliminate any noise that could come from an installed HD.

Id give this a 9/10 if I had to be specific. Other enclosures have had some complaints from some users and I would just like to say that this was painless and a breeze to install. No special prep for the HD or enclosure was needed. just plug everything in and you're ready to go. If I had to recommend an enclosure to anyone it would definitely be this.

title: It's ultimately like starting over in New Leaf
text:
If you're a fan of the series it's certainly worth the purchase and you'll have many hours of enjoyment playing it but ultimately it felt like I deleted my New Leaf data and was starting that game over again.

You can set furniture outside. Okay. You can craft furniture and tools. Or should that read: you HAVE to craft furniture and tools. I'm not sure that's a plus. It's fun at first to gather materials and craft stuff, and the crafting animation is so cute and awesome, but what does it ultimately add to the experience over time? It can become tedious and a bit of a drag.

I played almost all of the "summer" season before, I think, they added the ability to venture into the water via diving which if I recall correctly was included in New Leaf but I'm sure it certainly wasn't added through an update. I also think I saw that they eventually added, again through an update, the "dreaming" ability where you can visit other people's towns without having to be connected through the multi-player mode restricted to your friends. And I'm wondering if they will eventually add the coffee house place where you can hang out and buy a beverage a day, or whatever neat thing it was in New Leaf, and then, finally, you'd have a fully featured new version of New Leaf.

So yes, to me, it just felt like New Leaf but without everything included right away and so, unlike New Leaf, I found myself losing interest in about three months. Oh well. Maybe if I had more friends to play with, because that was super fun to visit a friend's island and have them visit mine. It'd be nice if they had more things you could do as far as interacting whilst visiting like mini games etc.

I'd still recommend it to Nintendo and Animal Crossing fans.

Cheers!

title: Initial Impressions
text: I've only been using this for two days, so maybe this won't count for much, BUT my initial thoughts are that for someone looking for a fun, motivating program, this isn't it. I'm not talking about all the folks who can motivate themselves to work out. I'm talking about people like me, who typically exercise for a month, and then watch tv for nine months before getting back to it. The Wii Fit programs are at least more entertaining, although I can say those programs got old over time, as this one certainly will. As far as this program, I of course, started out on 'easy', and the first day's workout was easy. The second day was harder - but it was suppose to be a mix of upper and lower body, and creamed my lower body with lunges and high-kick running, but didn't do as much as I wanted for upper body. I haven't had any trouble with the nunchuck being in the leg strap, other than the wire occasionally getting in the way while using the resistance band. It is awkward to move between exercises when you have to stop and put the nunchuck in the leg strap, or take it out, or get the resistance band in place. Since it can use the Wii balance board, it seems it should use it more (maybe it will eventually) - take advantage of the capability. My round of exercises on the first day used the board twice, and not very effectively. The second day's round didn't use it at all. I did have issues on the second day with the program recognizing when I was moving my arms up or down. AND, I ran off to the bathroom during a tutorial video, thinking the program wouldn't start until I pressed a button ... it did start without me, and my character had already done a rep by the time I got back - that's not impressive. Your motivation to keep at it are graphs and trophies. I find it amusing that the "Half Way There" Trophy is awarded at 10 out of 30 days (30 days being your big goal - to complete 30 days of workouts). Overall, if you are self-motivated to exercise, this program will probably make a nice addition to mix with your other workouts. I do so wish someone would make a really fun and entertaining workout program for those of us who need extra impetus. Bring on Raving Rabbids Aerobics or something. And please get rid of these lame trainers. I've generously given this three stars - it more or less does what it was made for.

title: Got some time to kill?
text:
I just got done playing Duke Nukem: "Land of the babes" and noticed a few reviewers where saying that game was nowhere near as good as Time To Kill or the other title. So after enjoying Land of the Babes, I couldn't wait to get into this one and see what made it so much better? But to my disappointment... what the heck makes it any different or better????

This one here I say is pretty much the same game as Land of the Babes, apart from different stages and a few enemies, only a small amount of guns are different from the other title, but none the less, they could easily have both been part of the exact same game.

Now, I'm not bagging this game, don't get me wrong, but I think it's just as equal to Land of the Babes. Maybe this one stands out a little more because some stages resemble that of Zero Hour on the Nintendo 64, but lets be honest, Zero Hour is a far superior game on every level. Literally.

Maybe Time to Kill requires a bit more searching around to get through levels, that part may be a little bit harder, but in the end, I felt like I had played the same game twice, and was a little bored by the end of it. By the time I blew away the final boss, I expected the ending to be disappointing, and low and behold, possibly the most disappointing ending in Duke Nukem history.

Of coarse, maybe had I been playing this 10 years ago or around the time this game came out, maybe it might have seemed a lot better at the time... but no wait, Zero Hour was made too, and that game rocked my world... but this one here, euhhh, I can see why some might like it better than Land of the Babes, but it's only by a small fraction.

Overall, if you play another DN title on the PS1 before this, you may think either "Ummm, this is the same game" or "Oh, goodie! More levels!".

title: Not Bad But I Got it For Free So . . .
text:
I called EA about a problem I was having with the Ambitions expansion pack. The guy was very helpful and it didn't take long to resolve my issue. As a bonus, he gave me a coupon sent via email for World Ambitions (which he explained should have been installed BEFORE Ambitions but I don't buy every expansion pack all the time). Anyway, the coupon was for $[...] and as of Friday when I logged on to EA's website and bought it, it was $[...] so I paid nothing for it. I had no intentions of buying it, so getting it free was worth the exploration.

Well, I played all weekend and so far I've only explored France. The few adventures I've had haven't been very difficult; just enough fun to keep the game interesting. I did hit one "glitch" when I entered a tomb and couldn't figure out how why I was supposed to slide some statues around, but after about 10 minutes, I figured that out. Since the Sim I was playing is an Angler, I caught some frogs to take home with me so I can now make frog legs for dinner. I just throw one in the Omni plant to keep from having to return to get more.

I agree that the cities could be a bit more populated but then again, when a vacation starts out at 3 days, you don't have a lot of time to meet people if you're exploring adventures to get coins and VISA points.

I give the expansion two thumbs up but only 3 stars for now because I have to play some more to say whether I love it or not. But for free, I like it enough.

title: Would be a great workout tool - if it actually functioned properly
text:
I'm completely mystified by all the glowing reviews this game has gotten, and I felt compelled to share my own experiences with Wii Active.

I bought this game because I had been using Wii Fit for about a year, and I was looking for a way to expand my workouts to make them a little more varied and challenging.

The one positive thing I can say is that the exercises themselves are quite good, and the routines the game puts together for you should make you sweat much more than Wii Fit (and ache more the next day). Unfortunately, that's about the only good thing I can report. As a person who is used to the amazing accuracy with which the Wii Fit senses your movements, I find the Active interface so clunky and unresponsive, it's impossible to get through an entire routine without 2 or 3 major glitches.

With Active, you have an Avatar on the screen who's supposed to mirror what you're doing, but the Avatar's movements lag at least 2 seconds (sometimes more) behind your own, which can be really distracting when you're supposed to do an exercise at a certain pace. But the bigger problem is that quite often, the game simply cannot sense what you're doing. The routine will not continue until you complete the exercise "properly," but because the game cannot sense your movements, it will just get hung up while you frantically try to figure out what you're doing wrong.

For example, you'll be doing a set of lunges, and on the 5th or 6th one your Avatar will just stand there motionless. You keep repeating the lunge, but try as you might you can't get the game to "see" it, and you can't figure out what you're doing that's different from the first several reps you completed with no problems. Or you'll be jogging at a steady pace, but your Avatar is all over the place running and walking at varying speeds, and the game keeps telling you you're not going at the right pace. Or you'll be holding a squat, and suddenly your Avatar will stand up for no reason, and the game will make you do the exercise over because it says you didn't hold the squat long enough.

I'm fairly experienced with motion sensitive games and exercise programs for the Wii, it's not that I don't know what I'm doing. I've never had a problem like this with any other game, so I'm certain the fault lies with the way the game itself was designed. It's very frustrating, and it ends up taking twice as long as it should to complete a workout.

It's tempting to credit this game with at least giving you a good workout, but without properly functioning motion sensors and interactivity, you'd be much better off just doing a fitness video. It would be less frustrating, and you'd get a better workout without all the starts and stops and hangups.

title: Good work-out, but still buggy
text:
My boyfriend and I have been using the Wii Active for about 3 weeks now. For the most part it is very effective, but there are times when it seems like they didn't do much product testing before they released it. For example, the other day I was doing the biceps curls with shoulder raises (or something like that) and for about a minute it kept telling me to lower my arms and hold still; my arms were down, ad the only way I could have been stiller was if I was dead. That's just one example of how buggy it can be at times.

Another major problem with it is you cannot select for exercises that will be gentle on your joints. The exercises are definitely not for anyone who has ever had a knee or foot injury. They do a lot of stressful bending at the knees and put stressful weight with movement on the feet. I'm hoping that after I'm done with the 30 day challenge I can exclude it from doing exercises that are so stressful on the knees.

The last problem is the leg strap. We'd been using it less than 2 weeks and it began to come apart at the edges. I repaired it, but now it's coming apart in other places. It is very low quality. If we want to continue to use this (which we do even with the problems) I'm going to have to make a new strap that will be more durable.

Despite these problems it has, thus far, been very effective at getting us in shape. I would only tentatively recommend this product to others and only under certain conditions.

title: Is this a Beta?
text:
Overall, EA Sports Active feels a lot like a pre-release of a game that will become an excellent game just as soon as the people who purchase the game find all the bugs for them. In other words, the first wave of buyers are their Beta testers.

Numerous people have posted their frustrations over the problem with the intermittent failures of the game to properly track the movements of their arms and legs. I have had the same issue, the game stalls and goes into an annoying waiting mode prompting you to complete the exercise, not because you haven't but because it is not reading your movements properly. Normally you can get out of this mode by widely swinging whatever body part it has failed to read. It's annoying to have to do this, and so far this is the only Wii sports game I've played that has this glitch.

The resistance band have almost no resistance, and the idea of holding the Wii controls in each hand along with the resistance band is just plain bad design. However, I suspect that they ended up like this as the lesser of two evils. You can't do the exercises without holding the two Wii remotes in your hands, however if you used the right resistance while holding the remotes you have a safety issue. I noticed that Everlast released a set of two pound weights that hold the Wii remotes inside of their handles which allow for the correct resistance without the safety risks. If Everlast ends up releasing an entire range of hand weights for the Wii console, then the EA Sports Active resistance band could be replaced with those weights. Problem solved, but then again, if EA Sports Active had thought this all through when they designed this software, it would have been a non-issue, solved before the release of the software.

This is why I feel this product is more of a Beta then a full release. The designers and managers behind this game had to have known at some point that the resistant bands were not a good design, and they should have come up with a solution before releasing this to the world.

If everything worked right, and the resistance band was not an issue I would give EA Sports Active five stars. As it stands, I only give it a three. I have also decided that I will rent any Wii sports games before I buy. Wii sports games seem to always get high reviews, in spite of some real problems with the quality of the software.

On a side note there's a workout you do with the band for your shoulders where the trainer actually says "At no time should you allow the shoulder to come out of the socket." I can't tell if it's suppose to be a joke or not, but either way, it's pretty funny.

title: A motivating workout that makes you sweat
text:
Whereas the incredibly popular Wii Fit is focused on form, posture, and balance, right down to exercises devoted to breathing and sitting still, EA Sports Active is the more Americanized offering containing a heavy focus on cardio and strength exercises. The short story is EA Sports Active will make you sweat and, at least for me, will motivate you to exercise regularly more than any other game on the market. This is due to the calendar style system of planned workouts via the 30 day challenge. It's recommended, you don't need the balance board, and I will be surprised if anyone except a fitness trainer doesn't lose weight with this game.

Unfortunately, there are some gripes that keep me from giving it five stars:

1) The resistance band is useless to anyone except maybe a four year old. They tell you to fold it and step on the folds to provide more resistance but that's also a joke. The only way to get enough resistance to provide an effective upper body workout is to stretch to the point of breakage. Don't expect an upper body workout unless you can find a replacement band somewhere.

2) The (huge) leg strap will probably annoy a lot of female users who don't have thunderthighs. They provide an accessory to once again play the foldover game and tighten it to fit on someone with a body shape similar to the trainer on the box but I can't imagine it being comfortable.

3) The instructions say loose, slick. or baggy clothes "may" cause the leg strap attachment to slip. Wrong. They WILL cause the strap to slip. I can't wear this over any shorts or sweats, loose, tight, or otherwise, without it slipping, even if it's tightened enough to cut off blood circulation. For me, the only way to fasten it securely is to strap it directly on my leg and cover it with shorts.

4) The jabbering trainer motivates way too much (like every 10 seconds).

5) I think EA did the best they could with the control system available but there are still issues with certain exercises not being recognized on occasion. I have problems with fast paced running and kicking exercises being not recognized. I can keep the same running pace yet the game will flip flop from telling me I'm doing perfect to telling me I'm too slow. Once the trainer starts nagging you every 10 seconds it'll put you on tilt. For the record, I had the same problem with Wii Fit.

6) The game does include the balance board in some exercises but it seems like more of an accessory item to add variety rather than to actually tap into how it can help in a workout. I get the feeling the developers didn't really know what to do with it.

7) Your daily "score" involves completing surveys every day asking you if you slept enough and ate your veggies. Even though they're quickly completed they're annoying and redundant. Maybe they should have hired Mr. T to ask me if I drank my milk. Plus, when it asks you what other activities you've completed there is no "none" option. To my knowledge, there is no way to get around this. In other words, unless you make up something each day it won't say the survey was completed.

For people having trouble getting the game to respond correctly, here are some tips that have helped me:

First, regarding the strap slipping around, notice on the pictures on the box and the instruction booklet that the strap is way up there. If you're putting the strap on the lower half or even the middle of your thigh it will likely slip down to your knee.

Secondly, about the game not responding to your movements correctly. Watch the animated characters carefully to make sure you are moving the Wii joystick in the correct position. Many exercises have you twisting the controllers in specific directions and will not register correctly unless this is done. Also, I have found if I move the sensor bar from below the TV to a spot above the TV (remember to change the Wii settings to reflect this) that my movements are registered more accurately. I have no idea why this is the case but it worked for me. Finally, when you have to stick the nunchuck in the leg strap, make sure it's jammed down there far with the end pointing straight up. If it's angled in any way the movements don't register as accurately.

Third, if you want an upper body workout, plan on getting a higher resistance band in addition to this game. There are many sold right here on Amazon.

Hope this helps.

title: Prefer EA Sports Active More Workouts
text:
By chance, I bought the 'more workouts' version first, which I think was better than this one. I liked its 6-week challenge better than this 30-day challenge, which automatically sets me up to do 2 days on, 1 day off. I haven't done all these exercises yet, but this program seems to have some problems recognizing my movements with at least a couple of them. The in-line skate exercise, for example, is very frustrating as it doesn't recognize a lot of my squats and jumps even though I think I'm doing them the same way every time.

That said, I think had I used this program before trying EA Sports Active More Workouts, I would have rated this 5-stars. However, even though I also own and prefer More Workouts, I am sure I will still get more than my money's worth out of this program (at current used prices, for sure, and probably also had I paid full retail price).

title: Motivates me in a way that other exercise options don't - love it so far!
text:
I jumped right into the 6-week challenge and am enjoying the workouts enough that I am sure I'll get all 24 workouts done by my deadline. If that sounds like a lot, know that you may choose an 18-workout challenge instead or just do workouts one at a time on any schedule. Every activity/exercise is also available to do on its own, either in combination to make a customized workout or on its own if you want to practice a certain thing. The program also encourages you to document your nutritional habits and physical activity outside the program. You may set custom goals for how many workouts or hours of workouts, etc. you do within a certain period.

Pros: A lot of variation in activities. The predesigned workouts are plentiful and mix things up so I'm not bored and so that different body parts get worked on different days. I can do it alone but it doesn't feel like I'm alone. Pretty nonjudgmental in the on-screen hints and audio coaching from the on-screen trainer guy. Activities (like squash, water-skiing, paddle-boarding) are pretty believable/realistic and can be somewhat challenging. You have the option to work your way up in difficulty by starting with easy-level exercises.

Cons: A few exercises have given me problems where the Wii hasn't recognized my movements correctly. At first, this was usually my fault for not precisely following the instructions for how to hold or orient the controllers. And over the first dozen workouts, I learned how to tweak my movements so it happens much less frequently, but sometimes it still happens when I don't think it's my fault. It's not a big deal when you're doing fitness exercises where the Wii will wait for you, but if you're doing a time-sensitive activity like water-skiing (say it's not recognizing that you're leaning to the right, for example, it means you miss some of the flags). It's not a problem enough for me to deduct a star from the rating in my review, but I could imagine someone who's not patient in working out a sort of understanding with the Wii over time might get a little frustrated by it. Finally, I am in my 50s and am of above-average fitness but am not really an athlete, yet I did fine choosing the highest degree of difficulty and highest frequency of workouts (4/week as opposed to 3/week) on my first 6-week challenge. It was definitely good for me, especially for the parts of my body I hadn't been working, but I can't really say this kicked my butt, which I think means that it might not pose enough challenge for people fitter than I unless they assemble their own workouts, in which case they can, for example, include repeated sets of exercises, use stiffer bands, or use a riser under the balance board for step aerobics, for example. If you're self-motivated and are looking for a killer workout, a good 1-hour spin, step aerobics, or boot camp class will make you sweat more than this program.

Other comments: You need a remote and nunchuk and I highly recommend buying the activity kit for its leg strap and its exercise band with strap handles (rather than hard handles) which allows you to hold the straps and Wii controllers simultaneously. I own a balance board and think it adds a lot to the exercises, but you can tell the software only to select exercises that don't use the balance board. I think this software would still be a worthwhile purchase if you don't have a balance board.

UPDATE: I finished my first 6-week challenge about 3 days early, even after missing all of my scheduled Week 2 exercises due to being on a trip. I was motivated enough to work out on what were scheduled as rest days, including about 9 days straight, after I got back home! And although sometimes I had to push myself to get started on the workouts, it never felt like a burden to actually do them after I started. Unlike other things I say I like (like going to spin classes, taking bike rides, or going for runs), I never find myself looking at the clock or wishing I were done - there is so much variety in this game that the time always seems to go quickly. I worked out with my husband a few times and he liked it too even though he wasn't getting his activity recorded. (You can supposedly work out with a friend but I was committed to my 6 week challenge, so I made him do my workouts and we haven't tried that option yet.)

The only thing that has been bad so far is that there wasn't anything at the end of the 6 week challenge that prompted me to start a new one, which might have prevented me from taking at least four days off before starting something new. I'm ready to get back to it again, though, because I don't want to lose what I gained - and I can definitely tell my arms, legs, and abs are more toned after the 6 weeks, even if I didn't lose any pounds (although that wasn't my primary goal).

Bottom line: with EA Active More Workouts selling used for as little as $12 right now, I can think of no reason not to buy it (even though you also have to buy the EA Active leg strap and band accessory kit). I got way more than that much value from it after doing one 6-week challenge alone and I am sure I will use it many times over again.

title: Fundamentally broken multiplayer, endless time-padding for every action, Nintendo’s worst
text:
First off, I’m a huge Nintendo fan, for over 2 decades & 7 console generations. Their attention to detail, endlessly fun gameplay across genres, and non-stop innovation keep me coming back!

I wish I could love ACNH, but it is truly abysmal. No idea why there are so many positive reviews. It isn’t really even a game, it’s a collection of mildly interesting activities buried under repetitive and time-padded sequences, dialog boxes, and menu actions.

Multiplayer is fundamentally broken - anyone besides the first player can’t do much other than wander around and pick up stuff while the first player leads. They can’t even access their inventory unless you switch leads (which, unlike everything else in this game, is actually fast to do). Worst of all, whomever first sets up the island (resident rep) is THE ONLY PERSON WHO CAN DO *ANYTHING USEFUL* in the game. No one else can make ANY progress, build anything, interact properly with NPCs, etc. So, basically you get one person who can (barely) play the game PER SWITCH, while everyone else is never able to play it unless you shell out another $300 for another Switch. That’s right, no multiple saves/islands. One per system.

If you live alone, great!

Truly, one of the worst things Nintendo has ever crafted. Save your money and play something that is actually playable whether solo or multi, like Stardew Valley.

title: Frustrating As Hell
text:
The Thing is one of my favorite horror movies of all time, so I was excited to find out that there was a game that was a canon sequel (according to John Carpenter, who also makes a fun appearance in the game as an NPC). Needless to say, my feelings were very mixed by the end of the game.

To start, I love the story overall; if this was to be turned into a movie, it'd be a worthy sequel to The Thing. Strong lead character? check. Corrupt corporation? check. Betrayals? check. That's about all the positives I have to say about the game, gameplay is where everything starts to lose its luster.

Why do I fear fire more in this game than the actual alien creatures? Maybe because fire is everywhere and drains your health way faster than any Thing creature will. Seriously, maybe they should make fire the last boss in the game, I'd be terrified. Not to mention the floaty controls that will insta-kill your character trying to walk across a simple beam, leading you to think that maybe your character had a little too much Jim Beam himself, and decides to fall to his death with the slight twitch of the left control stick.

The worst thing about this game is the "survival horror" aspects, where you may find yourself stuck at certain points out of ammo or health, and with the nearest save point 20 minutes of progress away before facing a boss that throws in a cheap shot during the cutscene (seriously WTF, really?). I know of quite a few people who have stopped playing this game because of just that reason, unable to progress.

Even for a very conservative ammo & health spender, you'll eventually end up running into your old friend fire (sometimes courtesy of your own NPCmates), and you may find yourself in the aforementioned can't continue situation.

The game also only seems to have one difficulty level (frustrating), although changing the difficulty level changes the "cone" of your bullet spread, with "Easy" almost guaranteeing you'll hit whatever is in front of you, not necessarily making the lack of ammo and health any easier in turn.

Lastly, the whole "team" dynamic that was a big selling point in this game is insignificant. Certain teammates will turn at predetermined spots, and others will disappear as soon as you add them to your team. Sometimes, putting them out of their misery and taking their weapon is the most efficient course of action.

The last part of the game is fighting other human enemies, and at that point I was just eager to finish "The Fire: Subtitle The Thing" game and go back to watching the movie a few times every year.

title: A middle of the road product
text:
I wanted to wait until I had the product for a while before commenting to provide a balanced review.

Positives:
1. It is a solid game for those who are just getting started in a fitness program. The exercises really don't cause you to over exert yourself while each exercise has three levels: Easy, Medium, and Hard.

2. It does allow you to select your music in some of the exercises. However, it is very limited and in cases like the step classes you do not have any choice.

3. Whether using the Step or Wii wands the game captures two essential points of your movement: your initial position and the final position. Because the movement between the two is not registered you can do what you want. For example, I hold the nun chuck in my hand for the activities it tells me to put in the leg band.

4. Think of it as a good exercise routine with minimal interactivity with the WII gaming devices.

5. It does successfully graduate you to having more flexibility, a little more aerobic stamina, and overall readiness for something next.

Negatives:

1. The leg band. This is a useless concept. I wish I could have the designer explain how they came up with that concept. Unless your knee is wider than your thigh the leg band always will fall down as you perform any of the exercises in the game.

2. The exercise routines are very redundant. It did not take long for me to top the program where I have the activities set to Hard and run multiple times because the level is not sufficient to challenge any longer.

3. This is the next problem, it take roughly 30-45 seconds between transitioning between activities even if you have the same exercise back to back. So, there is dead time which leads to frustration if you are trying to run a circuit.

Lastly, if you are one who is a mid level fitness shape, this is NOT the product for you. You will exceed its maximum challenges. I recommend it highly for beginners.

title: My personal experience with this device
text:
I ordered this some time ago, but after using it for a long time, I am posting this review on 9/7/16:
Ok, I ordered this a while back, and after I got it, I wanted to see how other people reacted to it. I can see it's roughly an even split. After reading some reviews, doing some online research, and instructions from the package itself, here is what I would recommend.

For starters, do web research. I would also recommend looking at other people reviewing this. Look at some of the Q/As, at some of the 4 and 5 starts for instructions and set up, the 3 and lower stars for issues.

1. It says to not get a HDD over 2 TB. My system only had 500GB, so I figured I'd be adding three times more space and I'm Ok with that. I've seen others say they got up to 6TB, but I am NOT tempting fate.
2. The HDD in question is a WD Black 2TB Performance Desktop Hard Drive: 3.5-inch, SATA 6 Gb/s, 7200 RPM, 64MB Cache WD2003FZEX. I think the price is good.
3. The HDD makes a little noise, but that means its working and since I use headphones, it doesn't bother me.
4. Make sure you after you have it installed that you are getting the entire software update installed, not just the latest patch. PS, check the official site the day you work on this to make sure you are up to date.
5. Make sure you do this when you have A LOT of free time, because after you get it set up, the internal software and updating takes a good while, so you'll want to keep and eye on it while doing other activities.
6. I've seen people talk about this overheating. Out of paranoia, I keep a fan next to it turned on when playing. A time or two I have played a few hours of Batman without the fan. But I don't want to risk it, so I just keep using the fan. Yes, it gets hot, but I figure if I don't binge for hours and hours and if I use the fan, the system will be fine. I also make sure to keep the fan on after I'm done for a little bit. I figure it could help it cool down. (I don't know how many hours I played at longest with the fan off, but I don't want to chance it.)
7. I got a data recovery warranty with purchase of the HDD. I haven't used it yet, but it doesn't hurt to have peace of mind.

Now, I have had a small issue or two since the instillation. Nothing to destroy my system, but a few hiccups, some weird graphical issues, and a time or two with a loading screen that was going nowhere. I was able to get around these, but I cannot be 100% sure if it was the games or the system with its new HDD and equipment. Again, I'm only speaking from personal experience.

What I'm getting at is that this device isn't flawless, as noted by other users, but for me my experience has been positive. I hope my tips and feedback help whoever reads this. Like many others, I was excited at the idea of upping my system to A LOT of TBs, but with reviews about how the system acted funny at 4TBs and up, I am happy with 2TB.

For our situation, the Wii unit is next to the television, so therefore, he can not sit too far away from the screen.  We have a 32" screen so it isn't as big of a deal, but if you were playing on a larger screen, it is really too close to sit. title: Beautiful and heartwarming game and story, but not so much for Player 2 onward.
text:
I want to be very clear: I absolutely adore this game.

It is beautifully done. It's peaceful, meditative and engaging. It is everything I love about this kind of game. It rewards adventure and whimsy, and I am loving working to slowly develop my island and invite new faces to it. I haven't felt so invested in a game like this, so fulfilled, since Stardew Valley.

But here's the thing. I'm Player One of Three in my household. And for Player Two and Three, it is still enjoyable but a far less fulfilling experience.

Having everyone on the same system share one island is not the end of the world. We personally like that. We would have liked the option to have our own private islands to sculpt, but whatever. What we don't like is that the experience P1 gets is not the same experience P2 and P3 get. I get to build relationships with villagers, I get quests to unlock buildings, I get to move the story forward--and they just kinda hang out and have to wait for me to do it. They don't get to actually participate in the story for the most part, and feel like bystanders in their own save of the game. Even their interactions with the villagers so far don't seem to matter as much. That just feels bad. I was so excited when I realized they would want to play this with me, and felt so sorry when I realized they would only get a fraction of the experience I was getting. Over the past couple of days, we keep stumbling over things they are ultimately missing out on or don't have access to as additional players, and I keep feeling the need to apologize.

Not to mention, if any of us play to our hearts desire on any given day, the other two hop on later to find there is little for us to do, no resources left to collect. There are three of us. I have no idea how this island and its resources is supposed to support up to eight players.

I hope the developers of this game seriously weigh the feedback they're getting on this and patch in something that at least attempts a compromise. Please give P2 + a unique storyline experience of their own that actually matters--something not tied to P1 progress.

The Direct for this game asks, "What kind of life do -you- want to live?"

This household's answer: the kind Player One gets to have.

title: Slow But Satisfying
text:
I’ll lead with this. Your enjoyment of this game will hinge on whether or not you are okay with some tedium and slower paced games. The payoff is a great story and a uniquely satisfying setting.

The Wild West may not be everyone’s thing in gaming, and there’s a reason it features in so few games. To accurately portray (in a gaming sense) the genre, you have to slow things down. This means traveling by horse takes longer than driving across GTA by car or flying by helicopter (shocker!).

The game adds in more bits like needing to eat, sleep, and bathe, that annoy some folks who just want to jump in and rob trains and blow things up. That’s their prerogative, but skipping this game for the tedious bits means you miss a beautifully set game with a solid story. Some of us even enjoy the more life-like aspects like hunting for food, stopping in at the general store, and greeting passers-by.

The spontaneous interactions are what make this game seem like the most realistic Western sim I’ve ever played. Random encounters galore here.

There are some major issues like the bandana (robbery mask) not working the way you’d think it does- just google it to see the complaints. Bumping people on your horse can start wild gun fights. Even finishing fights that other bandit gangs start with you can get you a bounty. So there are some annoying bits. No game is perfect though!

Overall the story and solid gameplay mechanics have been enough to keep me hooked and coming back for more. Sometimes you just want to ride your horse through the Wild West and bag a Buffalo before heading into the saloon for some poker. This game is great for lazy enjoyment with some thrills and fast paced action thrown in for fun.

title: *UPDATED 2x* choose your drive carefully
text:
The problems this product has are beyond Nyko's control. If Sony chooses not to support this 3rd party mod (which they'd have to have a LOT of motivation to do) this product is dead.

I've tried 6Tb drives from two well known manufacturers, as well as 4Tb drives. In all cases you can not use rest mode because the drives are recognized as 3.5 which isn't supported. That's not a big issue, and the initial setup works; you can download games for a few hours maybe without any problems. In my experience over all of the drives during the past week, every one was riddled with random freezes, reboots, and corrupted data that had to be re-downloaded. I don't think this is any issue with the Nyko Data Bank, it simply doesn't work with the Ps4 firmware at this time. Currently, a drive of any size appears to be working at first, but with any use shows that it does break the system and is unusable.

*Update: I've started renting games from Gamefly now but NONE work. The error codes are CE-30012-6 if the Internet is on and CE-30034-4 if it's off. No one really knows the exact problem, but the possible culprit is that the single power cord can run the Playstation 4 and a hard drive up to about 4Tb without errors, but drawing more power for more platters on a hard drive or trying to spin a disk draws too much power and causes the errors. If only Nyko made their Data Bank use a separate power source it would actually play disc games, but then there would be other problems (such as turning off and on with the console).

2nd Update: keeping the power issue in mind I used a 6TB WD brand "purple" hard drive which is specifically designed for always-on security video systems. It's supposed to use less power, run cooler, and be optimized for constant overwriting. Suddenly the problems with random freezing and rebooting are gone. I still can't use the disc drive to play games and rest mode doesnt always work so I just turned that off. So now I have a functional 6Tb drive that I don't ever see being filled and I don't feel like I'm missing out on anything. If I knew all of this to begin with (ie Nyko listed power spec requirements or compatible drives) this would have been a 4 or 5 star product. Since I had to figure this out via spending a month testing $1,000 worth of drives and configurations I'm only upping my stars from 2 to 3.

title: Great Controller. Might be Better than the Pro Controller!
text:
This is a fantastic controller. I'm amazed at how well a 3rd party replicated the Gamecube controller.

The Gamecube controller adapter for Wii U is highly sought after. The Gamecube controller really is the best controller to play Smash Bros. I wanted that adapter, but I'm not going to pay $90+ for it. And it *only* works for Smash Bros!

This controller is perfect for Smash Bros. But it's also perfect for other games. Even though I own 2 pro controllers, I'm finding this to be my go-to controller for other games such as Mario Kart 8 and the NES Remix games.

It is not truly wireless since it's tethered to the Wiimote, but that really doesn't matter. It *is* wireless in that you can be far from your TV and console and play. This is really a genius solution. A Gamecube replica controller that acts as a classic controller by plugging into the Wiimote - so, as I mentioned, you can use it with other games - not just Smash Bros.

I do miss rumble functionality just a little, but the official Nintendo Pro controller has weak rumble that you barely notice. The lack of rumble is far from a deal breaker and not enough to keep this from being a 5-star product.

I highly recommend this controller!

title: Best fitness game on the market!
text:
After trying Wii Fit and some similar fitness games for Wii, I have to say that this is far and above the rest. Because:

*Good workouts, at a pace you choose (Low, Medium, and Hard)
*Doesn't take a long time to get started (no long menus or long load times between exercises)
*A great variety of workouts
*Good use of the remote and nunchuck sensors (speed, tracking your movements, etc)
*Included elastic band (although a bit on the flimsy side, you can use any generic band in its place)
*Uses the balance board, but doesn't require it (most of the exercises do not use the balance board and all of them can be done without it.)

One other thing that I appreciate about this game is the positive feedback from the computer. That might sound silly, but after hearing from Wii Fit what a slacker I was and how much more I should be doing, having this one take what I give it and be grateful for it is a real relief. My life is busy enough and has enough stress as it is to have a computer criticize my efforts. This game doesn't do that.

On the other hand, I will need to purchase a wireless nunchuck because the cord is often getting in the way. However, this is the first game that has earned my respect as a realistic replacement for a gym membership. It is probably worth twice what it costs considering how much I was paying for the gym.

I love it!

title: I like it but it IS buggy
text:
Got mine yesterday and played most of the day. You have to give the game a chance and play it for any significant length of time before deciding on whether or not you like it, simply because there IS a lot to do, only you have to do a lot of vacationing in order to do it. There's lots of hidden things that take exploring to find. LOTS of stuff to collect (money, gold, gems, relics, and more)! Lots to do (Quests, challenges, and more)! Lots of new stuff for your Sim to learn! This EP is more like a game within itself because you have to do certain things in order to get other certain things to work in order to proceed forward on your challenges.

I don't want to go into detail on what all is offered in the game because it would just spoil the surprises for everybody else who hasn't played it yet. Suffice it to say, I like it and I'm glad I got it. I think it was well worth the money. There really is a lot to do in the game, you just have to explore, look, do a lot of traveling, and be willing to do the challenges.

Also, there are bugs and glitches in the game. I've found some stuff I had purchased in France didn't make it into my inventory/backpack (the nectar rack), and one of the new bookshelves doesn't work...you can open the bookcase and add books but when you select 'read' or 'read something' the new books don't appear on the list for you to read. However, if you open the bookcase again they show up. I'm also getting thick green 'streaks' that come down from the top of the screen at an angle and end on the object (for lack of a better way to explain it) whenever I try to move objects or furniture. I don't have ANY custom content, never have. I can't delete any furniture now either for some reason..once its bought, I'm stuck with it unless a burglar comes and steals it (which happened to my old crappy bathtub luckily so I was able to get a new one to put in its place). Hopefully a patch will come out soon, but in the meantime it's not detracting from my fun of playing the game in any way, so I gave it a five star rating.

I personally feel that this is a must have EP. It really expands your Sims' world. There are even PUZZLES in the game that YOU have to figure out (albeit somewhat easy for an adult) in order for your Sim to go forward on their quests and challenges. If you get bored after only playing for a half hour, that's your own fault, you didn't play long enough to give the game a chance, nor could you have done much exploring to find the fun stuff.

I'm happy......now just need the patch so I can be even happier..lol.

Overall, very pleased.

title: Get "Lego Marvel Superheroes" if You Want Lego Avenger Action; This is the Worst Lego Game Ever
text:
This is the most poorly designed Lego game since Lego Batman (1). It's extremely buggy and unpolished, but what really stands out is how well they implemented BAD IDEAS. The "puzzles" are terribly contrived and offer confusion to adults without even providing a thought-provoking challenge for children. It's just awful.

If you want a Lego Avengers game, get Lego Marvel Superheroes. It has more heroes, an original story, good writing, good puzzles, and the EXACT SAME open world Manhattan. I could go on - let me know if you want details to back up WHY this game is a terrible mess, because I have numerous examples. Here's a couple primary sins though:

1. The scene at the start of Avengers where Coulson interrupts Stark and Potts talking? They have a conversation in the movie. They turned that into an action scene in this game. "Contrived" and "pointless" are a start, but they don't cover the frustration I experienced.

2. The scene where Hulk jumps from building to building, smashing aliens at the end of Avengers? They made that into a cinematic. In short, you play the pointless unfun parts that weren't in the movies, and you watch (without control) during the fun, cool parts of the movies.

Playing as a giant Fin Fang Foom was the only bright spot in this game, and it wasn't nearly worth the hours I slogged through the movie-based storyline. Do not inflict this on friends or family.

title: I never thought I'd say this, but...
text:
this game makes working out FUN! I'm into the second week of my 30 day challenge, and am noticing results, already. My husband is noticing the results, too! I like to work out, but I get bored easily. I don't think I'll get bored with Active.

I tried the 30 day challenge workout, but I prefer to create custom workouts. For my preference, the 30 day challenge workout offered too many exercises I don't like to do. With the custom workout option, I can work out as long as I want, doing exactly what I want, at the intensity I want. Perfect. I have created short and long workouts with sports drills and calisthenics, focusing on upper body, lower body, and cardio, depending on my mood. Due to some orthopedic injuries, there are some activities I cannot do comfortably two days in a row, so the custom workouts are a work-out saver!

I think the lifestyle questions and additional activities log are a very good idea. If you use the journal (you won't get a perfect score if you don't), you can log things like how much you slept, how stressed-out you feel, how much water (or sugary soda!) you drank, etc. Also, the game gives you credit for doing yardwork, household chores, and other activities during the non-Wii portion of your day. The journal is pretty simplistic, but it makes you think about how rest, stress-level, water, motivation, & activity level are important to your overall fitness.

Why four stars? The cons:

---The controls are a bit glitchy, making completing some exercises difficult. It's pretty frustrating to have the nunchuk secured in the holster while using good form, and still be told that you're not doing the exercise correctly. I've had to quit a few exercises because the Wii wasn't sensing my movements.

---The thigh band for the holster is of ample length to fit almost anyone's leg, but the holster pocket seems too tight for the nunchuk. I'm afraid that my nunchuk will eventually be damaged by placing (cramming) it into the pocket.

---A few---JUST A FEW---of the sports drills are lame (basketball, you know I'm talking to you).

This is the first workout software I've bought, and I'm extremely pleased with it, overall. I hope this review helps you decide if Wii Active is right for you.

title: A very nice production
text:
"Letters from Nowhere" is possibly an ultimate hidden object offering as there isn't much else to the game. If you're a hidden object nut, you're going to be right in your element! You will be peering into a lot of scenes, and although some hidden objects will land right into your lap, others are very reluctant for you to find them. Luckily the hint mechanism revs up fast. Puzzles dispersed here and there are for the most part the usual tired old things: putting a torn letter together, matching turned down cards, uniting zodiac figures with their proper symbols. The game is divided into chapters as Audrey, the protagonist, marches along from scene to scene searching for her husband Patrick who has disappeared, and reading as she goes the strange typewritten messages that flutter out of the blue. Piquancy is added to the search environments as you will have to assemble certain artifacts, such as putting the head back on a doll, popping bread into a toaster, painting over a graffiti on a door, loading a gun with bullets.

The game boasts a bonus system which makes for great replay value. In each chapter you will earn points that will accumulate to unlock a bonus. The first "trophy" is a thermometer which will be hidden in every scene in that chapter. You poke around until you find it and when you do your cursor will morph into a hot cold detector which will flash red when you're near an object you should click on. You have to work fast, though, as the trophy will expire. Each trophy, a thermometer, a camera, a palette, a necklace and more will require you to do something different in every case, so your mind is kept busy. Each environment also contains three hidden postage stamps and if you find all 50 of them you'll unlock Unlimited Mode at the end of the adventure. Gathering various trophies helps to secure interest in the plot and keeps it moving. You are always involved in doing something!

The art work in Letters is very fine with each chapter being introduced by a stunning sepia-colored drawing and each environment rendered beautifully with pinpoint sharpness. The game is introduced and is ended by comic book -like drawings which personally I do not care for, but that is a minor issue. The game is linear and straight forward and the strange letters, typewritten and creepy, will keep you forging ahead as the story line and the gathering of trophies will spark your interest. The game is unabashedly linear: you come, you see and you conquer, just like Caesar.

"Letters from Nowhere" is a solid, interesting game although the ending is a cliffhanger where you are left dangling. It's a very good value for $6.99 and hidden object buffs will undoubtedly purr with joy!

title: Nice Upgrade / Needs Work
text:
To find out what the game is about read the Amazon.com review above. I am just opining as a seasoned player here.
I have been playing SimCity since it first came out. Each evolution has made significant advances in both look and performance, and this version is no exception to that. I appreciate the level of detail, the complexity of the simulation engine, and the overall performance of the game. The problem lies in the pre-release hype that was inaccurate or at least highly misleading.
Maxis / Electronic Arts promised much during the months leading up to the (delayed) release of this game. They promised increased control over traffic (such as timing lights at consecutive intersections - to be released in their expansion pack, SimCity4: Rush Hour). I will not list all of the items that were touted before release here, but suffice to say that it seems the game was not ready for release. A significant case in point was the patch that was released about a month after the game shipped.
I have a fast machine, so I have not had the problems of hanging and freezing that others have had. Having read of many other gamers who HAVE had many problems with performance tells me that we should not expect to have any more expansion packs for SimCity 4. In my opinion, the good folks at Maxis / EA need to redesign the graphics programming so that it performs better with more modest machines.

title: Good workout, frustrating accessories for those trying to lose weight.
text:
Let's start with some full disclosure here. I'm fat. I am trying desperately to undo that situation, and with all the recommendations from colleagues, folks in my WW group, and my primary care physician, I went ahead and ordered this, along with the "More Workouts".

The software is fine, although the trainers are a bit annoying, but what trainer isn't? The issue I have is with the hardware...

At 6' 0", and 300lbs, my thigh is just a wee bit big for the dumb leg strap thing-a-ma-jig for the nunchuck. Now I know for a good number of already fit folks you are going to say big whoop dee right? Remember, it's the fatties that are the majority these days! (Thank Bill Gates and the Internet age for that!). it just struck me as silly that this thing is sized for already fit people when I would suspect that the average customer is like me...

At the very least they ought to include something to more easily extend the strap...

The resistance bands leave a LOT to be desired. They resemble baloons, and you have to tie them off to the handles yourself. And the knots very easily slip while you are working out...

All in all, I am wishing I had figured out a different rig for the nunchuck, and just used some power bands from the sporting goods store with the software... These hardware pieces seem like a real waste of money.

title: Old Time Animal Crosser (Hints included)
text:
This was worth the wait. Played it on release day. Due to the pandemic everyone was pretty much screwed over this week.

Please ignore the reviews from all those who DID NOT READ before purchasing. The information about it being one island per a console was included in the Nintendo direct for the game weeks before the release. It is not a SURPRISE. (as well as everything else they're complaining about...)

I don't recommend this game for people who lack patience or do not want to do the WORK involved to fully enjoy this delightful treasure filled masterpiece 😍💜

I've been playing animal crossing since the first gamecube release in the early 2000s. I was 8 or 9 then. I'm considering this game to be filled with Easter eggs because I didn't play the original release of new horizon. But this updated version. Kudos to Nintendo for reviving such a great title on the switch. Was rather surprised this was a global release. But it was worth the wait.

I love how you can choose your island layout then later change the layout. I didn't like the 2 neighbors I had at first so I reset my island twice until I ended up with two cute animals (Cherry and Hamlet!) The pick of your neighbors and fruit are totally random. Pfft ended up with my usual apple and oranges lol.

Once you unlock 1 thing everything else gradually unlocks. If you don't know what you're doing go to Google. Getting stuck in progress is completely normal, everyone needs a little direction.

There's tons to do for a good 2-4 hours but I do expect this to die down soon as I continue to unlock more things in the island. At the moment I'm focused on tidying up so I can invite my friends in.

Finished unlocking Nooks Cranny , Campsite , Residents Service Building , Museum etc on March 23rd.

Along this line I was able to travel to other islands.

I'm hoping I can swim in this one like new leaf. Waiting for the guidebook to be released April 9th so I can keep track of all my fossils etc. So far I don't check them I just dump them on Blabbermouth Owl.

Spoiler/Hint for newbies:

Things I have noticed from personal observation.
donate to nook 5 creatures and pay off your moving fees asap in miles to start a house. The quicker you do that the sooner other options will unlock for you. The big blue butterflies (Emperor) will help you rack bells quickly. Rebury money you find in the ground to grow money trees.

Unlock your house to unlock more inventory space! Dig two holes behind you before you hit a rock this way it will kick out 9 goodies! So far I've seen 16k max in bells for money rocks.

When in doubt just Google (or continue to poke Nook!) :]

title: Definitely a must-own if you're looking for good Wii workout "games"!
text:
I have to say that I thought that the hype over the original EA Sports Active was a little overdone. Yes, it's a good workout "game", but I just didn't "feel the burn" quite as much with that game as I do with this one.

Of course, as is the case with any workout, be it via video game console, personal trainer, gym equipment, or simple self-motivation, YOU are the catalyst in truly determining just how effective your workouts are, but the original EA Sports Active just didn't grab me and suck me in as I'd really hoped it would. EA Sports Active: More Workouts, DOES.

The game does not, as other reviewers have stated, offer up the exact same exercises as EA Sports Active, nor does it directly piggyback off of the first game as Wii Fit and Wii Fit Plus do, but the exercises to be found in "...: More Workouts" actually add to the options offered by the first game, albeit individually, and require that you switch disks.

Here, with Squash, you're not just stuck standing there, as you are in SO many of the tennis-type games already out for the Wii. No, you won't feel like Andy Roddick or Serena Williams at the end of your time playing squash, but at least this version of a tennis-like game will get you doing more with your legs than just standing there on them.

With the boxing station, your legs are also added in, via kicks, although I do have to say that I find that I have to do a half squat just before the kicks in order to get my balance board to recognize that I actually HAVE lifted my foot off of it to kick. No half squat? Well then, no credit or acknowledgment for the kick!

The Island Outrun, Sprint, and Obstacle Course exercises are some of my favorite - most especially, the Obstacle Course exercise. I really get my muscles warmed up and break a nice sweat when I do the Course, what with the rafting, stump and other jumping, and lever crank exercises, all preceded and followed by quick sprints to each new "station".

As with the first EA Sports Active, you're expected to use the resistance band that came with the original game, as well as the leg strap (a necessary evil). I'm sure that, like me, you'll soon feel that the resistance offered by the lightweight band enclosed with the first EA Active (but not this one) loses real workout value - it's just not challenging enough after a few weeks. In order to push myself to a deeper, more intensive workout, I bought myself a set of resistance bands here on Amazon ([[ASIN:7245456208 New Set of 5 Stackable Resistance Bands Cords Tubings with Door Anchor Great for P90x and Physical Therapy]] - LOVE 'em!), and some nylon luggage strapping/belt material from my local fabric store, along with a set of D rings, and made myself some longer straps so that I can use my resistance bands in my EA Sports Active workouts.

With the deeper resistance, and the exercises that this newer game has to offer, I'm definitely more motivated to get off my butt and get in my regular workouts. I swear, I used to think I was allergic to exercise, but between this game, the resistance bands that I bought, the longer straps that I made for the bands, and Wii's [[ASIN:B001DZF36M Boogie Superstar]] (another recent workout favorite) I really feel like my workouts have become less of a chore, and more of a gratifying sweatfest. It feels good to get off my butt and get some exercise in, especially when the workouts are engaging enough that I forget that I hated working out in the first place! ;)

title: Non-Nintendo-made nunchuks don't seem to work with this, but it's worth picking up for a good workout!
text:
I've had this game for about a month and a half, and have tried to get a workout going with it four times. Apparently, checking EVERYTHING is important if you're having issues with it picking up on your movements.

I took the original disc back to the store I'd originally gotten it from, certain that the problem was with the game disc itself. After I got a new copy (just this afternoon), I decided to try the original Nintendo Wii nunchuk that came with my system, instead of the Nyko nunchuk that I use for EVERY other game that I play. Problem solved! The Nyko nunchuk is a bit larger than the Nintendo nunchuk, so that probably affected how it fits into the pocket on the leg strap. I'd also picked up a Wii MotionPlus, just in case that might help the disc pick up my movements better. I never even needed to open up the MotionPlus packaging - the problems were ALL solved by just sticking with the original Nintendo nunchuk.

If you're experiencing the same sensory problems that I was, see if using the original nunchuk solves those problems - it probably will. As for the workout ITSELF, I fully expect to be unable to walk properly tomorrow, due to all of the sore muscles I anticipate having! ; )

In previous attempts to get in my workout with this game, I was only able to get a few features to work with my Nyko nunchuk - one of which was running around the track. I own Wii Fit, Gold's Gym Cardio Workout, and My Fitness Coach, but even with those three, for some reason I'm MUCH more motivated to work hard on the run around the track with this game. The day after I'd done just two of the "long" running sessions, and not much else, my quads were SO sore that I couldn't walk without wincing. GOOD workout! The inline skating is also good, and motivating. Volleyball and tennis are fun to do while you're working out, and provide an opportunity for you to let your heart rate decrease a bit while still moving and exercising. The lunges, squats, tricep kickbacks, and other similar exercises are really no different than any you could do on your own, or with any of the other Wii fitness games, but the addition of the resistance band IS a plus. I DO question how helpful the leg strap is and accurate the readings are when taken with the nunchuk in it, but if those readings help me improve my form even minutely, I'll consider that a plus.

Overall, if you're not against dropping around sixty bucks for another fitness game, I think that this one IS worth adding to your collection, and I expect to get a good workout from this game, along with the other fitness games that I have. It's a good option for a real workout that'll get you sweating, really work your muscles, and make you well-aware of exactly which muscles are where. If you're NOT keen, however, on dropping sixty on a game, you can probably do without this one. As long as you don't try it before you decide NOT to buy it, you'll never know what you're missing, and won't have the opportunity to regret skipping the purchase of it! Don't mind spending the purchase price on it? Then get it! I firmly believe that it'll help you get into shape, if you're more couch potato than hard body!

title: The Wii Fit Choice For a North American Workout
text:
If you're like any of us gamers and Wii fans (and yes, there is a difference these days), who were sorely disappointed with the Wii Fit and want something that actually works than THIS review is for you.

Nothing against the Japanese but as we've noticed with many of their products such as their cars, motorcycles, and the Wii Fit, neither were designed with the physiology of Westerners in mind (the Nissan Maxima and the Yamaha Roadliner being the exception). The Wii Fit game and balance board were NOT designed with Westerners in mind as many of us are well over six feet tall and, if we're overweight, than we cannot use the Wii Fit as the maximum weight limit is 330 lbs.

For instance; I am 6'5 and just over the limit. I can remember trying it out and, in a Garfield-esque manner, the board informed me that it is not a freight scale and begged me to get off of it. End of story, now what do I do? Exercise outside of the Wii perhaps? Where's the fun in that?!

I later tried to workout alongside a friend of mine, who was not the size of Manny the Mammoth, and mirror the movements on the screen. This would've worked except he got bored of the mundane and repetitive workouts and stopped playing, leaving me in the proverbial dust.

Enter EA Sports Active.

Electronic Arts advertised the "Active" as a Wii Fit alternative that will does not limit itself to simply weight loss and more of a regimen to improve your overall physical fitness. Wii Fit places its emphasis solely on weight and balance, which is not the end all of a workout. How the Active achieves this is through a 30-day challenge where the AI pushes you through three workout modes in increasing difficulty (low-intensity, medium-intensity, and high-intensity). The AI will then track how well you do with some basic workouts and then determine which exercises you will do next. For instance, I had trouble crouching during long inline skating so the AI had me practice squats again... and again.

Now, to address the level of difficultty, I made the mistake of trying the high-intensity workout straight out of the box and couldn't walk after 15 minutes. I woke up a few hours later and barely was able to stand out of bed. So take it from me, DO NOT *I REPEAT* DO NOT OVER EXERT YOURSELF. Start out slow.

Now, to avoid over-working out, the Active gives you a time limit before it stops you from working out any further. This is good since it's all too easy to over-exert yourself and cause personal injury. The Active also gives you days off where it will not allow you to work out. Of course, you could just load up another profile and start from there, but seriously, is it worth getting injured over? I think not. Even Jillian Michaels knows when to stop her contestants before they hurt themselves.

So, now onto the unique equipment of the Active. Normally, I would say that the Active is designed for the North American audience but the hip-strap certainly isn't. The hip-strap is designed to house the nunchuck for certain stretches and jogging (with a silent "j"). I had a difficult time getting the strap around my upper leg and felt as though I was about to give blood through it. Just grin, grit your teeth and tie that sucker on as best you can; if it can fit me, it WILL fit you.

Next is the resistance strap. It kinda readjusts to the heigth to the user but, rest assured, it will NOT break under normal use. Be advised that THIS IS NOT A DARE TO TRY. The resistance strap will help you do arm curls and shoulder stretches designed to work muscles and improve flaxibility.

Lastly is the Wii Fit balance board. Unlike the Wii Fit game, EA Active removes the weight limit and lets me workout with whatever I want (Suck on THAT Nintendo!!). It doesn't seem to use the balancing measurements, but it does help with kick boxing.

Now, does the Active really work? Does it fulfill it's mission to get you in better physical fitness? Oh, yes it does! I can finally run the mile without too much trouble whereas I couldn't do even the half-mile before. I feel a lot better about myself and can actually do a daily workout that doesn't involve picking out very boring regimens.

Lastly, for the cost of a Wii Fit versus the Active... I think it's more than apparent.

title: Massive grinder, relaxing, but lots of development oversights
text:
This is my first time playing Animal Crossing, but have played similar games like Stardew Valley in the past. There's a lot to love about this game, and it's a welcome break during the Covid madness, but there are also a lot of oversights that make this game quickly becoming lame for me.

What I love:
- Relaxing - Simple activities without much of any action. You fish, you plant flowers, you interior design. That's about it.
- UI/Design - The simplicity of the design for things like fishing (no on-screen icons, just you, your rod, and the water). The characters are also super cute.

What I don't like:
- Multiplayer - We bought one copy to share on our single device, with two separate online Switch accounts. My partner and I were forced to share the same island. Further, only the FIRST person to play the game gets to progress the story (e.g. unlockable events from Tom Nook like building bridges and getting key recipes).
- Repetitive simple tasks - You need to eat food to do heavy-lifting chores like digging up trees. You need to eat each food item individually, so in order to move 10 trees you need to eat one apple 10 times, which is annoying because each apple takes about 10 seconds to eat.
- A culture of prioritizing grinding (i.e. requiring the user to spend countless hours playing to unlock simple upgrades) - There are many ways to use the game design to get money quickly, such as tarantula hunting. Granted, some of them I'd consider "cheating" such as changing the timestamp of your Switch to move ahead in time, or duplicating expensive items, which I support them getting rid of as they aren't fair and against the point of the game. With each new update that has come out, they've found ways to ensure people can't make money quickly. The tarantulas on islands is a popular one, but they have been making it difficult to actually make use of it - such as adding "water bugs" that force tarantulas to not spawn, or adding 3-layer islands so you have to constantly use pole-vault/ladder which is very time-consuming. Some people don't want to spend 30 hours of gameplay fishing for the same fish, so why force people to do this?
- Online play: You have to go to the airport and open/close the gate, and unless you do this, you can't do many actions on your island such as redecorating. Again, a waste of time that they seem to encourage.
- "Second active player" - When someone "dials" in another user on the same Switch, they can follow the main player around. However, there isn't much that player can do aside from simple emotions and using tools. Picking up items is time-consuming (again) as it does a celebration graphic for every single item. There's no access to your inventory. And when the second player is away from their controller, there is no "auto-follow" option which makes the camera angle a huge hindrance to the primary player.

I think this game can be good, but it's got a lot wrong with it that seems to be intentional by the game designers. All in all a fun game, but I wouldn't recommend it to anyone for any reason other than to visit my island. :-P
