title: My Thing Review
text:
First of all, as one of the biggest John Carpenter fans (I even kind of liked Ghosts of Mars) that I know, I was both eagerly anticipating and dreading this game. I knew that there was no way for it to live up to the 1982 film, but I was hoping that it would. I am both pleased and somewhat disappointed. As a Carpenter fan I enjoyed the way that the game managed to build upon the film. You do find out who was infected at the end of the movie (was is MacReady or was it Childs) and you get to look at the spaceship that Blair (A.k.a Wilford Brimley) was building - and all of this happens in the playable prologue in a visit to the site of the original film. The nice mood that the game builds up in this prologue (and trust me, its really creepy) eventually winds down into a rather average first person shooter. Now, as a fan of both half-life AND all of the resident evil games (yes, even survivor!) I like first person shooters as much as I like survival horror games - but this ends up being almost too much of the former. While much has been said here about all of the great aspects of this game, little has been said about what just doesn't quite work. Yes, the whole trust aspect of the game is interesting - but there are problems. Certain squad members only follow you so far during levels before they change into a version of the thing and attack you (i.e. they will change just before you fight a boss - they won't go any further - so whether you kill them when they are a thing or save yourself some health and just put a bullet in their head before it happens is up to you. I prefer the latter since it saves ammo and it usually takes off the top of their head in a nifty video game gore way.) Now, I have no problem with this - it was in the movie and so it should be here. However, I see no point in being able to test the blood of your squad if they change into the Thing whether or not the blood test comes back positive or negative. Why even put the blood test in the game? So far, I have had about 5 team members - all of whom who have changed into the monster despite my giving them blood tests in which they tested negative for being infected. So that's a problem.
Second, the real time weapon switching (as opposed to Resident Evil, in which you have to switch to an inventory menu) can be really frustrating. Espescially when you are looking for a weapon, scrolling through a list, and getting jumped by five of those hopping chicken things from half-life. I've been killed many times because I pulled up a sniper rifle instead of my shotgun. Also, the weapon icons are so small that its hard to tell the difference between weapons - and since I only have a 29" TV - it can be tough.
The controls are much nicer than the "turn and move design of resident evil - however, since (at least on playstation two) the same joystick you move with is also the crouch button, I often find myself trying to run from a particularly tough foe, only to find myself duck walking away in a crouch since I pushed down on the joystick nub while running.
All in all this game is great for the gamer who likes survival horror or for the fan of the Carpenter film who has never played R.E. or Devil May Cry or Silent Hill. However, it will never replace R.E. Code Veronica in my collection.

title: This is a single player only game, marketed as a multiplayer game
text:
My daughter loves the game. The biggest problem? She wants to play it with me. There is no reason to play two player mode. Honestly, it is deceptive and dishonest advertising for Nintendo to claim this is a multiplayer game.

The first person to play the game becomes the "primary player." This isn't explained in any way, and has to be discovered by realizing that any subsequent player can't play the game. The island is frozen in the state that matches the primary player. This means you can't expand your home, modify the land, build bridges, unlock the shop, unlock the museum.... You get the point. You can't do ANY of these things unless you are primary, and you can't contribute to any of these unless you're the primary player. If your primary player happens to be a four year old girl who can't read yet, your game is frozen in the day one state.

Playing two players at the same time is almost even more frustrating. Player two can only interact with the game by harvesting resources. Those resources go to a general saved storage, and only player one can open the storage. Player two cannot control anything.

This is not a game you play together. It is a game one person plays while the other holds a controller and watches the same TV. It is ridiculous that Nintendo sold this game claiming it was multiplayer. Unfortunately it takes long enough to discover this that the game isn't eligible for refund by the time you realize it sucks.

text:
I tried this for the first time today, and overall I really enjoyed it and got a decent workout. I'm definitely a sweaty mess, so obviously it did its job!

I chose to do the 30 Day Challenge and set my workout intensity at Medium. It had me doing squats, bent over rows, shoulder raises, walking/jogging, side lunges, inline "skating", and boxing. The boxing was definitely my favorite and the exercise that made me feel it the most.

The cons I have after the first use are:
1) The font on the screen is incredibly difficult to read. I don't know if it was just our tv or what (I wouldn't think so since the Wii Fit appears just fine), but the font was very small and skinny and very hard to see.
2) The resistance band... I made the mistake of not putting it together before starting, so then all of a sudden I needed it. Well, there is no "pause" feature that I could find, so it was ready to start the workout and I wasn't because I was still putting the handles on the band. So then it started telling me I wasn't doing it right (DUH! I wasn't doing anything). Once I did get the band together and start using it, it's way too long and doesn't have hardly any resistance to it. I would recommend definitely getting a better band or cord to replace the resistance band that comes with this. I couldn't hardly feel anything on the rows or the shoulder raises with this one.

Overall, though, I enjoyed the first workout and definitely broke a sweat! I look forward to seeing what else it has to offer.

title: Installation Failed
text:
If your game installs and runs, I wish you all the best. I wish I could play the game, but I can't. It will not install.

I've spent 3 days (I know stupid, but I really wanted to play the game) following EA's website instructions for uninstalling and reinstalling their Download Manager. I THEN finally resorted to their live chat option (yeah, I finally admitted that it had me beat). Their live chat technical support consisted entirely of:
1). Checking to make sure I actually owned the game, had legally purchased it, and had 4 forms of legal ID and a strip search (ok the last two are a purely fictional manifestation of my frustration but I feel pretty violated after all the procedures we went through together)
2). Telling me to do exactly what their website told me to do (ok some people don't follow the directions, but I did)
3). Copying and pasting the links to the tech support pages I had already tried out into the chat window.

No really, I shut down my firewall (it's back up now so don't get any ideas), my router's firewall (yep, that's back up too), my antivirus software (practically had to uninstall it (yep it's back too) and changed computers - there are four in my house. And the download manager insists that I am somehow running the software on two different windows accounts (which my computer only had one until the tech support guy suggested I create a second one - just to run Sims 3 - yep that's gone too now).

So I asked the tech guy, "where do I file a complaint about the installation software?" And he says to me -- "would you like to submit your ideas?"

Ok, I lost it. Seriously? I've practically torn apart the software on my computer system for 3 days, uninstalled everything I don't use (just in case it was conflicting), and now I'm supposed to come up with how to solve their installation nightmare?

I don't normally write bad reviews, but hey... there's a point when you just have to stand up and say... "THAT WAS BAAAADDDD!!!!!!" Ok, I've said it. I hope it helps someone somewhere. Cheers!

title: Wished for some THING better
text:
"The Thing," based on John Carpenter's classic sci-fi horror film, is a step in the right direction for the survival horror genre in many ways, but it never truly lives up to its potential. The game designers could have taken a great leap forward in terms of gameplay and character interaction, but instead they chose a slight hop in favor of more action-oriented gaming. It's a shame, because the best thing about "The Thing" is recruiting allies, all the while keeping an eye on them lest they be Things themselves, even as they're keeping their eyes on you to ensure their own personal safety. These guys get scared, get sick when they stumble into a chamber splashed with gore, and sometimes demand that you prove your loyalty to them at gunpoint. But most of the time you'll just be running around shooting creepy crawlies that are fairly identical to one another, and just aren't very scary. That's not to say, though, that the game is completely devoid of scares - every now and then you can expect to be startled by some unexpected event. It's just that from a game based on "The Thing" property, you expect a little more than you get. Add some bland, if sometimes atmospheric, levels into the mix (they all look pretty similar to one another), and you've got a game that disappoints as much as it excites. I only hope another game (or a sequel) builds upon this unique gameplay concept and therefore makes the ultimate survival horror experience. In the meantime, this should tide you over, if you don't expect too much from it.
Final Score: C

title: A Great Game but not without Flaws.
text:
Finally the MOBA's arrive on consoles and for those wondering what a
MOBA is it's a Multiplayer Online Battle Arena. this style of
play has been popular on pc for a number of years now with games like
League of Legends dominating the market, so making one for console
was a great idea. another great idea they implemented is
no microtransactions like the pc counterparts have.most pc MOBA's
usually charge real cash for characters, items etc. here Guardians Shines
by not charging a cent for anything. you unlock characters by earning coin
(Gold) by doing battle with up to 5 human enemies (10 players total)
this may sound fantastic but as of this writing, I have not
been able to play and finish a true ten person game (no A.I. Bots)
so here's the rub, while it's a really fun game especally with friends
you will usually have 1-3 human opponents on a team and the rest
will be filled with A.I. Bots that perform pretty well considering
they're A.I. Controlled.
the gameplay consists mainly of killing enemy guardians (players)
destroying enemy Towers (defencive- fires on enemies)Upgrading your towers
and upgrading your Barracks (barracks when upgraded can produce mounted units, Siege units like Ents and elite fighters good for taking on players)
and finally destroying the enemy base. destruction of an enemies base immediately
ends the game. if the timer runs out the game ends as well.
there are a number of game modes to choose from including an all
A.I. vs Player Match setup called Skirmish Mode. it's a good place to start
for the new player.
the 2nd mode Battlegrounds is the meat of the game and has the choice of
three lane (more strategic) or One lane (full on head to head battle)
then there's Elite Battlegrounds for pure player vs player matches no Bots
However again another flaw shows up with wait times for a single match
taking up to 15 minutes to start, then later one might start in ten.
other times there's not enough players for a match and you have
to wait until the queue is filled.
Once you've chosen your battle type and get into a game it
is fantastic with glorious spell effects and all sorts of team buffs
like shields, healing, shrouded in darkness etc. and there's
Commands in addition to abilities that have a longer cooldown but allows the player
to have a quick heal at level one but maxed out at level 12 you can
summon a Balrog or an Ent. there's about five Command Power choices
per level and four levels each unlocking at lvl four, eight, and twelve.
finally, there are Relics that you can equip up to three of and fill with gems
these apply various effects from regeneration to the more expensive
relics shrouding the player in a shield each time an ability is used.
others increase damage and others still speed up cooldowns.
the animations are excellent but nothing new with an isometric style of view
of the lanes or lane.
Characters to begin with you have on each side (good and evil)
three unlocked characters and 5000 gold is required to unlock another
though they have a great "Featured" group of characters each week that are free to use for that week only. as of this writing I do not know if they will cycle.
a really fun game that could have been more fun with all ten friends.

Gameplay: 5 stars a blast to play and a deep amount of strategy

Graphics: clean and nicely animated 4 stars

Sound: nothing beyond the expected 4 stars

Controls: 5 stars simple and easy to pick up and play.

Overall: if it weren't for the wait times for matches
with human players this would easily be a Five Star title
but the wait times are annoying. I have read on the official
forums that several patches are coming to address the issues I stated
about the long wait times and games with ten live players failing
to remain stable long enough to complete a match. so let's
hope they bring out a patch for these soon since it truly
is a Gem on the Psn and XBL marketplaces.
the game only falls short of greatness due to those two flaws.
don't overlook it try the demo First!

Downloads off your service (I Used PSN)
so in this retail box you get a cardboard disc that has a voucher code on it
good for BOTH the full game and the Season Pass. this pass get's you eight more guardians as they are released. so if you're wondering if there's a disc
in the retail ps3 version, the answer is No.

title: Nyko Data Bank; Does the job
text:
My Nyko Data bank arrived and I decidded I was gonna install it on my PS4 as soon as I got it. Didn't really know what to expect. Turns out it was an easy install, except for a few confusing bits in the process. I was able to install a 4TB Seagate SSHD into it, which was what I was looking forward to the most. Current gen gamers know how much of a burden having only 500GB of space in their PS4 can be. And while a 1TB 2.5" drive would've sufficed for a while, why not just go bigger? And this little device does the trick to do just that, install a 3.5" Hard Drive of your own or a Hybrid Drive of course. Also, one last note; I was worried that the drive input wouldn't be able to hold the drive well enough, but I tried to pull it out just to test it and it was in there pretty tight.

Update: I had an issue when shutting off my PS4; I would turn it back on from it being completely off, not rest mode. I don't know if it was a problem with the Nyko Data bank or an issue that occurs when changing a hard drive, but I did some research on the internet and apparently there is this thing called a "Safe Mode Loop" where no matter what you do, it'll continue going back to safe mode when you turn on your PS4 from a complete shutdown.
Well, the fix was to disconnect the PS4 for a few minutes then turn it back on, wait on the "Safe Mode Screen" for about 10 minutes then having your PS4 controller plugged in, press the PlayStation button in the middle and then when prompted to choose an option, choose option number 4 in safe mode, which resets your settings and somehow got rid of the "Safe Mode Loop", at least for now that is. After that process was concluded I then went ahead and turn the PS4 on and off with the controller, 3 times and turning it back on did not give me that dreaded "Safe Mode Loop". Here's to hoping that 1, the Nyko Data bank will not malfunction in the near future and 2: that the "Safe Mode Loop" will not come back.

title: Challenging but glitchy
text:
After using Wii Fit, then Wii Fit Plus for 6 months I was finally ready to step it up a bit. I did my research, looking over all the exercise programs available for the Wii, and settled on EA Sports Active, More Workouts. I am NOT disappointed! It is a lot of fun, much more efficient than Wii Fit and definitely challenging for me.

There is a 6 week challenge portion which is designed to keep you working four days a week, with focus on varying muscle groups. The cardio portion changes often and I am never bored with these pre-set routines. The warm-up and cool-down portions are always the same but I actually appreciate the repetition in those portions of the workout. There is also a portion where you can design your own routine, or follow a number of pre-set routines.

Rather then rehash what other reviewers have already covered I'd like to mention the few items that need a bit of tweaking by EA.

1. During several of the exercises the interface between the Wii and the remotes does not track properly. There are ways around this for some of them, but there are a couple of them which I need to skip entirely when they come up, since the program will not sense my movements.

2. I have my preferences set to use the Wii Balance Board (this is an option, but is not necessary for use of EA Sports Active) but when I do the 6-week challenge routines it does not use the Balance Board. When you create your own routine, you CAN specifically select Wii Balance Board exercises.

3. The step aerobics are fun to use but there is no step, you must purchase one separately. If you plan to use your Wii Balance Board as a step, be aware that the 6-week challenge program does not incorporate it in, even when selected in preferences. Of course, you can still use the Balance Board as a step, even if you don't have it turned on.

4. The Daily medal that is awarded is down right irritating. It is not accurate to real life so if you are goal/reward oriented you will find this portion frustrating to you. You may have a scheduled skip day, which the program encourages you to take, however you are penalized in the medal portion because it gives you credit for a workout, and takes away points when you don't perform a workout. The nutrition measurement is based on a very basic quiz you take that only asks you about how much water you drank, how many veggie servings you ate yesterday and what is your attitude about working out, and eating right. It doesn't measure your calorie intake overall, or make allowances for any types of variations.

Overall, I'd say it is worth the purchase as an exercise tool, for a person of my size and ability, however, I'm sure that we are going to see great strides and improvements in this arena and this program is only the beginning. For now, it is probably the best available, and it does make me work hard, burn calories, tone muscles and ENJOY IT!!!

title: This is Simcity 4 only.. Rushhour expansion (or SC4Deluxe) is crucial
text:
This game was released about 2003 and developed over the 5 years prior to that. It also is completely unsupported by its "owners" EA (which bought it from Maxis)and has been for pushing a decade (it is a "cash cow" only). It is out of it's element on todays machines. The game is single-threaded and has its own scheduler. It is not well-adapted to a multitasking environment. It also can be rather snarky in getting along with some graphics cards. This means it has some real quirks and issues such as occasional failures to save, or lost cities, or "crash to desktop" (CTD's). On the other hand these can be countered by frequent saves and backups along with certain "habits" in the play methodology.If one does this, this game has some real appeal to many people.

The game was released as a core game, Simcity 4 (SC4) and an expansion, Rush Hour (RH) which in combination was dubbed "Simcity 4 Deluxe" SC4D. The Rushhour expansion used to be available seperately, but is quite scarce and/ or very expensive now [[ASIN:B00009V3NQ SimCity 4: Rush Hour Expansion Pack]].

This particular release is only SC4 and frankly is essentially unusable by itself as much of the elements of the game, and much of the expanded customizable hooks, especially the "networks" part.. that part which handles the commuting and travel mechanics, allowing a wide array of "transportation" simulations. To be really useful you MUST (IMO) have the FULL set available in several forms (see below). My low rating is for THIS VERSION ONLY. I really quite like the game itself in its full, properly-registered form.

There also is a very active community, especially in the USA, Germany and Japan and lessor followings in many other countries. This group is very community oriented and supportive. Maxis was clever to embed into the game "stubs" which support a wide array of end user customization content, and this community generates active interest which carries the game well beyond its years. This group congregates on a half dozen or so "support sites" (all free) which are accessable by all. I'd estimate there are probably about a half million fairly active players worldwide.

The game is not played versus other players (other than in comparing accomplishments or progress or sharing custom content). It is a "strategy" game based on figuring out the operation and biases of the game and designing your city designs to best overcome and conform to these needs. There isn't "an answer" but rather a broad array of approaches that work to varying degrees based on what you are trying to achieve (dense ghettos, idylic contryside, sleepy towns, etc) A single "regional development" can easily take weeks to months of off and on attention to work through these issues. If these kinds of things appeal to you, this may be the game for you, just not in this version.

The game uses a copy protection scheme that requires the CD to be in the machine to play (or in the downloadable Amazon or Steam versions a running "game support" program that validates the game) Some folk are rather put off by this.

In summary, though this is still the core of the game, DON'T BUY THIS VERSION.. buy the full set. [[ASIN:B0000C0YW2 SimCity 4 Deluxe Edition]] or the downloadable version [[ASIN:B00457VJ3G SimCity 4 Deluxe Edition [Download]]] (also available via Steam) or as a subset of a box set with other games included [[ASIN:B0014468XE The SimCity Box]] I have heard there are support problems with the patches on the box set, but don't have personal experience with it. The downloadable versions should be "pre-patched".

Be VERY CAUTIOUS buying a used version from eBay, etc as you MUST have the registration membership in the EA/Maxis web site to update the game with it's patches.. only buy if you can get this membership with its User Name and Password included or certification that the serial number has never been registered... many people have been burned on this matter Even buying "new" versions is risky as many are just pirate copies of the game and the registration number will report "already in use" even though you "bought it" as "new". Get the seller to guarantee the version is register-able

Sorry to be so long-winded, but I felt most of this needed to be touched upon. In whatever form you buy it, I recommend immediately taking a look at web sites which have active communities interested in the game. You can happily invest many hundreds of interesting hours in the game if you're willing to invest the time.

title: Action packed follow up to the movie!
text:
Don't be fooled by other reviews. This isn't really a survival horror game. It's a squad based action game, with horror elements. Expect lots of shooting and running!

John Carpenter's classic movie The Thing, a remake of the awfully cheesy movie from the 1950's, has a classic premise that John W. Campbell originally wrote in the short story that spawned both movies, "Who Goes There." Finding a shape shifting alien frozen in the ice, and then dealing with it when it wakes up and isn't happy, is a really good setting for a horror story.

The game is a direct sequel to the Carpenter movie, and although it lacks Kurt Russel, it does a great job of re-creating the atmosphere of the film. The isolation of the antarctic research outposts is palpable, and the danger of freezing to death and getting lost in the perpetual darkness add to the tension. Your team mates will get more and more upset by the death that you discover, causing you to take measures from disarming them to killing them outright.

And I haven't even mentioned the monsters. From tiny little things that resemble facehuggers from alien to gigantic boss monsters, you will encounter a wide variety of bloodthirsty killers. Sometimes your teammates may even suddenly mutate into monsters, wreaking havoc on the sanity of the remaining members.

Unlike many survival horror games, this one gives you plenty of ammunition, so there is no need to hold back on shooting the baddies. It does use a stupid tape recorder saving system, so you have to keep on the look out for places to save the game. The story is pretty good, but if you've seen the movie you can pretty much guess the plot of the game.

title: Good workout-- cardio a little short
text:
I got Sports Active on this release date (my birthday!) and I have been so excited. After using it the first day, I do really like it. I find that it is very much like a good workout video with variety, feedback and interesting graphics. So far, I have only done day 1 of the 30 day challenge, so I know there is more that I haven't seen. I feel like I got a great strength training workout. I was a bit disappointed in the cardio part though- the only thing I have found so far that is really a cardio workout is running, and on low intensity (which I was thinking meant low impact) you only run about 2 minutes at a time. Running really doesn't work for me as I have problems with my arches that cause pain when running. I could do 2 minutes, but I still hurt after. I enjoyed the boxing/kickboxing, but since it isn't a rhythm boxing like Wii Fit, there really isn't much of a cardio component. Perhaps there would be at a higher intensity level though.
One great thing about it is that there seems to be a huge variety of pre-set programs, and I also do like that you can select which exercises you do not want to do before you start the program. I also love the way that you can use the balance board, and how you can actually do the same exercise differently whether you use the balance board or not (ex: in line skating- jumps without balance board, leg lifts while squatting with balance board)
A few annoying things: cord does get in the way. I agree with another reviewer, I think I will be looking for a cordless nunchuck. Also, I found it a bit annoying that you had to switch around the direction of the nunchuck in the leg strap depending on the exercise. In the directions, that part went by quite quickly, so it was easy to miss (it might be running was the only one that it faced left, but still a little annoying)

I look forward to continuing to explore the program, and I am hopeful that I will find more cardio in it, but if not, I will need to supplement with cardio and use this for strength training only.

title: Good workouts but awkward controls
text:
I'm into my 7th workout of the 6 week challenge and have these thoughts:

Pro:
These are really good workouts. I think this is what people thought Wii Fit would be. I like the mix of cardio, full body and upper and lower body choices.

At the end of them I am sweating and the next day I've been sore.

The trainer and "show me how" videos make it easy to learn the moves

You can choose to skip exercises at the beginning of the workout and it calculates your calories based on your choices.

You can follow the 6-week challenge or create your own workout.

Con:
The resistance band offers very little resistance even at very short lengths. I tried holding my own free weights and the wii remote in the same hand but it slipped around and I felt like I would crack the wii-mote when I squeezed it against the dumbbell bar. To make up for it, I do a set with my own weights and then repeat the set with the band just so I get the credit and the calorie count on my graphs.

The leg thing is uncomfortable. Attach it tightly to stay on, it feels like a tourniquet and if you attach it loosely, it sometimes slides off during jogging. To remedy this, I wear shorts with deep pockets and stick the nun-chuck in the pocket. It works well for the weight routines and running but not so well for water-skiing and lunging. For those I still have to use the Velcro leg thing.

My big complaint: the Wii remote and nunchuck seem out of sync with some of the exercises. When I try to do crunches with punches, the trainer says "too fast, too slow, try again," over and over, even if I am just laying there. I end up doing the crunches on my own and then faking out the software with hand gestures. Its also frustrating when I want to get into a good routine of doing 15 crunches and I have to either wait, try again, hold it, start over or watch the videos to satisfy the trainer... it takes 5 minutes to do a set of wii crunches that take only 30 seconds in the gym.

The controls are sometimes inconsistently unresponsive so if I swat the ball 10 times in a row in squash, the 11th time my arm won't move for 3 seconds and then it'll swing to catch up. And with water-skiing, I'll successfully squat 5 times in a row and the 6th time I miss the flag even though I am moving the exact same way as before.

It's not very fun. The exercises are the same basic ones you can do on your own: lunges and crunches and bicep curls with weights. No hula hooping, skiing or snowball fights (like the wii). True, there is water skiing but that is basically squatting down and up and there is squash but that consists of mainly swinging your arms, lunging and swattingat the ball on a drab court by yourself. Would be fun if it were more like Wii tennis with a crowd, good scenery and partners.

For the longer workouts, you end up repeating the last 5 exercises you just did. Gets a little old.

The trainer is annoying sometimes. When he says "niiiiice!" I kinda want to smack him. I like Wii Fit's mellow, unobtrusive trainer.

So despite the long list of cons, I am still happy with the software. I feel like I am making much more progress toning up than with the wii fit and that was the whole point of buying the software.

title: Proof that traditional HOGs can still be fun
text: I was pleasantly surprised by this game.  It is a traditional HOG - each level has certain places to visit on each level and lists of items to find in each place.  Since I've played a lot of these by now, I thought I would be rather bored (read my review on Margrave Manor 2), but I wasn't.  The lists of objects included "description" names which, albeit nothing new, I thought were particularly well done in this game.  It also had some interesting "hint" tools on each level that you could purchase with points earned from previous play (like a painter's palette that, once activated, turns your item list from words to pictures).  It also gave bonus points for finding objects in quick succession, which I happen to like.  I also thought the graphics were very good.  Some of the objects were hard to find, but the hint system worked well.  If what you really want is a traditional HOG game, I would check out the free trial.  Some warnings: (1) It is very short.  I didn't time myself, but I don't think it took more than a couple of hours.  (If playing the free trial, keep in mind that it only has eleven levels).  (2) This is the first installment.  It ends abruptly in a cliffhanger so that you will buy the second installment.  (3) I thought that the main voice-over was terrible as far as acting is concerned. title: Good concept, not so good execution
text:
Having a video game that helps you work out is a great motivating concept. But I don't enjoy doing the workouts on this video. If you start the 30 day fitness program, then the 15 or so exercises that you do everyday alternate constantly between those you do with the numchuck in the leg pouch (which by the way has such a small pocket that I think it will soon break the numchuck putting it in and taking it out), those you do with the numchuck in your left hand, and those that you do with and without the elastic band. Constantly having to move the numchuck around and pick up and put down the elastic strap is enough of a pain. But then in addition your hands must be EXACTLY positioned during each moment of the exercise for the Wii to be able to see if you are doing it right. If, for example, you don't twist your wrist in just the right way during a certain moment in the exercise, then your exercise "leader" will assume you don't know what you are doing and will just wait for you while some messages appear on your screen telling you various hints on how to get in position. All that starting and stopping and false messaging about whether you are doing it right is distracting and demotivating.

So while you COULD get fit doing these exercises, it is infinitely easier just to turn the Wii off and exercise on your own.

title: Best I've tried yet, but could be better.
text:
Intro: I am an out of shape athlete with 2 small children, so this was my first big foray back into the fitness world. Something I could do while they were napping. This was perfect!

I did one 30 day workout cycle, and while I didn't lose weight, I absolutely put on muscle (hence the not losing weight thing). I sleep better, and feel much stronger already. I started at medium intensity, and ended up doing hard for the last week. Overall, it's a thumbs up.

I have a few concerns, and requests for EA Sports, though.

First - as a former runner, I have a history with shin splints. This game brought them back, and brought them back in a big way. I'm about a third of the way through my second 30 day workout, and I'm going to have to stop and take some time off to rest my shins. I think it's the kickbacks. I can do the regular track running without too much difficulty, and I can do the slow kickbacks and high knees, but the fast kickbacks put too much stress on my landings, and it just kills me. I did the long (2 laps) version yesterday and damn near started crying. Yeah, time to take a break. And when I come back, I'll be un-checking the long kickbacks when they show up in my workout lineup.

Additionally, my knees, which I have NEVER had trouble with, are also very, very sore. My quads are getting super strong super fast with all the lunges and squats, but the repetitive stress of doing such similar exercises so frequently is giving my knee joints some serious grief. I am careful to keep my form correct, and never let my knees extend past my toes. I go into and come out of the lunges & squats with as much control as possible, so that I'm not throwing myself into the pose and expecting my knees to stabilize everything. I go slowly, and concentrate on form over speed. Again, I have never had knee pains, so this is a huge bummer for me. I think that the jumps, in particular, are a problem. I have stopped doing anything involving jumps (with the exception of the straight up squat jumps, as I can land squarely on both feet), and the pain is starting to subside a bit. I think some hamstring strengthening exercises would round out the focus on the quads so that the counter muscles would have a chance to build, thus better supporting and strengthening the knees.

Whether or not the focus of the day is upper or lower body, my upper body is never worked as hard as my legs. This may have something to do with the fact that I have a strong upper body, and I'm overweight, so my legs are working extra hard, but...well...I'm just sayin' my upper body is never as tired as my legs.

More core. My abs should hurt at least every now and then from working out, and they don't.

Equipment. You know it's crap, I know it's crap, we all know it's crap. My leg strap started to split about 2/3 of the way through my first 30 day workout. My red band started to split shortly after starting my second 30 day workout. Yes, they were very cool and are sending me replacements, but still....c'mon. They should at least price the replacement sets more realistically at like, $8 so I won't feel hostile towards EA Sports when I inevitably have to go buy another set. $20 for a cheapo leg strap and red band? Please. It's insulting.

Dancing. Needs to go away. It's not dancing, it's a joke, and has no place among the other more serious activities in this program. Shopping cart? Start the mower? Raise the roof??? It's embarrassing - for me and for EA Sports.

Wishlist:

- I like the calorie burning chart, and seeing how it lined up with the expectations the game had for me. I wish I could click on parts of the chart, though, to see what I was doing during that peak or valley on the chart. In particular, if my actual calorie burn dips below what the game expected me to be burning at a particular point, I want to know what I was doing so I can work harder at that activity.

- I should be able to tell the game if I'm wearing ankle or wrist weights so that the program can be a little more accurate in its calorie burn estimations (yes, I do know they are just estimations, but I still value them). I, for example, wear 2 lb weights on each wrist and would like to be able to plug that in somewhere.

- I appreciate being able to uncheck activities before starting a workout. However, it would be awesome if the program could compensate for that and maybe give me something else to do in its place, instead of just having me do less than it had previously expected me to do. Like, if I uncheck the fast kickbacks, it could give me the option to take a trip to the track with slow kickbacks and slow knee raises instead. Or if I uncheck Dancing (soooooo lame!), it could give me some other low intensity cardio activity to do instead, rather than nothing.

- Or a better answer? Master list unchecking: this would also solve the problem of unchecking certain exercises before starting a workout, and getting less of a workout than the program intended. If I could go into a master list and tell the program I NEVER want to do Dancing, Fast Kickbacks, Jump Lunges, etc it would make it easier for the program to create a better list of activities for my 30 day workout. And of course, if I get over the knee thing and want to add some of the jumps back in, this would be a great way to do it. It should be noted, however, that I would never EVER go back and re-check the Dancing. Jeez, that's lame.

- Better resistance strap management. Perhaps something that wraps around my wrists so I don't have to try and keep a grip on the strap and the remote/nunchuk at the same time? Or some sort of glove-like thing that they're attached to? I don't know, I just know I don't like the strap slipping and twisting around while I'm trying to do overhead pushes or tri kickbacks.

That's it for now. This game has definitely started getting me back into shape, and for that I'm happy and thankful. Here's hoping I heal soon and can get back to it asap. :)

text:
Buyer beware, for households with multiple players. My sons been begging for this game for months. I usually play his games after he goes to sleep, staying a bit ahead of him, so I can help him or answer questions he has if he needs. So he gets the game for Christmas and fires it up, messes around for a while, gets stuck and moves on to another game.

I turn it on that nighttime start working ahead of him to clear up the confusion. Except nothing is triggering. No milestones, no goals, I didn’t get to pick or name an island, I’m just wandering aimlessly in the same island my son made and named.

So I do some research. Apparently all accounts on a single switch system are locked to the same island, and only the first player to start a game can progress the story or make major decisions about the island. So basically, one person can play the game per system. Period. And to make matter more irritating, the resources I used trying to make the game DO something, are absent from the island on my sons account now as well, preventing him from completing goals.

For a full priced game, this is insulting, and Nintendo should be ashamed of themselves. They need to patch this ASAP. This is not a full release and it is not communicated clearly on the packaging.

title: You'll need this and a 3.5 hard drive, it'll cost a lot. Getting everything working takes some work
text:
Well I finally got everything working. My hard drive was way too small, I had to delete a game to enjoy another. A lot of money and a lot of work later, and now there's extra room for my system. This Nyko Data Bank plus lets you keep you're original PS4 hard drive in addion to the hard drive you need to buy separaly (like I said, took a lot of money). To swich hard drives, your system must be turned off (not in rest mode) before pressing the button. Once you have the bigger hard drive, the 3.5 people frequently buy with this Nyko Data Bank Plus works for me, you need to download the latest PS4 update (link provided in the instructions didn't work for me, so I had to search for it myself) with a computer connected to the internet. Save the download to a USB flash drive formatted to fat32 (instructions will tell you what to name the files). Windows 7 didn't offer the option to format to fat32, but when I checked the flash drive's properties It was already formatted to fat32. Check the properties of the flash drive and you may find you don't need to format it, but if you do just hope your computer let's you do it (there could be a solution on the net for any computer lacking the fat32 option). The controllor plugs into one slot of the PS4 and the USB flash drive with the update goes into the other. If you aren't finding the instructions clear, there's information on the internet including YouTube videos (like I said it took a lot of work). The data on my original hard drive wasn't even lost, but you can back it up to the cloud (or a USB Flash Drive, probably also formatted in Fat32, if you don't have PlayStation+) if you're worried. Having this is great, even if it took me some time and a lot of money ($100 is a lot of money to me) to figure out how to get everything working.

Additonal info: So I had a power outage and couldn't access either hard drive when the power returned. Took me longer than it should to notice the light on the switch was out. Hitting it once turn it on. Hitting again switched it, so make sure the light is on before freaking out

Additional Update 4.50: So I installed the latest update on my 2.5 & then my 3.5 couldn't be read, I'd assume it'll update like everything else. I went back to the PS4 site and got the new update on my flash drive fearing I'd have to download everything from the cloud again. Once it was updated, all my memory & settings were still on the 3.5 hard drive. Phew. So when you update your 2.5 hard drive, you can download the update on your computer and keep playing on your 2.5. I recomemd keeping your top favorite games (Dragon Age Inquisition/Skyrim/The Witcher 3/Mass Effect Andromeda in my case) on the 2.5, unless you have either more patience or a really fast computer

title: By Far The Best Game!
text:
First of all, the game has actual scenes included from the movies. Yes, it has scenes from both the Two Towers AND the Return of the King. This is because you fight in Helm's Deep in the beginning of the game and work your way up from there. The actors from the movies did the voices of the characters as well.
Second, the actors are interviewed for the game, and they are shown playing the game themselves and talking about it. A little something extra to make it even more interesting.
Third, the graphics are great! I love how they morph from a scene in the movie to the game characters and vice versa. The game characters look very much like the real actors too. Beware: the movie scenes will morph back to the game characters without warning so you'd better be ready to begin playing again or you may find yourself the victim of a nasty orc or mountain troll.
Basically, you fight in the same battles that occur in the movie, but because it's a game, your battles may involve more than is in the movie. You can play as Aragorn, Legolas, Gimli, Sam, Frodo, or Gandalf and when you beat the game you get 3 more special characters to play as. I won't tell you who they are - I don't want to ruin the surprise. Hint: After you beat the game you will be given secret codes and secret levels. Now, usually I don't like to use secret codes to win, but in this case the makers of the game GIVE you the codes, and they do it for a reason. Once you've beaten the game fair and square, in order to beat the scret levels you WILL need those codes or you won't beat the secret levels! Trust me, we tried it with Aragorn at level 16 and Legolas at level 12 - we could not beat "the Palantir of Sauron" without the codes, and even then it's tough to do! Hint 2: After you beat the game, you can play ANY character in ANY path you want. For example, you can take Aragorn and Legolas to "The Crack of Doom" with Gollum instead of Frodo and Sam. Or you can take Frodo and Sam along the "Path of the Dead." It's great, and much more than the 10 hours of play time one other reviewer mentioned.
In the game you choose between three different paths: The path of the King, the path of Gandalf, or the path of the Hobbits. As you level up and win battles you get to learn new techniques and purchase new weapons for your character. You need this in order to win at higher levels. One interesting feature is in the battle at the Black Gate. You not only have to fight the enemy but protect your party as well. If any of your party members die, you lose.
Finally, you can play as a single player, multi player, or if you have network capability, you can go online and play in the online world of Return of the King. My only complaint is that I wish there were more places to save the game. You have to finish a battle before you can save it - there's no saving part way through a battle. Also, some of the camera angles are not the best, but oh well. Don't let it ruin your fun. Overall, it's a great game! Of course, eventually you'll beat the game or grow tired of it just like all your other adventure/action games, but that's to be expected. However, if you play as all possible characters and take all possible paths, you will end up with quite a bit of playing time. I highly recommend the game!!
One last word. I've read some people's reviews saying it's just a slashing game - well, duh! The movie is one battle after another, not an adventure as it may have been in the Fellowship of the Ring. This is a fighter's game, not an adventure lover's game. If you want to search and explore in a game, and you love Lord of the Rings, I suggest you try "The Fellowship of the Ring." That game is not made by EA, so the graphics are very, very different, but it's a good game none the less, and the storyline actually follows the book rather than the movie. Also, the first four levels of "Return of the King" are NOT fighting the dead. The only place where you fight the dead is in "the Path of the King" ON "the path of the dead."
My son and I have beaten the game, and we still love to play it. It has great replay value, so buy it and enjoy!!!

title: An excellent wireless option with some quirks
text:
I pre-ordered this controller and the Luigi version in hopes that it would be an excellent alternative to official Gamecube controllers and a Gamecube adapter. And for the most part, my hopes were fulfilled. If your wish is to have a mostly authentic Gamecube controller experience without having to deal with wires, and you have a Wiimote lying around, this is probably your best bet. Note that this review also applies to the Luigi version.

Ergonomically, this is indeed a Gamecube controller. Anyone with a nostalgic taste for the Gamecube will automatically feel at home with this product, or at least regarding the shape. The plastic, however, feels a bit different from an actual Gamecube controller. It does not by any means feel bad, it just feels "cheaper." It also maintains the matte finish of an official Gamecube controller, so there isn't any worry as far as fingerprints are concerned, especially when compared to the Wii U Pro Controller.

This product also feels a bit lighter than an official Gamecube controller, though this is most likely due to a lack of rumble features rather than poor build quality, since this is essentially a Wii Classic Controller with a Gamecube-type feel. The buttons feel exactly like they do on an official Gamecube controller, as well as the sticks. The only real differences in terms of buttons are in the d-pad, the shoulder buttons, and the buttons in the middle.

The d-pad is now much larger than the official Gamecube controller and feels excellent, though it is made of a slightly different plastic. The traditional "slider" buttons have been replaced by "short-stroke" buttons, more akin to the Wii U Pro Controller, and there are now TWO Z buttons instead of one. There are now four buttons in the middle: a "Minus/Select" button, a "Home" button, a "Plus/Start" button, and a "Turbo" button. With the Turbo button, what you do is hold down a button you want "Turbo'd" and press the Turbo button, and then use the slider to increase the frequency at which the button presses. I have not found a use for this yet, but be wary of cheaters.

After playing with this controller for a couple of days, I can safely say that this controller is a perfect fit for Super Smash Bros. for Wii U. Everything feels natural, and there is little input lag through the Wiimote, if any. I have not tried Brawl yet, but it would probably lead to the same results. I have also tried it with Mario Kart 8, and it also feels really good. It took only a little while to get used to the short-stroke triggers, but after that, all control over all games is smooth as butter.

Overall, this is a really good controller, and considering this is made by Hori, this makes perfect sense. If you would prefer to save a few bucks in order to play Super Smash Bros. with a Gamecube controller, this is an excellent option. Those with more nostalgic taste, however, might not like this, and may prefer to get official Smash Bros. Gamecube controllers and a controller adapter instead. However, what the Hori Battle Pad for Wii U accomplishes, it accomplishes well, and comes easily recommended for those who need a wireless option for Smash Bros. and other games.

Pros:
-Familiar button layout and feel
-Larger d-pad
-Playing games like Smash Bros. feels natural
-Serves as an excellent wireless option (provided you have a Wiimote)
-Turbo feature could have some good uses

Cons
-Some plastic feels cheaper than an official Gamecube controller
-Short-stroke buttons may take a bit of getting used to
-Turbo could be abused in the future

title: All About Compromise.
text:
I own two expensive HDMI NES clones and bought this one as a Christmas present. Based on a few minutes of testing I can say it's a compromised NES experience, but one that's priced right and should satisfy most people. The picture is a bit soft but pleasant and saturated. The sound is sometimes fine and other times awful, almost comically so. Super Mario Bros sounds okay but Castlevania III sounds like the school band covered it.
I'm guessing this machine adds about 1 frame of input lag (delay from when you push a button to when you see the result on screen) based on my time with it. Perhaps there is an A/D converter inside, which would explain the delay. This amount of lag is no big deal and games are entirely playable (but more expensive alternatives add zero lag).
At the end of the day I'm glad that an HDMI-enabled NES clone is now affordable to people who don't want to spend a fortune. Gamerz Tek can be commended for making a low-cost option that doesn't promise more than it delivers. Gamers who want a more high-end experience, however, would do well to buy a better alternative like the RetroUSB AVS or Analogue NT.

title: Great Workout - Feel the Burn!
text:
So, after having this game sitting around for a few months, I finally decided to try it. And after trying it, the game told me something I already know: Boy, are you out of shape!

I've only tried the "Easy" mode, and that alone kicks major [...]. Although I've selected short sessions (17 to 20 minutes), I've found that it takes a lot longer than that to get through them.

The reason for that is the equipment itself:
- The resistance bands get twisted and time is wasted trying to "flatten" it out, as well as getting the proper grip with the straps.
- As other reviewers have noted, the nunchuk holder that you strap around your thigh WILL slip (if not completely fall off!) every time! That is the biggest pain! No matter how hard you try to strap it on, it manages to slip off. Perhaps it could be made of more static material so that it will stay on, like some sort of "gripper"
- Since many of the exercises involve using the Wii remote and Nunchuk, untwisting them is a pain as well. Are there wireless versions of the Wii remotes and Nunchuks? If not, this would be a major improvement for playing this game.

My overall impressions:
(+) - If you're out of shape such as myself, this will definitely get your heart pumping and muscles working
(+) - It's more customizable, allowing the player to choose levels, music (more about that later), and can even play with a friend
(+) - The "trainer" offers praise and you even get trophies once you've accomplished your goals
(+) - Everything you need is in the box, although you would be better off using your own resistance bands if you have them
(-) - Equipment (see above) could use a little fine tuning
(-) - Music is horrible! You'd probably enjoy Elevator music more!

title: has potential but needs improvement
text:
This game/workout has a lot of potential, but it could definitely use some enhancements to become one of my "go-to" workouts. It's one of the customized workout programs that I enjoy, because they track your progress and change things up a bit so you don't get bored.

Pros: The exercises take good advantage of the Wii system - particularly the obstacle course and boxing. As long as you select the right difficulty level, it can be very challenging.

Areas for improvement... like many of these workout games, it's not easy to get credit for "outside" workouts. I simply get bored doing the same game/workout all the time, even if it does customize it, and I want to see my tracking take proper credit for it. Also, the workouts are a bit too short mostly, all under a 1/2 hour so far - it'd be good if I could select how long I want to work out that day. The band that comes with it is not strong enough, I'm going to pick up a thicker one to replace it to provide more resistance.

One other complaint, although it's likely more the Wii itself that's the problem here - there are a number of exercises where it obviously is not quite tracking my movements properly. I have to "jiggle" the remote to get it to recognize where I am.

All in all, I do mostly enjoy the workout, and I think it's worth buying.

title: Loving This!!
text:
I have only tried one day of this program but I already love it!

I am not a newcomer to workouts - I own 30+ Tae Bo videos, Jillian Michaels workouts, and random other workout videos, when I bike my average distance is 8 miles, and I work out 3-5 days a week on average (depending on time availability). I purchased this program over the Wii Fit because I heard it was more intense - and it is! I sweat and worked as hard as I do with a Tae Bo video - it's very effective. They have a 30 day challenge in which they make customized workouts based on your weight/height and intensity preference, and I'm really excited for it. You get trophies as you go along and they set goals for you, and from what I've read online you can add in your other workouts that you do outside of it and it takes those into consideration. I have to explore it more.

You get a leg band that the nunchuck goes into for a lot of exercises and it was a WORKOUT! I do Tae Bo and other workout videos on a regular basis, and when I bike my average distance is about 8 miles...so it's not like I'm a beginner. I definitely sweat as much as I do when I do my typical workout video, and I'm definitely has sore!

And I'm not sure how Wii Fit is but they constantly check your posture and how you're doing things...when you do squats they have a meter on the side so you can see how much further you should go, or where you're at. Today they have me set up for tennis and something else - it's supposed to alternate your workouts so you're not using one muscle group over and over - yesterday was a bit of everything to get me into it - I'm really interested to see how the full thing is structured. You run on a track and if you're "mii" (a real person like The Sims, not the typical Mii) isn't going fast enough it blinks at you...I was running and screaming at the screen, lol. The worst was rollerblading - you had to squat low - the lower the faster you went, and then you had to jump off these ramps. What a workout!

They give you beginner resistance bands, which I didn't even bother with - I have better ones from the store and I'm using those (as I've found from the reviews most people do). You can wrap them around your hands to give you more resistance as well - the handstraps for mine are a bit bulky so it was tough trying to maneuver those and the controller and nunchuck, but I got the hang of it.

Like I said, I've only done this for one day and I'm already completely sold. It's a great product and if you're new to working out, it'll definitely get you into shape and give you ideas on what you should be doing. If you're experienced, you don't have to worry about this being under you, you'll still benefit from it.

title: One island save PER SWITCH, not per account
text:
Having never played Animal Crossing before, I was excited to try this out and have another slow life sim for my kids to play. What you should know is that the game only allows one island per CONSOLE.

I played first, chose and named an island, made my character, and collected resources. When I tried to allow visitors to my island or visit online friends’ islands, the game prompted me for a (paid) Nintendo Switch Online subscription.

My daughter started today on her own profile and she can make her own character but she MUST share the same island and its time-locked resources with everyone else in the house. Only the first player can advance the story, too. There is no way for siblings to have their own islands unless you buy each child their own Switch console.

I never would have bought this game if I’d known about the profile restrictions. Apparently this is a common Animal Crossing feature, so while I disagree with it strongly as a game mechanic there is reasoning behind it. However, it should be made abundantly clear before you purchase what you’re getting. As it stands, it’s one more thing for siblings to fight over and even if your entire household is phenomenal about sharing and getting along, someone will ALWAYS miss out since only the first profile to start the island has access to story progression.

title: Not much content & needs more balance board usage
text:
I purchased this title (EA Sports Active More Workouts) along with EA Sports Active (the original game package), both at the same time as a new user to both. I also use a Wii Balance Board.

The "EA Sports: More Workouts" disc has fewer sport topics to choose from than the original game set even though it's almost as costly as the original title that comes with equipment. Also,very few activities use the balance board, which is a shame and a waste of potential. Usually only 1-2 per sports/activity use the balance board. And the ab workout section they use as a selling point is a just a half dozen super basic exercises like crunches and leg lifts, not something you need a game disc for. They are basic ab exercises most people are familiar with and can do without an expensive game to urge them on. I was very disappointed to see so few and so basic an ab selection. Also, adding a yoga selection would have been nice.

I really feel that the game description (of both titles) should list the full set of exercises provided online or at least the back of the box so you don't have to buy it to find out what they are or rather what they aren't.

Also, as with the original game, you have to create your own workout to see the "sports" related exercies you can pick and you can't see in advance them or get a demo without selecting several of them into a created workout and just doing them and/or skipping them (which is odd if you don't know what they are and really kills the flow of a workout to skip them if it's something you can't do, etc.). I feel the game should have had a menu to view and pick exercises/activities you want to do like Wii Fit or Wii Fit Plus does in addition to the ability to create a workout from a string of several exercises once you had experimented with them separately. I also think it would have been nice to have all the old and all the new on one disc so you couldn't incorporate whatever you wanted into a workout.

Also, I had SEVERE problems with the EA Active leg strap staying in place which made both the original game disc AND this one too unusable. The leg strap fell down my leg continuously despite what I wore or how much I tightened it, making both games totally unusable since it would not stay in place. I even tried holding it in place which isn't feasible. So, as a result of the leg strap slippage, the game did not read my movements properly which in some activities could lead to injury if for instance during squats you are urged to keep squatting lower and lower to get in the graphic zone on screen merely because the leg strap is out of place and you end up squatting too low for instance. You can't workout without the leg strap and nunchuck up high on your leg but it just falls continuously. Also, the game was slow to mirror movements and didn't always register properly even when it was hand movements with the remote, etc. so the problem isn't entirely due to the leg strap slipping. Also, the resistance band is very weak even if you shorten it making it more hassle than it's worth.

I really feel there should be a chip you can just pin to your leg to read the leg movements. I know a lot of people adore these games from the feedback, but, across both titles I also see a lot of people who have trouble with the straps falling down. At $53 for one title and $30 for another, a total of $83 is a lot of money to spend only to find out you are one of the people who can't keep the leg strap up due to your particular leg contours. etc. I'm sure some lovers of the set will post how it fits them, but, it doesn't stay up on me and other reviewers also, so it might be something you try to rent of borrow from a friend first to be sure before investing the money to be safe. I am really saddened that I spent the money on these 2 titles and it was money wasted since the games are unusable if you can not keep the leg strap in place.

Frankly, if you want to do step aerobics or dance yourself fit, you can get exercise dvd's for a few bucks and you can run in place for free unlike these EA Sports Active pricey games and dvd's work without a leg strap. So, if you truly want to sweat, just get some workout dvd's. You'll probably save money and have a more intense workout and won't have all the leg strap fustration.

title: Poorly designed equipment & poorly structured workouts
text:
I purchased this title (EA Sports Active) along with EA Sports Active More Workouts also, both at the same time. I also use a Wii Balance Board.

This review addresses both the "EA Sports Active" and the "EA Sports Active More Workouts" games.

I had waited to purchase this (EA Sports Active) workout package due to many initially poor reviews due to the leg strap not fitting people or falling down one's leg while working out which had me concerned. Back when it debuted, this seemed to be a problem. I later saw reviews that replacement straps had been created and so I figured this problem had been fixed. Since I was looking for a workout option on days the winter weather is horrible, I thought I would finally get this to workout at home on days I missed going to the gym. I do have a balance board and did use it with this game.

The leg strap is still a problem with this workout game title. The current leg strap is very large and will adjust to both very large and very small leg sizes. It comes with extra velcro to help make it even smaller though I can't imagine that ever being needed. It also has a slight non-skid rubber inside to supposedly keep it from slipping. This however does not work. I tried various fabric workout clothes underneath, tightening the strap more and more, etc. all to no avail. After a few minutes, it's slips down and you have to keep stopping to reposition it only so it can fall down again and again. Possiblly if you have really slim straight legs that are uniform in width, it might stay up like it does on the demonstration model in the video instructions/commercials. From the glowing reviews of this product, I'm sure many people must not have a problem with the leg strap and I finally gave in to buy it. However, I do not think this will stay up once anyone is very active. I personally have more muscular legs so the leg strap is not uniformly snug when worn causing slippage constantly. Even tightening it does not help, it still slips, and having anything tight on one's leg is a bad idea. Not sure why I can't get it to stay in place better. Since you can not choose to perform the workouts without the leg monitoring of the nunchuck in the leg strap, this makes the game pretty much unusable. Furthmore, having a nunchuck with it's short wire is not a big hindrance, but, it can be annoying at times only adding to the fustration since the leg strap won't stay in place either.

The resistance band included is cheap and very low resistance. It's not as thick as the free ones Shape magazine gives out. I wouldn't complain about this, but, not everyone at home has stronger resistance bands to substitute and wrapping the extra in the middle to tighten it still didn't help, it's a very weak resistance band. And since this game is a higher priced item, a buyer should not have to substitute their own work out bands in order to use the game. Workout bands are cheap to produce. It should have come with a either a better resistance band or maybe even a couple different tensions for different strength levels. The band and it's tie on handles are really poorly made and just not that good to use.

On to the EA Sports Active game. The initial fitness workout I received in the 30 day challenge required quite a few exercises and is actually rather long for a novice. It starts with running in place (no marching, stretching or basic warm up), which depending on the items in your home might not be the best idea. Next it goes to squats for instance. Not being sufficiently warmed up from trying to run and stopping constantly to fuss with the nunchuck means the squats required might have been placed too soon in the workout for any novice since squats performed incorrectly can be dangerous or likewise for those with those with any kind of knee weakness/problems, etc. The game required that you squat, hold it in the downward position, and then stand. The game did not respond in sync with my movement and constantly thought that I was not squatting low enough despite the fact that I was. As a personal trainer household, I did have someone watching my form to ensure I was squatting properly and it's an exercise I routinely perform anyway so I am very familiar with proper form. I think this was due to the constant slippage of the nunchuck leg holder or it not staying high enough on my leg. I attempted to hold the leg strap in place, but, the game still did not respond correctly or fast enough to mirror my movement accurately. You were instructed to squat, hold it, then stand, and at times it showed me still squatting even after I stood up, or vice versa. Squatting improperly can cause injury and so I worry that people not aware of correct form might overextend, etc. as the game incorrectly urges them to keep squatting deeper despite already being low and in position. The game also does not give enough hints on proper form either. While it shows a graphic of a person squatting that you watch face to face head on for timing, it does not show a profile or give an tips such as never allowing your knee to extend forward over your toes, etc. as it keeps nagging you to squat lower and lower. It then went on to an upper body exercise that was totally unchallenging with the weak resistance band despite shortening it as instructed. Next was an inline skating exercise that would require you to crouch down (on the balance board) to gain speed, lean forward, and then perform and hold a lateral leg lift to avoid several obstacles. This is a very challenging move since you are not lifting and lowering your leg but holding it up for several seconds to avoid several obstacles. For a novice or anyone without great balance, this could be really tricky especially on day 1 of the workout challenge on the EASY setting. It was a challenge even for me. Then it went back to medium running in place (goodness more running in place) and then squats again?? As a muscle building exercise, squats should not have come again in this work out and definitely not in a harder setting. Something to focus on other leg muscles for symmetry would have been better. I had the game set on easy since I was new to this program and am surprised they repeated this exercise so soon. I really am concerned that someone could over work or ever strain certain muscle groups, etc. following this game's exercises in the order given, etc.

I gave up in fustration over the leg strap since you can't really use the game without it in proper place and checked out the create your own work out to see if there were non-nunchuck exercises I could use to still salvage any usability out of the game I had paid so much money for. There are not any ways to use it without the nunchuck. Also, only a small fraction of exercises use the balance board, only 1 per category. Since a full list of game exercises was not listed in the product description, I was not aware so few use the balance board which was disappointing as that's a great tool.

I went to the create your own workout to see the "sports" related exercies you can pick and you can't see them or get a demo without selecting several of them into a created workout and just doing them or skipping them (which is odd if you don't know what they are and really kills the flow of a workout). I feel the game should have had a menu to view and pick exercises/activities you want to do like Wii Fit or Wii Fit Plus in addition to the ability to create a workout from a string of several exercises once you had experimented with them separately. The extra sport related games on this game are things like boxing, tennis, volleyball, basketball and inline skating and nothing else. There is no Yoga group, so if you were hoping that would be in this title, it isn't. There are only several categories, so do not expect dozens of sports to choose from. The "EA Sports: More Workouts" disc has even fewer sports/topics to choose from given you have to buy it alone at a price not much lower than the original set that comes with equipment. And the ab section they use as a selling point is a just a half dozen super basic exercises like crunches and leg lifts, not someone you need a game disc for. They are basic ab exercises most people are familiar with and can do without an expensive game to urge them on. I really feel that the game description (of both titles) should list the full set of exercises provided online so you don't have to buy it to find out what they are or rather what they aren't. Frankly this should be the EA Calisthenics Active as it's not heavily based on sports but on basic items like lunges, squats, jumping jacks, etc. that you don't a game to do in your living room. I have and like Wii Fit and Wii Fit Plus and expected more from the supposedly more advanced product.

I think the product should come with a chip that sticks on pins your pants leg in some way less bothersome than the leg nunchuk holder. And I think the workout should be more balanced as it progresses. for instance, Having 3 quadricep leg exercises back to back with nothing for hamstrings is a bad idea. Possibly if you can keep the leg strap on, you might reach some, but, the makers should have made balanced workouts to account for drop out in the middle which will happen to even the best of us and especially those new to exercise choosing to work from home rather than in a gym or group environment.

So, I guess I just stick to the gym. It's a shame, so much potential wasted.

title: Technical Disappointments for a Halo Fanboy
text:
I've been playing Halo since it came out while I was in middle school. It shaped the majority of my teenage years. I love the universe and the games ALOT. When the XB1 came out, I didn't have the money to play Halo 5. I finally got a good job so I bought an XB1X for this game and it was shocking when I first played it. The first thing you notice is that it breaks from virtually every other halo game with control set up. I still had the muscle memory available from previous games and the new experience was terrible.

For some reason 343 decided that a 70 degree FOV was a good idea. You have very little situational awareness so say good bye to reacting to something in your peripheral vision. One might say that the helmet would restrict the FOV. Nope. The screen edges cut out the edges of the viewing area of the "visor". The visors in the game cover at least 120 degrees. If you want to have a successful, high speed game, you have to give the players some viewing room to avoid things like motion sickness and disorientation, but they give you the FOV of a horse wearing blinders so it won't get scared.

On top of this they give you three AI teammates who in the opening scene are complete BAes. Once you start playing, they are less effective than grunts. They can't fight other than a few shots every now and then without being directly controlled. They can't pick up effective weapons without being directly told to. If they run out of ammo, they usually pick up a plasma pistol with 50 other better weapons at their feet. The plasma pistol would be moderately effective of they actually pulled the trigger more than once every 5-10 seconds. If their big updates made the AI team more effective, the other problems would be absolutely bearable.

The final issue that I have might be related to previous problems that I listed, but it seems like 343 is trying to go the way of "Difficulty is content." Playing on Normal is a nightmare with the limited FOV with numerous, seemingly endless, very fast enemies. There's always one that stepped two steps to the right too quickly for the eye to track with their speed and FOV and end up owning you from somewhere logically visible, but impossible to see with everything that's going on. I'm not going to talk about the enemies that blink away with effects that appear outside your FOV at close range. It also seemed that 343 thought it was a good idea to increase the number of enemies for what I am assuming to be compensating for the Allies that you have, but allies are literally no help when you don't have the free time in a fight to take your thumb off the stick to direct them to a target. One by one by one by one by one.

These issues are making me really sad that I spent a lot of money to play the halo games again. I have never felt like I wasted money on a Halo game before. Never.

There was this one time at school when I started to sing a song in class. I woke up three days later in a hospital bed. The nurse was very sweet and explained to me that I was mercilessly beaten. A student called an ambulance for me, but before it arrived the teacher had enough time to run home, grab his dogs, and race back to set them loose on me.

Once released from the hospital I was not able to engage in many fun activities, for you see, I had three broken legs and half a broken lumbis. It was right then that I purchased an arcade stick and began to enjoy my time in disabled isolation. Now I have this arcade stick.

The moral of the story lies in the fact that this is a great stick to play around with and/or purchase for guests. Also, be nice to teachers.
