title: This Blows Wii Fit Out of the Water.
text:
I bought Wii Fit, and when I opened it and played it, I thought, "Well this is fun" but it wasn't serious, nor anything I TOOK serious, and eventually, it began collecting dust.

I recently started a diet/fitness program. I'm already a member of the YMCA, and would do about 20 minutes on the Elliptical, and a few reps on some of the machines. I never felt out of sorts the next day.

I got Wii Active for when I was unable to get to the gym. I had read the reviews, and they impressed me.

I got it home on Sunday night after working for 12 hours, with full intentions of working out that night. Instead, I cracked a beer and posted on facebook.

The next day, I decided to try the 30 Day Challenge. The day after that, I felt like I had been run over by a truck. More muscles than I knew I had had been worked. The first day started with running/walking/cardio boxing. Again, remember, I was used to doing the elliptical and a few machines 3x a week. When I woke up on Day Two. OMG. I was in pain. REALLY GOOD, heavy muscle straining pain. Except I didn't feel strained during the workout.

I am only on Day 3 of the challenge, but I'm already confident enough to say that this will work you out like you can't believe, if you do the exercises properly.

I highly recommend it.

title: A Fun Experience, Marred By Unneeded Complexity
text:
This is my first Animal Crossing game and, after sinking a number of hours into it, I've had a pleasant experience. This is as casual as video games get and it's a breath of fresh air, especially in times like this. Performing what might seem as menial tasks, such as fishing or chopping wood, feels rewarding in the end as you begin to craft new items and upgrade the island town around you.
The game performs and looks great. The music evolves over time with your island and invokes a peaceful mood. The time switching actually makes for a different experience when you play and visiting your friends is a quick and breezy experience.

However, the lack of quality-of-life enhancements is disappointing. Inability to craft multiple items at once, long dialog trees, and convoluted UI choices really bog down the experience after hours of play. A few updates to the experience would really solidify this as a five star game.

title: Completely disappointed after high hopes...
text:
I'm one of those people who needs to be tricked into working out. If I feel like I'm exercising, I won't do it. At all. Therefore, I have found that the Wii Fit & Wii Fit Plus are the best options so far, as they're very fun and I've experienced some real results from it. However, one can't help but get bored after 2 months straight of the same thing. So I bought this game.

Overall, I sincerely dislike this game. It's too much like a video, it's patronizing, and the motion-recognition is garbagey to the point of it halting the workout and stalling it so long you stop sweating.

I use Wii Fit Plus every day, and it's light years ahead in ease of use, physical feedback, look, graphic design, music, and fun. So disappointed.

Pros:
The workout, when it works, works well. It kicks your butt like whoa.
There's a lot of variety within the workouts, which will keep me from getting bored and quitting.
The additional tools (journal, calorie counter, etc) are useful tools for weight loss purposes.
The instruction is pretty easy to understand.

Cons:
The trainers are so annoying that I find myself cussing at the television. A lot. They are patronizing and the actors have ridiculous perma-grins on their faces that make it hard to watch them.
The motion recognition is crap. It often won't register that you're doing anything when you're working out, causing the whole workout to stall. It, however, didn't register anything wrong the one time I fell on the floor due to over-lunging. Garbage.
The videos are really long and put too much rest time in between workouts.
It's clunky and cumbersome to try to hold the remote, the nunchuck, and the handles of the resistance band if you're small-handed like I am.
The leg strap slides off a lot, and barely fits my mid-thigh. I'm not skinny by any stretch of the imagination, but I'm not obese, either, so it ought to fit a little.
The pseudo-encouraging chatter by the trainer is incessant, and becomes so annoying that I've muted it within 10 minutes.
Having to constantly press A to skip the videos is a bit intrusive.
It doesn't provide opportunity for modification of exercises due to injury or disability, which is a bummer.

Listen, if I wanted a crummy aerobics video, I'd buy one. I don't, though. I want an interactive game that tells me how to maximize my exercises and makes me actually have fun while doing so. This thing fails on both counts. I'd give this thing a D+.

text:
This is a great workout "Game". My wife and I are two weeks into the 30 day challenge and we love it. I always follow up with a bike ride after my workout.

While it is a great workout "game" there are a few things I need to mention:
(I want to say that I am NOT a professional trainer and am reviewing this as the average consumer.)

Other than these minor issues, we love it. If you do it right, you will be sweating after your workout! I do like how you can choose how extreme you want to go on your workout before you start each day.

title: Another 1 Star Review Because of One Island Per Switch
text: While I can see that the decision to allow only 1 island per switch was made in an attempt to foster cooperation between the people who play the game on the same console, not allowing the individual profiles to opt-out and start their own island is a crippling mistake. For anyone who uses their switch by themselves this game is pretty fun, but anyone who shares their switch with another person and wants the ability to play this game on their own, and only occasionally play together, will be sorely disappointed to find that the first island created on a given switch is forced upon every subsequent player who plays the game on that switch. Nintendo, please consider removing this arbitrary and, for many of us game-breaking restriction so those of us who share a switch console with others can enjoy the game how we choose to enjoy it.

title: A Relaxing, Wonderful Time
text:
As a fan of Animal Crossing: New Leaf, I can happily say that this is an amazing game. It gives off the same relaxing vibe as the others, with some new and great ideas.

First of all, the improvement to the controls gives you some serious quality of life. Being able to quickly switch between your items with the wheel is a grand idea, and I hope whoever thought of this at Nintendo received a raise. I love it, everyone loves it, and we love you. Plus, they took notes from Animal Crossing: Happy Home Designer with how you can arrange your furniture. It makes decorating rooms much more interesting and less frustrating.

The graphics, of course, have improved from the last game. New Horizons is very pleasing to the eye. Nighttime is my favorite because the sky looks phenomenal, and I adore waiting to see a shooting star. Not only that, but they have vastly improved the graphics on clothes you can create! I find myself far more tempted to snag outfits from creators now that they're not so extremely pixilated.

Lastly, the ways you can customize your island are endless. There is now terraforming. TERRAFORMING!! You can do almost anything to your island thanks to terraforming! I've seen so much creativity from people with this one tool. Plus, items can now be displayed outdoors however you want. Would you like a couch on the beach? That's weird, but go ahead! The freedom is endless.

TLDR: New Horizons is a vast improvement on New Leaf, a game I already loved as is. Get it if you haven't yet. Enjoy yourself. Be creative. Relax.

title: Kicked my butt!
text:
I just turned thirty and my sister surprised me with a Wii. So here I go--a new decade of my life and a new me! Time to get in shape! I immediately purchased EA Sports Active and Wii Fit Plus and just received them today. I started with Fit Plus and found the games fun albeit a bit hard to control the first time around. I then moved to EA Sports Active and LOVED IT! I just finished a thirty minute routine from the first day of the 30 Day Challenge and chose the medium difficulty level. It had me sweating half-way through and when it was over I had to walk outside in the brisk evening air to allow myself to cool down. What I like about this game is that they have videos showing you how to actually use the Wii remote, nunchuk, balance board, and resistance bands correctly before you complete an exercise the first time. When you come back to an exercise the second time, you can just skip through the video unless you want a reminder. So, with EA Sports I felt like I could instantly sync myself with what the game expected and therefore had a better workout experience; with Wit Fit Plus I feel like it's going to take a bit more time to figure out how to get my own body to sync with the screen so that I can maximize my calorie burn (although if nothing else, Wii Fit Plus has taught me that I need to be more aware of my body movements)!

I agree with others here that the included resistance band feels a bit flimsy. Honestly, when I first opened the box I thought they had made a mistake--it looked like a stretchy ribbon. I had some problems with the game recognizing my arm movements when I was doing bicep curls with the band. I have much stronger resistance bands from an old Billy Blanks workout DVD and think I will use those going forward. While I have larger thighs, I did not have a problem with the leg band over my Old Navy yoga pants. It did fall off once after some kickboxing, but I think that was my fault for not tightening it enough. I foresee having to wear it with yoga pants or some other type of tighter-fitting pants--I can't imagine being able to wear it comfortably over bulky pants or in shorts. I didn't have any problems with the nunchuk wire getting tangled although I obviously haven't tried all of the exercises yet.

Bottom line: on day #1 I'm very happy I purchased this product. I think having the balance board is a definite bonus to keeping track of your movements, so I'd recommend buying it in tandem with Wii Fit Plus if you don't already own the board. My biggest problem has been finding time to get to the gym. With this at home, I'm already excited to get up tomorrow and start working out again!

title: A great investment!
text:
Despite the negative reviews here, I had no problem hooking it up and dropping in a white label "Mediamax" 5700 RPM 6 TB hard drive from goharddrive on ebay. I was mainly going for more space so I skipped over the faster 7200 RPM drives, the minor loss of bootup speed isn't a problem for me and is typical with this accessory. Games seem to run smoothly.

This device makes the PS4 top-heavy and can be a problem for gamers who like to keep their system vertical with a stand. One solution is to remove the stand and rest it with the hard drive side down removing the stand altogether.

I wish the hard drive had some cooling device connected for higher capacity drives which seem to run a lot warmer, I modded mine with a pc fan on the side and a grille across the front for this reason.

I wish it were connected to the playstation a little better; every time I pick up the playstation it has to be picked up from the bottom because this thing slides right out. Time will tell if this damages the sata cable this device uses in the front.

Rest mode and rest mode downloading is impossible with any device that allows you to use 3.5" hard drives. Turning on the PS4 to download something is not a problem for me and is a small price to pay.

Mediamax 6 TB hard drive was $150 new and this device is about $40. For $190 you're getting 12 times the space of launch day PS4 (500 GB). And a slightly improved 5700 rpm over the 5400 of launch day PS4.

Since disks can get lost or stolen, I believe most games will be downloaded in the next gaming era, this is worthwhile.

title: EA Sports Active
text: For those of you disappointed by Wii Fit, this is the game for you. This game picks up the slack and really gives you a great workout, and I can guarantee you will sweat. The exercises are well proportioned in the 30 day challenge, and they definitely don't push you too hard until you want to choose a higher difficulty. The gradual easing into the program is a big plus. The game is essentially like having your own personal trainer, but of course at a fraction of the price. And for those who would rather work out at home than go to a gym, this is an excellent idea. There are a multitude of different kinds of workouts, different skill levels, and you can combine them into your ideal program. I highly recommend this game/exercise aid, and it does complement Wii Fit as well. Not only can you use the balance board, but since Wii Fit is more focused on Yoga and balance, and Active is more about cardio and exercise in general, playing one right after the other will yield great results. Just stick with it, you can do it, and you will not be disappointed.

title: Never run out of things to do
text: I’ve loved Animal Crossing since the very first game. I’ve been playing previous versions of the game for years, and was super excited about the release of New Horizons. So excited in fact, that this game is the only reason I purchased a Nintendo Switch. Although I don’t regret it because I’ve found lots of Switch games I like now. But none are as amazing as Animal Crossing New Horizons. There is so much to do in this brilliant open ended game. You can customize the inside and outside of your house. You can add more rooms to your house (after paying off your debt with bells, the in game currency). You can customize your island with terraforming and outdoor furniture. You can fish, participate in fishing contests, catch bugs, participate in catching contests, sell your things in a local store, shop for furniture or clothing, collect bugs, fish, fossils, and art to fill up the museum, plant flowers, etc. There is no shortage of things do. You can visit other islands, either your friends islands or special Nook islands. There are cute animal villagers on your island that you can talk to and help them too. Plus there is crafting of items, which is a new feature added to this game. I am so happy with this game, and highly recommend it to anyone who wants to relax with a fun game. It couldn’t have come out at a better time. With everyone staying home on the daily, this is something exciting to look forward to every morning.

title: Good For The Price If You Game Or Use Something Like Zoom
text:
These headphones are good for the price point, especially for playing video games and talking over Zoom or something similar. I used them to play a video game online with a few people and they could hear me fine and I also used them to talk to a therapist over Zoom with no issues.

The box looks professional enough and the headphones came with instructions. There is also a cord so you can hook them up to a computer that needs you to plug in both the headphones and the microphone. Usually you don't have to worry about this, but if you need both plugs, it's an option.

Sound quality is decent enough for the price. The only issue I have with the headphones is that the bass frequency is fairly weak. And, to test out if it was just my console or my computer, I hooked them up to my phone and played a song with lots of bass. You can hear it, but it's not going to blow you away or anything.

They fit tight on my head, but that's not a bad thing because they keep outside sound out better that way. I do have a larger head than most so if you don't like something tight on your head for a long time this may not be for you. I would say they were comfortable to wear for a couple of hours while gaming.

All in all for the price you are going to be happy with these if you need something to just play games with or to use for talking to others through something like Zoom. They would not be good for listening to music, but they would work in a pinch. The cord is also sturdy and is made of some cloth material so I assume that it's a bit stronger than the typical plastic wires.

title: Customization equals motivation- a personal trainer in a box
text:
EA Active has improved upon the Wii workout experience greatly. I own Wii Fit and several other cardio workout programs. All have an ability to make a simulated character and set specific goals. What Active does that no other program does is let you set your very own workout and then stack them up one after another so there is no waiting time between exercises like in the Wii Fit. You don't get scores for every segment but have a routine without stops and starts. In 20 minuntes, I could do 5 yoga moves on the Wii Fit. In 20 minutes, I can get a complete workout on Active.

I have had this for over a month now and find I really enjoy working out. I look forward to the combinations in the 30 day challenge and can add specific exercises in the custom workout section. This is a fantastic addition for someone like me who cannot do some types of exercise because of medical conditions (for me arthritis brought on by years of running and bad genetics). I am in shape, in my early 40's and lead a fairly active lifestyle. I simply cannot do every exercise. In the Wii Fit, I could avoid the running and hula hoop which left me only with the step section for cardio. I did step 176 times in one month trying to get at least 30 minutes of cardio. It became routine, monotonous, and didn't really get my heart pumping. With Active, there are so many options that don't involve running and jumping that I can have a varied workout experience and still get a great workout. It is a great feeling to need a shower when I finish.

Active suggests you take a rest day after 2 days of working out. I don't do this. I work out 5 days a week when I am in town, which is about every other week. This brings me to the only downside of the Active program. It is not meant for people who travel. Even though I exercise in hotels, the Active does not count this so I look sedentary on the graphs. I can add other exercise, it even encourages it, but it's meaningless in making your goals. I have learned to work around this by setting two week goals that include only time I am at home. For instance I set 8 workouts in 14 days. A future improvement would be better integration of multiple workout methods. If runners could add miles, weight lifters could add reps, and swimmers could log laps, it would be ideal.

If you have been working out with weights, even light ones, be prepared to buy your own resistance band. The one that comes with the game is not sufficiently challenging. A $10 band from Giam solved this easily. I am far from muscular but like having some real resistance without having to make layers of plastic banding on the floor like the video instructions. That's not the game's fault, making one band for every potential user is impossible. I like that they erred on the side of caution and make something that beginners will enjoy.

Give yourself a few days to learn the techniques behind the moves. I was frustrated the first few days when my movements didn't register. Learning where to point the Wii remote makes all the difference. I have read a few reviews where this was the main pain point. If you consider it a learning curve instead of a game weakness, you'll have a better experience. Just as we have to learn new strokes in swimming or gain proficiency in a new sport, this game takes a few days of doing it wrong before you get the hang of it. All said, it is much easier to learn than golf. :-)

If you have special needs, physical limitations, or strong preferences, this is a great game for you. Take time to get to know the system, check and uncheck exercises, make your own workout...don't be shy. The system is made for everyone. Make it yours and enjoy!

title: Having trouble getting it to work properly.
text:
I am a novice/casual MAME gamer with minimal knowledge of joysticks and emulators. I bought this joystick to play older MAME games occasionally.

I found this joystick attractive because of its size, heft, number of buttons, and relatively-low price.

Physically, the controller feels sturdy and responsive. It has a nice weight and solid construction. The nonskid feet at the bottom are a nice touch. Comfortable to hold on my lap or place on a desk or coffee table. Good craftsmanship for an inexpensive, Chinese-made, third-party joystick.

The instruction manual is minimal, inaccurate, and somewhat difficult to understand. The included driver software seems to be buggy and poorly-written. Neither the CD nor the instruction sheet contained a help/FAQ/troubleshooting/readme file. This is a problem for me.

I read the instructions and installed the driver from the CD. I tested the joystick from my computer's control panel. It worked fine.

I played five different MAME games using the joystick. It worked fine.

I tried to create macros to map different keyboard functions to the joystick buttons. This was where I ran into problems.

When I tried to map the joystick's button #9 to my keyboard's key #1, it didn't work. When I tried to change the macro, I was not even able to access the macros. Each time I tried, I would get an error message saying "Windows Shell Common Dll Has Stopped Working," and the program would shut down. After numerous attempts, I got the Blue Screen Of Death. The computer completely crashed and rebooted itself.

Reinstalled the driver. Tried to test the joystick. It completely stopped working.

Installed a different driver from MayFlash's website. Joystick is working again. Still unable to access the macros. Got the Blue Screen of Death again.

Joystick is physically working, but it is making my computer crash.

If this stick is intended for "novice" or "casual" gamers, it needs some work. It is not user-friendly at all.

title: Overall Great But Pros and Cons
text:
Pros

- Learns and gets harder and is not monotonous.
- Music is cool and diverse.
- The avatar on the screen actually moves around as the player (you) moves around.
- You really do get a very tough workout, and I am sore.

Cons

- The guy trainer is annoying as hell, and I had to switch to the woman. The woman is not "yo dude" annoying but she is kinda a b#tch when you do a routine wrong. But I guess that's what you need a personal trainer to be!
- The resistance band is wimpy and I may need to add weights or buy an add-on band to get it to where I think I should be.
- The balance board utilities are not that great and the game does not have the body monitoring / measuring tools that Wii Fit Plus does. I am thus still using Wii Fit Plus to do my daily weigh-in and BMI test.
- There are no "games" or "fun" things in the package. For those things - such as Island Cycling or Segway Mole Hunt - I switch back to the Wii Fitness Plus.

Oh, my other complaint about the EA Sports Active wii game is as follows. The woman in the instructional videos quite obviously has a much longer nunchuck cord than exists in reality. When she is holding the controller and the nunchuck in her hands, the cord seems to dangle down to about her crotch area. When I do the same stance with the IRL equipment, the cord rest right below my chest - much higher. My cord is shorter. The shortness of the cord does make doing some of the routines a bit tougher than the ease you see in the instructional video with her super-long cord. Some of this may be due to the fact that I'm a guy. But I am petit, so that cannot be that big of a factor.

Again though I complain, I am liking the workout and recommend it.

title: Intense workouts
text:
I've been working out on the Wii Fit and realized that after a while, the exercises are not as challenging and the workout loses effectiveness. I still want to do it from home so I was recommended to get this game.

This makes the transition from a "Fun" to a "Real" workout. I've been using the 30 day challenge and within 5 minutes of the workout, I'm sweating and I feel my body working hard. It takes me about 30 minutes to complete, the software guides you through routines and ensures that the motions you are executing are done properly; it monitors this by using the wii-mote and the nun-chuck. Although this game is capable of using the balance-board, it is not used very frequently.

The coaches on the game talk to you throughout the routines but it not the chatty type like the Wii Fit, it does not slow down the pace at all, they talk to you while the exercises are in motion. I've given it a 5 stars because it is doing all I want it to do.

title: Cardio joke
text:
I'm reading all of these reviews, and I can't believe how positive they all are! I guess if you've never worked out before or want some light exercise then this will be fine, but otherwise don't expect too much. Here are my issues:

- Working out with yourself as an avatar instead of following the movements of an on-screen coach was too weird for me -- there's a lag in the action between you and what your cartoon self does, so it doesn't really move with you. You're even supposed to try to make it look like you, which I found slightly creepy.

- There are several times during the workout when you're told to keep still when you're not moving at all, and it won't proceed until you hold still for about thirty seconds. Kind of kills the whole "cardio" flow.

- There's no stretching or real warmup/cooldown. There's a jerky kind of walk/jog on a track at the beginning which I guess could be interpreted as such, but didn't work for me.

- There are very few low-impact exercises available. I have a bad Achilles tendon and can't jog. I opted out of as many exercises as I could, but when told to break into a jog from a walk, I just ended up shaking the nunchuk in my hand to make it think I was running. The exercises that remained weren't very cardio-challenging (even set to their hardest), and there was WAY too much fussing with the band and holstering/unholstering the nunchuck between exercises.

- The resistance band is way too weak. I ended up using my own, which was much stronger.

- Cardio boxing? Please. Even set at the highest level, you punch at the targets so slowly you could get coffee in between!

- It offers a "customized workout" option to design yourself, but this, too, was disappointing because it pauses between each exercise -- there's really no way to maintain an elevated heart rate and have a truly successful cardio workout with this.

Bottom line, I was looking for something WAY more challenging, and actually feel like this was a waste of money. I was looking for something to supplement My Fitness Coach (which also has some issues, but overall takes a much better approach and makes you work a lot harder over time), and this just didn't fit the bill, sorry.

But just so I'm not 100% negative, the in-line skating was fun and more difficult than expected. Hard on the Achilles, but definitely challenging.

Tip1... For Win8 users running MAME ROMS with this arcade controller... do not install drivers from the included CD or from the Mayflash website- they won't work properly with the MAME ROMS. Just plug the controller in and use the Win8 default drivers.

Tip2... My controller wouldn't work (computer would not recognize new device plugged in) on my USB2.0 ports, but worked perfectly from my USB3.0 ports- just keep that in mind.

Tip3- For correct functioning on MAME ROMS... press the "Auto" and "Clear" buttons simultaneously once you plug in the controller for correct joystick functioning. If you unplug the controller or turn off the computer you have to repeat the above procedure before running the MAME emulator.

title: Expensive, but worth it
text:
First, let's address the cost - yes, it's expensive, but $60 would get you at most two months at a gym, so in the long run it's worth it.

The leg strap - yeah, it tends to fall down if you don't super tighten it down, but I've not had any circulation problems because of it. I'm not super fit and don't have skinny legs.

The resistance band - it could be stronger, but if you are looking for a stronger one - there are plenty on the market. This is a good intro resistance band for people who aren't used to strength training.

Vs. the Wii Fit... another reviewer said Wii Fit was better hands down... I call it. If you polled the users out there the majority would agree Active is better. With the Wii Fit you spend more time navigating the menus between exercises then you do working out. It is just not possible to get more of a workout with Wii Fit than Active in the same amount of time.

The game has not locked up on me - I've worked out 6-7 times with it already and no lock ups. It's fast and smooth for me.

What I love: you get a nice workout at home and it KNOWS if you're doing it or not - so you can't cheat! You can't even go too fast or it won't count it. It's a good workout for my fitness level. I like that it tells me how many calories I burn. I like the variety of exercises - especially the boxing and the dancing - they make it feel fun. I like that I can skip an exercise - my knees give me problems sometimes so I can't always do the squats.

What I don't love: I wish you got performance based incentives - like after you brun 500 calories you get more music or a new backdrop. Instead you get a trophy. Sure - it tracks your progress, but I like rewards. I wish you could go back and see your past workouts in a chart - like how many calories you burned, etc. It does not track your weight (at least not that I have found), but it does let you track your health habits - seems kind of pointless to me.

Overall - I like this game, I'm glad I bought it. I have a very young son and I don't get a lot of time to work out. With Active I can work out in less than 30 minutes and really break a sweat. I highly recommend this game for anybody with a Wii.

title: Know what you're doing and this is the best thing ever!
text:
I hooked up a Toshiba 4TB SATA 6Gb/s 7200rpm, 128MB Cache 3.5" drive and I shouldn't have to worry about running out of space for a couple years.

The 500 GB drive that comes with the PS4 will fill up in a year (if you don't buy a lot of games in the cloud) or a month (if you're a serious gamer).

So you can swap it out with the largest 2.5" drive you can find (2 TB?) which will last a couple more years (or months if you're a serious gamer) or you can buy one of these.

I read the reviews from other people, and was worried that I'd select a drive that wouldn't work with the Nyko, but then I found someone on Amazon who successfully got it to work with the Toshiba 4 TB drive--so I bought the Nyko and the Toshiba.

The install went fairly quick (the only hiccup was that I had the wrong update file from the Sony website--there are two on their page and you have to make sure you have the larger of the two).

NOTES:

1) make sure you back up your saved games. I went one further and did a System-->BackUp (so it saved all my user date, facial recognition, etc) to a USB drive. If you're just backing up saved games you can do that to the cloud if you have PS+ but you'll have to do them individually for each game. If you back up the system, it's a single select.

2) After you install it (and restore your backups XOR System-->Restore) be sure to turn off all the features that put your PS4 into REST MODE. Right now (November 2015) Sony can't handle this large of drive, and will occasionally lock up when it goes into rest mode. If you disable the power saving functions (you can still let it power off the controllers, just not the PS4 as a whole) you'll be good to go! Eventually, Sony will fix this. When they do, simply re-enable the power saving/rest mode feature at that time.

title: Great exercises
text:
I got the EA Sports Active-Personal Trainer and fit board as a Christmas gift. I'm almost done with the 30-day challenge and so far I like it. In fact, I recently bought EA Sports Active-More Workouts and completed one routine. One major difference between the two is that the Active-More Workouts provides a warm up and cool down whereas the original Active does not.

I use the Active-Personal Trainer & Active-More Workouts as supplemental routines to my daily workout...call me crazy but I like working out, or more accurately, staying active so these two workouts are good for that. I do work up a sweat and feel great afterwards. I especially like working out with a personal trainer i.e., workout buddy, which keeps me more engaged in doing the routines. In addition, I like the idea of keeping track of my daily activities and recording them in the journal after working out. I tend to monitor what I do, eat, and drink more now knowing that it will be recorded.

Even though I really like the EA Sports Active I want to share a couple of issues: 1) I found that the cord between the nunchuk and remote does get in the way with certain exercies, which can be frustrating. My suggestion, make the nunchuk wireless. 2) The system freezes during the reps because the signal isn't detected from either the nunchuk or remote. Even though I did the exercise according to the routine, and in some cases shift myself to be more in line with the TV, I'd get messages telling me to finish it correctly. Sometimes I'd do it 2-3 times with no response...ugh! Not sure what the solution is for this issue, oh well. 3) The exercise band doesn't seem to have a lot of tension; however, I found that by stepping on the band takes up the slack thus creating the tension I want. Also, you could buy yoga bands and substitute it to provide the tension level you want, i.e., light, medium or heavy.

Long and short of it all, I really like EA Sports Active and highly recommend it to people who want to have a fun workout with a trainer in the convenience of your own home.

title: Making Fitness Fun
text:
I purchased this game about 2 weeks ago and am midway in the 6 week challenge. I've lost about 3 lbs so far. I bought Wii Fit Plus before this game and found while it was fun, it was hard to create a good workout. I used the preset workouts where you do three different activites at a time, and found that the only one that really had me break a sweat was the cardio boxing.

So I was at Target, looking around and I saw this game for 40 bucks. I didn't have the original game so I had to purchase the resistance band and nunchuck strap pack for 15. From what I understand, the one that came with the original was flimsy, however the accessory pack band is very sturdy and I never feel like it will break.

I too have had an occasional leg slippage of the nunchuck strap but for the most part it stays put.

The huge difference between this and Wii fit is that I sweat a LOT more and feel that I am getting a better work out. The 6 week challenge allows you to pick 4 days to work out, and 3 rest days, and on medium intensity, the average calorie burn is about 170 per workout. I found that Wii Fit only showed you your calories after you were done, like it was some big mystery, but this game ticks them down as you go.

The exercises have a wide range, and while the warmup and cooldown remain the same, they're mindless and not so bad because I can tell I am getting warmed up. During your six week program, every day will give you different exercises that focus on different parts of your body. I can't say at any one point that I felt like giving up, because of the differences in exercises given. Some ARE more challenging than others, especially the jumping.

So yes, buy this game, you won't regret it! I look forward to seeing how my weight loss will progress (along with a sensible diet!)

title: Not a good option for your PS4, stick with the drives it was designed for
text: Beware this device.  Although technically it works (it is just a SATA extension cable in an enclosure, it would be hard not to work), there are some things to keep in mind.  A 3.5 inch drive takes more power to run than a 2.5 inch drive which was designed with low power consumption as a requirement.  More power equals more heat, and more wear on a power supply that was not made for this device.  It would have been CHEAPER for Sony to put a 3.5 inch higher capacity drive in the system, so there is likely a reason they didn't (power requirements, heat, vibration, airflow for cooling, etc.)  Personally, I recommend using a 2.5 inch drive as it was designed for to avoid all STATED problems with this product, as well as many which are not.  If you fill up the drive later down the road, higher capacity 2.5 inch drives will be lower in price at that point than what they are now, and possibly even faster, without the issues.  After all, what use is a higher capacity drive that you never get the chance to fill because it caused too much stress on your system and killed it.

You do not need to have a balance board. During setup it asks if you have one and would like to use it, just make no. You will want some kind of floor mat if you don't have carpet. You are on the floor for the stretching and crunches and is pretty uncomfortable without it. You can workout on your own, with a friend or choose to do the 6 week challenge with goals set and days programmed for you to work out with your "trainer" through a preset workout that is very effective! title: Great workout for everyone
text:
Already plenty of reviews about feature etc so I'll skip right to my review 'value add'. We got this around Christmas time last year but never really did much with it. A week or so ago I decided to jump on the scales and noticed an extra 15 pounds that shouldn't be there. Guess my desk job and age are finally catching up with me. So I pulled this one out and started the 30 day challenge figuring I may/may not actually use it till the end thinking it wouldn't keep me engaged and that the workouts wouldn't be effective (guy thinking).

I'm now a week into it and I will testify that it will keep you going and I definitely get a good workout. My quads are a bit sore even as I type this today. I set it at high intensity (even with my 15 extra pounds, I feel I'm still in decent shape), upgraded the band, and feel confident that I will see it to its completion.

Pros:
Great mix of exercises that simulate gym type workout.
Trainer's videos and encouragement are spot on.
Catches when you are doing right or wrong form and helps to correct/motivate.
Works in 'rest' days so 2 on 1 off etc.

Cons:
Resistant band way to weak, but easily remedied by buying one that best suits your fittness need. ($9-$20 depending on what you get)
Since I don't wear biker shorts, the leg band will slip on some of the cario workout parts (but I'm getting better positioning it so it doesn't)
No actual weight loss goal built into program (so i use the wii fit channel to track this part)

Bottom line: If you are trying to decide which workout routine to get, Active is a great purchase for an overall body workout. Just doing the 30 day challenge pays for itself.

title: Surprisingly Expansive & Enjoyable
text:
When I heard the first expansion, in what is sure to be another long line of expansions, for The Sims 3 would be a pack based on the old theme of `travel', I was a little disappointed. With The Sims 2, the developers were smart enough to vary each expansion pack to be a new theme altogether, followed by a reinvention of a pack from the original Sims game. Needless to say, hearing that the first pack would be vacation-oriented - one of the least popular themes based on community feedback - I put off getting this for quite some time.

What I found upon finally getting the game was that I was pleasantly surprised. The developers have continued on in their quest to make the game `mean' something - for everything to be a lot more interconnected and have slightly more closed gameplay than the original games. This isn't necessarily a bad thing though! The game is more limited in that there are tangible goals to reach, rather than the purposeless open-ended gameplay of the original two games. However, it's still dramatically expansive over the original games because there are so many goals to aim for, it'd be impossible to achieve even a fraction of them with a single sim - something I imagine will only continue to grow with future expansions.

There are three destinations to explore based loosely on the stereotypical portrayals of China, France, and Egypt. Each destination has a base camp where your sim(s) reside, but they can also save up their simoleans and work to upgrade their visa to purchase a vacation home. And how does one upgrade their visa? They complete missions that are typically related to the set of skills your sim has upon arriving at a destination.

These missions range from scouting metals, making friends, and purchasing items to fishing, reading books, or - most excitingly - exploring underground tombs for treasures. The tombs are really the crux of what makes the game work. They add a million hours of gameplay as you figure out (relatively simple) puzzles and go through maze-like basements, collecting loot and treasure along the way. Whenever you complete a mission - tomb or otherwise - your sim will earn money, increased relationships, visa points (the higher your visa the longer you can stay), and other bonuses.

Beyond that there are other things to do in each of the destinations. Your sims can pick up one of three new skills - photography, martial arts, or nectar making - or expand upon existing skills by catching new types of fish, learning new recipes, harvesting new plants for you garden, and other neat cross-expansion points.

Things aren't quite so exciting for your sims back at home with this game unfortunately - players who are tired of the limits of home life won't be too embroiled in this pack. Taking your sims to a new city freezes time in the regular world - which is a boon if you're working on building skills and relationships, but a pain if you're eager to keep things moving in regular time.

Also the game doesn't lend itself well to controlling multiple sims on vacation. Only teens and up can actually complete missions - sims younger than that will sort of flounder and be bored (unless you buy a vacation home and deck it out with kid-friendly items). I can't even imagine having two adventure-seeking adults on a trip really, because the missions are so intensive that you have to keep a sharp eye out for your sim and what they're doing. The life of a relic hunter is a lonely one, unfortunately.

In general though, I'm surprisingly happy with this pack. It offers an escape from the everyday, but in a meaningful way, and I can hardly wait to send my sim on a world adventure over and over again. It's a little pricy, but it's definitely an *expansion* of the original game.

title: If you are looking for a great way to exercise, this is it!
text:
I purchased my Personal Trainer yesterday morning, but didn't get a chance to try it out until late last night -- after I had already walked for 40 minutes. I thought I would set up my profile and check out a few features before bed; nothing too hard.

Setting up my profile was quick and easy. When the option came up to start the 30 day challenge I selected it. It told me how long the workout would be with the tutorial videos (cool option) and I figured I had 29 minutes to spare to see what it's about.

I didn't expect to get such a good workout! I was wiping away sweat mid-way through. This is not a game. This is truly a personal trainer for your Wii. I like how it goes from exercise to exercise, just like if you were at the gym with a trainer.

I selected the medium intensity and it was just enough for me. I will have to say that the resistance bands they give you are a bit light (for me). So I used some bands that I already had (except on the shoulder raises, I had to use the bands included in the game).

The game is very responsive to your motions. There was no lag that I experienced. However, you do have to make sure you hold the remote and nunchuk exactly as they show you, otherwise it won't register your reps (I had issues with the bicep curls as I wasn't curling my wrists all the way in). You will get a nice message that you aren't completing them correctly and tips on how to do them right.

I had no problem with the leg band as some others posters mentioned -- and I don't have little thighs by no means. However, in the info book, it does give you advice on what to wear with the leg band (close fitting pants) and how far to have it on your thigh (it needs to be pretty high, when I first put it on, it slipped off because I didn't have it placed correctly). After the intial adjustments, I had no problems with it slipping off.

I only did the first day workout, but was very impressed with the types of exercises and the variety. Reading other posts has me excited about the other activities out there. The music was okay, but honestly I can't remember what it sounded like as I was concentrating on doing the exercises correctly.

Honestly, there is no comparison to Wii Fit and Personal Trainer. Wii Fit is more fun but incorporating exercise. Personal Trainer is serious about getting you in shape with a little bit of fun.

I can't wait to explore some more tonight. I can't believe that I am looking forward to working out...that right there is worth the price of the game.

title: Not all that original ...
text:
... but really well done. This game is a direct sequel to the 1982 Kurt Russel Film.
Pro's:
The game is basically another game in the 'survival-horror' genre that games like Resident Evil, Dino Crisis, and Silent Hill popularized. However I thought there were a few really nice additions to this game.
*Use of non-playing characters
*need for constant awareness of exposure to the elements
*Less need to conserve EVERY SHOT of ammo. You can't exactly go on a DOOM style free-for-all, but it's not like Resident Evil where you're counting every single round of ammo either.
*The idea for the use of blood tests to identify infected characters
*Use of the Stress meter
Con's:
*They flubbed the use of the blood tests. Sometimes I'll test a non-playing character, he'll register as human only to break out a minute later anyway. The results of the test don't seem to have any bearing at all, wether or not you keep a character you don't absolutely need seems totally random.
*Characters you absolutely have to have to move forward in the game, don't seem to break out. Unless maybe I just had exceptionally good luck ...
*In regard to the game sound, I noticed a few times that I couldn't hear enemy gunfire, that got very annoying toward the end of the game.
*At the VERY end of the game, I thought you went a little too long without being able to save.
*I never actually HAD to hold a gun to any of my characters heads to get them to trust me, careful use of your resources (which Resident Evil should have taught us) and you can avoid the situation. I would have liked to be put in a "Mexican Stand-off" type of situation. That would have been kinda cool

title: Fantastic Game; Refreshing Updates To Classic Title
text:
I purchased this digitally from Nintendo's store, and I've gotten so much out of it.

Basically, if you've played any animal crossing games before (I played the very first one when it was released and fell in love), you're pretty much guaranteed to enjoy this one. There's a great balance of new features and classic aspects of the game that are done really well; for example, gyroids have been added and their new designs are refreshing, but true to the original concept. They're a great collectable that, just like in the first game, when placed, will make sounds randomly (in quiet spaces), or along to the beats of different songs that are played near them. There's also been a lot of improvements to decorating: when in your house, entering decorating mode allows you to place and put away items in your inventory and storage and move them around much more easily. In the first game, all that had to be done one item at a time, and physically moved or rotated by your character. Changing your clothes is vastly different now too: there are tons of outfits and garments you can mix and match, and you can change your appearance at any time as long as you can find a mirror. Other features include swimming (and diving for sea creatures), growing crops, crafting, gathering resources, cooking, and improved clothing / design customization.

For those who have never played it, or maybe you're thinking about purchasing it for your kids, there's something really important to keep in mind. I noticed a lot of negative reviews talk about how you only have one island per console. This is correct: it is one island per system, and all users on your console have to share it. Generally, the first person to start the game is more in charge than the others: they have extra options to build and demolish bridges / inclines, and move buildings and houses of residents (with the exception of the other users, who are the only ones able to move their own homes). The issue with this complaint is that, the game has always been this way. The very first game on the Gamecube was a town shared on the same memory card. This is required because, unlike most games, it is in sync with the system date and time. Changing the date and time of your system will change it in the game as well, so having multiple islands - one per user - isn't possible, unless they somehow made it so that each user could change the system date and time independently. I really don't think that's something Nintendo would be willing to do, but claiming it's a rip-off or an unacceptable flaw ignores the way this particular title works, and has worked for a long time. This might not apply to everyone, but to those who have left negative reviews without fully understanding things... If your kids aren't able to share a digital island, it isn't the company's fault. They're not forcing you to purchase additional consoles, and honestly, if your kids can't learn to share spaces, respect other's property, and collaborate, then you've got more serious problems on your hands. Maybe if they have these issues, you should be a parent and teach them how to handle conflict and disagreements in a healthy manner instead of immediately passing blame. I'm sure most people reading aren't like this, so I apologize if it sounds directed at everyone: it's not. I just find those reviewers very frustrating, and even more so that so many people agree with them.

What can I say other than the fact that my husband and I have both really enjoyed playing Red Dead II.

I played Zelda Breath of The Wild last year and was amazing at how they went into enough detail with the horse mechanics that if you ran through a forest your horse didn't run STRAIGHT into a tree (like a real horse). But with Red Dead, the horse mechanics are the thing that is most lacking in my personal opinion and the greatest downfall of the game. title: The Verdict Is Still Out
text:
Ho boy. I'm not sure where to begin. There is really a lot to say about the long awaited addition to the Animal Crossing family and to be fair, some of it is positive. To be honest, plenty of the criticism is deserved as well.
As a mother of four kids and a fan of the game myself (yep, I played it on the wii and fell in love. The ONLY video game I've ever truly been a fan of- what can I say? It helps me de-stress!), I'm not going to pull any punches when I say that the one island per Switch thing is ridiculous and could in fact damage future development and/or releases. This is a deal breaker for a lot of families. We went ahead and bought the game knowing this was an issue but were hoping to give it a try. After all, we shared City Folk just fine. But one of the main issues is that the person who starts the game sort of gets everything and takes over the development of the island while the other players are just kind of left in the dust for a while. Sure, they still gain points, manage their homes, get DIY plans, but everything they do comes slower, fewer, and is held up by the first player. They're not really creating their own story- they're following in the shadows of the story the first player started. I say that as the first player of our game and it stinks. I would have loved to have passed on some of the challenges and rewards to my kids to complete but instead I just felt rushed to get as much done as possible so they could progress as well.
Another interesting tidbit- and many won't care about this but conservative parents might so I'm mentioning it for them- are the few LGBT references in the American or English version of the game. The Japanese version strangely doesn't contain these references but they were included in the English version and this is notable to me. I firmly believe in equal rights but in what is very much a children's game with talking animals, I fail to understand how it was necessary to include these references. Why do sexual preferences even need to play a part in a game such as this? Without warning, the creators have chosen to include references that feel out of place and a bit like pandering. I'm left scratching my head and wondering, "Why?" And if it was so important to include, why was it left out of other versions? Can't we decide what we deem appropriate for our home and kids rather than having Nintendo make a blanket determination of our culture and then plopping something into the game that they won't even include in their country's version? It's just an odd choice for this type of game. If this seems vague, search it out. The information about this is available. Another issue along these lines is the deletion of gender. I'm aware that there was a group of people that wanted non-binary options in the game, but it seems that gender pronouns have been erased entirely in only the US version. Players are referred to as "they" and "their" by the animals. This is probably my biggest gripe. There is a VERY small population of the US that identifies as completely non-binary. Of that group, it's another small population that plays animal crossing, but any references to "she" and "he" have been replaced in the game with "they." My entire family would prefer to have our pronouns of "she" or "he" used but, so far, this is not an option. It would be great if we could at least choose to have standard pronouns acknowledged rather than erasing the option entirely. An update would take care of this.
As far as some of the changes, like crafting your own tools, there is good and bad. It can be fun to get new plans for building and it adds an element of excitement as the game progresses. However, it can be incredibly tedious trying to constantly gather resources for the many tasks you will have thrown at you. And as the first player, you will be hogging resources the other players will need as well and there simply aren't enough to go around at first. I quickly grew tired of having to gather, gather, gather for Nook's demands when I really wanted to just explore the island. But much of your exploration largely depends on getting those things done.
Also, some islands start off with only about a quarter or less of the island available to build on. We stupidly chose one of those not realizing we wouldn't have access to the rest of the island for a while. This meant we had to place four human player tents, two animal tents, the museum, and Nook's nephews' shop all in the same tiny area. Needless to say, some of us are relocating as soon as that becomes an option because we're all horribly cramped into one space. Keep in mind, relocating is expensive. It becomes more expensive as the game progresses and you gain more control over the island's design.
As for some of the positives, the graphics are lovely and pleasing. The island setting is fun and the water, the sounds, the scenery are awesome. This makes for delightful game play. They nailed the sound of rain, the distant rumble of thunder, the wind picking up in the afternoon- such fun elements!! Visiting other islands is a cool bonus even if it does get a bit tedious when four islands in a row are pretty much the same, but it's a great way to pick up resources. The animal characters are more interactive, have more personality, and are fun to watch as they seem to do their own thing rather than walk around aimlessly. In spite of its flaws, there is something delightful and addictive about the game.
Some fun bonuses: tarantulas are a bit easier to catch, you can uproot trees and just transplant them whole from other islands if you eat fruit first, and you can bring harder to find flowers in crossbred colors from other islands and transplant them on your island (this is rare however!). Also, after acquiring shoots from other islands, you can grow bamboo on your own island. This is a fun bonus, however, so far, I've visited about about 8-10 other islands and haven't seen another type of fruit other than my own and only came across bamboo once. My son has visited other islands about the same amount and has only seen one other type of fruit.
All in all, this game offers some pleasant entertainment and a nice escape from real life for a bit. I'm giving it sound 3 stars because the verdict is still out- I need to see how things develop before I decide if this was a fail or if it will unfold nicely over time. Overall, there is some disappointment and frustration, but the positives are worth noting so I can't pan it. Hopefully, as time passes and updates are made available, we'll be pleasantly surprised, but until then, I'm not going to gush about this game.

Edited 3/27: I'm going to add another half star to one star. Things are picking up and there are more fun bonuses we've discovered as a family as we've played. The other players still don't have as many diy plans as the original player and they've missed out on some things because of their status in the game, but those things become less important as the game progresses. A few still cause issues but we're hoping that will be fixed in the future. In the meantime, there are a lot of things that make this game worth playing and it's easy to see the incredible work that was put into creating the game. So. . . For our family of six, we're currently giving it 3.5 to 4 stars after one week of consistent game play.
Edited 4/21: Plan on having to spend a LOT of time to get the necessary DIY recipes to create furniture. The game is designed to absolutely need an online connection and to play with friends so you can get every type of fruit, flower, DIY recipe, etc. Count on months and months of consistent playing in order to unlock a few things to decorate your house unless you catalog with other players. Count on a lot of repeat DIY recipes you won't need, few furniture options for long periods of time, and count on having to track down other players in online forums in order to catalog items or share resources because there is no other reliable method of getting what you need. I don't like my kids playing with strangers or inviting strangers into our island (I didn't in past AC versions and we did just fine) and I don't have friends who are playing so this puts families like mine in a difficult situation. I appreciate that there were more options in past AC versions for people who didn't want to do a lot of online play but it seems ACNH depends very much on online interaction and help. Hopefully some future updates will remedy this. In the the meantime, our score remains at around 3.5 to maybe 4 stars.

A final thought, and I feel this is very important.....THERE IS NO LEFT-HANDED SETTING! title: Makes working out fun! However...
text:
First I will say that I love this game for working out, it really switches up the routine and makes working out... kinda fun. There are a variety of workouts for all over strength to concentration of various areas. Plus there are a variety of pre-programmed workouts lasting different durations from 20 mins to an hour. My problems with this game are this:

1. I've only used the wii balance board the first time I worked out. I've checked my settings, recalibrated the board, but I never get any more workouts using the balance board.
2. The band that comes with the game isn't challenging enough to get a good workout. And the band loosens from the handles constantly. So I bought some tubing with handles, but I can't hold the wiimote and nunchuck in my hands while using these. Unfortunately there is no way to turn off a setting to do the exercise w/out the remotes. So I do the exercise with the tubing I bought and then re-do it with the game so I can see the estimated calories burned. I'd like to see this option in More Workouts.
3. No core strength training and the variety of cardio is lacking.

If you're thinking of buying this I would recommend waiting for version 2, EA Sports Active More Workouts, which I believe is being released on Nov. 6. They added over 30 more workouts which includes abdominal exercises, I don't know if that means core or not, but it's a step in the right direction.

title: EA Active Has Highs and Lows
text:
I have played EA Sports Active for a couple of weeks now and parts of the game are done well.
Pros:
-Sports tab workouts are fun and challenging.
-The games workouts can be modified to suit your needs. You can go through the workouts and click on the green checkmark, so they are deleted from the workout.
-The female workout trainer has a pleasant voice, and there are many motivating statements imbedded in the exercises.
-The Fit Balance Board can be used for special exercises.
-Three workout intensities: low, medium, and high.
-There is a choice of music to choose from for your workouts.
-The custom workout feature is the best I have seen. I have saved 6 different custom workouts.
-You can set three different goals to meet and earn trophies. The game keeps track of the calories, time, and exercises you do.

Cons:
-The game is very difficult with a wired nunchuck. It slaps around when you are performing the exercises, and the cord isn't long enough to perform other excercises. Bought a wireless nunchuck, but the one I bought works well with exercises that do not use the leg band. It doesn't work at all when the nunchuck is in the leg band.
-The band that comes with the game isn't strong enough to give a good workout for many of the exercises. The band does well with the shoulder presses and upright rows.
-The game gets stuck in several of the exercises if you don't move precisely and have the wii remote and nunchuck exactly right. Hit the + button to skip the exercise and have the game move on.

title: More like 4.5
text:
I preordered this before it's release date so this review is long overdue. Having been a fan of previous Animal Crossing games, I was super excited for this one! The game itself is fun and cute, but it is not perfect. Compared to previous games, you can essentially decorate your entire island however you want. There are also a lot more customization options. What I think can most be improved is the "quality of life". There are just some little details that can improve the game play such as faster and more convenient island building features and unlimited shopping cart for shops for fast check out. There's a great video on YouTube about quality of life improvement suggestions for this game that makes me wish Nintendo sees.

The prices to move buildings is INSANE but it's a game. But what I think definitely needs to improve is the multi-player option. I wish there's also an option to use two remotes for the 2nd player and for them to have the same power as the 1st. It's annoying having to switch off to access inventories. I also think a split screen should be implemented for multi-player use (think Mario Kart) so that the players can have fun building the island together. DIY gets annoying and getting recipes or good furniture takes forever, but the game IS fun. It's relaxing and a great way to kill some time. The game also gets regular updates so there's still hope for some improvements.

title: Great for Smash Bros and  MUCH More!
text:
Great controller, ill be going in depth here. So far I own a Wii U pro controller, gamecube with adapter, and the fight pad. To be perfectly honest my favorite out of the lot is my Wii U pro controller which I outfitted with Xbox One analog stick however this controller is a great alternative to the gamecube adapter and it has more functionality. My gamecube adapter only works on one game, Smash Bros Wii U, this beauty works on smash, any game that supports a classic controller, Wiiware, and emulators and loaders. This controller is also wonderful for use with Wii games since the pro controller doesnt sync up. Using this on wind waker makes me relive the gamecube days except better. Compared to the Fight Pad this thing blows it out of the water, the triggers are much more responsive and the analog sticks feel VERY similar to an actual gamecube controller, the Fight Pad has awful analog sticks that will have your thumb slip and lide all over the place. The only advantage to the fight pad is that they have more designs available like the DK and Metroid variations. The buttons on this are pretty solid and the turbo is a plus, the only complaint I have is that the right trigger rattles a bit but it doesn't have an impact on play. It should also be noted that the L and R buttons have been swapped with the Z buttons, usualy the L and R buttons are the shoulder buttons but on this theyve been put in the trigger location so keep that in mind.

Currently I own 1 of each of these Hori controllers and I recommend you guys buy now, people are scalping Nintendo products like crazy and you dont wana miss the opportunity to own a great controller like this. With the issues with the Majoras Mask 3ds and Amiibo I could see these selling for around $50 in the future so id pick one up now.

title: It works!
text:
EA Sports Active works, and is worth every penny!

A little about me: I am less than 20 pounds overweight, and in fair shape. That being said, this game makes me sweat and my muscles burn every time I use it. It is well put together and effortless to use, and I like that. Previously, I used Wii Fit and Wii Fit Plus. I found them boring, unmotivating, and frankly not much of a work out. EA Sorts Active is everything Wii Fit is not.

The 30 day challenge is awesome. You set up your profile and can enter things like whether or not you want to use the Wii balance board (you do NOT have to have the board to use the game), music selection, and difficulty level. I started on easy and switched to intermediate after a week and saw a big difference. You can also set up how many times per week you want to work out, how many calories you want to burn, and how long of a workout you want...and you're all set! A calendar is set up for you showing which days are your "rest" days. Start up the game, and your entire workout is set up and ready to go...no long pauses between excercises to go back into menus to choose your next one. After each routine the next comes up (there are tutorial videos at the beginning of each) and so on. The workouts are easy to follow and there is always variety. I am 3/4 through my first 30 day challenge and I've not been bored yet.

There are a couple of cons to EA Sports Active. As with many Wii games, the motion sensors can be a pain sometimes, you have to hold the remotes just right for them to register. But once you've done the workouts you get used to how to position the remote & nunchuck. Also, the resistance band that comes with it is crap, just get yourself a good one at a local store and you should be fine.

If you are looking for a game that provides a real workout, without a hassle, this is the game for you. I highly recommend it.

title: No Idea How This Sells For So Little
text:
Let's say you want to make your own joystick like this using a zero delay usb converter board for 10 bucks. First you'll get your joystick and buttons. You can save money and get a set for about 19 bucks that isn't terrible. Now you need to get a case and you are already at 30 bucks. Quick Update: Ordered a second one as a backup. That should tell you something.

The reason: You can tell they went out of their way to try to please everyone, even if they didn't use top of the line parts. The buttons may not be sanwa 30mm, but they feel like it. even if they are bottoming out on a capacitive array rather than a contact point. The joystick is not sanwa, but has some things going for it.

1) they added an oversized actuator so the tilt of the stick is only about 15 degrees rather than the 30 on a stock sanwa jlf. This is great for all games.
2) The spring effort is also almost identical.
3) While the plat on the bottom isn't octogonal, because the actuator is oversized, it's a little easier to nail diagonals.

If I could figure out how to get a shorter shaft then add a 45mm balltop, I might keep the joystick stock.

title: A troubling trend
text: As is well known by now, only one player can control the Island in this game. What this tells me is Nintendo has decided willfully to put their consumers in a position where they need to purchase multiple $300 game consoles if they have more than 1 person in their household that wishes to create their own world. I am as emphatic as anyone when it comes to making my children share with one another. If I thought for a minute that Nintendo was trying to make this world a better place by encouraging cooperation I would applaud this unprecedented game play model. But that is clearly not their intention. It's beyond just a quick money grab, as well. Nintendo is trying to normalize an ownership model where the products producer can retain absolute control over sed product. You may never really own any media on Amazon but at least multiple people can listen to the music , or watch the tv show you've "purchased". Nintendo wants to control their products so that only the purchaser can use them, excluding any multi person access and this game is clearly only the beginning. But that's not the troubling trend i reference in my headline. What concerns me is how passive the user community is about this new strategy of Nintendo's. How willing they are to buy multiple consoles and games and sit in their homes within 20 feet of other household members, playing the exact same game on the exact same game system and thinking this is normality. Nintendo's strategy is really an indictment of the people who willingly walk into the trap. Which seems to be be most of us. A world is developing where it is not strange for every member of a family to own a game system that costs $300 as well as their own copies of the games. And looking at the overwhelming positive responses on Amazon, I realize most people are completely at ease with that paradigm. Beyond just the incredible monetary investment this entails, it also begs the question: at which point do we stop caring about other people's existence all together and melt into a world created by and for us? We become more inexorably enmeshed into the fabric of the matrix every day. And no one cares?

title: Great value! Great fun!
text:
I recently bought this "game" for my wii. This game has lived up to all that I read about online and in the reviews. I am currently on day 3 of my wii active 30 day challenge and I love it! I have already done all different cardio and strength exercises. For instance, on the first day, I did a low impact routine and did some running and walking, inline speed skating, boxing, squats and arm curls. On day 2, I did some more walking and running, tennis, squats, lunges, and shoulder presses with the elastic band. I am already wondering what the game will have me do today! I am impressed with the variety of exercises they have you do. Each time you do a new exercise, a little video comes up on how exactly you should do it and your trainer is very diligent about telling you if you're doing the exercise just right. All in all, I am very impressed. I'm one of those who gets bored of exercising after a while and can fall off the band wagon pretty easily - but I suspect with this, I'll be more inclined to exercise.
Also, the varied exercises reminded me of a boot camp I did last spring at a local gym. In addition to the $[...]/month membership fee, I paid an extra $[...] for a one-month/8 class boot camp class. I can tell you that this wii "game" is very very similar to this boot camp - and look how much less costly it is! So even though the cost of this game may seem pricey, if you think about the big picture, it can actually save you a lot of money.

A few extra thoughts:

*My first day, I decided to do a low impact routine. I had read that folks had gotten a pretty tough work out from the exercises. I wholeheartedly concur. I was still really sore the next day even though I did a low impact routine. caveat: I'm also not in great shape! but be prepared for a tough workout either way!

*I can see why people suggest getting a wireless nunchuck. I can deal with the wired one for now. It might bother some folks more than others. I am considering getting a wireless one.

*I like how you can choose to work out with your wii fit. tho the exercises with the wii fit aren't great in number, when I did use the wii fit with the exercise, it added an extra element of difficulty and fun. I wish that they had more exercises with the wii fit!

*I haven't done any of the exercises with a friend yet. We'll see if I end up buying another set of gear for it. We'll also see if my husband decides to join me. I'm not sure how likely it is for me "playing the game" with a friend. so am also holding off on that purchase for now as well.

All in all, an excellent buy! a great, fun game and worth the value.

As a guy that loves all things basketball and has almost as many games and films of the sport as he has books, he's a credible critic. He says this game is "the best."

In my initial review, I gushed accolades that apparently failed to convey how good this game is. In a followup interview with MVP, I asked for specifics. He said that he would rate this a 6-star game because (1) you can tell this is a real upgrade compared to NCAA 9, and (2) NCAA 10 has no real competition in or out of the PS3 format. There are so many functions in 10 that are not available in 9, e.g., you can choose ESPN or CBS; fully create players with an array of physical attributes, like body build, skin tone, hair style; and select any shoe type, style and brand. Another plus: The player's college major and class status are displayed at the free-throw line. To sum it up, the graphics are so true that you will think you're watching a TV broadcast.

title: I never knew NES games could look so sharp and lovely on my 47" HDTV.
text: I have been a NES collector for years I have around 770 different titles. I wanted to try one of these HD clones out because tbh NES composite video looks ok on a smaller LCD but when you get up to a 47" not so much. That's where this system really shines imo I mean everything is so sharp and colors vibrant. Another good thing is the audio comes through the HDMI and actually comes out both speakers on my TV so no worries about audio y splitters. I picked up the 143 in 1 cart on here as well & it's superb combination with this little HD NES clone by gamerz tek. It takes up hardly any space. The controllers with this system I can't say enough good about. They actually feel better than the original NES controllers and this is coming from a guy who grew up loving the old rectangle shaped pad. The rounded corners are just more comfortable plain and simple, especially for longer gaming sessions. The buttons even have that little concave touch that just feels right and the dpad is great. The select and start buttons are round but made of the same rubber type material as the original. The system also has AV output and comes with those cables as well as a good quality HDMI cable. Only one output functions at a time but I don't see that as an issue. Main thing with these little systems is NEVER put a dirty game in. A dirty game is any game that has not been taken apart and had the pins polished with metal polishing paste and a cloth. Simply using a qtip and rubbing alcohol just don't cut it. Invest in a security bit and some metal glo polishing paste and clean every game. If you buy the multicart you don't have to worry about that either and actually can just leave it in the system all the time if you like. I have the standard versions of the gamerz tek 8 bit with the AV output only and it's great as well but image quality not close on a big screen when compared to hdmi. For some reason Super Mario Bros looks really crappy where as Super Mario 3 not bad or even Zelda. On smaller screens the AV fairs better but if your TV has HDMI definitely spend the extra $$$ and get the HD version. It has a cool blue LED light on front where as the AV only version is red which is a neat touch distinguishing the 2. Also I think the HD version controllers look better with the same color scheme as the originals. I've heard people say the sound is off but to me it's not noticeable enough to make a difference. The really great thing is no lag which I expected with hdmi because even Nintendo's very own NES classic which I have as well and it has a small amount of lag which I instantly recognize since I played Mario so much growing up. I gave this little console 5 stars because I just don't think there's a better value out there in 8 bit gaming. Now I'm considering getting gamerz tek 2 in 1 NES and SNES HD system because I've seeing good reviews on it and am curious how SNES would look on my HDTV.
