title: fun fun fun
text: First, you need to know what Animal Crossing: New Horizons is all about. It starts off with you, buying the Deserted Island Getaway Package. You are dropped off at a completely deserted island along with a few other random villagers. What I mean by villagers is talking animals which each have completely different personalities! For example, Jitters, the green duck who can never get enough exercise. He even dreams about running thousands of miles a day without stopping. Or Bubbles, the hippo always wearing dresses who can never stop talking about becoming a pop star. The island starts out covered in weeds and is swarming with bugs. All you and your fellow islanders have are tents with radios but as you progress, your island does too. You and other villagers begin to live in houses which you can customize to the very last piece of furniture. A museum is forged which displays fossils, art, fish and bugs that you gather. A convenience store is built where you can sell almost anything for some extra cash. The tailor shop is made which sells the finest of clothing. A town hall is installed which provides all necessary help and information to make an island that suits you! Every time I show my mom this game, she falls asleep because of the beautiful songs that the birds sing and the image of a tree’s leaves getting rustled by the gusting wind,which leads me to my next point. The audio is so realistic and the visuals are calming, colorful and just a pleasure to glance at. This game is set with real time so when it’s dark out in real life, the shooting stars rain from the dark night sky in this never ending story.  Plus, you will never get bored! There are always things to do like do favors for villagers, make some paths or even expand your house! The amount of lively energy that was poured into this amazing creation is incredible! Islanders now send you mail, do yoga in front of the town hall, talk to each other about starting bands and even doing daily activities like fishing. Even for people who don’t like video games, you should give this beautiful piece of art a shot! I guarantee you will enjoy every last minute of it!

title: DO NOT get this game for family play, really disappointed with the local multiplayer in this game.
text: We bought a digital copy for our Switch, because NIntendo said only one island per Switch, so we thought it would be a great game for our family of five to play together.  Unfortunately, the game is unplayable because it requires one person to be the  Resident Representative (witch is by default the first person to log into the game).  AND you cannot progress with any of the other characters in the game until the Resident Representative does everything first.  This is terrible for families.  Our daughter, who was the first to log in the first day, is the Resident Representative.  But, recently she has a lot of school work, and cannot play the game much, so all our accounts are stifled and we cannot progress in the game.  I love Nintendo and have owned every system they have ever produced (except Virtual Boy) , but this is inexcusable.  I have put 20 really enjoyable hours into the game and now the game is worthless, because my daughter is busy with schoolwork and I cannot become the Resident Representative.  Until they get rid of the Resident Representative feature the game is not a good option for families sharing a Switch, which is how they marketed the game.  I want to give this game 5 stars for it's content, but at the present time, without an update to the local multiplayer sharing, it's a 2 star game.

title: The Sims 3: World Adventures
text:
The Sims 3: World Adventures added plenty of new features to the game. My favorite features of the expansion are basements and travel.

Basements allow me more creativity with the space on my lot. I can pretend to have lots of underground housing or an evil madman-like cellar. I am normally not a huge Sims fan; however, in regards to traveling to China, Egypt, and France, I love how World Adventures added so many "quests" for me to enjoy. It has really forced me into putting more of my time into the game. Would I buy it again? You bet.

Unfortunately, this game could have benefited from a bit more bug testing. A personal experience I have had is my Sims' family names changing. They also find themselves to be parents of random children who live in a country they visited. These are minor issues, nothing game breaking, but worthy of losing a star in my opinion.

title: Double-tapping issue
text:
My awesome boyfriend wanted to get me a gaming keyboard for Christmas. I wanted a gaming keyboard mostly for macro functions, so it was great that this keyboard had the buttons.

The keyboard, unplugged, looked amazing. It was heavy, so I assumed that perhaps this would be of quality.

That was not the case when plugged in, however. It took me many, many frustrating tries to just type in my computer password for Windows. At first I thought that was so strange! Must be my fault though, because I have a tendency to type fast, and having never owned a mechanical keyboard before, I truly believed it was my user error.

Turns out ... the "shift" key only worked if I pressed it down really hard. Additionally, random keys were double-tapping! Most notably, the J key, U Key, and Q key. Obviously this doesn't help when I have to type reports for school ... having to go back every other word to just type one page would drive me crazy.

HOWEVER, gameplay-wise (in Final Fantasy XIV), the keyboard was exceptionally responsive.

But realistically, I need a keyboard I can type with. Afterall, I'm also talking to my in-game friends in chat.

So what happened?

My boyfriend returned it to Amazon. With a price tag like this, I had high expectations for this keyboard. It even came with a USB and audio port! Among the double-tapping issue, the caps lock light in the upper right corner barely shined through the laminate. It was also blurry. It is NOTHING like the picture at the top shows you, so just keep that in mind.

Never buying Razer again ... but I applaud them for their advertising work. I was actually planning to get one for my boyfriend down the road, but obviously not anymore.

Went with a Logitech G105 instead. So much better, so many fewer problems.

title: Was a hater, now a lover
text:
So I have to admit when FFXIV ARR first came out in 1.0, I was one of those people who left a one star rating. I was so disappointed how I couldn't log in due to the server being full and when I did, I hated the quest system. The UI wasn't impressive and the gaudy achievements like DUTY COMPLETE really bothered me (and still does a little). I put down the game after an hour of playing and vowed never to pick it up again.

Fast forward six months and my boyfriend's friend is raving about the game. I thought "no way! Worst game in history!" But when my boyfriend pick it up, I couldn't help but join him. Wow, was I wrong about this game. I've never had so much fun after GW2 lost its luster for me. The landscape is beautiful, the music is pleasant and I could listen to it for hours, and the primal fights are so exciting.

I'm more of a casual gamer, so anything that screams HARDCORE turns me off. My boyfriend tried to get me to play WoW once ... didn't last long. Anyways, I always look forward to new dungeons and I am loving the hard and extreme modes. I was once so unsatisfied with my performance on Titan Hard that I played it over and over until I got it down ... now everything seems like a breeze. I'm super stoked for coils now and I can't wait to see what ARR comes up with next in its new patches! My main is a white mage, but I've already started on black mage and paladin is coming up next.

Some cons are the community though. Sometimes people can gripe on you if you wipe once or twice because they expect perfection. Some people can also be super elitist and not understanding of new players. People rage and quit parties if the dungeon isn't going how they like ... BUT there are a lot more good people than bad. Lots of players are always willing to give advice and walk you through things. :)

I like ARR so much that I bought my brother a 2 month subscription so he could play with us, and I bought the playstation 3 version to play on a bigger screen ;P I'm a subscriber now and I plan to play for a long time.

Because the interface is so clunky and user-UNfriendly that it's impossible for a layman like me to even start creating something.  Tasks that you could accomplish in one screen in RPG Maker 1 now requires two, three, even four separate steps to accomplish, requiring that you save your work, leave to the main menu, then open another screen each time.  The instruction manual is useless because it's practically in another language, and even buying the strategy guide didn't help.  This is definitely NOT a pick up-and-play game.

title: A nice stick if you hate fighting games
text:
I purchased this stick with the knowledge that while it wouldn't set the world on fire, it WOULD be a nice introductory arcade stick for a player looking to transition from a gamepad. Imagine my shock when the old adage rung true: you get what you pay for.

The stick itself is awful. The four main directions read almost instantly with just a slight touch, while the diagonals will only read if you push the stick to the absolute farthest corner of the square gate. This means if you want to do a quarter circle during an actual match (when you're inputting the commands a lot faster), you need to push the stick to the bottom corner, then forward, because before you even reach the corner, the controller will think you're already pressing down. But if you, say, try to do a half circle motion quickly, the controller will only register back, down, and forward, with no diagonals. In order for the controller to input ANY motion properly, you need to be insanely deliberate, which isn't very feasible in a match.

The buttons are also abysmal. Buttons should not have input delays this bad. They're cheap, and a real pain to replace.

If you're a beginner to using arcade sticks, this will seriously discourage you from ever trying anything else. Don't buy this and swap the parts; either buy a better stick, or build one yourself. But don't waste $40 that can otherwise go to something that can actually function as intended.

title: Buy this stick, mod it, mod it heavily
text:
I don't have to say much more but I do have to type at least 20 words.

This stick isn't a high quality build. It's not meant to take into a tournament. If you're a casual player and enjoyed playing fighters in the arcade and are getting back into it with the consoles this does support, you can go unmodded.

But not for long. The ability to throw in a Sanwa Stick with an 8 or 4 way gate is just too tempting. The Sanwa Stick costs just about as much as this entire Fighting Stick. The same for a set of 8 buttons. That brings you to potentially still less than a c-note for a custom stick that's supported by several consoles (including Windows PCs).

The price of this stick begs you to crack it open and modify it with a screwdriver, dremel or epoxy. Maybe all three. Break it, buy another one, rebuild it however you like. Add graphics and a layer of acrylic. At this price you should most definitely have fun with it.

The stock stick has a really squirrely stick. The gates are unresponsive and don't give you a satisfying click as you move to a corner. This leaves you with feedback that's just wrong. The buttons are rather soft but don't give you the same feedback as micro-switch buttons do. This is a personal preference thing but the joystick itself is a matter of function.

You need precision and a swift, forceful return to center. You need to feel the gates as you engage every quarter-circle or even just a simple down-forward or down-back. One can live with the stock buttons, but it's hard to even break the stick out without a more responsive joystick.

Update 09/04/14

Finally got around to modding it with a Sanwa JLF Stick and OBSF-30 buttons. Also threw in an 8 way gate. Man, what a difference.

Modding wasn't too difficult. 6 screws and the removal of the rubber feet separate you from the innards of the case. Basically everything went except for the Mayflash mainboard. The removal of old components is easy enough. On this model, the buttons will need a daisy chain common ground. The majority of sticks you can buy are common ground and need to be converted to separate grounds.

The hardest part of the mod was soldering the button connections onto the mainboard. The clearances are really tight, so go light on the solder and try to keep the connections as clean as possible.

The weight of the stick with the new components is just right. The response from the buttons, from the click to the force needed, is perfect. The action of the stick and the 8 way gate, the meaty click of the microswitches, all completely awesome.

I've found that workout gloves help to keep the straps of the resistance band from cutting into your hands and the resistance band itself could be a little more durable (we just bought a replacement; the original one started to rip).

I love the custom workout options. You can create your own total-body workout that works out the physical areas that need the most improvement. Alternatively, you can select a pre-made workout from a list or you can opt into the 30-day challenge and REALLY get serious. Keeping tabs on food and beverage intake, rest time and other forms of exercise helps maintain accountability - even if it's just to a virtual personal trainer!

My advice would be to customize your profile as accurately as possible (weight, height, body shape, etc.) and work out at the hardest level you can. Start on the hardest level and work your way backward. Overall this is a great game and a great workout. Good luck!

title: Great product, with a few caveats.
text:
Note: Rest mode will work with the PS4, but you must power off the console by holding the power button down for 6 seconds, almost like you were going to go into safe mode, but when the console is in rest mode, this will actually turn off the console. Then just turn the PS4 back on and anything that was downloading should either be done or close to done. This will in effect disable Suspend mode though because of powering off the console. I credit Konessha for this information, so look at Konessha's review for more information.

To my review: I had a lot of hassle with this at first because I kept having to backup my data multiple times, and every time I would restore, it would get to 65 GB before saying that it "could not read the USB storage device". When it finally did restore everything (I had to shorten the description of the backup for this to work, which I learned from a support forum on the Playstation website. Shorten it from 17 or 18 characters to 5 characters. Example: Description says "PS4-700 (06/29/2015)", shorten it to "PS4-7"), I went to play a game that I have a physical copy of, and I got the corrupt data error message. I was mad, but then I found out on a Playstation website forum that the hard drive had to be initialized, so I did that, backing up a few things (P. T. mainly, which still works for me BTW :D) and deactivating my system first. Restored that data, put in the disc, and it works fine now. Redownloaded everything IN REST MODE, read my note if you didn't already, and now everything is all downloaded again after about a couple of days.

Performance: it performs like it should, and it actually doesn't give off too much heat, though maybe I just got lucky with mine. I am using a Seagate 4 TB SSHD, spindle speed 5900 with 64 MB cache, and while the benchmarks for the drive are average to subpar in most categories, this drive actually performs its best when running games (source from hardware.info, link: us.hardware.info/reviews/5313/seagate-desktop-sshd-4tb-review-the-ultimate-hard-drive, go to the PCMark7 and PCMark8 scores pages). The games load up faster in my opinion vs. the 1 TB 2.5 inch SSHD from Seagate that I had installed prior, and the spindle rate was 5400 RPM so just so, and I have not encountered any problems while using the Data Bank with this hard drive. It runs quietly, and so much so that even getting close to the system I can just barely hear it. It gets warm, but that's how it should get. It doesn't get hot, and it has no problems maintaining a running state for long periods of time.

I think the reason why people may run into problems with this product is because of the fact that Nyko in its early days did not have well functioning products. They have gotten better in recent years though, but people will still hate on Nyko anyways, and that's fine if they want to. Nyko's most recent failed product was a battery for the Wii U Gamepad I believe, and that was because they reversed the polarity on the connection, which would cause the battery to not generate enough power to the gamepad. There were people that did get it to work, and those people reported excellent battery life with the gamepad as opposed to the stock battery. Case in point, some Nyko products may require a little tinkering before they will work.

Summary: There will be a few steps people will need to take before this will work properly, but once those steps are taken this works like a charm, so for those that have a little patience, this will not disappoint. Four stars though because of the hassle I went through with my games, though I was still able to save P. T., and play it! :D

title: BE WARNED: Terrible value for $360
text:
Why $360 and not $60? Because the game is effectively good for one person per console, so if you expect to get the full experience of the game (which I'm sure you do), you'll need to buy one Switch per player. Yup, one Switch per player. For some god awful reason, Nintendo decided it was reasonable to ship the game in a state where only user per Switch gets to play the full game.

Don't want to shell out $300 for another Switch per player? Then you can look forward to being constantly gated by the primary player's progress at every turn, having zero role in building out your island and its residents, sharing limited island resources, missing all the major story moments (unless you use the equally awful local coop mode, more on that below) and their rewards, and having to buy all the tools and recipes the primary player gets for free.

Planning on only playing together using local coop? That helps with not missing out on the story beats, but expect all but the "leader" player to be little more than a glorified spectator. "Follower" players cannot talk to villagers, access their inventory, pick things up without a long animation for each item, choose where to go, enter/exit buildings, use the tool belt, and worst of all: only the leader will receive any of the quest rewards or world drops.The game still gets a two star from as I'm sure playing as the primary or sole player is still very fun.

title: Challenging and Fun with a Few Kinks
text:
A little bit about me: I'm 28, a woman, and out of shape (like 30% over my ideal weight). I used to play sports and be in great shape, but then I got married five years ago and had my first baby in September. I'm just now getting back into an exercise routine that doesn't involve taking my baby on walks. I've tried the game once for almost two hours. I know it helps me to know a little bit about the person reviewing to see if their review applies to me, so I'll just tell you that if you're in great shape right now, my review doesn't apply to you.

Pros:
*Good tutorials.
*A LOT of workout routine options, including a 30-day challenge and custom workouts you make yourself from the different exercises available in the categories of cardio, upper body, lower body and sports.
*Sports options (basketball--shooting and passing; volleyball--serve, bump, set, block; tennis; boxing--targets and heavy bag). Movements for these are fairly comparable to actually the skills of the sport (at least for basketball and volleyball, which I used to play).
*Cardio, upper and lower body targeted exercises.
*It estimates the Calories the routine will burn for you.
*Goals with time-limits which keep you motivated to want to get on again (only being very sore is keeping me off).
*You can uncheck exercises in the routine that you don't want to do and it shows how your Calorie burn will be affected.
*It tracks your workout times, total Calories burned, etc. for you. Supposedly, you can add in other activities that you do outside of the game and it will track it for you.
*Overall, pretty fun for something that's sole purpose is working out, though there is only so fun a workout game can be.

Cons:
*Leg strap doesn't stay on me well. I've tried several locations and tightnesses and it seems to slip eventually no matter what I do. When it slips and I have to adjust it, it interrupts the workout and the personal trainer starts nagging me that I'm doing the exercises wrong. Maybe trying a different pair of pants or shorts will help. Also, my husband has huge (muscular) quads and his barely fits. They give you an extra piece to adjust it smaller, but not bigger.
*Lower body exercises are NOT good for people with bad joints (in my case knees and ankles). I haven't tried the "low impact" options though, so maybe they have some better exercises?
*Some routines really overdo it. I killed my quads and knees the first day because the toning circuit had so many lunges and squats. Immediately after that, I tried the one of the sports workouts and had no problem with that.
*I would prefer the option to actually play the sports in a non-workout option. I can always switch to Wii Sports for that, but it doesn't have basketball or volleyball, which are my two favorite sports to play.
*I wish it guided you through some stretches at the beginning and end of the workout. It has warmups, but I kept expecting it to do stretches not realizing I should have done them myself first.

Overall: Pretty good game and worth it for me to get, since with an eight-month-old, I don't get a lot of activity that isn't walking and playing with her. For the price of Wii Fit (which I don't have and have never played), we were able to get the game and an extra accessory set for my husband to play with me. I really do feel worked out (read: very sore) and think I will actually be able to start getting in shape with this in my home until my little one is mobile and I can be more active with her.

title: Only a few flaws.
text:
This is an edit of a review I made in August 2020. I saved up for months to buy a Switch Lite just to get this game. I played New Leaf for 7 years and I loved it. For a while after I bought it I was frustrated with this game, but after all the updates, I'm satisfied. There's only a few minor problems with this game.

PROS
-This game is obviously GORGEOUS. I actually gasped when I saw the water.
-You can customize your appearance right away. I'm pretty sure you can change your gender any time too if you're into that.
-You can choose where villagers and projects go, and eventually place pathways and change the environment of your island.
-There's more choice over which villagers move into your town.
-It carries on features of New Leaf like swimming and custom designs.
-The holidays are soooo cute and fun!

CONS
-Some options are based on whether you paid for internet. No, not the internet you already pay for monthly. NINTENDO'S internet. Oh, you wanted to play with your friends in self-isolation for free like you could with EVERY OTHER SYSTEM? Too bad. Local only.
-The villagers' dialogue does not vary much.
-Speaking of which, you can't change their catchphrase, as far as I know. They also don't give you cute little requests. They just waddle around.
-There's nowhere to go. Just your island and the randomly generated ones.
-I personally think the hourly music is weird and a little annoying, but the holiday, shop, and K.K. Slider music are all the same as New Leaf.
-IT WAS OVER SIXTY MC-FREAKIN' DOLLARS.

In summary, if you can afford it and you liked New Leaf, go ahead! It probably will be years until the price goes down, though.

title: Not a 2 player game!!
text: I have been a fan of the Animal Crossing series for a long time and was excited to play to this game with my boyfriend.  Unfortunately, if you plan to play this game with someone else on the same Switch console, you will be quite disappointed to find that you are only allowed to create one island per console and only the player who first created the island will let allowed to access many features of the game.  For example, only the "Resident Representative", the first player, is allowed to select plots for new homes and buildings, get the DIY recipes to build the furniture for those buildings, or set up municipal structures such as bridges.  This creates an entirely different game for later players, who are basically just living on Player One's world with no way to help develop the island or progress the game.  Multiple players can play on the same Switch at once ("couch co-op"), but it is very frustrating for all who are not the the "Leader" because it is difficult to access your inventory to use tools or collect resources.  You can also visit other players' islands, but only via the paid Nintendo Switch Online subscription.  Even so, online play is tedious if many players are trying to join a single island as the game continually interrupts your play to display players comings and goings.  Overall, the game is a test of patience.  This game doesn't stand up to previous AC console titles and is, instead, basically a handheld game intended for a single player on a $400 console.

title: Nice alternative workout, even for a lefty
text:
Active is fun, every day is different and presents a new challenge. I really wanted to write a review because I'm left handed and I thought I would share my experience.

There is no way to make your character left handed. It takes some getting used to but this is a game, not an actual sporting event. Keep your eye on the ball and get used to the timing and even lefties can play. I do almost every exerise as a righty. Most exericises are squats, lunges, curls, etc. For those, you just get used to holding the remote in your right hand. The sports are a little different.

Tennis- I hold the remote in my left hand and nunchuck in right. I play back hand as forehand and vice versa. The game doesn't notice. Just keep your eye on the ball and not on your character.

Baseball- Again, I change hands and batting stance and keep my eye on the ball and it works. Pitching too!

Volleyball-I keep the right handed setup. Everything except serving is the same on both sides. I just am not very good a serving. . .yet.

Basketball-Just like volleyball. If you want to shoot like a lefty, the game doesn't notice with the right handed setup.

Boxing-I keep the righthanded setup.

You might want a stronger resistance band, it's pretty weak. If you are in great shape, this probably won't be a challenge. If you are in okay shape, you'll still end up sweating.

title: Another Animal Crossing game with vast improvements over it's predecessors!
text:
Firstly, You can only have one island per console. If that bothers you, Animal Crossing isn't the series for you. Animal Crossing has always been this way since Game Cube, Wii, DS and 3DS versions. You always got the one village/island and had to share it or have another console.
That being said, this version is loads better than earlier versions! There are events that unfold with updates! You can host a party online for up to ten people! You can terraform on your island and move buildings. You can build bridges!! Expanding your house is easier! It's so much nicer to be able to trade items with friends. You can easily switch your look or gender at any time!!! The new DIY recipes give you something to do and collect in between events! Flower breeding is back, of course, and this time there's more flower breeds! If you happen to have Amiibo cards from Happy Home Designer and Animal Crossing New Leaf Welcome Amiibo you can USE THOSE CARDS to invite specific animals (invite them 3 days in a row) and they can move onto your island!
The new graphics are gorgeous! The museum is so beautiful and peaceful. The island itself is fun to watch transform from a wild forest to something more like a small town that you create!
Basically, this is a MUST BUY for fans for Animal Crossing or anyone who wants to take some time to relax and do some daily tasks to build up a little island with some animal friends.
If you like to collect and trade, this game is for you.
If you like to design outfits and living spaces, this game is for you.
If you just want to have fun fishing or catching bugs, this game is for you.
This game lets you do what you want at your own pace. So take some time and relax on your own island!

title: Heart pumping work out
text:
Wow! This work out game really got me sweating and my heart pumping. I'm doing the 30 day challenge on high-intensity (you can choose if you want high, medium. or low intensity) and it is a good workout. My legs are pretty strong from wii fit, weight training, walking, and biking so I hold up well during the lunges (to my surprise as I don't do many lunges regularly) but the inline skating was intense: you crouch down and jump at the ramps--my legs were burning! The work outs I have done have been about 30 minutes, so easy to fit into the day.
Several reviewers have mentioned that the game sometimes doesn't register them during some of the exercises. I have had this happon but found it was either because I wasn't holding the controllers in the right position or that I wasn't holding still --for some exercises you must hold your position for a second or two.
It is a different type of game than wii fit. As others have mentioned, it doesn't have balance and yoga exercises and not so much for your core as the wii fit does. It isn't as cute as wii fit either (this may be a plus for some, like my husband). EA Sports Active is more like having a personal trainer work with you. The cardio is more intense, there is more upper body work, and the work out is continuous--you move right from one exercise to the next. There are also lifestyle questions to answer each day and a place to add in other activities.

I have not done the custom workouts yet, so can't give any feedback on them.
I like the leg strap with nunchuck as it gives good feedback. I've been thinking that such a device could be fun in a regular video game to give you a workout while dodging fireballs or jumping over obsticle. . .
I'm happy with my purchase and have enjoyed incorporating EA Sports Active into my exercise routine.

title: Not as good as I remember it...
text: I had this game as a kid and recently had nostalgia and ordered a NES and some games.  Karate Champ is a very basic karate game where knocking down the opponent results in a point.  The first one to 2 points wins the next round, and after a few rounds, the difficulty and scenery change.  The fight sequences are usually in what appears to be an outdoor setting.  Graphics are basic, and there are limited kicks and mobility in general.  While it is fun to progress through the levels and play the two-player setting, this game is not one of the best NES games and probably better suited for someone who played the game back in the day (and wants to rehash some memories).

title: I wanted to love you, but probably the best cheap (under $50) NES clone
text:
I truly wanted to love the Gamerz Tek 8-bit HD. I had one a couple years ago, and I wanted to try again in hopes they fixed the abysmal sound that suffers from reversed duty cycles in the cloned CPU. That means certain games sound wrong, like the jumps and coins in any Super Mario game, and in the best case scenarios some games just sound slightly out of tune while also lacking sound depth. The video on the other hand is pretty good. While the color palette is off, the HDMI visuals are sharp, the colors vibrant, and it produces an overall very clean image. I would have been really happy even while not color perfect if the sound complemented the really clean visuals. Even the composite video is really nice while outputting to a CRT/tube TV's. Input lag is a thing unfortunately while using the HDMI port, it's just off and you can certainly feel it. Oddly enough, I couldn't really detect input lag while using a CRT over composite, so there must be some odd processing going on as the image is processed for HDMI. So, since the whole point of this is a plug and play HDMI solution for modern televisions for most people, input lag will really kill your experience. If you wonder why you aren't doing as well as you remembered playing Mario, it actually may not because of you not playing it for a while, its the lag over HDMI. There seems to be a perceptible delay when you press a button to when an action happens on the screen. The controllers are awesome. They just are. I wish the cord was a little longer (I think they're 5FT), they just work well, but buttons responsive, and they are comfortable. The controllers are the best part of the package and since there are 2 of them, I don't feel as bad as I would have otherwise.

Bottom line: I use the controllers on my real NES. The 8-bit HD is Ok. For someone looking for a cheap NES in a box that is plug and play, it's Ok. You'll be disappointed if you want to do any real action gaming on this thing, but for simple games that don't rely on twitch mechanics, it's fine. A real NES will always be better for most people that want to actually experience what they remembered growing up if your TV has a composite input and of course there are more expensive solutions available or devices called scalers that will help convert a composite signal to a more modern HDMI output. Just be careful with those however because cheap scalers can also add input lag, but at the very least you'll have accurate colors and sound.

title: More intense than Wii Fit
text:
I am doing the 30-day Challenge program and when I select moderate intensity in the using settings, I am getting wrung out in about 20 minutes. All in all, I'm on my fifth workout day.

What the 30 Day Challenge does well is to move you through a cross-fit like cycle of alternating lower and upper body exercises. The AI, while not perfect, was good enough to get me to do the exercises you need to do but often will skip on your own (lunges, running fast enough to move your heart-rate to 130 bpm).

Yes, the included stretch band does not provide any significant resistance, so I went over to the local Sports Authority and bought another one from SPRI for less than 10 bucks. On lower-body days, I often do a second sports workout (boxing, basketball, and baseball) just to keep moving for an extra 20 minutes.

The main benefit is getting a balanced workout at home with the time savings of not having to go to a gym or wait for the equipment you want to use. Great for people who do not want to get outdoors during the winter.

text:
The Return of The King is based on one of the most magical worlds ever created , the first two installemnt of the movie series were a hit with the final installment approaching with a promise of never before seen experience , and as we all feel that the third installment will be better,bigger and more dark than the first and second installemnt , also the Rotk game promises the same....and more .
The two towers game was a very good game which only suffered from longevity issue , i have felt that the game should have been more long and also the AI and the controllers should have been more easy and accurate , and fortunately the Development team at EA Redwood Shores knows what they will do this time .
The first improvement here is the execellent capturing of the cinematic charcters , and i don't mean only in the graphics terms , but also in their behaviour,actions and even the way they are walking , so you should feel the aggressive and conidence way in the behaviour of somecharcters while you find the contrary in the Hobbits behaviour , also the enemies are more powerful and intelligent than before , the AI is more aggressive and smart , so you may find the attack coming from all the directions instead of a bunch of orcs waiting in a line for thei turn to hit you .
Another important elemnt has been added , which is the stealth element , you know that Frodo and Sam are taking their dark journey alone , and they are 2 frightened hobbits so how they will evade all the orcs in the way? so you have to be careful and implement all of your stealth capabilities , and that is helped by the improved attack system where you can use the analog stick for aiming your fists or weapons which gives more accurate targeting , and that is necessary due to the enhanced AI so you can beat the hords of the enemies more effecient .
The game will be more long than The Two Towers with two separate paths to take , the playable charcters features the same of the previous game's charcters along with six unlockable chacters , and that also adds one more great addition in this game which is the CO-OP mode which enables you to team with another player to invade the dark lands of the LOTR world , the playing process will be on the same screen not on two split screens which may means that there is a very reat difficulties out there to overcome .
The overall gameplay is more powerful and enjoyable , along with the stunning look of the graphics and the characters animations , so be ready to take the dark paths to face the ultimate explosive finale .

title: Fun, But Sometimes Difficult
text:
Let me start by saying that I'm a HUGE LOTR fan, and so of course I had to get the video game. I wasn't disappointed, for the most part. You can play as 5 charcters: Gandalf, Aragorn, Legolas, Gimli, and Sam. 4 more are unlocked after you beat the game. There are 3 paths to choose from: the wizards path(Gandalf), the path of the king (Aragorn, Legolas, and Gimli), and the path of the hobbits (Frodo and Sam). Also has clips from the movies as an introdction to most of the levels. There are several pros and cons to this game:

Pros:

- Awesome, realistic graphics. Return of the King by far has the best in the series.

- Smooth movement. Every movement and attack is super realistic and super smooth...just like watching the movie.

- Plenty of locations from the movie to play in.

- Allows you play with a friend in co-op mode. The best part about that is there's no more split screens- just one big screen.

- After you beat the game you unlock several secret characters (Merry, Pippin, Frodo, and Faramir), along with interviews of some of the acters from the movies. But the big bonus to me are the codes they give you. After you punch in those codes, the game is all too easy.

Cons:

- Some of the levels are just too darn hard, even when you have the game difficulty set to easy. It took me a couple trys on some of the levels to get past them.

- The introductions to the levels are too long. They include clips from the movie before almost all of the levels, and after you've already seen them it gets annoying. However, you can just skip them by pressing X if you've already beaten that level.

- After you've beaten the game, there's not much to do except endlessly slay orcs and men.

Overall, if you enjoy fighting games, then this is for you. If you're a diehard fan of LOTR, this is for you. If you're neither, then I'd rent it first, and if you fall madly in love with it, get it.

** Select Codes**

While playing, press start. Hold down the L1, L2, R1, and R2 buttons at the same time while punching in these letters. You'll hear a confirmation sound every time you've correctly entered a code:

Unlock Faramir: X,X,triangle,triangle

Unlock Frodo: triangle,circle,circle,circle

Unlock Merry: X,down,down,X

Unlock Pippin: triangle,circle,X,circle (this one won't work for me sometimes)

The following codes are character specific; enter the code that corresponds to the character you're conrolling:

+ 1000 experience points:

Aragorn: up,square,triangle,X

Faramir: square,triangle,up,square

Frodo: down,triangle,up,down

Gandalf: circle,triangle,up,down

Gimli: circle,circle,triangle,X

Legolas: X,triangle,up,X

Merry: down,down,square,X

Pippin: triangle,X,square,X

Sam: triangle,X,down,X

I absolutely love this game! I originally bought it because i was getting tired of the same old treadmill routine every day and wanted something that would switch it up. Here are some of the other things i really liked about the game:

1.) You don't need to have a balance board to use this game! - One of the reasons i had been turned off from getting the wii fit was because of the balance board. it might just be my stubbornness but i had a real issue with spending $50 on a agame and then dropping more money on top of that for a balance board. 2.) 30 day challenge. - I really am finding the 30 day challenge useful. One of the reasons i wanted to get a more interactive game is because i had plateaud just running on the treadmill at the gym. i knew i had to switch up my workouts but i didnt know how. The only thing i dont like about the game is that sometimes the remotes can be picky sensing movements.

title: It's the only game I play now
text:
I previously owned March Madness 2005 and Hoops 2K8, both for PS2. I know there are a lot of die hard 2K fans, but I really like the EA games better. In fact, I preferred MM 2005 over 2K8. I thought MM 2005 had a better "floor" angle camera which made me feel like I was in the game. 2K8 players seemed too shiny and the crowd noise bothered me as it seemed like it played in a constant loop with an annoying whistle.

That said, NCAA basketball 10 is a huge improvement over both of those games. First off, the graphics are much better, which should be a given since we're comparing PS2 vs. PS3. There are a lot of little cool features that are at least new to me since I haven't bought the EA version of the game since 2005:
-Real schedules (dynamic update required)
-Live scores and ESPN radio at the main menu. This seems to udpate several times per day.
-Real weather updates from your favorite school
-Easily download the rosters of real players names and the announcers will say SOME of the player's last names during the game

I really enjoyed the dynasty mode in MM 2005, but never got into it in 2K8. There doesn't seem to be that many improvements to the dynasty mode in 2010, but that doesn't bother me as much because I really enjoy online matches. Playing against real opponents is much more fun than playing agains the AI computer. Online games are generally fast (80% of the time), but once in awhile you'll get a choppy connection. It is fairly easy to find an opponent if you select "Play Now". Finding opponents to play in the lobbies is much more difficult. Online matches are fun too, because you get ranked compared to all other people.

The only bad part about playing online is 50% of my opponents seem to choose Kentucky, but they are pretty easy to beat if you double-team John Wall (point guard).

As other people have noted, there are some glitches. The one that I've seen the most is there is a bad camera angles that occur every once in awhile for an entire game. The only way to explain it is that the camera is not centered around the ball. For instance, when shooting a free throw, sometimes it shows the players feet, which makes no sense. This happens 1 out of every 20 games or so.

Another glitch is the crowd noise sometimes is really wrong. In a few games, the crowd booed the entire game, even when I was the home team and I was winning.

Other things that could be improved:
-There is no traveling in the game
-There are no "held / jump balls ", even though they have possession arrows
-The auto-subs needs to improve with the default settings (for online play). Michigan State will never sub during a 10-minute half during online play unless someone gets into foul trouble.

Overall, however, this game is a lot of fun and I recommend it if you're into college basketball. It's nice to have an option to not listen to Dick Vitale and choose CBS sports instead.

title: Love Sims, but disappointing expansion pack
text:
I love the Sims franchise and have bought almost all expansion packs from the prior games. Found this one to be terribly disappointing.

It adds mini-games in the form of travel to three locations, with further mini-games there (explore tombs, learn skills, find people). The mini-games are plain, easy, and boring. The tomb exploration is like a badly executed dungeon-crawl game. The rest of the missions are not much more exciting - find this person deliver this thing, etc. Unfortunately, to gain the 'visa level' to do future trips, you have to do all these silly games. The result is that trips are not as fun and open ended as the rest of the game. The best expansion packs were always those that were open ended but added fun new features - like Sims 2 Nightlife or Sims 1 Makin Magic.

Second complaint is additional content is very sparse for this expansion. And many of the 'extra' features in game play came via a base game update anyway. So, overall the expansion only added a few bad mini-games, and not much else. Hope that's not a trend for future expansion packs.

Third compliant is the bugs/gameplay issues. I had tons of trouble with the game after this installed, a few crashes and one freeze. A few patches later it seemed fixed, but that level of issue was out of character for the usual highly-stable releases that EA has put out in the past. I almost wish I'd never installed, my base game was just fine before the expansion pack.

Overall I'd skip this one, not worth the money and definitely not worth the bugs.

text:
I had the problem spending a lot of money for a larger 2.5 SSHD. I had a 1 TB drive and I somewhat quickly found myself deleting games to make room for newer ones. This wouldn't be a problem if I didn't play most of my games consistently, but I do. On top of that, friends that want to play larger games online like black ops 3 or GTA 5 while you want to keep the games you solo play. I gets annoying having to delete...install the new game and updates.

When I heard about this, it piqued my interest but I was VERY hesitant. Scared of a slower load time, breaking, how does it handle crashes, etc.

After deleting and installing a game for the 30th time, I got tired of it and bit the bullet, researched and took the plunge. Definitely research. The other reviews here are helpful. I got this with the Seagate 4TB Gaming SSHD(Solid State Hybrid Drive) SATA 6Gb/s 64MB Cache 3.5-Inch Internal Bare Drive (ST4000DX001) and it's been a dream. No issues with rest mode. No hiccups and I didn't notice an impact to load times.

Threw my entire collection at it, and I still have 2.6 TB to play with. I would definitely recommend. The install is fairly straight forward. Back up your old drive (including PT if you have it). The initial transfer depending on how much you carry over can take some time but it's a one time thing and worth it.

I've read it works with larger drives but research and see what's best for you.

title: Best Expansion Pack!
text:
This is my favorite Sims EP ever! Maybe I like it better than most because I've always had an interest in history, archaeology, and (especially) Egyptology. I love exploring the various ruins, collecting artifacts, working out the puzzles, and generally living out an Indiana Jones fantasy.

I don't find the game to be any buggier than any of the others. There are two tombs that have spaces that are too narrow for Sims to fit through, but you can either Zeneport around them, give them a skip (they're not crucial areas), or, if you are brave, you can use cheat codes to edit the tomb and fix the issue. The only other "bug" is that there is no maid service at any of the base camps, so there are frequently dirty dishes left out and broken plumbing. I usually go in and add a Bonehilda (from the Supernatural EP) at each base camp and she will keep it clean and repaired.

Some people have complained that you can't live in the country permanently. With a Level 3 visa, the Seasoned Traveler opportunity reward, and a Certificate of Partnership from the special merchant, you can stay for about 3 weeks. I've read that if you are traveling with others who have those things, the time you can stay stacks, so you can conceivably stay there for months. But I think it gets a bit boring after a while, especially if you've done all the adventures and explored the extra tombs. You can't work a job while you're there, for instance, so you can't climb the corporate ladder. The cities are also smaller, so there are fewer Sims to interact with. So while the initial 3 day period feels dreadfully short when you're first exploring, you will eventually get enough time there (and have little left to accomplish) that you'll probably find yourself going home early.

And yes, it does take a few thousand simoleons to go on vacation (I think it's 1,800 for a 3-day trip, plus you will need to buy a few hundred simoleons worth of supplies before going into any of the tombs: food, tent, and shower in a can). But I always make my money back (and usually much more) by completing adventures and collecting metals and gems along the way (not to mention artifacts, but I usually horde those or set up a museum for them in my home town). For instance, if someone tells you to bring them back two pieces of metal or gems, the map will show you the locations of a bunch of it. Pick up everything you can find--maybe even wait a game day and let everything respawn; you'll deliver the couple of pieces that are needed for the adventure and pocket the rest as easy money. So, as soon as you have 2,400 simoleons, go on vacation. You'll come back richer than when you left!

title: Probably not for everyone
text:
Many aspects of this game are fun at first and I had a couple of months of playing here and there, sadly I've hit a plateau in the game play. This is the second AC game I've purchased, and the first I've spent more than a few hours on. I gave this game a chance due to the excellent reputation of the series. There is a lot of stuff that's good about this, it looks charming, it's easy to play, and it's serene in it's lack of any kind of pressure to perform pretty much any in game task. It can be relaxing to play, but I've gotten to a point where it's too repetitive. For the past week I've just loaded the game just to check turnip prices.

Pretty quickly you learn the interaction with your fellow animal villagers is extremely limited. It's one thing for a game to rely on self motivation, but there is very little incentive to keep playing, or even to use the limited set of tools available to decorate/terraform the island. Once a certain goal is met and credits roll, there is no driving force to move forward, despite most of the collectibles still out there to collect. After numerous Ubisoft games over the years, I'm no longer motivated to collect items for the sake of collecting items. It could be I just need to take a break for a few weeks, maybe when the seasons change in game things will draw me back. I bought on the eShop so I'm obviously stuck with it at this point. The addition of summer activities helped, so maybe more features are forthcoming, all I can say is right now it feels more like a chore that's keeping me from finishing the superlative Bug Fables, which I've been playing after I complete the daily grind in AC.

Bottom line: maybe this isn't suited for me. The crafting system isn't deep enough, and I can't say I've come to find the process of grinding to collect fish/bugs/etc to sell for bells to buy more stuff to decorate my in game house or island particularly compelling. In the end I'd rather play something with a story/goals, more varied interactions with NPC's, or more varied environments.

text:
This item was purchased for my game console largely because my flat-screen TV had no S-Video plug and I had to deal with the lower quality of the composite video cable it came with inbox for years. title: Sports Active just got better
text:
I bought the first EA Sports Active game for my wife and I as I was a little bored with the fitness games that we had already. We started with Wii Fit, progressed to My Fitness Coach and then Cardio Workout.

Each of these programs were a good workout but with Wii Fit there was very little to get the heart pumping. My Fitness Coach certainly got your heart pumping more but with a limited amount of space it was hard to do some of the step aerobics, in the end I had to modify the routines. With Cardio Workout it was a great little program for getting the heart rate up but I wanted to move a bit more.

EA Sports Active came along and my wife and I were taken with the program. We stuck to the challenges and saw a noticeable change in our bodies. With My Fitness Coach we were doing the routines and felt fitter but I felt that I was doing the routines in the wrong position because my knees would ache and it was difficult to bend down and in my job I did that a lot.

The only downside I could really see was that with EA Sports Active I would be too competitive with my wife. We did a joint workout once and when we were running around the track I was in the lead. My competative streak got to me and I tried to run faster - of course something happened and I pulled a muscle in my calf. We laughed about it later but it hurt like crazy.

When I saw Ea Sports Active More Workouts coming out I was thrilled and hoped to get it straight away. I thought as the original game was so well made then I could expect the same quality from the new game. I'm happy to say I was proved right!

EA have taken the original game and tweaked the workouts so that they are a little different but they have kept the core exercise routines and made them more fun. In the original game my wife and I hated the fast kick ups and high knees, now they have changed them slightly and although it's not my favourite it is a little better and doesn't feel as much as a chore.

They've now added water skiing which is a good game involving squats. The band work has been tweaked a little and is a little more of a challenge. In the previous game I had already bought the purple and silver band to add more resistance but I find myself going back to the purple a little more while I find my feet with the new exercises.

The main reason I'm writing this review is that I discovered 2 days ago the custom workout option. Okay, I knew about this already but this was the first time I had set one up in the new game. I had just tried the step aerobics in my daily workout and I was thrilled! This was the step workout that Wii Fit and My Fitness Coach needed in my opinion. The tempo is fast and even not using a step you had a great workout. Along with the basic step you had kicks, high knees and leg curls all with single or sets. I also included a hard squash game which really made me fly from side to side with my lunges, the pace gradually got faster until you got to the bonus balls where I struggled to keep up, I managed to get 7 out of 10. I also included skipping, I haven't skipped since I was a child so that was a little hard to start with but now I think I could keep pace with a boxer! The final item in my routine was the boxing where the target scroll down the screen and you have to jap and hook to hit them.

I tried this routine which was to take about 24 minutes to complete. I kept on saying wow as I progressed and hit 100 calories during the 10 step routine before I had even finished it. As I had said with the squash it certainly has you moving to the left and right as you need to lunge for the balls. The boxing was great as I tried to hit all the targets. after the 24 minutes were up I could hardly believe that according to the program I had burned almost 100 calories more than it estimated I would. I don't know if the calorie count is accurate but that was such a great morivating factor that I couldn't stop telling my wife when she came downstairs. She tried the workout last night and she was thrilled and could really feel it.

At this moment in time I would have to say that Ea Sports Active More Workouts is a great game to get as it's taken what was good in the original game and made it better. I was blown away by the step aerobic program. Okay it doesn't have the more advanced step aerobic exercise in My Fitness Coach or the cute graphics in Wii Fit but the tempo is great and the time just flies by. My wife and I liked the tennis but you just stood to one side and tried to hit the ball on the same side - which was okay. The squash game is so much better in that you move more and is so much fun. The boxing is better, I like the targets that scroll down, my wife prefers the sparring partner where you also have to duck and dodge just like in Cardio Workout.

I'm concentrating on the items I love in this workout but there are more. My wife likes the island runs where you have an obstacle coarse where you can do lunges, stride jumps, hand cranks, hops on either foot. There's also a run where you have to sprint past runners before you reach the finishing line. I'm still undecided about the push ups and the abdominal exercises such as reverse crunches and punches but I'm sure I'll get to like them when I do have abdominal muscles!

One of the things I've often said to my wife was that I would like a fitness program that I would like. I said of Wii Fit that it was fine but I wanted a step program that challenged me and that I could fall in love with - I think I've found it now. I feel confident that I will continue to use this program for a long time. So far my wife has spent 70 hours using the original EA Sports Active and has burned over 50,000 calories. I can now imagine that I will be spending longer on this program as I'm so pumped up with the step program. My wife loves this program as she can carry her information from the original to the new program and she has more choices of exercise.

In conclusion if you love the original Ea Sports Active I would seriously consider buying this one too. The games are inproved over the original and in my opinion it's worth it for the step aerobics,boxing and the squash!

title: Good with some tweaking
text:
Pros:

Easy to use. I recommend doing the 30 day challenge to familiarize yourself with the various exercises available with the game.

Easy to create you own customized workout. I did this after completing the 30 day challenge, once I figured out what I liked/didn't like.

Wide variety of pre-canned workout routines. What is really nice is the variety, both in terms of length, intensity and focus (i.e. you can do low impact, upper body, lower body, etc etc).

Cons:

Doesn't pick up your movements, with certain exercises in particular. Like bicep curls - I curl, I wait and after holding your hand in the curl position, it is still not picking up the fact you are doing it right. Additionally, once it thinks you are doing the exercise wrong it can take a LONG time for it to determine that you have actually corrected your position.

Workaround: just finish the exercise without paying attention to the screen and select SKIP. You can skip an exercise by pushing the + and selecting skip.

Annoying trainer 'encouragement' and criticism. The criticism is particularly annoying when you are actually doing the exercise correctly.

Workaround: put the TV on mute and put on your own music. After you've completed the 30 day challenge you really don't need the trainer tips anymore and your own music will be far preferable to the rather boring music that comes with the game. Best of all - no annoying trainer dialog!!

Leg strap is somewhat uncomfortable. Unless you really cinch it tight, it falls off when running.

Workaround: put the nunchuck down your pants! I know this sounds stupid, but if you are wearing legging type workout bottoms, just put the nunchuk on your leg under the pant. It is far more comfortable.

Resistance band - offers almost no resistance.

Workaround: buy better resistance bands. Then buy a couple of carabiners and connect the handles that come with the game to your purchased resistance bands. Reason being, it is extremely awkward to hold the wii remote and nunchuk with the plastic tubing that comes on most resistance bands but if you attach the handles that came with the game, it is much more comfortable. Still not great - I still find it a bit uncomfortable to deal with the remotes plus resistance bands.

title: Easy is NOT easy
text:
I bought this workout game because I couldn't find Wii Fit Plus with the Balance Board. As others have said, this game definitely will give you a workout. However, there are two major things that detract from it, in my opinion.

1. The Easy workout is not easy. I am not in stellar shape but I'm not a total slob either. I cannot do the Easy workout without cheating. Basically, doing all the squats and lunges is WAY too much for my legs. The game just starts right in with something like 20 squats for a warm up. I'm lucky to do 20 squats period. Even with cheating, holding a chair so I could go all the way down for the squats, I started to cramp up bad half way through the workout. I couldn't complete the EASY workout. So, I'm just telling those of you that are really out of shape that you might have some trouble keeping up with this one because there really isn't a gradual way to get into the workouts unless you completely leave out a step.

2. The whole switching the nun-chuck in and out of the leg strap is annoying to say the least. The 20 minute workout will take you 40 minutes because you have to switch the nun-chuck after just about every workout. If the leg strap had an easier method of securing the nun-chuck other than cramming it into an undersized pouch, then it might be ok. However, the pouch on the leg strap is so small that I'm afraid that the nun-chuck will break one of these times.

So, if you are already in really good shape and just looking at a home workout game to fill in the gaps, then this is for you (as long as you can stand the whole nun-chuck thing).

title: A good addition to your workout routine
text:
I caved to internet peer pressure and picked up a copy of EA Sports Active. I was getting a little bored with Wii Fit, and sort of annoyed that it takes you 45 minutes to get in 30 minutes of exercise because you have to pick a new task each time... you can't just queue up a workout.

Plus I wanted to see if it lived up to the hype.

So far Sports Active is being touted as THE MOST AMAZING EXERCISE GAME. As of this morning 100% of its reviews on Amazon were 5 star.

The game starts off like pretty much every other workout video/ad/pitch you've ever seen. Some guy in a fleece vest starts telling you how awesome and perfect your life will be once you follow him and stop being such a pathetic lump. There's some upbeat ambient music to emphasize this point. It's cheesy but inoffensive.

I started the 30 day fitness challenge because it required the least amount of thought. Over a 30 day period the game picks workouts for you each day, mixing it up and making sure you're getting an even workout. If you don't feel like doing that you can do any of the dozens of pre-programmed workouts or build your own. But, I'm lazy. If I wasn't lazy I wouldn't have bought an exercise video game, now would I?

After day 1 I'll concede that it's a strong title for the Wii exercise genre, and fills some voids Wii Fit left behind, but I'm not sure it's my new religion. I had trouble getting some of the exercises to register - particularly the lunges. Overall things seemed a little sluggish - my avatar would follow me about 2 seconds behind. The balance board didn't bring much to the experience, and I'll probably leave it out next time just because it was one more thing I kept having to bring out / push out of the way.

The exercises themselves were pretty good, and things changed up pretty quickly so I didn't have time to get bored... which was nice. I've had a hard time motivating myself to do 10 minutes of WiiFit hula hooping now that my boyfriend isn't around to appreciate the effort. I worked up a sweat, although it didn't leave me exhausted the way other games like DDR do. Maybe that's a good thing?

My biggest beef is that it felt cumbersome to switch back and forth between all the gear. Nunchuck in leg strap. Nunchuck in hand. Get on the wii balance board. No, with the nunchuck in the strap. Now stand on the resistance band. Oh but holding the nunchuck this time. Yeah.

It's a title worth picking up if you want to add something to your exercise routine but don't actually want to join a gym / go outside. Also it tells you how many calories you've (theoretically) burned, and that's a lot like points. And I'm a sucker for points.

title: The Good and the Bad
text:
This game is great for people that are driven by visual feedback of progress and avoid gyms.

When I work out with my free weights I see results over a long period of time and it is hard to tell how close I am getting to my goal. The fact that I can see the progress on the screen drives me to work harder. This game is a great alternative for people that don't like going to the gym. I don't like people seeing me strain to push a few more reps out or drenched after running for an hour.

To make it simple.

Good: Visual tracking, journal and encouragement to make sure you are on track, privacy, invent your own workout, makes working out fun and addictive, creates a desire to work harder through achievement trophies, and you can workout with a friend.

Bad: Band broke on the first day, trouble tracking movements from time to time, cord gets in the way during workout (this is more of a Nintendo issue... make a wireless nunchuck without lag please), and that is the few things that upset me.

The band is no big deal. I did not plan to use it because I could tell it was not going to be enough resistance.
Just get a few different strap weights for your wrists and ankles and you will get a lot more from the workouts.
I don't recommend heavy weights on the boxing, I almost ended up with a burn on my wrists from throwing so many punches and having the fabric rub the skin right off. When the system does not track your movement smoothly, it will sometimes have you holding the weights up for a second or two longer. This will frustrate some people, for me, I looked at it as getting more out of that one rep.

To sum it up, if you like privacy and a fun workout that pushes you to go further, then this is a good choice.
If you are easily frustrated, then you might not like this.

And Nintendo... get on that wireless nunchuck design. ;)

title: Lots to Explore and Do
text:
I have really enjoyed The Sims 3 World Adventures. Unlike the vacation expansion for The Sims 2 this EP has a lot more to do once you get to your destination.

You still have the option to just hang out and get to know the locals and pick up rocks, fish or find new plants and so on but, if you pick up the quest like story line, you also have the ability to go on mini adventures touring hidden tombs and catacombs while solving mini puzzles to get through them.

These quests and the limited time you initially have at your vacation destination (3 days- more as you build your visa points) makes you want to go back for more. I feel as though I am getting a lot more from my vacation (and consequently the EP)than I ever did with the Sims 2 EP. I also liked how they have opportunities in the regular world that lead you to the vacation spots available.

All in all, a respectable and enjoyable EP.

title: Great controller if your not a pro Fighter player.
text: This is not a super high end controller but it works great for things like MAME arcade games.  It's feels far more authentic than using a 360 or ps2 controller.  For Fighting games it works but I'm sure there's better out there.  They'll most definately cost more though.  I can use this controller with Street Fighter IV without issues or additional software or adapters but this controller doesn't work with Street Fighter V out of the box.  You either have to use a software button mapper or (I recommend) a PS2 to XBOX 360 controller adapter.  The second option requires very little setup of the controller but adds about $20 to the cost of the controller. It's worth it though to not have to deal with the legacy (like windows 95 legacy) direct input controller setup.  The joystick switches are clicky and movements are loose but not so much so that its sloppy.  The button presses are soft but you can definatley tell they've been pressed.  I've watched videos of people modding the controller buttons to authentic Sanwa arcade buttons.  It's quite a bit of work for a $30-$40 controller.  If your buying this to mod it, I'd recommend just buying a better controller.  It's a lot of work and the build quality of the rest of the controller doesn't justify this type of mod and it's a fairly complicated mod.  The buttons aren't the same size as Sanwa buttons and the button holes in the enclosure need to be filed to a slightly larger size.  If you like messing around, go for it.  Everyone else should either accept what this controller is or move up to something nicer.  Overall I'm happy with my purchase.  It's a good value for an arcade stick and works reasonably well

text:
I was very excited about this when I first heard about it but the actual product leaves me disappointed. Aesthetically, it looks like it was made for the console but the instructions aren't that great, zero troubleshooting incase your hard drive doesn't work. The power cord should've come with its own separate plug in instead pulling from ps4 cord.
I tried several different hard drives and got the same result from each one. The 3.5 drive wouldn't even spin up and the ps4 would know the hard drive was there but it wouldn't format or anything. I tried said hard drive in computer and it worked just fine. So I'm thinking it was faulty a power cord (yes, I had the plug coming from the data bank plugged into the console with ps4 cord plugged in as well.)
I've read success stories about this and it working fine but it hasn't worked for me and honestly wished I had just bought a 2tb 2.5 drive for my ps4 instead of this product. I think with a separate power cord for the data bank itself would be better instead of leeching off the ps4 power cord.

Update: To the error of my own folly, this is a great product. Most of my trouble was getting the Ps4 OS to install. Be sure to download the restore version firmware and not the normal firmware. The restore version will be about 800 mb whereas the normal version will be in between 250-350 mb. I used the restore version and it booted up fine.

title: There is NO ENDING!
text:
I have NEVER felt this betrayed by a video game in a long time. I have been a huge fan of the John Carpenter film THE THING since 1982. Hearing that this game was a direct sequel to the film and having read some favorable reviews, I had high hopes for this game. The game does deliver on many fronts (good story, cool NPC who responded in a realistic manner, great sound, creepy monsters, swearing and the CONTROL THE FEAR feature. On the down side, the game is ridiculously hard at times and can be very frustrating so I recommend using the AUTO AIM feature or you will never make it! which brings me to my BIGGEST gripe of all. After struggling for far to long to beat this game, I get to the final boss monster fight only to have it just end abruptly and cut to the credits! WHERE IS THE ENDING????!!!!!!!!!!! Unbelievable! There is no closure to this thing! (no pun intended) It's like reading a great book only to get to the end of it and you find the final pages have been ripped out! I can't BELIEVE the makers worked so hard to make the game so well in so many areas but could'nt write a simple story segment to finalize the story & justify all the time I just WASTED playing the game??!! AARRGGHH!! Where is my flame thrower so I can melt this damn game and my PS2? I recommend this to HARD CORE THING fans only.
(Ocobter 2007) After I posted the above review, I did replay the end of the game and there WAS and ending cut scene after all! I must've hit a button and skipped over it the first time I played. Now I really like the game and take back my above comments!

title: Not Quite There
text:
I am basically a lazy person looking for a quick way to keep from being a total couch potato. First, let me say that I think this is basically worthwhile but has some definite shortcomings. I plan to keep using it but I just wanted to warn people of its shortcomings:

Too much running. I am a walker and running makes my bones and joints ache. You can opt out of running entirely but then there's no cardio in the workout. My compromise is to walk fast during the running but then I have to put up with the trainer's incessant insistence that I need to keep a faster pace.

The trainer's chatter is repetitive and inane. There has to be more than 10 things that trainers say to encourage or correct. I find myself muttering obscenities at the trainer's voice after a while.

A 20-minute workout takes about 45 minutes because there are so many pauses and show-me-how videos. Even if you skip those videos, it still takes 45 minutes. I don't really know how long it would take if you watched all the videos.

The positioning of the remote and nunchuck are fussy. I have a feeling I'll get better at it as I get used to it but it's more like positioning your hands for ballet than for exercising.

The thigh strap tends to slide off unless I put it on really, really tight.

The low intensity workout is not really low intensity in my opinion. I needed to start out slowly and I couldn't even make it through the first session. I tried again the next day and managed better but I still think it's a little tough for someone just starting out. (I know there are some people who will think I'm just a wuss but I suspect there are many other people out there who feel the same way.)

title: Excellent screen protector
text:
I bought a new 3DS system to play Metroid Returns.

Since this was the Samus edition, with beautiful gold and orange metallic paint, I need to make sure it stays in mint condition so i got a case and this screen protector, because I'm super clumsy.. and paranoid about making scratches with my dishwashing-rough fingertips.

This screen protector is easy to apply with no mess, although it took me two tries. They provide three sets so it's great for trial and error.

1. Just clean the screen with soft cloth provided (i also used wet tissue paper).

2. Protector is sealed with two sides of anti-dust peelers. Peel back 1 side of protector half way, ensure its aligned with screen, peel back the rest and apply, and then remove bubbles with the flat plastic piece also provided. Then just easily peel back second peeler.

3. Repeat for second screen.

Key steps are just wiping off any dust from the screens before application and aligning the protector before removing that first peel.

It's a dream come true, and now I can relive my childhood days of 1987...while the wife is asleep of course =D

title: Great game for ONE player, terrible for multiple
text:
I didn’t purchase this through Amazon, but I’m writing a review here hoping that if enough of us do it, the developers will fix the only issue that causes most of us to take away stars. That issue is the inability to either a) be able to change the resident representative, or b) allow multiple islands on a console. The resident representative is the only person who can make changes to the island and advance the game. For instance, the first bridge that’s built MUST be done by the first person who signs onto the game. You need this bridge to gain villagers and advance. YOU CANNOT CHANGE THIS without wiping the game and starting over, and by the time you realize it, you’ve already invested a lot of time. Since you can’t have an island for each user, every other player is stuck doing nothing important except fixing up their own home and character. I made the mistake of letting my 9 year old daughter sign in first and she finds doing things like gathering materials to build a bridge tedious, so it doesn’t get done or I have to sign in as her and do it. I read the reviews before purchasing and thought, oh, that issue sounds like NBD, but trust me, it’s a real drag and it turns an otherwise excellent game into a 3 star game.

It *is* a fun game, but getting to the finish line is just the start.

title: Getting Active Again
text:
I bought this from Amazon a couple of weeks ago. I am 55 and just beginning a fitness routine after too many years of doing nothing. I received a Wii Fit Plus and enjoy those games, but wanted some diversity, so I bought EAS Active. After experimenting with it for a week, I started their 30 day challenge yesterday. It is much more of an aerobic workout than WFP. The resistance band is good for a beginner (like me) but based on what I have read, it won't last long. Easy enough to replace.

I hated the leg band because it never seems to stay where I want it, and the 30 day challenge makes you put the nunchuck in the pouch, and back out - repeatedly. I sewed a small pocket on the leg of two pairs of bike shorts and it works out much better for me.

This game raises my heart rate and makes me sweat (I am at the lowest level of intensity). I am sure that many people would bump up the intensity and the resistance bands. I hope I get there!

Generally, the directions are easy to follow, but sometimes the signal doesn't seem to transmit properly and it makes you wait until it senses you are in the right position.

Many people will say, "Just go to the gym," or "Go outside and walk." I prefer to exercise at home, in my comfy clothes (or jammies) without having to worry about other people judging me, or bad weather.

EAS Active is a fun way to get moving again, and even though the trainer says really hokey things, the positive reinforcement helps.
