title: By Far the Best Expansion Pack
text:
This Sims 3 expansion pack is by far the best one out of the lot (I own all expansions except "Showtime" and the upcoming expansion "Supernatural").

You have the option of sending your Sim on vacation to three locations: China, France, or Egypt. Each world is highly detailed and contains many adventures and puzzles for your Sims to explore. While on vacation, your Sim has the option to do various "Adventure" tasks which build up their local connections and Visa levels. The three different Visa levels each come with benefits as you increase them, such as the ability to buy rare artifacts that are specific to that respective location, being able to stay longer at each site, or the ability to buy a local vacation home.

Many of the adventures involve exploring hidden tombs and/or searching for treasure. Beware of mummies and booby traps! This is by far the most fun part of this expansion pack. However, once you figure out all the secrets of a particular tomb, that's it, you're done-- I suggest exploring each location at leisure to spread out the fun of the tombs a bit, that way it's not as repetitive once you've gotten through all of the tomb locations.

You can also level up new skills: martial arts in China and nectar-making in France. Plus, every location is intricately designed and absolutely beautiful, especially France. I wish my Sims had the option to live there permanently! I have fun just visiting these locations and exploring the various scenery and marketplaces with my Sim.

This is hands down the best expansion pack of the bunch. If you're debating whether to get it, just go for it! You will have hours of fun in store.

(Also, an interesting tidbit: Fans of the original Sims game will be pleased to discover that some the background music for the France location is taken directly from the Sims Makin' Magic expansion pack. Being a huge fan of the original series, it definitely brought back nostalgic memories! Here's to hoping that the Sims 3 Supernatural expansion is half as good as Makin' Magic.)

title: Great game for those without knee problems
text:
I'm in my 30's and have problems with my knees when I exercise. Unfortunately, this game has lots of lunges, running and jumping, which is really taking a toll on my knees. The worst so far is the lunge-jump-lunge exercise where you have one leg in front and one leg in back in a lunge position. You have to then jump up from that position, switch leg position (like front-back scissors) and land back in a lunge position. Ouch!

I simply can't do some of the lunge exercises so I try to improvise because it does not give me any substitute exercises and I want to try to keep my heartrate up for the entire timespan. When I improvise, my digital trainer tells me I'm just not giving my all, etc. Way to motivate!

I do like the game because of the 30 day challenge - you build on your exercises each day, you do get cardio benefits from this game (which I didn't get with Wii Fit) and its different exercises each day (no boring routines). I also like some of the exercises that feel more like games, like shooting baskets, hitting baseballs and hitting tennis balls.

I've noticed sometimes my online self will move before my real self moves and that's frustrating.

If you are in really good shape already or you have strong, healthy knees, I recommend this game. If you have any sort of knee problem, I'd either borrow a copy and try it out for a few weeks, or steer clear of this game. I haven't used it in three days while my knees recover.

title: Ruined my game!  Saving Error 12, random crashes glitchy!
text:
Ok. The Adventures seems like EAs attempt to bring back an expansion that they already made twice. At least this time they spiced up the "Vacations" a little bit, making it into more of an Adventure.
When you get to either China, Eygpt, or France, you have a Visa (This is a game! Visa's take all the fun out of it...) which makes sure that you can only stay there a certain amount of time (So no living there...).

You can talk to people, but new recipes, explore tombs, collect gems, and of course, take care of your sims moods. This is pretty fun, not as good as some previous Sims expansions (Seasons, Open for Buisness, Vacations, Making Magic ect).

Ok now for why I gave it a one star.

My first adventure to China went glitch free. The next (real life) day, I took a trip to France. One of the sims was sleeping in a tent in the Celtic tomb. The game randomly quit. I had to restart the vacation, and made sure to save it more. It quit again while using that tent. I eventually made it past that part.
Ever since then, I have been having "Error 12" saving bug, that makes saving the game fail, and and sometimes even crash. So this has pretty much ruined my game.

It is NOT just on the new adventure neighborhoods. The glitches happen in the normal town also.

Thank you EA, for making another almost un-playable game!

title: Not a bad controller. Not bad at all.
text:
It took me about an hour to get used to its quirks, but this fight stick has really grown on me. In some ways, it outperforms my $300 Hori, but in other ways, it's clear to see that I'm getting what I paid for.

PROS:
-nice, responsive square gate.
-the joystick feels sturdy and well crafted.
-the buttons have just the right amount of give and resistance.
-the turbo and memory options are a nice (but mostly useless) touch. I'm looking forward to using this for a glorious SHMUP I have packed away somewhere.
-plugs right into my ps3, ready to go.
-can be used on just about any current console, given that you have the right adapter (SERIOUSLY, ALL fight sticks should have this option!!!).
-nice set of rubber feet to keep the stick from sliding around.
-very well constructed case that's just begging to be modded.

CONS:
-this stick is relatively small; the button layout for my right hand is fine, but movements with my left hand inevitably cause the side of my hand to chafe along the uncomfortably sharp edge of the case. A bevel would have been nice... a bevel and about 4 more inches of material added to the left.
-this stick is light and is poorly suited for holding in your lap.
-I didn't have much luck with that driver disk.
-I don't understand why the manufacturer couldn't just include the console adapters in the box. It's not a big name manufacturer so the likelihood of being able to find a GC or XB adapter in 5 years is slim.
-now this might just be me, but I noticed input lag or a complete failure to register input when I first got it. This could be owed to a bad connection as I haven't been able to reproduce this, but it's something to bear in mind.
-this stick is absolutely not going to win any beauty contests.
-This *CLICK, CLICK* fightstick *CLICK, CLICK--CLICK, CLICK, CLICK* is really *CLICK-CLICK, CLICK, CLICK* loud. If you're married, you better have a soundproof man-cave. Try to imagine a beach full of demon crabs mating in the dead of winter. That's what this arcade stick sounds like.

All in all, this is definitely the stick you let your honored guest use when he wants to spar in SF4. If he's your enemy, you let him use your un-modded standard 360 dual analog gamepad.

text: I love this game! In fact I just finished doing a workout on this game.  This game is such an improvement over Wii Fit.  I love the pre-constructed workouts. title: Better than the Wii Fit!
text:
From the first day I tried this product, I was sold. Even after only a twenty-minute workout, I was sweating in my living room! I'm in pretty good shape because my job requires me to pass fitness tests, but I'm a lazy couch potato at heart. Now, I have no excuse to lounge about because this game is right next to the TV remote, reminding me to get up and active.

I love the variety of exercises, and how even if you do multiple repetitions of an exercise, they'll place another exercise in between to mix it up. (I'm on the 30-Day program.) I am the kind of person who loves aerobics/dance classes because of the variety; I often get bored on a treadmill or just lifting weights, losing motivation. The avatar on-screen makes it more interactive to me, and I don't feel like I'm exercising, just playing a game... but feeling the burn!

Now I'm walking around and can actually FEEL in my legs and arms the results of the workout. And for twenty minutes of my day, that's something! Definitely worth the investment; it what the Wii Fit should have been from the start.

title: Seriously EA?
text:
I loved the Sims 2 all the way thru. LOVED IT!!!! The only reason I moved to S3 was for promise of virtually no load screens(a real buzz kill back in the land & times of Sims 2) AND for the added enhancements that surely would come of the newest incarnation. I mean the programmers by this point have had lots of practice right? They know after so many S2 expansions what we'd like- Nay,what we DEMAND from our Sims game, correct? But sadly that has not turned out to be the case. S3 on it's own I find is terribly boring. No pets, no businesses, no seasons, no college, no nightlife to speak of. Not much going on. Just work and school. Heck- there isn't even a drum set or piano to play. Just a dumb guitar. And when they do have a piano- you'll probably have to "purchase" it off the ever dominant online "exchange" with your oh-so-fun "sim points". So EA actually just stripped the game down to the barest of essentials, re-packeged it and re-sold. I guess that's fine if you never played S2 and have no knowledge of how intricate and complex that game eventually became. S3 is like starting over from scratch. I know this is a strategic moneymaker- start from the bottom and charge the players to build it back up.

Which brings us then to S3EP1: Sims 3 World adventures (known in another life as Bon Voyage for Sims 2). Quite simply this game blows. Getting past the fact that for some reason EA would have us believe that a "world adventurer" only visits 3 desitnations. Sorry guys- but China, Paris, & Cairo do not make up the "WORLD". So more cities would have been in order before giving the game such a sweeping and worldy title. Next up- the price of the game. Initally retailed at $40 and like a sucker I payed that because as I said I LOVED Sims 2 and desperately hoped for Sims 3 to take it to that next great level. But $40 later my game (which is not terribly fascinating to begin with despite the wonders of jet-setting) is now laden with bugs. It worked perfectly fine, before the mandatory game update which was required prior to completing the install of the EP and its subsequent patch. Seriously EA? You release an update that you immediately have to patch???? Or release a patch that you immediately have to update?!? Either way now my game is almost unusable. The thing crashes to desktop sporadically. One of my families has now disappeared off the face of Sim 3 universe (THANKS ERROR 16!). The aging is botched so that my elderly sims are 90 one day but wake up the next looking younger than their youngest adult offspring. Trying to complete missions whilst on "vacation" is not only not relaxing but sometimes impossible as after completing hours of time on these scavenger hunts they call missions- suddenly the target you need to report back to in order to complete the action is nowhere to be found- EVER. So there went your very short 3 day vacation trying to build up your Visa level. Racing around to complete tasks that ultimately are not able to be finished. Oh- and should you make progress, actually somehow get through the journey and then get whisked unceremoniously back to you homeland- Perhaps your Sim shows up on the other end safe and sound but they arrive sans the spouse or the children that they ventured off with!!! What the heck? How are Sims being left behind on vacation? Or maybe, just maybe, everyone does actually show up on the other end- but then the game just immediately crashes back to desktop once more so you've lost days upon days of your Sims lives and Hours upon Hours of your ACTUAL life in terms of playing time. Sigh....

Let me mention- my computer is new. Purchased almost exclusively for Sims 3. 750 Harddrive, 8G Ram. Quad Core. Decent graphics card. Up to date drivers. So it ain't me. This game is broken. I supsect EA knew too it. They MAKE games. That's what they do. They know how to test them so see whether they work or not before releasing it to the public. And It was strategically released in the 4th quarter to gain EA end of yr profits. I totally get it. Holding to fix it would have lost profits. But they released a shoddy product. They really should be ashamed and bending over backwards to fix it. But they aren't. Taking money like thieves in the night and leaving their gaming fans holding a very broken, very irritating expansion in the bag.

Seriously EA?!?! They actually outdone themselves this time.

title: AWESOME GAME!!  Great to do with your hubby & kids too!!
text:
I, like other reviewers, was hesitant in spending the $60 this game cost; however after getting it I love it and am glad to have paid the money. It is much better than My Fitness Coach (which is really just a workout DVD made for the Wii); I like that it measures you; counts your calories and tracks your progress.

I have started off with the 30 day challenge and after doing the workout for a week I can FEEL it working my body! My 4 year old daughter does the exercises right along with me and loves it!

I love that you can create your own workouts based on what you enjoy doing or you can do the preset workout. I LOVE that you can use the balance board with it. The video trainer they have showing you to do each exercise is very detailed and helpful and you can skip it if you want to or replay it if you need a refresher.

I love Wii Fit but hate that you can't create your own workouts with that which is where EA Sports Active is great. It has a large variety of exercises and I feel it has given my whole body a work out. It's also pretty neat that 2 people can work out together and shows them on the screen.

Most of all I think it is fun ... and to stick with anything you have to enjoy it. I wanted something I could do in addition to Wii Fit and this is it.

title: Good fitness software, still room for improvement
text:
Very happy with my purchase, but still can't help but think that they could have picked up some features of other programs. For instance it doesn't weigh you or track your weight. If you want that you use the Wii Fit's no disk channel. I will just use a real scale to save me from the little balance games. Sill it would have been a nice feature.

You start off entering your age, weight (max 300), height and picking an appearance. Very limited things to pick from for looks. You pick an outfit, shoes, sunglasses, hat, skin color, and hair style and color.

Then you go to your journal where you can set goals, workout, answers questions about your eating habits on the previous day and enter any activity outside of the game. I left the goals as the default which are to burn a certain amount of calories in a week, work out a certain amount of time in a week, and do a certain amount of workouts. After each workout it tells you how close you are to completing your goals.

I started the 30 day workout first. It gave me a list of exercises that will be done and you can unselect any you do not like. It gives you an estimate of how long it will take and how many calories you will burn. The first workout it says will go slow and ease you into it. I had selected a medium workout and it took 26 minutes and projected I would burn 156 calories (the time was very close and I burned a few more calories, which I don't think is too accurate, but still its a nice idea).

For every exercise it gives you a video of how to do it first, it is skipable. The videos are nicely done and give you a few tips. Then you go into the workout and see yourself as if looking in the mirror, with the trainer in a window in the corner. The trainer tells you what to do, and again watching her is like looking in the mirror, i.e. if she tells you to squat right, if she was real she would be squatting to her left.

There is a slight delay from your onscreen character using the controllers for some exercises. For instance doing curls there is a 1/2 to 1 second delay for your character to catch up with you. Not a big deal, but noticeable. Boxing was very responsive, although sometimes it appeared to register a lighter punch. Exercises using the Fit board were also very responsive. Control wasn't an issue at all, just a little annoying when I wanted to do my curls quicker.

If you are not doing an exercise right, the trainer points you in the right direction and repeats what to do. In my case it was because I was holding the controllers wrong. For instance it's important that you point them in the direction the game says to, or your movements might not register right. It wasn't a problem, but you do need to pay attention to where the controllers are pointing sometimes.

Once you have done an exercise the next time you come to it you can watch the video again by pressing the - button, or you can just press A you start the exercise instead. The game displays a window of what you will need for the exercise (Fit board or the band) so you can get ready (or get a drink) before starting.

My first workout had me sweating, but not really tired. I didn't feel like I had done a lot, but I am in ok shape as it is. It gave me a bronze medal and a percentage score.

When you are done you can take the nutrition survey which asks about what you ate the previous day. How many fist sized servings of vegetables? How many glasses of water? How many fast food meals? Etc. It has a recommended amount for each of the 10 questions and plots each question on a graph so you have 10 graphs showing your day to day changes for each question. After the survey it adds to your percentage score.

Next you add anything else you did the previous day. You enter an activity (biking, running, yard work), how long you did it and rank the intensity on a scale of 1-10. I had a gold medal for the day after finishing the workout, the survey, and the extra stuff I did.

You also get trophies (similar to XBox achievements) for doing things like burning your fist hundred calories in game.

One note about running: it isn't as good as Wii Fit with the scenery, you run around a track in Active. There are other runners who speed up or slow down at times and give you someone to chase if you choose. It is well done, but the running scenery is one of the few things Wii Fit did pretty good.

Graphics are good, they won't blow you away but they are nice.

Sound I didn't really notice. The trainer is easy to hear and there are various other chimes to let you know to do something. The voices are good and not annoying or over played. It plays a variety of music styles in the background, but I only noticed them when I thought about it and then quickly forgot about them again.

The included leg strap fit me with plenty of room to spare (6' tall, 205 lbs). I did have it fall off once, but that was mainly due to my clothing and not putting it on tight enough. I had no problems with the rest of the time, but it does take some playing with to get it how you like it. Also follow the tips in the manual for a better fit, they work.

As everyone else has said the resistance band is weak. Really weak. If you never do anything physical at all, it might be of some help, but for me it felt kind of useless. Also flat bands are a pain and the tube variety is far superior in ease of use. The good thing about the band is that you hold on to the ends by a nylon handle, this makes it very easy to hold the controllers while using the band. Any resistance bands you can buy in stores have hard plastic handles. Plastic handles make it much harder to hold on to the controllers while using the band. I did have good luck with using the Active's band handles with a tube band I already had, but it didn't seem as secure as they do with the included flat band.

The only other fitness game I have played is Wii Fit which I really liked but quickly grew tired of with the lack of workouts and lack of being able to move through the exercises quickly. Sports Active is much better than Wii Fit. The workouts that rotate each day and the training schedule is great. Plus it lightly touches things like nutrition without going overboard, which is nice. I do wish Sports Active would have included yoga. It is missed, but everything else it seems to do well. I am happy with the purchase and look forward to spending more time with it.

Not sure if it will get you fit, but if you try, it can't hurt.

UPDATE AFTER WORKOUT 8:[[ASIN:B002678YTY Thera-Band Assist Attachment Device]] I bought these handles that are practically identical to the included handles so I have various resistance bands that I switch out depending on the exercise. Having stronger bands makes a HUGE difference.

The workouts are varied, but it LOVES lunges. You will be doing at least one kind of lunge at least twice doing a workout, if not more. The program seems to completely skip abdominal workouts which are sorely missed. I think they really could have expanded on the types of exercises and not been afraid to include stuff where you don't hold a resistance band or the controllers (like Wii Fit has exercises that don't need the board).

The Fit board is used very little, even when it is used, it's just for some minor addition. I can't help but think the board should be mandatory and took a lot more advantage of it.

In my review I commented that the onscreen image can be a bit slow, this isn't necessarily the case. Each exercise is all about which way your controllers are pointing. The sooner you learn this for each exercise, the faster your onscreen character follows you. If you are off on your controller pointing, the game may say you are doing the exercise wrong. You probably aren't just not point the controller in the expected direction. Using resistance bands with plastic handles makes the controllers hard to handle and makes pointing the controllers in the right direction is harder to do resulting in the game thinking you are doing the exercise wrong.

I like the software, but again, I can't help they could have put a little more work into it and made it so much better. A cross between Fit and this would be great.

title: Good Game, Right on Time - But Could've Been Better
text:
Animal Crossing is one of Nintendo's biggest and most successful franchises. As a Nintendo entity, you won't see this game on any of the other major gaming platforms (Sony, Microsoft) - although you can get smaller renditions of Animal Crossing in general on older Nintendo systems and mobile. I'll mention below what I like about the game, dislike about the game.

Pros:
- Stuck at home, and if you have a Switch, it's a nice break. You can play with friends or make friends in the various Animal Crossing New Horizons (ACNH) communities all over the internet, where you can trade items that are the same but different colors, fruits (you get one core fruit, you can grow coconut palm trees, and you have a sister fruit on some deserted islands) and even designs.
- Speaking of designs, there's a cool feature that allows you to make neat new and items. You can also create your own tiles to walk on - some people in the community are REALLY into it... and have made some pretty extravagant designs which you can also pick up.
- You an lose yourself in the game for a few hours. Doing mundane tasks or if you are a 'completionist', running about making sure you have the bugs & fish you need. And be careful! Each month could bring new critters to collect, while expiring others that you may then need to wait months - or maybe even a year - to catch again. And that's a year in real time if you play the game 'fairly'.
- Thus far in 2020, Nintendo has had a few updates. And unlike a lot of games, they didn't make it part of a +$20 enhanced package. A very welcome, nice touch, especially in the current climate. Since April (these are not spoilers in any way - if you get the game today you should have it all available), they have added a character that sells flowers/plants, Redd, Luna with a dream realm that lets you visit other islands (but saves the other people's islands so miscreants cannot just take stuff from them), and even swimming & diving among other things.

Cons:
- Of course there are some cons though too. The biggest... there is a 1 island per console limit. So if you are a family of 4 with 3 people playing it, you would have 3 people on the same island with one 'main' family member.
This has huge implications - only the 'main' member can put down bridges or create inclines, or move items. I get it - maybe it's nice and the family decides. But the problem I have with this approach is that I don't want to get a bunch of Switche's for one household, or the same game 3 times for one household. Also - Nintendo is Nintendo, and they are NOTORIOUS for limiting supply so while the game is nice during the current crisis, good luck getting a Switch at retail thanks to upsellers - and I don't think it's worth paying the absurd upseller charges for the console. A big miss there... you can play up to two people at teh same time, but it's a very clunky and limited experience. Clearly Ninendo wants you to get another console and game. Which is ridiculous.
- Another issue is that you better make sure that you get it right the first time. You can edit your terrain in the beginning of the game, but your options are limited later in the game- which means that edging up, or evening out coastlines, etc. is a no-go. The only other fix is to... restart your island. Ditto if someone entered in a birthday wrong, etc. Not a big deal if you get the game August 1st and need to do it August 15th. But maybe not so nice if you got the game in March and it's now August 15th.
-Kind of a plus and minus, but when you 'order' items in the game (for the game of course) they will arrive in your game mailbox the next day. Not a huge deal - but if you are working on something and would like to get it done, but are missing that one thing you need... like a final blue ring corner... you'll have to wait until tomorrow to get it. And that's real time - not game time.
-Maybe the biggest miss for me with this game is the in-game interactivity potential. You can actually buy arcade games for your island residents. But you can't play them. Ditto ping-pong, billiards and pin-ball machines. A cool feature would've been to have at least basic 8 bit level mini-games built in to some of these. Or for ping-pong, maybe be able to play against a friend you invite to your island or against the CPU (an island resident perhaps). Either way, I felt like this was an easy win that ended up being a miss.
-Not sure if this is a huge 'con' but the online is available with the Nintendo Subscription which I think is about 35 dollars for the year. Then you can connect with friends or others in the community to play.
- Finally - I for one, after a few months, lost steam playing. You get into a routine with the game but after reaching the 'game' objective - which is getting your island to a 3 star level so KK Slider, a singing dog, visits, you're left to your own devices. Granted, you can design the island, your home and move things around to your heart's content but with the randomness of items in the shops, you can lose interest.

In the end I found this to be a very fun game and honestly it is a game that allowed my kid to connect with his relatives from afar and play and talk to one another with the game. They could trade items and since he's still learning to read and struggled with it, it motivated him to read a bit more with the help and connection with his older cousins. I doubt there will be another Animal Crossing on this generation of Nintendo (the Switch), but I'm optimistic that the next Animal Crossing title does add in those interactive elements and allows significantly more freedom for families that simply can't purchase multiple systems and games, but still want the best experience (that only one user gets with this game).

title: Three Weeks In
text:
I was at first very hesitant to purchase any fitness video game for my Wii, fearing that it would eventually suffer the same fate as my pilates DVD: gathering dust on the shelf. A friend had purchased Active for her Wii, however, and would tell me frequently how good her latest workout was. So I decided to take a chance.

It's now three weeks in and I have to say I'm pleasantly surprised. I wasn't sure how much you could do with just an exercise band and a couple of Wiimotes. I'm finding, however, that many of the exercises I did in the gym I can do at home, with the Wii providing feedback on rhythm/cadence and form. There's also the sneaky addition of some plyometrics, which are excellent for me, but continually kick my tail.

If there is one complaint I have about the program, it's that Active doesn't include any decent stretching, core, or other flexibility exercises. These are important to me, as I train in martial arts and need flexibility as well as strength. For this reason, I find that yoga with the WiiFit acts as a very good compliment to the Active; I'm sure that efforts with My Fitness Coach may also work. I only wish these type of exercises had been included in the program so I wouldn't have to stop, switch out discs, and start again.

So what's the overall verdict? Well, after three weeks with the pilates DVD, I was looking for another solution. With Active, I'm still going strong. It has a great variety of effective exercises for cardio and weight training, but leaves you on your own for core and flexibility. Thus, I highly recommend it, but make sure you take the time to stretch on your own!

( For a complete reinstall of the PS4 system click here.) Do that and in those instructions there is a download link to the update file that your going to need for installing a new HD. Some people say it may over heat the ps4 but the investment in a cooling station or a good laptop cooler stand is cheep compared to what you would spend on 2.5 high capacity hard drives. The largest one I have found is 4Tb and it was over $200. That was not in my budget and I went this rout.

title: If you think that you've found the perfect GCN controller alternative, you might be unpleasantly surprised.
text:
This controller could be the poster child for the phrase "Looks can be deceiving." I, like many others, missed out on the Gamecube controller adapter for Smash 4 and found myself weighing my other options. HORI is a well known brand and, by God, this thing looks exactly like the GCN controller. Seems like the perfect alternative, right? Wrong.

I'll get right to it. HORI would have nailed this product if it weren't for a single, huge, deal-breaking flaw: the left analogue stick is way too sensitive.

I had been playing Smash 4 since its launch - so about 4 months - with the Wii U gamepad and had gotten very used to it. From the moment I first used the HORI pad, something felt off. I figured that I had just gotten too accustomed to the gamepad, but after a handful of sessions and a lot of frustrating losses online I decided to investigate the issue. Turns out that if the left stick on the HORI battle pad is pushed halfway in any direction, it registers as pushing it all the way. What this means is that it is very hard to preform delicate actions, such as turning around or simply walking because the game thinks that you are inputting the command for the more deliberate action, such as dashing, or a Smash attack when all you wanted to do was a forward attack. I tested the HORI pad against the Wii U gamepad to verify this. I even went so far as to test the HORI pad against my Wavebird in Smash Bros. Brawl on my original Wii, just to make sure that it wasn't some quirk with the Wii U, Smash Bros 4, a deliberate design choice, or, best case scenario, a busted controller. The results were identical. Smash Bros. is a game in which your character will preform radically different actions depending on how gingerly you move the left analogue stick. The wonky sensitivity of the HORI pretty much breaks the game. I'm going to stick with it in the hopes that I'll adjust, but it's really lame that there even needs to be an adjustment period.

That deal-breaker aside, the controller works flawlessly. Heck, you might not even care about the sensitivity issue if you're a really casual fan of Smash Bros, or are just in the market for a Wii Classic Controller. Which is why it's such a huge bummer. This could have been a fantastic product.

It's a shame that Nintendo bumbled the controller situation for Smash 4 so badly, as now we're forced to turn to these sub-par attempts at resolving the issue. Nice try from HORI, but ultimately I cannot recommend this to anyone who would take Smash 4 at least a little bit seriously.

title: just like a Classic or Classic Pro controller
text:
Overview:

The Hori Battle Pad is a very capable Nintendo GameCube (henceforth "GCN") style controller that works by connecting to a Wiimote, just like a Classic or Classic Pro controller. It is a solid value and a great alternative for games like Super Smash Bros. (works with both the new Wii U game and the older Brawl).

Technical:

The Battle Pad functions as a Wii Classic Pro Controller, and must be plugged in to a Wiimote. If you don't have a Wiimote lying around, this controller will not work. It doesn't require any batteries, since it derives power from the Wiimote.

The controller works wonderfully with Super Smash Bros. for Wii U, as well as any game that supports the Classic Pro (or Classic) controller for Wii. This includes several Wii U and many Wii games, including Mario Kart 8, Mario Kart Wii, Super Smash Bros. Brawl, most Virtual Console games (both for Wii U and Wii), Xenoblade Chronicles, The Last Story, and Monster Hunter Tri (for Wii). The controller did NOT work however with Wind Waker HD and Donkey Kong Country: Tropical Freeze. This is of course no fault of the controller itself: those games simply do not support the Wii Classic or Classic Pro controllers.

Build Quality:

The Hori Battle Pad is a solidly constructed and attractive piece of kit. The plastic shell has a slight matte finish, which helps grip when your hands inevitably get sweaty. Similar products, such as the PDP Fight Pad, are glossy and get slippery when wet. Despite my best attempts, I was unable to cause the controller to creak or flex when applying significant pressure. It's rock solid. The primary face buttons (ABXY) are all identically placed to the original GCN controller and feel great when pressed. For comparison, I used my GCN Wavebird controller, and the face buttons felt identical. The c-stick is an exact replica of what's on the GCN controller as well, which will please purists but likely annoy anyone who found the original c-stick too small. Other controller's such as PDP's Fight Pad have enlarged the stick in their revisions, but Hori remains faithful to the original. That isn't to say everything is faithfully reproduced 1:1, as Hori has made some modifications and tweaks in other places, for better or worse.

The original GCN controller had two analog triggers (R and L), and when fully depressed they would "click" in. The triggers were very "deep" and had a lot of travel to fully activate in certain games. Likely some find this ideal and others annoying (I count myself among the latter). The Hori Battle Pad eschews the deep analog triggers of the GCN controller and replaces them with digital buttons for R and L, which can best be described as "paddles." I was hesitant about the change, but in actuality they feel great. The buttons have very short travel, and in games like Super Smash Bros., it means blocking can be executed much more quickly and reliably. Additionally, Hori improves on the original GCN controller design by providing two Z buttons (or ZR and ZL, as on the Classic Pro controller) on the right and left. The effect is similar to most modern controllers which have both shoulder buttons and triggers. These buttons are a marked improvement over the original Z button, of which there was only one on the right shoulder, and it was finicky to press. These additions alone may make the Hori Battle Pad a sweeter option than even an original GCN controller for Smash fanatics.

The other tweaks Hori has made come in the left analog stick and the d-pad. The left analog looks identical to the GCN's analog, however in practice it feels different. Hori has opted to flatten the top of the analog stick, whereas Nintendo's GCN controller had a rounded feel. The grippy rubber also feels less plush on the Hori pad, making it easier for your thumb to slide. I prefer the GCN's analog, but it is a subtle difference that is not a deal breaker. Hori's d-pad, on the other hand, is a huge improvement. One of the biggest criticisms of Nintendo's GCN controller was the diminutive d-pad, tucked away almost as an afterthought - a reflection of the 3D nature of games who only relied on the d-pad as glorified buttons (rather than a directional movement). Hori's d-pad is much larger than the original, and the controller benefits from it. Since the pad also works as a Classic controller in Wii and Wii U Virtual Console games, the larger d-pad makes playing SNES and NES games enjoyable. It should be noted, however, that the Classic, Classic Pro, and Wii U Pro controller all have much larger d-pads which feel substantially "clickier" than Hori's, which will make them go-to options for most retro gamers.

It should also be noted that the Start/+, Select/-, and Home buttons on the controller are all made out of an awfully mushy rubber, and they feel awful to press on this controller. Thankfully these buttons are not essential to gameplay, and I never had an issue with them failing to activate. It's clearly Hori skimped here, but the truth is I barely notice them. Finally, the cord on the controller, which must be plugged in to the accessory port on a Wiimote (where you attach the Nunchuck), is of generous length, and satisfactorily pliable. My biggest complaint with PDP's Fight Pad was it's super short cord, and the fact that it was very stiff - so much that it caused the attached Wiimote to turn itself over, and fall off my couch when moving the controller. I never had such an issue with the Hori Battle Pad, and in fact the length of the cord is a big improvement over Nintendo's own Classic and Classic Pro controllers.

Odds and Ends:

The Hori Battle Pad includes a turbo function, which I relegated to "odds and ends" status since most serious gamers won't ever bother with this feature. I don't see how it could give you any real competitive edge, but it works like this: holding down Turbo (which is near Start/Select/Home on the controller) and then pressing the desired button at the same time, will result in the controller spamming that input. There are 3 presets for speed: 5, 10, and 20, which can be changed on the fly with a slider. I don't use this feature myself, but it's there for anyone who wants it.

I generally avoid third-party controllers because of poor build quality and their overall cheap aesthetic, but by and large the Battle Pad looks great. One weird thing really undercuts what Hori has accomplished here, however: the Luigi logo painted on the controller appears off center. This is such a minor thing, but reinforces the stereotype that third-party controllers are cheap and low-quality. Perhaps mine was just an aberration - I've included a photo. It's barely noticeable and doesn't affect my use of the controller whatsoever, but I thought it worth mentioning.

Summary:

The Hori Battle Pad is a fantastic, solidly-constructed controller which emulates the original GCN controller faithfully, with the exception of a few notable improvements. The controller works with any Wii or Wii U game that is compatible with a Classic or Classic Pro controller, and is a great value at $25. For comparison, Nintendo charges $20 for their GameCube adapter for Wii U, and a controller (if you don't already own one) is another $30. And that GCN controller will ONLY work with Smash Bros. Wii U, whereas the Hori Battle Pad works with ANY game (including Smash) that accepts a Classic/Classic Pro controller. If your a fan of Nintendo's original GCN controller layout, or just a huge Smash Bros. fan, buy this controller!

title: Works Great with the Seagate 4TB Drive, but beware of changes to new PS4 hdd screw Location.
text:
This Device is Great, but please please please make sure you read up on everything before you begin. I Got this after seeing that the 4TB HDD from Seagate I bought was a 3.5 instead of the Laptop sized 2.5 HDD in the PS4. Now there are folks saying you must preformat your new 4TB HDD to exFAT before you place inside the Data Bank. That is False, jus Slide the HDD inside the Data Bank once you have installed the Data Bank onto the PS4. Also Note: The PS4's have been modified in the HDD area and Nyko probably hasn't implemented the change in its product yet. The Change is that the Metal Sliding Bracket that protects the PS4 HDD is different and now the HDD screw is in front of the HDD instead of on the Side, and Nyko's HDD Adapter has a Screw side arm for screwing and securing the HDD Adapter in place, but since the screw hole is now in front and the metal bracket is different than what the illustration says, I had to do alittle engineering modifying which probably screwed up my Warranty on the Data Bank. Happy to say that everything works great after the modifications I did. Also people are saying that you cannot put the PS4 into Rest Mode because it will cause issues, well for 3 Days Now I have let it sit in Rest Mode For hours then allowed it to power off after 3 hours in Rest Mode, and the Unit Booted up without an issue each time, so I guess they have fixed this problem. The Firmware out now is 3.11 fyi. Be sure to format a thumbdrive in FAT or FAT32 and download the Latest Big Firmware File which is the Full Installation it will require like 900mb on your Drive also make sure you follow Directions to the fullest. All Folders Must Be In CAPS! Be sure to reinstall the Firmware first after powering on your PS4 holding down the power button for 7 or 8 secs until you hear a Double Beep(this takes you into safemode), Make sure your Thumbdrive is connected in a USB port and your Controller connected via USB also.The PS4 will then set the HDD up itself and put all is needed like a fresh install on the drive. Other than that you should be Good, I love having so much Space now. Hope this will Help everyone out. Peace

UPDATE(11/16/2015): Need to make a correction about Rest Mode. The unit still acts up if you Enable Rest Mode and not allow it to Power off the System in 3Hrs as it is in its Default Setup. But if you were to leave Rest Mode Running after maybe 5 Hours and you power the system on it will try to go through Installation again. Just Decline the Installation, the Unit will Power off, and you can jus power the unit back up again and it will start up Normal! Jus a Small Hiccup but jus leave the Rest Mode in its Default setting which is 3hours or Off and you will not encounter that issue. So far that's it.

title: What A WORKOUT!!!!!!
text:
There are already more than enough reviews, but I want to stress a subject that others have found an issue with.

First off, my $.02. This game is a great way to start exercising. It is fun and motivating and it makes you excited about the next day. You get this little journal in the game that shows your daily activity. If you are familiar with fit, then it is similar. This version however, tracks what you did what you ate and the exercise that the program made for you. There is a 30 day challenge feature, meaning, the program chooses exercises for you and mixes them up day by day. I don't see how anyone could get board. Or you can pick or choose the exercises you want. The progress bar shows what it expected you to accomplish and if you pushed yourself a littler harder (faster pace) than it expected, you can view it on the graph. I do suggest getting the 2nd players pouch and band. Things do get kind of sweaty after your 20-30 minute workout. I'm even the type of person that walks 45 minutes to an hour every day, and still don't get the workout that I got with this game in 25 minutes. Previously (before EA Active) I had lost 56 lbs in 3 months using my meal plan and exercise routine. I have a feeling I am going to reach my other 65 lb goal in no time at all using this game.

Now the issue others are having. When it doesn't recognize you doing the exercises right and you think it is the game that is messed up, think again and look at the way the nun chuck is in the leg pouch. I had it in wrong once and it was not seeing my movements correctly and once I flipped it around, it fixed the issue. Those that are too impatient to try to figure out what the issue is, just say F-it, write a review with a 1-3 star rating, are too mentally incapable to be writing reviews, so don't listen to them. EA Sports should have put a picture of the nun chuck and the way it goes in for these folks. In addition, stay still after every motion. It will think you're not holding the position if you are moving around, so naturally it will not allow you to continue or interrupt you, if you're moving.

I will post at the end of my 30 day challenge and let you know how the progress of the game went and how much weight I lost. Good luck, and just push yourself to be the way you want to be, Skinny, healthy and live your life to the fullest.

Cheers,

title: Good workout with a few glitches
text:
I bought the Wii Active out of curiosity. Will it be more comprehensive than Wii Fit? Will it give me a challenge? I got my answers.

Yes to both!

Unlike Wii Fit, Wii Active gives you a full workout program option. It predicts calorie burn and workout time based on your physical specs and the recommended slate of programs. You can also deselect any parts of the workout you don't want to do.

The how-to videos embedded in the workouts are really helpful. It shows an actual human (not a computer figure) using the product with proper form. This helps eliminate some confusion about how to hold the remote & nunchuk.

There's a lot of variety in the workouts -- so far, I've played tennis, done a ton of anaerobics (lunges, squats, and the like), ran the track a lot, and did a few plyometric exercises (skateboard jumps are fun!).

I'm not a newcomer to working out, but I was able to work up a good sweat when I set the intensity level to HIGH. One of my wishes for Wii Active 2.0 (you know it's coming) would be to add some tougher exercises for the intermediate to advanced fitness lovers.

Another wish would be to have stronger bands. I find myself wanting to push the limits by using much heavier weights, but I can't hold the remote AND the weights. Innovation idea people! :)

One other wish is about the leg band. My thighs aren't petite but they aren't massive either. I'm able to barely get the leg band on, but it's definitely not made for all sizes.

Lastly, I wish that there was more consistency in the remote's reading. Often, it doesn't seem to read when I'm moving my arms so I have to do a move over and over and over again before it proceeds. It could be a glitch...or just another way to get me to do twice the number of reps. Once you get the feel for how the remotes should be held or what movements trigger the input, you'll sail through the next set of reps easily.

Overall, you'll definitely enjoy this workout whether you're a novice to exercise or an avid fitness participant. I've done the workout for the past 2 days and I'm actually sore!

title: Fun, Motivating, and a Good Workout
text:
I'm glad I gave this product a shot. I have been using it for a week now, and I must say that the workouts make me sore in a good way. I can tell they are effective. I think I may get a more challenging band for certain upper body exercises, but the lower body workout is solid.

Unlike the Wii Fit, Active has a human trainer who guides you PIP, while you watch your avatar workout. There are also some pretty useful video demonstrations for each exercise. There are enough different exercises that you don't get bored. I'm doing the 30-day Challenge, and I like how it alternates muscle groups so you can work out everyday, but you're working different muscles. It's like having a personal trainer, in many ways. I love the trainer, actually. She sounds like she's planned special work-outs for me and she makes them sound so fun that I get excited about working out.

Here's an example of how this game makes a boring but effective move fun. Jump-ups from a squatting position are hard, exhausting, tedious, and make me want to throw in the towel after about 3 jumps, but with Wii Active, I'm not just squatting and jumping, I'm in-line skating (squats make you go faster) and jumping off ramps (jump up with a controlled finish). It's so much fun to watch my avatar on the screen that I forget that I'm doing squat-jumps. I actually look forward to them. I know they still work because I'm sore the next day in all the right places.

I don't love all the exercises, but you aren't doing each one for too long, so I can hang in there for 12 reps.

I generally work out at the gym, but with Wii Active I can get a gym quality workout at home in less time, plus no driving or gym attitude. If you have a Wii Balance Board, you can use it for activities such as kick boxing and inline skating lunges. I'm sure there are more, but the game paces you so you are constantly getting to try new moves.

I think you could probably cheat on some of the moves by manipulating the sensors, but why would you want to?

title: Not 100% what I had hoped for; but pretty dang close.
text:
I own every single Sims game, and had owned all of the Sim City series as well. With that said, let's move on to the review of EA's latest product, The Sims 3: World Adventures. I had high anticipation because I am used to the massive amounts of new things we got with the Sims 1 & Sims 2 expansions, which were offered at much lower costs. However, do not let this deter you. While you may not get a ton of new items, you do get adventure as promised. The pros:
1. You do get to travel, and there are goals when you do so. I didn't care for the way the Sims 2: Bon Voyage, didn't really give you a goal. It was go to a new place, relax, stay for a huge amount of time and leave. World Adventures gives you goals, while allowing you to visit various places if you would like. And in time you can buy a vacation home and spend more time there. You have to build up your "visa" to have stays longer than 3 days in each location, and you do this by completing adventures. I had a great time wandering around the maze like tombs, and avoiding torching myself.
2. There are indeed a few more items, and they have country themes. In the past few games we have really only had Asian oriented items; I love decorating the house with flaming chandeliers like the ones seen in the tombs.
3. I have not found all of the new social interactions, but so far there have been about three.
4. Basements! Yes you heard right, you can actually have basements to your house now; not only that but you can build "tombs" under your home.
5. A few new traits and music tastes.
6. Your sim, when they learn a new song, may come home singing- which I find very cute.

Cons:
1. As with any EA game that just came out, there are glitches. The first time I started up, my sim was no where to be found. The plumbob was deformed and I couldn't preform any actions. I uninstalled it, the problem still remained. So I uninstalled the base game; that fixed that problem. Then I couldn't get skills or buy skill books. This was apparently a conflict between the new patch (that is required it seems.) and game mods and some custom content. I removed by mods and custom content; now the game runs like a charm.
2. The loading time is much longer than with The Sims 3 base game. I have plenty of memory, a new graphics card and plenty of RAM. I am above the required specs with everything, but only slightly. If you are working with the bare minimums or just a little above, it may run a little slower.
3. I have noticed (it may be my computer) that some of the graphics are not as clear, such as a blurry pixelation of my sims eye sockets.
4. Still no memories.
5. Some of the new features have been hard for me to find, such as the collection for photographs (which is a nice new bonus).
6. Toddlers & pregnant women cannot travel. I assume this is because it would be unsafe for them to be caught on fire, but it still stinks leaving them home.
7. Some people have been having a lot more problems, such as the game not loading, codes not working and games not saving. I have personally not had any of these problems.

I will update this as I continue to play; but so far the adventures have made getting the game worth it. I really enjoy having the goals and feeling like I'm achieving something for my sim.

title: Weirdly feels like nothing more than an exercise in destroying the environment for capitalism
text:
I really wanted to like this game, as I've enjoyed games of a similar style (e.g. Stardew Valley). Even from the beginning, though, the game felt off in terms of message and execution.

You start as a visitor to a desert island (you're told), however, two random other characters, one of whom is an aggressive gym jock, have also moved onto this exclusive desert island with you, along with a predatory loan shark and his offspring(?), who run the whole organization. From the beginning, you have to gather supplies from the world around you and sell them to make money or craft goods, most of which have no bearing on survival and are just decorative crap. If you catch an insect, fish, or dig up a fossil, you can contribute to the building of a museum, which pleasantly operates more like a zoo, so the animals are kept alive and in nice habitats (despite the keeper telling you *at length,* in unskippable chat scenes, how much he hates insects and everything about them every single time you turn one in). Every animal after the first, though, has no purpose but to be sold in exchange for bells.

Aside from contributing to the museum, your first task is to repay the loan you (apparently) took out to move out to this desert island. The only way to do that is to continually snatch up wildlife from the island, the surrounding ocean, or neighboring islands, and sell it to the loan shark's children in exchange for bells. Once you've repaid the loan, your goal in the game immediately becomes upgrading your home...by taking out an even larger loan. This is a repeating cycle, where the loan gets bigger and bigger and your home gradually turns into a McMansion on a once-deserted island paradise.

To top that off, you continually run into other people who want to come live on your island, who *also* want McMansions and proceed to develop the heck out of your isolated island getaway. You, of course, help them, by plundering the island of its resources and selling them so you can craft the furniture, decorations, and other material goods they insist they need to be happy. You don't really interact with the islanders in terms of making friends or connections, they just occasionally give you gifts and check in to see if you've taken enough selfies or if you even lift, bro (seriously).

Aside from the loan shark that continually pushes you into ever-increasing debt to satisfy your urge to increase your house size, and people who push consumption and waste at every turn by coaxing you to fill your house with unusable crap, you are also forced (due to small inventory size) to release the wildlife you've caught, wherever you were then, into the native space where you are now, regardless of how damaging that would be to any ecosystem with a non-programmed lack of consequences.

Okay, you say, I'm not playing a kid's game because I care if kids are taught good practices or ecological thinking. I want to collect and build and have a good, escapist time without worrying about anything but my own collection of colorful crap. That's fine, then, except the UI is infuriating (digging a hole in the place where you want it, instead of the useless square next to it, is an exercise in futility and frustration), and there's no way to skip the incredibly repetitive dialog that interacting with *anything* in the environment brings. Did you catch a carp? Bad news, because your character is going to turn to the screen and take 5 seconds to repeat the same lame-ass pun it's said every single time you've caught a carp (and you catch a lot of them). Catch a bug? Same 5 second delay and repeated pun. Did your axe break? Great, you get to hear about it yet again. Every single thing you collect or catch in the game comes with a loooong pause and a weak, unfunny pun about the name. And since there's nothing to do in the game but go into debt and collect things, that's a lot of game time. Crafting has a similarly tedious, drawn out, entirely unnecessary visual of watching your avatar hammer and saw, only to produce one of a very limited selection of images (a toolbox, a medicine bag, or a leaf, which represents everything else, for the most part).

Or maybe you can put up with that and you just want to interact with one of the other characters, to sell your loot. You get to listen to the same, lengthy, repeated dialogue, sometimes filling two or three different chat bubbles, before you can sell anything. Once you're ready to make a sale, you get to watch them deliberate for another 2-3 chat bubbles before telling you the price...which you then have to accept, and watch another 3 chat bubbles while they say goodbye.

There are no settings options in the game that would allow you to accelerate the dialogue, or skip it, or shorten the tedium of reading the same unfunny "jokes" over and over and over again, when you just want to catch a butterfly and put it in your bag and move on, dammit. There are no settings to customize anything about the experience, which is amazing for a game that is supposedly about customization. You are instead trapped in a never-ending hell of increasing debt, pointless consumerism, and tedious conversations with the same, obnoxious people you'd avoid in real life (e.g. people who call you "squirt" every single time you interact with them). The people who are currently developing your "island getaway" into a soulless suburb and somehow crowing about how isolated and remote and idyllic island life is, while simultaneously pushing you to build a gym and litter the landscape with randomized merchandise.

title: Good compliment to Wii Fit!
text:
I'm fairly new on the Wii scene but have been using Wii Fit for about a month now... it had me sweating during the boxing and was good for toning but that was the extent of it. However, EA Active Sports had me sweating buckets by the end of the "easy" 30 minute workout (to the point where the leg band slipped off)! Unlike Wii Fit the exercises are continuous and just when you think you can't do another squat a new exercise pops up, which I really liked. My legs were practically jello after all the side lunges/regular lunges/squats but you do feel the burn and that's more than I can say for the Wii Fit. This was my first day and I think I picked a routine that focused on the lower body but I agree with other reveiwers that the resistance bands are weak for the upper. The push-up/side plank on Wii Fit was more challenging than any of the upper body exercises I did today, but buying a stronger band is a quick fix. That's my only gripe so far - doesn't do much for the upper half.

The best thing in my view is that it tracks the calories you burn and allows you to set how long and what routines you want to do. I wasn't thrilled with the jogging but loved the boxing so it can be tailor-made, where you can see the calories each exercise burns and the time frame it takes to do it! If you set up a custom routine it shows the percentage of time you're working on each area (cardio, upper, lower) and that lets you focus on problem areas. I thought the trainer was OK but was frustrated when I didn't do an exercise entirely right and had to correct it before moving forward (at that point I didn't know you could skip certain exercises!).

All in all, this is a great companion to the Wii Fit. On the days you're not sore from EA Active (I'm sure I will be tomorrow, just in time where I have to stand for hours at a concert!) you can balance it out with yoga and the additional exercises Wii Fit offers such as the plank (for the core/abs) and push-up plank (more abs/core). Fit is better for ab work and since Active offers no yoga poses or balance options shuffling between the two is ideal.

I'm pleased with the product and do not regret shelling out the dough for it! I'm in pretty good shape and wasn't entirely challenged with the "easy" program but my legs will need a recovery period. I recommend this for anyone who lacks motivation to go to a gym (i.e. me) and wants a varied program with a trainer that shows you how to do the moves correctly. The fact that you can choose your own playlist was also a plus!

Pros: variety, continuity in exercises, the ability to design your own programs that zero in on trouble spots, feedback to ensure that you're doing the exercises correctly, and cardio that Wii Fit doesn't have (outside of boxing).

Cons: weak resistance band, getting "stuck" in a exercise if you haven't done it right, the leg band becoming loose (I wore it on bare skin so I think that if it was on clothing it wouldn't be a problem).

title: BEWARE: Only works for one player per console
text:
The Nintendo Switch has one of the best profile systems of any game console. Each player can have their own profile, and games saves are kept completely separate.

Because of this, I was very surprised to discover that Animal Crossing: New Horizons goes out of its way to circumvent the profile system. The first player to play the game is given the full experience. All other players are given a downgraded experience. Parts of the game are just missing, like naming your island, or choosing its layout. And all players are forced to have the same island, with limited space and limited resources.

If I'd known this, I wouldn't have purchased this game, as we have one Switch shared by two kids. How is it fair to let one of them be the "island representative", while the other is treated as a second-class citizen by the game? One can unlock things, invite others, etc., while the other can only do tasks that don't actually advance the story?

I see others trying to excuse Nintendo's behavior here, saying "Animal Crossing has always been like that", but:

1. This is false. On the 3DS you could only have one game save per cartridge, but you could use multiple cartridges with a single 3DS. On the Switch you need two separate consoles.
2. When classic games with limited save slots are ported to the Switch, the number of save slots from the original are normally made *per-profile* on the Switch. For example, in Link's Awakening there are only 3 save slots. In the Switch version, there are 3 save slots *per-profile*. Likewise, one would expect that Animal Crossing would have one game save *per-profile* on the Switch.
3. Having mis-features in the past is not an excuse for propagating them into the future.

Nintendo went out of their way to make the game terrible for anyone but the first player. It's pretty clear that their motivation for this is greed. Instead, they've made me strongly consider returning this game, and avoiding their platform in the future.

title: I like the exercises but...
text:
I think the workout exercises are great and kept me very interested with the different scenarios. It is very hard at first because there is a lot of squatting involved, but after a couple weeks I really noticed an improvement in my thigh muscles. My advice to anyone starting any kind of exercise program is to skip two days after your first day. Because it really hurts the day after... hurts a lot more the second day after... on the third day, it hurts about as much as the first day after, but you warm out of it and then can work out without having near as much after-workout pain.

What I don't like about this DVD:
You should be able to skip an exercise when you are in the middle of the workout. Only way to skip one is if you uncheck it from the list before starting. If you go back and uncheck it, the whole workout starts over.

There is a lot of time wasted in intros to every exercise. You are forced to go through the "show me how" EVERY TIME... must ALWAYS click the plus to "show me how" and then click it again to skip to the exercise. There should be something to click to completely bypass the "show me how".

If you are not holding position exactly and perfectly, it tells you to "stand still" and wait for up to a couple of minutes BETWEEN EACH REP before the exercise resumes. That is also one heck of a time waster. If I only have 20-30 minutes to work out, all these pauses only allow me to do a few exercises with most of my time spent standing still waiting for the program to resume. There is no way to make it resume until it does it on its own. It can take 10 or more minutes to go through one 16 rep exercise because of this. It is very frustrating because to my knowledge I AM doing it correctly. Since it is apparently sensing that one's position is wrong, why can't it tell you WHAT you're doing wrong so you can correct it?

The exercise band that comes with the DVD is very wimpy. Fine for someone who never uses their arms at all I suppose, but it did nothing for me.

title: I own the PC version of this
text:
Theres mainly only one HUGE problem with this game:
Saving.
I thought we were pass the era of gaming were you couldn't save anywhere you want - or worst yet, save period. Some of the levels on this game are pretty intense, and are long - but EA for whatever god-forsaken reason, decided to be an absolute a**hole and NOT put "save anywhere" function (like 99% of PC games have) on the PC version.
There is nothing more anoying then getting 20 min into a level, only to die and start ALLLL the way back from the begining. The results? Only to get back where you were to die AGAIN. How lame is that? A reviewer said it earlier: The saving system in this game is a shame. A damn joke. A teaser.
Not only that, but I have been screwed by bugs more then once in this game. One time, during a cut-scence on the level Southern Gate (the Kings path) it showed the big elephant comming towards me (this is all a cutscene) and for whatever reason, it glitched there - the cutscene kept going, but I was never able to return to my character - I had to actually exit out, and re-do the ENTIRE freaking level, only to have it happen AGAIN! ARGG! Absolutely rediculous.
There is no excuse for crap like that. It wouldn't bother me so much if I were able to save right before it - but since you have to re-do the entire level, its' just outright abnoxious.
On the plus side - the game IS fun, and the mindless "bashing a million orcs" can set the mood if you just want some quick action. The coolest part about this game is probably just the sheer number of enemies on your screen when your battling. It's like Serious Sam, only in 3rd person.
But because the gameplay is so easy and brainless, you do have to take a break every 15 min.
The graphics are pretty good. The character details and lighting is above average. The sound is also good. The enviroments and levels could use alittle more help, but it's not bad at all really.
Besides the saving woes - the game pretty fun, but not worth buying. - perhaps just borrow it from a friend and test it out.

Anyway this "game" is great - being a zaftig gal I needed something that wouldn't be too hard, too easy but just right...

Sports Active gives you many options...

30 day fitness challenge - you can set this up to reflect Easy, Medium, Hard - at first I set it up on Easy and after a few days reset it to a Medium - the difference I can see is as you go up it adds a few more exercises so the time is longer - so in the Easy mode I was seeing about 17-20 minute long workouts...in the medium mode 20-28 minutes or so...I would assume the Hard would add in more exercises making the overall program for that day longer - It does allow for rest days - but you don't have to stick by the schedule if something comes up...once you have started a 30 day challenge each time you choose it - it automatically goes to the next day in the sequence

Preset workouts - this has a ton of preset workouts that you can do - they vary from full workouts to zoning in on specific areas like arms and legs.

With the two above before you begin your workout it shows which exercises are in the workout - if there is something you don't want to do you can click to remove it...I did this the other day on the 30 day challege as the workout had a Run (long) in the middle of the workout and I HATE to run (it had a run at the beginning and end as well) - plus I needed to shorten the time of the workout a bit...

The third option is to create your own workout using all the different exercises - I love this option and have created a number of workouts - you name your workouts and they are stored in the system...you can change or add things to your workout at any time...As you are creating your workout they hve 3 little people in the bottom cornor and the system will tell you what % is Cardio, what % is working your lower legs and what % is working your upper portion. My favorite one I have created is one that only has sports activities. My daughters each got to create their own workout - something I really liked as I was able to tailor it to stay under a certain amount of minutes so they can each have time to do thier workout

No matter which workout style you choose (30 day, preset or custom) the system will tell you before you begin how many calories you are projected to burn...there is a calorie counter in the upper left hand corner that will tell you how many calories you are burning (mine has always surpassed the projected calories) ...BUT note this count may not be accurate - in talking with friends who have used it with a Heart Rate Monitor their HRM has shown a difference - sometimes the HRM shows they burned more - sometime that they burned less...so just use the calories burned as an estimate

You will sweat if you do one of the 20+ minute programs...and if you haven't exercised in a while and start this up YOU WILL FEEL IT - after the first day my legs were like jello and I could feel every muscle...it hurt to sit down...but now I do those lunges and squats with the best of them

Some tips and tricks I learned

Wear some sort of long/capri pants under the leg strap - your leg will sweat if put on a bare leg and that can lead to slippage...also if you are a little rotund and have thighs that touch there could be a little chaffing of the leg strap if you aren't wearing longer pants.

It will take some time for you to figure out the exercise band and exactly how much you need to step on to provide resistance in your arm exercises - now that I have done it a bing of times I know how much strap I need for each exercise...

Now I do love this program and will continue to use it - but there are some drawbacks...

1) If you are serious athelete chances are you won't get much of a workout from this - but if you are just starting an exercise program or need something to help you along in your journey - this is great

2) There is a small amount of downtime between each exercise as they show a screen as to what is next and will launch into a tutorial - you can skip it by pressing A button...I do wish especially for the 30 day challenge if the exercise had been done in a previous day it would skip that screen and go straight to the exercise - but I figure if I was working out in a gym I would have the same amount of downtime switching form one exercise to another...

3) The controls can be a little bit finicky - on certain exercises you have to have the remotes pointed a certain way - up, down, to the side - if you don't it won't register the movement...the first few days it was pretty frustrating but the more I used the program the more I got into a rythem of the exercises and making sure the remotes are pointed the right way.

4) There isn't much in the way of core exercises or exercises that are specifically designed for core - what I have been doing is on the "Rest" days of the Challange is popping in My Fitness Coach (Love this as well) and doing a Core workout from there...

5) if you are looking for mostly cardio work vs arm and leg exercises you may not like this program due to the small downtime between exercises - if you are looking for more of an aerobic type workout I would go with My Fitness Coach

Overall I think for those beginning exercise - to actually do SOMETHING and sweat and burn calories or want sfun exercise here and there for toning arms and legs it is a great program...it is so much fun to do - especially some of the sports - there are times where I have done 20 minutes and been having so much fun I "workout" again as it doesn't seem like I worked out (but yet I have burned over 200 calories...)- an added bonus is my daughters (age 8) love it as well...I am planning on getting the extra leg strap/band package so they can either workout together or workout with me when I do a lighter workout.

I think it is very hard to judge it from just using it once or twice - the more you use it the more you get intuned with the program

There is plans for an expansion pack due out at Christmas time - according the EA website it will have more core exercises built into it, more sports like racetball and more cardio options like step aerobics...I will be pre-ordering mine as soon as it is available...
