title: Good, Save For a Few Things....
text:
If you're looking for a serious in-home workout -- more challenging and difficult than you'd get from Wii Fit -- then EA Sports Active is a good choice. The game is designed to seriously attack all muscles groups, and does a good job at mixing up exercises over time (some days will empahsize legs, others arms, for example). The exercises range from low-resistance single-motion "warm-ups" such as dancing a la DDR, to combination high-resistance exercises such as the bicep curl + shoulder press combo, to body weight balance exercises, such as forward, backward, and side lunges. I've worked out seriously off and on for a number of years, both with personal trainers and with self-guided programs, and I'm impressed at the game's commitment to true fitness and reputable exercises.

Two things keep it from five stars for me:

1. The included resistance band is very very very very light, and won't suffice for anyone with any modicum of strength. You'll need to upgrade your bands (there are plenty on Amazon!) if you want a muscle-killing workout.
2. On certain exercises the game is far too finicky about placement and rotation of the Wii remote and nunchuck. I've had to reset exercises numerous times because the game didn't think I was holding the controllers correctly and became confused and unresponsive. Talk about a momentum blow.

Otherwise, the good:

1. Solid, REAL exercises that WILL work for you if you commit and use stronger resistance bands.
2. Intelligent workouts that don't repeat day-to-day.
3. Trophies and goals that help you stay motivated.
4. The option to opt-out of certain exercises. (I can't run or jump in my condo for obvious reasons.)
5. The option to work out with a partner.

Room for improvement:

1. The meal surveys don't really add much and seem tacked on; the overall fitness profile stuff is half-baked
2. The music is meh
3. Would be nice to pick the duration of your work out (rather than just the level).

title: Read this if you have knee/ankle problems or are very out of shape
text:
Like many people, my resolution for the year was to get back into a regular exercise routine. I had knee surgery a little over a year ago and had to stop karate, but I never substituted with other workouts. Getting to the gym has been a problem, so a home workout seemed like the perfect solution. This product has great reviews, so I thought I would give it a try.

I'm still in my first week of the 6-week challenge (on medium), and overall I'm very happy with the workouts. They're challenging enough that you KNOW you worked out, but not so hard that you're too sore the next day. There's a great variety of exercises targeting a wide range of muscles. No thought required on your part to ensure a thorough workout. Also, being able to pick my workout days and have a calendar with everything planned out seems to be just the thing I needed to keep me honest and stick to the plan instead of telling myself that I will work out 'tomorrow' (which never came!).

The one major drawback that I see for some people is the fact that there isn't a low-impact option for the 6-week challenge. People with knee/ankle problems, or those who are very out of shape should proceed carefully. The only low-impact option is one pre-made workout, or you could build some custom workouts, but if you want this for the 6-week challenge with the progressively difficult pre-made workouts, you'll be in for quite a challenge. Even on easy, the 6-week challenge uses many of the same exercises as on medium, just for shorter duration and intensity. There are a LOT of lunges and squats involved, and some jumping motions that could be difficult for people who have knee/ankle problems or are very out of shape. You have the option to skip exercises that don't work for you, but if you eliminate too many, you may not be making the most of the product. My knee is holding up surprisingly well - I needed some ibuprofen after the first two workouts, but not the third workout. I take it easy on some motions as needed and push where I can, and I'm finding my knee getting noticeably stronger pretty quickly.

As for the accessories that go with it (from either the original EA Sports Active or the Accessory Pack), the exercise band is a joke. The resistance is far too light, so plan on having your own resistance bands available. And like others, I've had issues with leg holster. It just barely fits if you are somewhat overweight, and I have to anchor it very high on the thigh to keep it from slipping down. Still, that doesn't seem to have caused too many problems with registering my leg motions. Based on the reviews of competing leg holsters out there, this one still seems to be the best option, with the others running smaller in size, not larger. One reviewer made his/her own out of resistance tubing, which isn't a bad idea (use the flat type). If your thigh at its widest point is larger than about 28 inches, go that route and save yourself some money. (Here's a thought - if you already have the accessory pack and the leg holster is too small, use the red resistance band to make a leg holster and have your fitness goal to be able to fit into the 'real' holster!)

My only other warning would be that the cool-down stretches are nowhere near sufficient to avoid sore muscles. There are the same few stretches every workout, regardless of whether you targeted upper body or lower body during the workout. Plan to do extra stretches after the cool down, because you'll be sore the next day if you don't!

So overall, this will give you a great workout if you're only moderately out of shape, but it might be a bit much if you have significant knee/ankle problems, or if you're very overweight or out of shape. If you've got the guts to go for it, though, you'll be in better shape pretty quickly!

title: Feeling the workout, a little frustrated by what could have been
text:
I've used EA Active for two days now and wanted to chime in with a few thoughts. Most importantly, I definitely *feel* the workouts (was a little sore this morning from yesterday's) and I expect that by continuing the 30 day challenge I will benefit from the exercise. That *is* the most important, and so for the cost of a month or two at the gym, this title should be helpful.

However, there were a number of user interface issues that were frustrating, not because they were disasters but because it didn't need to be that way. For instance, when you move from exercise to exercise in the 30 day challenge, some exercises require the nunchuck in your left hand while others require it tucked into a pocket on the leg strap. The software does tell you which mode you need to be in, but it doesn't do so intelligently: e.g., if you go from one exercise to another where the nunchuck position doesn't change, I don't need to know about it, but if you go from chuck-in-hand to chuck-in-pocket, it's very easy to miss the notice on the screen (which is timed, not triggered by a button) and you can begin the next exercise in the wrong position. Putting the nunchuck into the pocket isn't hard, but it isn't smooth. You can't help but notice a number of similar areas where things could have been programmed a bit better.

The leg strap, for me, was slightly troublesome. If I make it tight enough to stay on my leg for all of the exercises, it's rather tight and I feel it squeezing my hamstring. If I loosen it so that it doesn't cramp the muscle, then it tends to fall down. Perhaps a different pair of sweat pants would help. [UPDATE: After 4 workouts, I continue to have leg strap problems, especially on all of the "jump" exercises, where no matter what I do or what I wear, the leg strap falls off mid-exercise.]

If you use the balance board, the video instructions for events like roller blading suggest that you to watch the instructions for without the balance board first, but then don't give you a way to do that. Some exercises seem a little risky -- doing high kicks during boxing while standing on the balance board seems like a recipe for future injury, but I guess no risk no reward...

Interestingly, both days 1 and 2 have you do biceps curls, but no focused triceps exercise (though I guess shoulder press does include some triceps work). [UPDATE: After 4 days of exercises, the biceps have been worked each day.]

For several of the exercises in today's workout, I found the nunchuck cord to be a problem. With the knee lifts, you end up whipping yourself with the cord when you bring your arms down. With the shoulder presses, the cord can hit you in the face unless you keep your arms forward a bit. Doing a backhand tennis racket motion with your right hand while holding the nunchuck in your left doesn't feel right as the cord isn't long enough to allow a full swing.

Compared to Wii Fit, I think that Wii Fit was a *lot* more fun, as I was compelled to play some of the balance games for hours at a time. After working out on EA Active, I was ready to be done -- that's not a bad thing, it is a workout after all, but it's not really a *game*. Wii Fit tracks your weight, which is helpful, while EA Active doesn't (surprisingly). Moving from exercise to exercise is smoother on EA Active since you have pre-programmed workouts ahead of time (on Wii Fit, it's rather a drag moving from exercise to exercise).

In summary, I think this will be an effective exercise tool, which is what it's supposed to be. I don't give it a higher rating because of a number of user interface issues that could easily have been avoided and because of the imperfect use of nunchuck and leg strap.

[UPDATE: After 4 days of exercises (1 day of rest), I am more frustrated with this software and wonder about the wisdom and safety of some of the exercises. Today's workout was very "jump" focused, with lunge jumps, squat jumps, and roller blading jumps (be careful with your knees). The system had a hard time detecting my jumps accurately. If you raise your hands too high on the jump, you'll pull the nunchuck out of the sleeve. Some of the motions are artificial (e.g., pointing your hands upward at the top of the shoulder press) so that the wiimote can detect a complete movement. In boxing, the success of your punch seems to depend a lot on how hard you "snap" at the end of the punch, which seems bad for your arms. The coach can go in one second from "Your form is a little off, this exercise owns you" to "your really nailing this exercise" in the next second, same exercise. I would swear I heard the video instructions for the curl-shoulder-press say, "At no time should you allow the shoulder to come out of the socket." Really! And two seconds into the warmup "walk", the coach exhorts "Nice!" I mean, I'm just walking for 2 seconds, I don't need the encouragement yet...]

title: Sim City 4, the latest and greatest Sim City.
text: This is the best Sim City game ever made!  Like older versions, you put in residential, commercial, and industrial zones;place police stations, recreational facilities, fire stations, jails, educational facilities,transportation systems, rewards, and landmarks.  However, it is vastly improved over previous versions.  First of all, city services have been expanded upon.  I haven't made it that far in the game yet,(my largest city has about 15,000 people and the region I am working on has about 100,000) but what I have seen so far is simply awesome.  The graphics are incredible!  Please stop complaining and get a new computer.  I have a older model and I have got the brains just to play the game at a freinds house who has a new computer.  The city services is where some massive change has come though.  You can now get large or small police and fire stations, there are now elementary and high schools, beaches have been added as recreational facilities, and many more.  Have problems balancing your budget?  Here is the key:STOP SPENDING TOO MUCH MONEY!  This version is a bit harder because you have too pay for everything, and I admit I had difficulty with this when I first started playing, but with practice I have overcome the problem.  The key to balancing the budget is making a lot of zones.  Once you have a significant tax base, you can add city services.  There is a budget window telling you how much you are making or losing per month, and each building has its cost listed.  There is virtually no excuse for not having a balanced budget other than inexperience.  Trust me, the time you spend trying to master the game is worth it.  It took me about 4 hours to learn how to play it, but since then I have had like over 10 hours of enjoyable time playing it, so it is highly worth it.  And contrary to stupid rumors, it is possible to get scyscrapers in the game.  You merely need to play it to where you have a large population of about 300,000 regional pop with all cities connected and then you need to put in excellent city services.  Sure, it is a pain how you can only get small houses and stores in your residential and commercial zones at first, but it is possible to get larger and larger buildings as you continue to play the game.  And in my opinion this makes the game better, because it forces me to diversify my cities more,it makes the game more realistic(ever seen the empire state building in a town of 5,000?  I don't think so...), it makes the game more challenging, and it gives you a reason to keep playing it.  Don't give up!  You will have that 30 story residential building sooner than you think!  And even before then you get bigger buildings as the game progresses which can help tide you over.  Plus, if you get frusturated or bored, you can always unleash cool disasters like robot attacks, meteors, fires, volcanoes, lightning, etc.  Also, riots occur if you are very unpopular(I must admit I have gotten them before).  To put down disasters, you must send out your regular police, SWAT(you get them when you have a large enough police force), and firefighters.  Also, there is a day night mode thing, where you can see your city in either day or night, and at the start out the game you get to change your terrain and animals in the mode.  To sum it up, this is a awesome edition to the sim city series with great graphics.  My only complaints are:The game requires must processing power, and it can be hard at first.  But never give up!  It's a awesome game, and its worth the time invested to learn how to play it.

title: Better than any game I've ever played!
text:
I've been a Sim City fan since the very first version way back years ago, before some of you wild and crazy kid gamers were born, and I've snapped up each new edition and addition, marveling at the evolution with every new version. As I say each time: This one tops them all, with bells on!
Better in every way: Everything I've wanted is finally included! Everything I've disliked is finally gone! Features I never could have dreamed of dazzle me as I discover them!
Trying to be coherent here for the benefit of normal people; fellow simians will know what I mean. More elaborate scenarios, sophisticated technical stuff (visual animations of weather, traffic, perspectives, sounds and music, etc.), more complex algorithms underlying sim city life and how to run or ruin it, refined interface, both more powerful and more intuitive, wittier (and wilier) advisors, and of course spectacular buildings rendered in tweezer-tight detail... well, I won't spill all the beans!
Argh! I'm bouncing off the walls!
Five stars with whipped cream and a cherry on top! Run, don't walk, to get this one! And then cancel all your appointments for the next three days at least, maybe even three months, because if you're a true Simaniac, you shouldn't plan on getting out much for a while!

title: One Island Per Switch is Lame
text:
I was looking forward to Animal Crossing - New Horizons after playing Animal Crossing - City Folk years ago. I was surprised when my son logged into his switch and could only fly to my island on startup. He didn't get to pick his own island name or layout. We have discovered that if one player gathers all the wood for the day, the next player can not get any wood unless they go to another island, spending precious miles. It also makes it harder to make achievements for any player who follows the first for the day.

It also means that there are island "firsts" that only one player gets to experience. Only one player can choose an island layout, the name, be the one to get Blathers to the island, etc.

While it *is* nice that islands can be home to multiple players on a switch, for those who would like to play that way, it shouldn't be mandatory.

title: Sunshine Islands VS Island of Happiness - Go for Grand Bazaar
text:
I am a huge Natsume fan and I buy every HM game I can get my hands on. I enjoyed this game the first time I played, but I groan when I think of making use of my second file - very low replay value. It is, however, a big improvement from Island of Happiness. Island of Happiness was so boring and aggravating, I gave it to someone else just a few weeks of attempted gameplay and, now, that person I gave it to doesn't play it either. Sunshine Islands is alot more fun, less work, and a more creative storyline. There are some annoying flaws though..

Pros:

*You don't have to rebuild the main island from scratch as in Island of Happiness
*Shipping items is made alot easier and quicker
*You're not limited to using only the stylus anymore
*Your field is easier to keep clear of stones and weeds
*Most the bachelors/bachelorettes are on the island from the beginning
*More variety in animal/pet colors and appearance
*The festivals are alot more fun and interactive
*The watering hole is alot closer to your field so you don't have to run across the field to refill your watering can each time
*At your wedding, you actually wear a wedding dress/tuxedo instead of casual clothes
*Upgrading your tools is made more simple so it's easier to keep a whole field of crops

Cons:

*The characters have a very small dialogue and it becomes VERY repetitive - especially after marriage
*Low replay value; gathering all the sun stones again is too much work and I don't want to do it again
*Fishing can get irritating and will frustrate you at times
*It's irritating that you cannot ride the horse around town and I also dislike that it's out in the barn with my cat and dog. I think the cat and dog should be kept in the house and the horse out in the barn with the cows and sheep. Also, the pig you can keep is located on a completely different island! It's annoying to go all the way out to Mushroom Island to feed it everyday
*Befriending the animals to help out with chores is a creative feature, but a hassle.
*Not enough character interaction. I wish there were more festivals to invite someone to and that there were more personal events instead of a few "heart events". For instance, I like how you go on a date and get a love confession like in Harvest Moon: Animal Parade for the Wii. It'd be nice if, in addition to the heart events, there were other more personal events with your intended spouse.
*Mining is just as annoying as it was in Island of Happiness. You pass out easily and the treasure you can find isn't usually worth that much.
*Lacks creativity and fun as experienced with Harvest Moon DS/Harvest Moon DS: Cute

Overall, I recommend you order Harvest Moon: Grand Bazaar for the DS! It's coming out very soon and is a huge step up from this game! If you have a PSP, I would recommend Hero of Leaf Valley as well. Sunshine Islands is good, but there's been better HM games and there will be more to come.

title: once the bugs are ironed out, it will be a truly great game.
text:
I've actually had pretty good luck over the years when it comes to the Sims games. While others complained of bugs and glitches and issues installing it and conflicts with their system, I easily installed and played my games with nary an issue. Until this one.

First the game kept crashing to the desktop after 20 minutes of playing. Also, my game would start and no sounds except for the load music would play for the first 15 minutes. I have a new computer. It more than meets the requirements to play the game. I do not have any custom content or hacks..what's in my game is what came with it. I uninstalled and reinstalled, and that fixed the crashing and the music issue. But then I kept getting the "error 16" save error. So I updated the game with the new patch, and that was fixed.

Now that I could play it for more than 20 minutes at a time, I set about adventuring in France. Very cool tombs and museums to explore, mysteries to solve, locals to help, and just a fun time all around. But there are still glitches. Things randomly vanish from the inventory. I cannot bring back the nectar maker from France. It does not come over with my sim when she travels home. I've tried twice now and it just doesn't work. She caught a load of frogs while she was over there, and the first time she came home she managed to bring them back with her. The second time, they all vanished from inventory.

There have also been a few glitches with missions. My sim couldn't complete one due to the "report in" action cancelling itself every time she tried. The sim she was attempting to report to never showed up anywhere again after that. There was also another mission where she returns a skeleton to a family crypt..but the mission vanished completely after she accepted it. Now she's got a skeleton in her inventory and nothing to do with it.

It is a really fun game once you get past the glitches. Also, they have fixed the "puffy face" issue. The new sim I created does not look oddly bloated the way the sims in the base game do. The new lifetime rewards are a nice bonus and worth earning, the graphics are really beautiful, and there are a lot of new plants and trees available in build mode. There are some really nice new decorations and furnishings as well. Only a handful of new hairstyles and clothing, but some new makeup and jewelry that are nice.

It is worth it, in my opinion. It's a fun game (I played for several hours last night and didn't get bored), and now that my sim doesn't look like the Stay-Puft Marshmallow man, it's nicer to look at. But it does have glitches that I wish had been fixed before it was released.

title: A good third party controller, but does not come close to GameCube controller greatness.
text:
Like many others, I was a little bummed when Nintendo announced that the new GameCube controllers would only work with the new Super Smash Bros. So when I saw this controller, I was pretty excited to be able to use what looks like a nice clone of the original Gamecube controller. The fact that it is officially licensed by Nintendo and is commanding a pretty premium price for third party controller, I was put at ease.

But, since receiving the controller and comparing it against the famous Wavebird controller (Nintendo's wireless version of the GameCube controller), I have to say I'm feeling the sting of disappointment. This is a classic case of a third party going 90% of the way to making a great product, but skimping out on the last 10%, ruining it in some way. Make no mistake, this is 10x better than most other third party pieces of junk. But after spending thousands of hours gaming with a real GameCube controller, it was instantly obvious that this is just a knock-off in the end (albeit a pretty decent knock-off).

For starters, the buttons have that classic knock-off feel. I cycled between pressing buttons on my Wavebird, then pressing buttons on this controller. It just doesn't sound or feel the same. It just sounds and feels cheap. The middle buttons (Home, Start, Select, Turbo) are not the hard plastic of the original, but some mushy rubber that is not easy or pleasant to press. The thumbsticks are... different. There is less resistance to them (a hallmark of a knock-off), and they travel far more than the real thing does.

As for positives, I would say the D-pad is improved as it is slightly bigger than the original's. That doesn't say much, as the original's D-pad was all-time awful. Maybe one of the worst ever.

The controller itself is incredibly light, which I assume is due to a lack of rumble features. The new triggers take a little getting used to, but that isn't a bad thing at all. They needed to make them compatible with Classic Pro control schemes and this controller does just that.

So, would I recommend this product? It depends. If you love the GameCube controller as much as I do, you will quickly see the shortcomings of the HORI Battle Pad for Wii U. To these individuals, I'd probably recommend something else. If you only occasionally used a GameCube controller and are looking for a Classic Pro alternative, you might not notice or care about this product's negatives.

For me, I think I'll be keeping it if only to have a Classic Pro type controller to use with old Wii games that support it. But for Wii U games, I'll be using my Wavebird or my Wii U Pro Controller.

title: And now the Sims franchise falls to EAs iron fist!
text:
Like many others with The Sims Series... I have been a fan of The Sims since they first came out with "The Sims" and "The Sims 2" And I would expect that with such a money making franchise as The Sims, that EA would NOT do what they have been doing... But they did...

DO NOT BUY THIS GAME!!!! It will destroy anything you have done in The Sims 3 so far and is buggy beyond belief!

If you want to know how I truly feel... Then think about a time you got that feeling in the pit of your stomach, that made you feel sick because you had just been blatantly ripped off or betrayed... That's how I feel!

It is not a VACATION expansion... It is an ADVENTURES "add on" taking a fun non-linear game and making it into a console game where you actually have to go from point a to point b.

It is just downright inhuman what EA does with employees, and how it impacts the finished product.

They constantly lay off hard workers because they are afraid that if anyone works on a game for too long that they may try to leave and start their own company... So EA moves development teams in 6 week to 6 month shifts... Rotating them from project to project... This means that every time they "rotate" the new team has to somehow pick up where the old team left off, relearning and trying to figure out what was going on before the "rotation"... And this creates MAJOR ISSUES. EA also rushes things to release dates even against the development teams wishes to hold off release so they can make a more polished product... EA does not care! They are all about the almighty bottom dollar! So what you get is a half finished, problem causing game, that otherwise would have been wonderful.

Now, onto the MICRO-TRANSACTIONS!!! Not only do you pay for this overpriced, half finished game.... But you will also have to pay to "unlock" items and features that were otherwise already in the game, but hidden, because selling millions of The Sims 3 wasn't enough for EA, they now want to charge you $20 a pop of REAL WORLD MONEY to get 1000 "SIM POINTS" so you can have the matched sets and items and features that should have been in the game in the first place. You can see forum postings and reviews about the REAL COST of The Sims 3 here on amazon.com

This is the FIRST expansion... If you can even call it that, as I see it more as a step backwards. All The Sims games have had expansions that do, in fact, make the base game better and better... Like adding PETS, and a NIGHTLIFE, and actual SEASONS with rain and snow and so on and so forth... The base games also had a great deal of content to begin with, from tons of matched furniture to pools with slides and diving boards, hot tubs, and musical items that you could make your own Sim garage band with... Then enter the Sims 3 with NONE OF THAT STUFF!!!

Then enter The Sims 3 World Adventures, Still not adding anything other than a ONE TIME adventure for your chosen Sims... Yes ONE TIME! Still no vacation... Still no hot tubs... Still no diving boards... Still no pets... No seasons. I can say it was quite fun playing through the new expansion with one of my Sims... But here is one of the many problems... My old towns and Sims have been destroyed with the addition of this expansion... Where my huge town with tons of custom houses and Sims once stood are now blue property sized holes. If that wasn't bad enough... I create a new town and a new Sim household to go on ADVENTURES... I am having some fun exploring and collecting goodies, and enjoying the new themes and whatnot... Until I get bored and decide to try ADVENTURES with a different Sim... This part makes me very angry... Well more angry after losing my Sim town... I CANNOT DO ADVENTURES AGAIN! Yes that is right! Once you go through the tombs and discover everything with one Sim, any other Sims you try to do it with will not get the same bonuses and benefits as the first one! All the paths remain open and revealed, all the doors stay open, all the traps found and disabled, all the ONE TIME ITEMS do not return, including a required item called "Pengu's Axe"... On top of this is a disappearing inventory glitch where every now and then, items in your Sims "backpack" up and delete themselves!

Also, get used to seeing "Error Code 13" and "Error Code 16" when trying to save your games... When this happens, the save game is corrupted and everything you have done has just been destroyed, and you now have to go into the game save directory and HOPE that there is still a working backup copy you can restore with some less that user friendly editing.

I could go on and on about other glitches and bugs, and the fact they have Day One micro transactions on or before the release date of this expansion showing that they are intentionally leaving things out of the game just to make more cash off the people dumb enough to pony forth said cash.

So that means that only ONE SIM HOUSEHOLD and one Sim household ONLY can get the full experience of the adventures... Any others after that just walk through the already explored tombs with nothing to do and nothing that would be considered an actual "Adventure." So unless you want to constantly create whole new towns and start over again just to reset the Adventures... I say leave this game off your holiday gift list... At least until EA pulls their heads out of their donkeys and fixes the glaring issues with this game.

I am 27 years old, I build high end gaming computers, and I have only had to call tech support 7 times in my life... Once 10 years ago for Windows ME, and six times in the last six months! Each of those six times for separate EA games that either didn't work because of something in the game itself, or that relies on some sort of stable connection with ea servers, or was so flawed and buggy that it annoyed me to the point I actually broke down and called them.

As a video game fan, I would rather wait a longer time and PAY MORE for a better, fully polished and finished product, than to have some half done turd that needs a year worth of patches and editing to make even barely playable.

I cannot play The Sims 3 anymore because of this expansion and it's massive glitches and errors, and I am having serious thoughts about Buying ANYTHING from EA ever again!

title: Best get fit wii game I've tried.
text:
I took the time to read quite a few reveiws and have to say I'm glad I went with the majority on this one. I bought it yesterday and started the 30 day challege. I set it to a light workout. Let me tell you I only lasted for 17 min and about 30 sec. Though they are 20 min I'm guessing the game relized that it was about to kill me and stoped. From some of the bad reviews there are some legitamate complaints (sorta).

No left hand support (though for most of the exercises I can't see this being a problem, however I'm going to bring over a lefty friend of mine and see how he likes it)

The demonstrations before each exercise getting your heart rate down. While this is true while your learning a particular exercise once you have it down you can skip it.

The music. Not the best but honestly you can play your own once you have the exercises down and don't need any help from the trainer talking.(none of the exercises were hard to get down)

Those are the biggest complaints I saw and I don't think either apply to me in the least. Loved my first day and hopefully will last the full 30 days. I doubt this is for people who are already in shape. This is for lazy people like I've been for years. And I have to say... if you actually want to use this to loose weight you'll have to eat right as well... don't think you can do this for 20 min a day and get awesome results while you are still downing a Big Mac every day. Once I master this I'll probably try and get on a more traditional exercise routine.

title: A Tremendous Product
text:
I admit I came from a skeptical perspective when I first bought this product. I'd read mixed things online. A buddy of mine had one, though, and said it worked great. Still, I was worried about the quality with Nyko having a questionable reputation, as well as potential overheating issues, etc. This is my experience.

As long as you follow the directions, installation is simple. You do need another hard drive to expand the storage, I chose the 1TB SeaGate [[ASIN:B01MFAITZ1 Seagate 500GB Barracuda Sata 6GB/s 128MB Cache 2.5-Inch 7mm Internal Bare/OEM Hard Drive (ST500LM030)]] and it's given me no issues thus far.

I think it's incredibly useful that Nyko allows you to use the original 2.5" hard drive as well. That means you don't have to redownload anything that you've already got stored. Now, I did it one small minor issue where after switching back to the 2.5" original hard drive to play Batman: Arkham Knight [[ASIN:B00IQCRKT8 Batman: Arkham Knight - PlayStation 4]] it wasn't recognzing the DLC on a secondary profile within the PS4. This was easily remedied by restoring licenses. I'm hoping this isn't an issue down the road and for now I'm not going to let it affect the rating.

I've had the product for a full day and have experienced no overheating or issues I can mention. However, I will update this review with any changes, etc. As it stands now, because it's fully operational and working great, it's got 5/5 for me.

title: The ultimate Animal Crossing Experience.
text: This is the first Animal Crossing game I've played since the original, and the series has managed to take significant strides forward, while maintaining the core experience. It is an almost perfect modern adaptation of what makes the series so charming and addictive. Like many games out there that rely on your own creativity to enhance the experience, you'll find yourself spending 100s of hours in the game. My only "cons" are that I wish the online was more streamlined and fleshed out for visiting other islands. And I wish there were a few more official buildings/activities to add to the experience. These are extremely minor nitpicky things, that don't bring down the incredible game. And yes, everyone shares the same island, but after the first couple weeks, there is nothing the second player can't do that the first player can (despite the factually wrong reviews you'll see everywhere about it). This mechanic has always been a staple of Animal Crossing, encouraging you to share the experience with your family, and it absolutely works. Don't hesitate, and this is a must buy!

title: fix for hard drives over 2 tb.
text: Ok so I have the answer to most peoples probems. When I got this it was easy clear instructions on how to install and it was fast and easy. did everything like it said to do and so I downloaded over 260 gb worth of games that I had previously had downloaded on my psn account with no flaw but actually ran over on my limit from xfinity, so beware and watch how much you try to download in a month. I used a Toshiba 3 tb 7200 rpm 3.5" drive and everything seem to be going good so I put in rest mode so they could all be downloaded by sometime next day. well when I went to play the games downloaded I kept getting errors an wouldn't even let me play and all my disc based games kept getting a different error telling you to delete game and reinstall. so im like ok this is crazy. try to call nyko support on and off all day and no one taking calls so I emailed them and got a reply. finally after few emails back and forth I found out the solution they fell to mention in all the pages of instruction sheets. if you already booted it up and installed or downloaded anything your gonna have to redo everything again. meaning your gonna have to intialize your hard drive again. because if you ever download or install anything and then put in rest mode it will not play games on anything more than 2 tb. so After you first install your new drive and as soon as you boot it up in safe mode and pick the last option to initialize your playstation it will finish that then it will load your newest update from your usb stick. then it will come back up with a menu with the rest mode options. I think there are four, and you can only uncheck 3 of them. I couldn't uncheck the one that lets you start playstion from the playstation app from your phone or whatever. so after you uncheck that continue on with everything else and then you can download your games and install your disc without any problems at all. just make sure to never put in rest mode and always turn off instead until sony does an update to support hard drivers over 2 tb.  Hope this helps someone because it was frustrating to me and I almost returned it.

title: A Wannabe Knockoff of Itself
text:
Never has a game frustrated me to tears before this game. I have played every single Animal Crossing title (sans the original N64 version, Dobutsu no Mori e+, Amiibo Festival, and Pocket Camp; only because I don’t have a Japanese N64, a Japanese GC, or a WiiU, and I don’t believe in micro-transactions), and I am thoroughly disappointed. Not mad, not salty, just disappointed. I have played this game for just over a month, I really did try to enjoy it, but...I just can’t.

First, the staples of the series that made Animal Crossing so unique are just...gone. No gyroids (sans Lloid, but he’s an NPC), the villagers are just not worth talking to most of the time their dialogue is just that bland and boring, and K.K. Slider...Okay. K.K. has always ALWAYS started his performances at 8 P.M. and ended at midnight. What happens when I pull up the game after getting a three star rating? An IMMEDIATE performance by K.K.! It wasn’t even 8 o’ clock! Why? Just WHY? Is it really worth interrupting my time? Can’t you just wait until 8?! Just why? And just tonight I saw he was already out on the plaza, and it wasn’t 8 yet!

Second, are all the things new to the game. There’s crafting (to my understanding this began in PC). I actually like making/customizing new furniture. You can make tools this way, too. The problem with this? With the exception of the ladder and the vaulting pole, tools BREAK! There’s no reason for this, and it bothers me every time I have to drop whatever I am doing, just because my net or fishing rod or shovel falls apart on me and I have to go make or buy a new one!

One of the few things that hasn’t changed is the museum. Blathers is still the curator, and I actually like the layout in this one. One of the best for the museum I have ever seen. I like going there, just to hang out.

The Nooklings (Timmy and Tommy) also run the shop in this game, just like they did in New Leaf. However, when you upgrade the shop, you get items with prices comparable to Gracie Grace’s merchandise.

Terraforming...I guess is fun. But it’s also really time consuming. I haven't even gotten my island the way I wanted for that reason. It gets tedious and tiring after awhile.

There’s no warning if there is a scorpion nearby. In previous games, there would be a distinct hissing noise if you were close to one. Here? If you don’t see it until the last second, you are done for.

Now I know it seems unfair, comparing games to each other, especially those within the same series, but even if this were my first AC, I think most of the complaints would be exactly the same (and deter me from exploring more of the series).

I am disappointed because I expect far better from Nintendo. When they extended the release date for ACNH, I kept thinking “you can’t rush perfection”, but this is far from perfection. They cut so many corners, that this can’t even be called Animal Crossing. I am fully aware there may be updates released down the line, but right now I have some serious doubts that any of them will change my mind. If by some miracle it does, I will gladly update this review. I do plan to play again, but only because one of my villagers has a birthday in a few days. Other than that, I can’t be bothered with this game anymore.

title: Gameplay laggy on 4K TV.  Resolution blurry and not sharp & high quality as you may be hoping for.
text: Disappointed and had higher hopes for this.  After testing the product with its HDMI port, the 2 games I tested (Super Mario 1 and 3) were lagging so badly, the games were completely unplayable on my 48" 4k Samsung Smart TV (6400) which was set into "GAME MODE" at 4:3 aspect ratio.  I tested the system with the AV cables on the same TV and no lag was apparent.  I own 2 other HDMI NES systems, the RetroUSB AVS and Kevtris Hi-Def Nes and no lag is apparent on the same TV.  Therefore the system's HDMI output is not compatible with my 4K TV causing the unplayable lag.  I did however test it on an older Panasonic LCD 32" TV and there was no lag, but the TV would not allow me to properly display it in 4:3 mode so it could only be played stretched out.  The image quality, although much improved from composite, is still lacking greatly from other HD NES systems out there.  Although it's outputting at 720, this looks to be 480.  There is a blurr in the resolution and is not as sharp as you may hope for.  See photos.  Lastly, the colors are way over saturated which can be fixed with the TV setting, but a hassle to do.  In conclusion, if I were you, I’d put out the extra $150 for the Retrousb AVS.

title: Workout for the Complete Klutz!
text:
Let me begin by explaining I'm a 38 years old female, approximately 25 lbs over a healthy weight and tragically uncoordinated. I don't enjoy sports and I was the last kid picked in gym as a kid.

With all of that said...I love EA Sports Active

I have been doing Wii Fit for about 2 months, but I wanted to change it up a bit.

1) The leg strap stays put if it's against my skin instead of fabric. Not a single problem as long as I'm not trying to put it over pants or shorts.

2) The resistance band appears to be fairly flimsy, but I can adjust it easily based on how much slack I leave in it. I'm 5' 3" so it can be long and provide no resistance, but if I fold it a little at the bottom and stand on it, I get perfect resistance. The important thing is I'm in total control.

3) The 30 Day Challange is fun. It's something a little different every day. Even though I can't walk and chew gum under normal circumstances, the work outs are basic enough that I haven't hurt myself or broken any furniture AND I'm sweating like a real athlete.

4) I have found the wiimote and chuck to be very responsive. When I get an error message about something the trainer isn't liking, if I look at the little picture of the Trainer, I usually find that Yep...I'm doin' it wrong.

5) On any day I can choose to not do the exercize that it has planned for me. I can uncheck something if for instance I have bad knees or in my case, because I'm too lazy to do jump lunges (but I do feel guilty later).

6) Strangely, my avatar looks just like me. I wish I could have her as my Mii.

My complaints are minor.
1) It doesn't track my weight -- that's o.k. I do my Wii Body Test everyday anyway to stay consistant.

2)The daily lifestyle survey doesn't do much for me other than to remind me that my vegetable intake is abyssmal.

3) I think I'd prefer a wirelss nunchuck as there have been some unfortunate cord incidents during high knee lifts and side jumps.

Overall, I'm loving it and my husband is giving my "Body by Wii" rave reviews.

title: UPDATE WITHIN:6 TB Hard Drive Works Great!
text:
UPDATE : Sony has released update 3.15 on January 13th, 2016. This update allows larger hard drives to be used natively in rest mode with the PS4. I have a 6tb drive, and it works perfectly now. No more messing with shutting it down or turning it on. Everything now works as it should.

I purchased this enclosure in order to upgrade my ps4 to a 6TB hard drive.

The enclosure comes in some pretty nice packaging, and is easy to get out.

The instructions are pretty clear and precise, and installation was a breeze.

Once installed, I loaded up my ps4 with new firmware, and all worked well.

At first I kept my playstation in rest mode, and had issues turning it back on, but after searching on the internet I found a solution that will allow you to use rest mode without the ps4 going into safe mode all the time.

TIPS

Using Rest Mode with 6TB Hard Drive
Rest mode can be used with larger hard drives but when turning it on you must physically press the power button, and hold it for about 6 seconds. If you turn on the ps4 this way it will not boot into the safe mode asking you to reinstall the firmware. About 99% of the time I do it this way my ps4 will turn on fine, and any game that was downloaded in rest mode has worked for me.

It's a bit of a hassle but the convenience of using rest mode to download games, and updates is worth it along with the extra storage space.

When turning on my ps4 this way I have encountered very little problems. While it is a bit annoying it is still worth it, and everything else works perfectly. I highly recommend this if you are looking to upgrade your ps4's hard drive.

EDIT: I am having issues with rest mode now.

My ps4 did have a power outage, and now it seems to always boot into rest mode. I am not sure if the outage is the cause, but I just wanted to notify all of you. My ps4 doesn't have anything to download anymore so that may be it as well. I am thinking of doing a reinstall to test, and will update once everything is completed.

EDIT 2: It seems that when the ps4 has something downloading it will work in rest mode, and shut down properly. But if there is nothing downloading the ps4 does not know how to shut down the large hard drive, and that is how the safe mode issue is caused. I also can't shut down the ps4 unless something is downloading, but modes have issues.

title: Good But Somethings Is Wrong.....
text:
As I write this, I see that this game has a 4 star average rating.
Please don't misunderstand, I liked this game but I struggled to find reasons to give this game 3 stars instead of 2.
The game is lacking in a few areas.
First, you never really seem to know what you are supposed to be doing. For example, on the very first level I was told I needed a key. I searched around for an hour and right before I was going to shut the game off, I tried the door again and it said I had the key.
The next few levels are basically the same way. You never really have a clear understanding of what you need to do. You always know why you are supposed to do it, but not specifically WHAT you need to do to go further in the game.
Second, you can only stay outside in the cold for a few minutes of gameplay or you die. Why in the world would a military group go into the sub zero temperatures and not dress warm enough is just plain stupid. You will spend HOURS, HOURS, HOURS, running around in the snow looking for who knows what just to run back into the little houses to get warm. Its frustratingly stupid.
Third, you will encounter literally hundreds of little tiny "things" that get seriously repetitive after, oh I would say the first 578,352 time you kill them.
Fourth, the game features "squad based" interaction and the squad members "trust" in you to preform simple tasks.
I would ask a simple question, do you really think a military medic would refuse to heal you because he saw a small "thing" 20 gameplay minnutes ago and is still so freaked out he does nothing? The idea was a good one, but it really takes away from the gameplay.
Last, I want to touch on some of the positive points. The game can make you jump from time to time. It can be a little scary early on until you get used to the "things" running around. I think the music was superbly done for the game. I also think the graphics are not half bad. Not as good as some, but better than others. The most realistic sounds you will find in a game as well. The way the snow crunches under your feet is well done.
Overall, I think the idea of this game was great I just think that some of the features take away from what could have been a super game!
Better to rent this one then to buy it...

title: Imperfect, but many good ideas
text:
SimCity 4 is the latest in the long-survived SimCity series of games. Much like the others, the goal of the game is to contruct a burgeoning metropolis from the ground up. There are no set goals or parameters, it is very much like a sandbox where you can dictate your own expectations and try to meet them.
As the Mayor, you lay roads and zone land for development as residential, commercial, industrial, seaport, airport, and others. You build power plants and water pumping stations. You approve and reject city ordinances, keep the city safe from crime with police stations, and entertain your people with massive stadiums. All while keeping an eye on your annual income. Make no mistake - it's complicated, filled with micromanagement, and sometimes feels more like "work" than a "game." But the rewards for your labor are pleasant to watch.
From SimCity 3000, SimCity 4 has several major deviations - for better and for worse. Here's a brief rundown of them:
- In a nod to The Sims (which you can also import into your city), SimCity 4's world is somewhat persistent. You have a large "world" to develop and any given SimCity occupies a space in this world. But, they are all interconnected. The problem here is that "neighbor deals" - a substantial source of income in previous games - suddenly cease exist. You are responsible for building your neighboring cities. It would have been much cooler if the map was already dominated by a few larger cities. On the other hand, specialization is key as the world grows. You'll find yourself building "the industrial city," the sleepy "residential city," and so forth. Another annoying side effect of the world system is that backing up your cities and work is rather strange - as you have to dig around in the game directories to figure out where the heck they stored your work.
- There is only one difficulty level, and it starts tough. In some ways, I appreciate this. Early on, you have to be a serious penny-pincher, viciously slashing funding for schools and other public services just to make ends meet and become profitable. This feels much more realistic as most modern US cities face the same troubles. On the other hand, it makes the game hostile to newcomers, and don't expect those tremendous skyscrapers to appear anytime soon. You'll be the proud Mayor of a slum for a while.
- The game makes a distinction between streets and roads. It goes insofar as to automatically place the weaker of the two when you zone land. The problem is, the automatic placement doesn't always make the best use of land, nor jive with your intentions or existing road layouts. You can't turn off this "feature" either, which is disappointing.
- On the flip side, the game has a neat implemention of day and night cycles. Perhaps the coolest aspect of the game, early in the morning you witness a mass exodus of automobiles and vehicles from the residential zones to the industrial zones. As night falls, the street lamps and headlights turn on and the exodus happens in reverse. It's really a sight to behold and a testament to some of the intricate programming that's behind the game.
However the game was, and still is, quite buggy. While recent patches have improved its stability, SimCity 4 is still quite vulnerable. There have been cases where it would crash the venerable Windows XP such that a reset was necessary. The game is also on the sluggish side, so you'll want a high-end computer for this one. This thing taxes my machine more than Unreal Tournament 2003 does!
It's for these reasons that I find SimCity 4 a difficult game to judge. While I appreciate the inspired focus and vision of the game and just how beautifully many parts came together, the performance and stability issues cannot be ignored. So, in closing, I rate this game as many gaming magazines have - giving Maxis the benefit of the doubt and an above-average rating. Hopefully they'll iron out the last of the severe bugs in future patches.
By the way, I'd like to make special note of the game's music. SimCity 4 has an absolutely fabulous soundtrack that easily ranks as one of the best I've heard in a long while, surpassing even its predecessor in my opinion. You want to listen to the included MP3s outside of the game - it's that amazing. From hurried rush hour beats to soaring atmospheric pieces, this soundtrack is breathtaking!

title: Love it!
text:
Let me start by saying I own Wii Fit, My Fitness Coach, and Gold's Gym Cardio Workout. I have had EA Active Personal Trainer for 9 days, and I have to say that I prefer Active over the others.

I like the variety of exercises and how wearing the leg strap encourages the user to keep good form when performing reps. Some have talked about this "game" being glitchy. I think the "glitches" are probably more due to user error than anything else because I have not had any problems except when I am holding the controls incorrectly. I think this is also true of those who have complained about a falling leg strap. I have not had any trouble with the leg strap; I put it as high as possible on my thigh, making sure the front of the strap is facing completely forward.

Though not fit, I am not horribly out of shape either. Active gives me a very good workout. The day after the first time I used Active, I was in so much, good, pain. The trainer, while very peppy, is helpful because he/she will call you on it if you are trying to slack. I like that.

Also, I have fun exercising. I look forward to getting out of bed and starting with exercise through using Active. I enjoy Active so much that I will exercise twice a day sometimes. That's saying a lot since I really hate getting out of bed any earlier than necessary and hate intentional exercise.

Like others, I have found the resistance band to be pathetic, but that was easily solved by a trip to Target. Another complaint I have is there are not core or flexibility exercises, though that isn't that big of a deal because I can use one of my other "games" to get those exercises. These two reasons are why I gave a four star rating instead of the full five.

Overall, I highly recommend this "game" to my friends. As others have pointed out, Active is cheaper than a gym membership and less stressful (if you hate going to the gym for fear others are staring), and so much fun!

title: A great addition to the collection!
text:
I currently own all of the major Wii work out games (sans Jillian Michaels) and this is my favorite. I hate My Fitness Coach, am neutral about Wii Fit and love Golds Gym. That being said, I think EA Sports Active is my favorite of them all. I think that it provides a better all around workout than Gold's Gym and in general provides a good workout. I am an ex-ahtlete, with knee and foot problems. I miss running outside and playing sports, but I experience a ton of pain and am forced to compromise my workouts because of it. I like EA sports because you can select the exercises you wish to participate in (or avoid- for me some of the lunges) and it is not too high impact. Also, I am a big cheater when it comes to exercise and often go too fast, which results in my workout not being as good or intense as it should be. While many people complain about the game essentially waiting for you to get in the right position, I enjoy it, as it ensures I am not cheating and going to fast.

I have 2 major complains about this game. First and foremost, the leg strap REALLY irritates my skin (which is super sensitive). Because it is so hot here, I don't want to wear tights or pants and don't own any longer shorts. That could help my skin, but even right now I have a little bit of a rash from the leg strap. Secondly, it is kind of bulky holding the resistance strap (sometimes I use my own tube, which is even worse) and nunchuck/remote. On top of that, you need to make sure you are holding everything correctly. Its not that big of an issue, but still.

I would definitely recommend this game. I build up a sweat and get a good workout. I still make sure that I do some other form of exercise too, but this is a great addition to my wii collection!

title: Works up a sweat!
text:
Pros:

- Transitions from one exercise to the next (unlike Wii Fit, where you have to go back to the menu between each).
- Follows your movement (unlike My Fitness Coach, which is more like a DVD that changes up the exercises - while that is good, it gives no feedback on how you're doing).
- Exercises don't take up a lot of space, good for those with little kids who tend to walk right in the middle of grapevies and other such exercises.
- Balance board (while under-incorporated in the game) is incorporated in interesting and unique ways. Also, if you don't have one, it's okay, your workout will not suffer.
- Leg strap makes running in place easier to track than the Wii Fit (can anyone say, "You're not keeping a steady pace" ? Just because you pump your hands too much when you don't have pockets).

Cons :

- Could incorporate more stretching and yoga.
- Balance board is under-utilized (still useful and good where it is used, just that there could have been more uses for it, i.e. a hula hoop game).

In my opinion, pros far outweigh the cons, and it's worth EVERY penny. Best exercise/fitness "game" out there.

title: Review-bombing doesn't reflect the quality of this product.
text:
This is a fantastic game. Let's get that nailed in right out of the gate, because while I agree with the complaints about Nintendo's handling of cloud saves, individual islands and so on, I don't think that reflects so poorly on the game that it deserves to be review-bombed. Though I do believe review-bombing has its place and if it helps, then so be it, I won't object.

This is the BEST Animal Crossing game. Period. It's not only visually stunning, it has tons of improvements large and small that have made this a joy to continue to play. Usually I'm done with Animal Crossing by now. I buy a copy, I play it for a month or two, then I drop it and rarely ever come back unless really bored and only for a few minutes, even for holiday events.

But with the wide depth of customization options for your villager, your home and your island, this really is the most control we've ever had in an Animal Crossing game.

To counter the negativity, let's point out some of the pros:

First, you can customize your character right from the start, rather than getting random hair and face options. You have limited options at the start, but you can unlock more later and it's as simple as checking your face in a mirror to change literally any aspect of your little avatar's personal appearance.

Storage items are linked to your house storage. Namely your clothing. So basically not only will your wardrobe serve as a wardrobe (even if placed outdoors), but so will your fridge, your cooler, your safe, etc. It's a little silly, but honestly it's a nice way of having a way of changing your outfit wherever you go while blending the furniture in. Don't want a wardrobe outside just to change? Put a fishing cooler by the shore or something. It's great.

Second, you can place furniture items outside. This, combined with the much-touted island designer tool (place paths, pools or rivers of water and cliffs), allows you to make your town look the way you want it like New Leaf could only DREAM of achieving. Gone are the public works projects for a bench that take a whole day and a ludicrous amount of funding (and weird celebrations about a piece of furniture being delivered). Gone are the days of feeling like your town would take YEARS to look the way you want it to, with cheap paths that hitting the wrong button over would get rid of (though that feature is still there for custom design paths and I HATE IT; fix this, Nintendo).

Now if you want to have a bench outside Able Sisters for your villagers to rest their buns, you just find a bench (or build one yourself with the handy new crafting system) and place it. That's it. You can even move it around like it was inside of your house.

Third, as mentioned, CRAFTING. Many people were worried about this when it was introduced and there are valid complaints about it that even I have, but this is 100% a change for the better, it really is. Yes, your tools now break. And that sucks. Especially since all tools break now and you can't even check durability, but making them is easy enough and that's only a small part of what this system offers. There are tons of basic, unique and holiday-oriented craftable items that you can make over and over if you're dedicated enough to find the recipes, the materials and make them. And since getting recipes is a daily affair (every day there will be a bottle on the beach with a random, hopefully new, recipe in it), you're going to discover tons of cool new stuff every week, as long as you keep turning Animal Crossing on and messing about.

Fourth, Nook Miles. I don't think I've heard anyone complain about this. And no one should. It's nothing but a good thing to give you incentives to do stuff like fish, catch bugs, hunt fossils, talk to villagers, etc. It's encouragement in the form of "miles" to get you to play the game, where you can then redeem those miles for special recipes and items for yourself and your town. Custom phone case, fence recipes (fences are great for customization and another perk of the new game), furniture items, nook miles tickets to go to a randomized island and hunt collectible fish/bugs and resources.

You'll first start off with static, one-time-only rewards like a couple hundred miles for catching 10 bugs, then a thousand or so for 100, then catch 200+ and you get 2,000 miles (along with titles for your villager's passport, if that at all interests you, which you also get miles for editing once). Then after paying off your vacation package with those earned miles, you can build a house and start earning miles in the form of daily, renewable objectives (shoot a balloon down for some miles or assess x number of fossils) so you never run out of things to keep working towards if you want to keep yourself busy. It's great motivation to keep playing, though eventually it does become a bit bland, I won't lie. Still, I like having it.

Overall the game has its faults, though, too. Among them:

You can't have more than one island per Switch. Not with a second cartridge (save data is stored on the system, not on the microSD card or cartridge), not with a digital copy (again, save data is on the system) and not with a different profile (profiles are used per player on the island and you're limited to 8 total player characters per island... meaning if you have nine people on the same system for some reason, which can happen, someone's missing out). You need another system in order to have a second island.

I hate this. I really hate this. It's worthy of criticism.

I have to share my system with my mother and my niece and nephew. I'm not going to be that prick uncle who isn't going to let the kids play on his system, but I knew ahead of time how their "interactions" with my island would go.

I'll share some of them with you:

I laid out a nice stone path months ago. Helped my niece build up her house by paying off her debt, getting her tons of furniture so she can customize her house's look when she came over if she wanted to play and put in a lot of effort towards making my town look nice.

What does my nephew do, being an irresponsible and thoughtless kid (as most kids are until they get older... hopefully)? He picks up fences, benches, bushes I planted, tosses items in random spots, puts down a random item he got in place of something I had already painstakingly decorated the area with and uses the complimentary island designer tool to mess up the paths I had set. For no reason, just deleting the paths I made because it seemed fun to him. I can't tell you the number of times I had to tell him to stop picking things up and that if he wanted to help decorate he should do it without destroying what his grandmother and I had already done or to find another way to entertain himself (the classic AC way, with a net and a fishing rod). And that doesn't even include when he got into the options and deleted his sister's character from the game, erasing all progress made and forcing us to rebuild her character from scratch. That was *fun*.

I get it. Kids are a disaster and they walk through every situation like a hurricane out to destroy the world, but Nintendo knows this. They're a family-oriented gaming company. They built toys back in the day for Nook's sake. They could have averted this EASILY. But instead they decided to have one island on your system and no others. You couldn't just plop the kids onto their own island to decorate and destroy at their leisure.

Unless of course you fork out $200-300+ for a new system.

You see why people are pissed? It's almost as if Nintendo is trying to exploit its longtime fans by holding their islands hostage. You can't even backup your save data for the game because god forbid someone duplicate their furniture and have TWO house ferns instead of one! Gasp! The horror! A non-competitive game having exploits and cheats! That'd ruin it for... literally no one, because no one else has to care.

I get it. I get why people are angry. Oh dear sweet Nookington to I get it. But even with those issues (and others I just don't feel like getting into right now), this is still the BEST Animal Crossing to date. It is a joy to play.

It's just not so great when you have kids to watch after. I'm honestly grateful they don't come over that often or I'd never want to play again. Cleaning up their messes got old after the first time. It's INCREDIBLY disheartening to build up your island with love and attention only for someone to sweep through like a natural disaster and rip it apart and having no way to stop it other than staring at the game the entire time, micromanaging their play session like some sort of overbearing nanny.

title: A great supplement to working out
text:
I have been using the Wii Active for the past five days and have done 6 of the workouts.

Most of the exercises range from 15 minute workouts to 35 minute workouts. They divide the intensity from light, medium, and heavy. The custom preset workouts give a wide range of variation such as workouts that focus more on cardio, resistance for either upper body or lower body, and sport games.

Most of the workouts push you fairly well. The first time I tried it, I was unable to complete the heavy workout, which is a blow to my ego since I go to the gym 3 to 4 times a week! You get a good sweat after each workout and is really geared for all types of fitness levels. There is enough variety that prevents you from getting bored in the workouts and are well-designed in that they start easy and then get harder as the workout progresses. Also they will redo certain exercises to target certain muscles during the workout. For instance during the first workout of the 30 day challenge, it will concentrate more on quads and calves. Therefore you'll do more squat jumps and kickbacks during the workout and the repeats occur right when your feeling the burn in your legs. It gives you that "evil gym coach feeling" we all had in high school, but nothing so bad where you're not having fun.

In addition to keeping track of the workouts you do with Wii active, there is also a journal in the main menu that allows you to add activities from other sports and also keep track of things like diet, sleep, and stress. It's a fun tool, but nothing that would greatly impact someone's health.

The personal trainer feedback is decent, but gets a little repetitive just like any video game with a use announcers. You can adjust how much the trainer encourages you or turn it off completely. The music that comes with the exercise routine fits in well, but is not mind blowing by any means.

Cons:
As mentioned before the resistance band is pretty weak. I did buy some higher resistance strength bands, but had some difficulty holding the Wii remote in my hand because the resistance band handles tend to be larger as the resistance increases.

It is a great option to workout with my wife in the preset custom mode. However if my profile is activated and I had her on to workout with her, wii active does not keep track of the hours she accumulates. So despite working with two people wii active can only keep track of one profile at a time.

There appears to be very little core strengthening. However I have not done the majority are workouts but I'm surprised that have not encountered any exercises that really focus on the core.

Overall:
The Wii active is really what I hoped the Wii fit would've brought. There is very little pauses between exercises, they have great custom made routines, and work you into a great sweat. The Wii active is a great tool for people who cannot find time to go to the gym for an hour or two. This program is great for toning muscles in getting your heart rate up. However for those really interested in losing weight and building muscle, this program is a great supplement but not an end all replacement to the gym.

title: Good In Theory, But Lacking In Practice
text:
I read a bunch of the reviews about this feeling more like a "real workout" than Wii Fit, and was sold enough to give it a shot - after two extended periods working with it, I'm going to be retiring it - it's just very frustrating and feels like it's "forcing a square peg into a round hole" - it's not intuitive and natural to work out like this...it's very awkward and I feel like it's probably a slightly damaging too - certainly to form. Mainly I'll be echoing some of the other middle-of-the-road reviews - with a few additional comments from my personal experience.

Pros:
1. It is nice to be able to dial up a full routine rather than like on Wii Fit, where you have to constantly be selecting new exercises.

2. The lower-body exercises aren't as clunky as the upper-body ones, and you can get a pretty good leg workout if you follow along.

Cons:
1. If the resistance that the game comes with isn't enough for you, using real resistance bands while also having to hold the controller/nunchuk in your hands is extremely awkward - and when you hold them in a way that the Wii accepts your movements, it really messes up your form and is very uncomfortable.

2. I'm not a large person (5'10", 175) - but some of the exercises just don't make sense while holding the controllers - like doing shoulder presses...the nunchuk cord is constantly slapping you in the face and threatening to choke you...it just feels unnatural and it's not a lot of fun. I also feel like I'm going to break the controllers while having them in the middle of a grip and doing bicep curls - that doesn't feel like something that could be sustained long term...and I also constantly feel like I'm going to pull the nunchuk cable out.

3. The vocal feedback from the game is extremely repetitive and annoying, and has nothing to do with what you're doing. There are about 10 phrases (max) that keep getting repeated, and even if you're struggling with trying to keep the leg band on (to echo another review - it either feels like a tourniquet or it falls off constantly) and aren't doing anything but adjusting it, you'll be getting perky positive feedback!

4. You have to do weird movements with the controllers to signify to the Wii that you've completed a rep - and it takes a while to figure out what you're doing wrong and why nothing is registering. Then you're like "oh, it's because I have to do this little wrist flip at the end of this movement" - which has nothing to do with the exercise itself...very annoying.

5. Sometimes as a result of #4 but sometimes not, you get feedback that doesn't make any sense...I dare you to try doing jump lunges without constantly getting feedback to "slow down". My wife and I tried this relentlessly, and short of being in "The Matrix", we can't fathom how we'd be able to jump any "slower".

I could go on but won't - there are a lot of glowing reviews here and I'm sure that if you're not super serious and want to get into a regular routine of some low to medium impact workouts this is a pretty decent tool. But there need to be a few more voices of reason on here setting the proper expectations for this package.

Until the Wii really catches up, I think I'm gonna lace up the ol' sneakers and head out for a run. =)

title: One of the best I've played in years
text:
The most oft-repeated phrase in any review for "Viva Pinata" is that it's "not just for kids." This is not without good reason. While the packaging and overall feel of the game is as bright and shiny as a candied marble and is specifically designed to draw kids in, the gameply is consistently entertaining and is challenging enough to daunt any experienced adult gamer...

I'd even go so far as to say that this is one of the most original and interesting games to come along in years. It's rare that I become so engrossed in what's going on in a given game that hours pass, seemingly, with speed of a blink of an eye- but such has been the case, since I installed Viva Pinata.

Now- a word of caution: I'm running the game on a dual 3.1 GHZ system with a Radeon 512 MB 3d accellerator, and the game automatically put my graphic preferences at the lowest level, when I started it up. I manually changed things to medium, which resulted in a very pleasing improvement in graphics. However, my system now routinely ratchets up to overdrive, during play. One can only assume that you need a pretty hot system to view the game in its full glory. That having been said, the game plays smoothly as silk, and lacks the lags during autosave that have been a bane to Xbox gamers.

In closing, I heartily reccommend VP. To those gamers who reject this game because of the "cute factor," I can only say:

It must suck to be you...

title: build and watch - that's it
text:
There is no strategy to SimCity 4 - I thought that SimCity 3000 had been a botched attempt by the designers, but in truth it appears the direction that they are heading with the SimCity series is simply the "Build and Watch" approach. The graphics are pretty good, although it seems to me that if they are really going to stick with this "build and watch" approach to gaming that they should expand the number of buildings - even a tiny city can easily have ten of the same "Bob's Grease Pit" ... I mean come on fellas... choose your weapon, but do it well!

I was eagerly awaiting the widely touted 'multi-region' capability (wherein multiple cities could be connected and interdependant) but this too was a fairly large dissapointment. The cities are utterly independent of each other, and the ability to create deals between two cities that you have created does not add notably to the gaming experience.

Also worth mentioning, the city map sizes are considerably smaller. Although there are some neat new highway building features, it just doesn't ever feel like there is enough space to warrant a highway in these maps. I suppose they were betting on the interdependency of the regions to give the feeling of a larger world to settle, but as I mentioned this is non-existant. Perhaps if they had given the capability for your city to actually overflow onto the next region (as opposed to starting a new city, with a new bank roll, on the neighboring region) the small map size would have been acceptable.

The Rush Hour expansion pack is supposed to let you walk individual sims from one house to the next, etc, etc... I have not even toyed with this option because I don't feel that SimCity is the right venue for this sort of activity. When playing SimCity I honestly have no interest in manipulating individual Sims, but rather would prefer to manage the "city". So for me, this feature (to which indeed an entire expansion pack was devoted) added nothing to the game.

All in all SimCity 4 plays like a loose collection of ideas. The gaming aspects are nearly completely eroded. It feels like there were 13 different developers who each had their own idea about how the game should play. The result is that it barely retains the status of being a game. The small map sizes and micro-management of sims kept yielding me to the thought "Why didn't they call this one SimTown and make a REAL SimCity sequel instead?!?". Do not expect more than 4 hours of enjoyable game time from this one. Somewhere along the way EA lost site of what constitutes a game. Although I was eagerly awaiting this sequel, I give it two thumbs down.

title: For two people
text:
Considering there are many reviews already on the singleplayer, I figured I would discuss the multiplayer option.
There are many choices...you choose "Workout with a Friend" and can do some special cardio exercises, preset exercises, and exercises from the Six Week Challenge ("Workout Day 1", etc, etc for six weeks). One caution before the review: You do need the second set of leg bands and resistance band for this to work-easily available.

I'm a regular Wii exerciser and have the whole set (Wii Fit, Just Dance, EA Active original, Hottest Party, etc, etc) and have done the 1 Month Challenge multiple times on the original Active and consider myself in reasonable, medium-intensity health.

My first pair workout was with a friend who was not very in shape and hasn't exercised more than a game of golf in the past ten years. We did the cardio workout for 30 minutes and surprisingly we were both tired but not frustrated. We each got two individual intensity bars of how we were doing and a team score. For all intents and purposes though, we were two individuals.

The second time, I played with another friend, who is more of a regular exerciser but disliked the Original Active individual setting. This time, it was more of a team as we played the generic island workout. For example, we might have 160 boxing shots. Our scores add up, so one person can get 100 and the other person can get 60. This is great if you have two matched friends, but I can see this being not as productive if one person is in much better shape than the other.
