title: Good ideas, sketchy implementation
text:
SimCity 4 has a great deal to offer the patient gamer. It is challenging, variable, and allows for extended amounts of gameplay. The features of educational incentives and inter-city trading of services offers the player proper motivation to build a workable city setup. In addition, the terraforming tools are easy to use, and can quickly shape the lands to the user specifications. Finally, the amount of variety offered to the visual representation of your city helps reduce the "xeroxed" effect that the previous SimCity games produced. Each city tends to develop its own special look and feel.
On the negative side, the game is slow paced, the controls are spotty, and the demands on the system resources are high. The greatest hurdle to the gaming experience is the time it takes to develop a city to scale. The inability to gain enough funds to maintain and develop your city rapidly results in a great deal of sitting and watching, rather than interacting with the game. Also, it becomes very easy to exhaust your funds (fortunately, SimCity 4 offers financial deals in term of army bases and missile test sites to offer additional revenues to your city), which results in the gameplay being reduced to watch and wait. The zoning tools and road tools occassionally have difficulty tracking the mouse position, and results in unintentionally zoned lands, and more lost resources. The feature to automatically add roads also serves to slow down the ability to quickly design your city. Also, the ability to alter the flow of time for your city can sometimes get stuck, and requires reactivation to get the timeflow started again. Finally, I operate my SimCity 4 game on a Pentium 4 with 1.4 GigaHertz processor and 768 megs of RAM, and my computer drags and churns when the city reaches sizes over 10 thousand. It can be quite distracting to operate the game under these load conditions, as it lends itself to choppy scrolling and delay of executing actions.
This game has a lot of complexity and thought going for it, but it will probably aggravate and irritate the lest patient gamer.

title: Good and Bad
text:
This is a really good game. The game designers however missed a couple of small things that could elevate this game from "VERY GOOD" to even "GREAT". This small things can make a huge impact to a players gaming pleasure. Couple of things they should change.
1. Difficulty level - Default is easy. Somebody should explain to EA what "EASY" means. I just think they could have made the default to medium and have a setting of easy that could cater to younger audience. Skilled gamers then could easily set it to hard if they want a tougher game.
2. Cheap Death - Instead of instant death, use the life bar for damage. Dying because of falling rocks that you cant even see is no fun.
3. Tight Controls - The controls are not tight enough. They should take a cue from SOUL CALIBUR on fight control. The combos are pretty nice to look at, its just that executing them feels a bit wierd to me (it seems I'm pressing the button to fast, might be my timing is off simply because I play fighting games too).
4. Saving - Give the player the ability to save the game at any point. Some gamers have a life, they cant stare at the TV too long you know... Now for so-called hardcore arrogant gamers out there, some will say this will make the game too easy. Two words for you, "DONT SAVE".
5. Game Length - I think the game is not that long. This is great too since you get to finish the game quicker. It would have been nicer if the game was a bit longer, like a ton of bonus stages (subquests) that you can play or not play (your choice).
The graphics in this game is absolutely gorgeous. I like the fact that in some levels, my characters are a part of the environment rather than the sole target. The first stage of the hobbits was amazing. A lot of fights all over the place and it remains true to what really happened in the story.
There will always be some comments that this game is a mindless hack-n-slash. This is very true if you always think that way, I mean you can always barge in straight to battle and come up victorious. To me, its up to you to infuse any strategy you seem fit. But hey that's just me...
Overall, I gave the game 4 our of 5 stars simply because I really enjoyed it. It is not perfect but I dont think its far off. I'm not sure if they would be able to make another game using the LOTR characters. I hope they can come up with something. Theres a lot of material in the LOTR saga that can be used. Even though I mentioned a few suggestions, this is one really good enjoyable game.

title: One Island Per Console! Terrible Multiplayer.
text:
Very disappointing. If my review was written based on the multiplayer alone, this game would earn 1 star.

I bought this game for my daughter, but I was also excited to play it myself. After a few days of letting her play and enjoy the newness of it, I started my new game on my switch profile. The game spits you into the first player’s island. You don’t get to choose the island or meet the residents for the first time, and you don’t get to advance the story at all. The only person who can advance the story is the first player. A big problem created by residing on their island is if player 1 already collected all the fruit (or twigs or weeds or whatever) for the day, when you log in to play, you can’t collect any fruit because the trees are barren. This animal crossing installment follows the seasons, so the game won’t respawn that fruit until the real-life next day.

If you actually play couch co-op, one person is the “leader” and one is the “follower”. The leader can play the game per usual, but the follower can only use tools. Anything they pick up in game gets sent to Nook’s recycling bin. If the leader goes too far away from the follower, the follower gets teleported to the leader’s location. I played this way with my daughter for a while and it was boring and frustrating.

She is highly entertained by the game as a single player game. Luckily I only have one child, because if you had multiples, the only way for all of them to enjoy the game would be to buy multiple switch systems and multiple ACNH games.

This was the greatest for the first couple of hours. It was exactly like starting up the original animal crossing on the gamecube and I had such high hopes. Now after my partner had started their person on the island (which again you can only have 1 island per switch ( Why this wasn't just tethered to 1 account that either had online (that we already have to pay for) or each account that actually paid for the game code, instead you literally have to shell out an additional $300+ (because demand is crazy due to COVID-19) just to play with someone in the same household. You really went the greedy route there nintendo.

BEWARE Parents and Partners of more than one gamer in the house. You do not want to get this game, as it will destroy any sense of peace you thought distracting yourselves or the kids with a cutesy fun game should have brought. I have already seen multiple friends no longer talk to each other and even a breakup or two over the terrible game design Nintendo has put forth (I know it's extreme of them but i also had to deal with high tensions in my household). It really is One overlord and the rest of the players are just their slaves, as they can NEVER progress the game, NOR will they ever have the same experience as the first person to startup the Island has. Only they will ever be Nook's favorite and actually be able to make any meaningful decisions. The amount of jealousy this will cause (that's already cased that i've seen) is horrendous and you do not want that added onto everything else given the state of world affairs and being stuck at home in the chaos.

It's so bad that now my partner refuses to touch the game anymore which has killed all joy for me playing on a deserted island, and even resetting it (yes you must LOSE all game progress to change who is the overlord) no longer appeals to them as they were already getting invested with setting up their home and getting a couple upgrades while enjoying the chats with the villages that they recruited. (yeah, it lets them recruit villagers which gives the hope they will be considered equal in Nook's eyes and that he will eventually dole out responsibilities to them so they feel validated, yet oh no. It was just a short term ploy). We had hoped after getting thru the initial stages of the 'tutorial' phase it would be corrected and we'd both be on an even playing field but no such luck because nintendo go greedy. It's now causing such a rift between us and our roommate (who later joined right before my partner stopped playing entirely over this fiasco) that they no longer play either (when they were avid fans of all other previous animal crossing titles) but now its just high tensions all the time. They both want to play, but it's pointless because they don't want to shell out another 360$ cash just to do so on their time, and even my offer of resetting for my partner falls on deaf ears due to the time invested already.

It's completely backfired in nintendo's face being as greedy as they are with this decision to have one ruler and the rest as slaves, that they both have refused to play switch or purchase anything nintenda ever again. (such that they immediately dropped around $200 each on Sony and Microsoft games just to spite Nintendo. (which i'll be honest didn't make too much sense to me, but hey now i have extra games i can play on those consols because guess what Sony and Microsoft didn't do? Get greedy over multiplayer...))

With that said, if you're a solo house/gamer in your house, well congrats, you lucked out and i wish you well as for a while i did enjoy playing this game, but it brought too much tension and frustration to my household so i'll never play again and have requested a return and my money back. For all others, DO NOT BUY THIS GAME, it's not worth the headaches that have ensued.

title: Fun Diversion from Sim 3
text: I really like this expansion pack. For one thing, while your sims are on "vacation" you can bring their skill-building books, etc. and then they have virtually unlimited time to max up abilities. When you leave regular Simland, you return at exactly the same time of day and day you left, as if you never left at all, even if you were gone weeks. Another neat thing is that there are an enormous amount of adventures. It is hard to complete even one or two in one trip. I've taken one trip to France, two to Egypt and one to China and only got Visa level 1 out of 10 levels.. and that's just for one sim. I imagine it would take many generations of sims to experience all the adventures. You also get cool unique items from your travels and two new hobbies: nectar (wine) making and martial-arts. I feel this is an excellent addition to Sims 3, esp for when you've played a long time (as I have) and gotten kind of bored. It spices things up!

title: A better workout...
text:
I had high hopes for this after all the great reviews. I was looking for something more challenging than Wii Fit. Based on the reviews I skipped Wii Active, and went right for More Workouts. Thanks to some other helpful reviews, I bought the accessory kit (so that I would have a leg band to hold the nunchuck) and a stronger resistance band. I would do all of those things again, though I may try Wii Active at some point.

Pros: I like the 6 week challenge...and I have broken a sweat during more than one workout, which is hard to do on the Wii Fit. I also like that it incorporates a number of strength and lunge exercises into each routine...I will not do lunges on my own at the gym (even though they are great), and this makes you do a million. It is better than a workout video, and I like that it schedules the days that I am supposed to work out for me.

Cons: I'd still like it to be a little more challenging. I started at "hard" -- and while it has a few exercises that make me wince (I'm looking at you "leg raises"!), I break a sweat, but I am not gasping for air. (I am active, but would not set any records at a 5k, and probably couldn't finish a 10k :) I'm at workout 15 (out of 24) in the 6 week challenge -- the workouts are getting longer, which is nice -- but like another reviewer mentioned, it is just a repeat of prior exercises from that day. My biggest issue (and the one they probably can't do anything about) is what a pain it is to hold the remotes properly -- to point them in the right direction, not hit a button accidentally, and still pull on a band using the proper form and resistance, is nearly impossible -- especially if you're sweaty. It "yells" at me a lot to stop moving at the end of my rep -- when I am just trying to move the remote back into position.

Takeaway: I'd still buy it, but I'm still looking for the game that can get me to end my gym membership. This does the trick on the days I can't get there, though. I use the balance board, and like it...but will echo other reviews that it is sporadic in what it registers, particularly with squats and the kicks in boxing. I was sore the first couple of days, so it must be doing something new!

My wedding is coming up in less than three months, and I've been using the 30 day challenge on medium to tone up. I'm almost done with the challenge and my arms definitely feel firmer. I'm taking away a star because the wiimote to nun-chuck cable sometimes gets in my way and the sensor doesn't always seem to detect some of the upper body reps immediately. title: A Real Disappointment
text: I enjoyed Sim City 3000 Unlimited a great deal, and I was rather hoping its creators would use it as the jumping-off point for Sim City 4, but they've gotten rid of what I liked about that earlier game and added almost nothing I do like.  Yes, the graphics are sharper and are really nice, but as one reviewer noted before, the game is now far more work than fun.  I think that's a pretty fundamental complaint, really.  I have a pretty powerful computer, and the game operates the way it should, but I must always restart my computer and repair the Internet functions before my system is in working order again after game play.  Too, the cheat code dialogue box rarely opens as it's supposed to do, instead, hitting CTRL X turns the cursor into a smokestack.  I'm going back to Sim City 3000 Unlimited.  I regret my expensive purchase of Sim City 4.

title: Hey Sweden...
text:
I am so happy they made a video game based on "The Thing". I am also happy that the entire game is geared for adults, choc full of general unpleasantness. I got this game 3 days ago and I haven't stopped playing. The controls & format are easy to operate and I have to admit, the game is scary. There are "Things" in the game that look very realistic down to veiny skin and [saliva]. (use the sniper rifle to get a closer look at them, otherwise your dead). Like GTA3, this game is rated-M for a reason, I love playing a game that was designed for me. I'm in my 30's and there is nothing cute or cuddly about this game. It's gruesome, gory, dark, violent and has no redeeming qualities that people want to expose their children too...kinda like the real world. But as an adult, I can say this game is well worth every cent. This will be one of the games that I keep in my PS2 collection, I still have and enjoy some of my older titles I bought when I first purchased my PS2.
Konami and the other developers who created The Thing did an excellent job, the detail and game play is top notch, there are parts of the game where you will jump and just like in the movie (JC's version) ...you don't know who to trust. There is no annoying music soundtrack to distract you, If you look at pictures that are posted on the walls throughout the game you'll see pictures from JC's Movie. The "Things" react like any other animal that wants you dead, they will react to sounds (such as gunshots) follow you up and down stairs and quietly wait for you around corners and dark areas. This game is not easy, I'm having a hard time staying alive. But that's a challenge I like, in this game you'll find out that it's not just a alien threat bent on seeing you dead... You'll find out that if someone in your squad has too much stress and flips out will shoot at anything that moves (including you and the rest of your squad). If you act too weird, you'll get waxed by your squad. If you hang outside in the cold too long, you'll freeze to death.
If your a adult that likes a game geared on the macabre ..."The Thing" is a game you should seriously get. You wont be disappointed.
One tiny little negative thing that I can say about this game that doesn't really matter...
The developers could have went the extra mile and included John Carpenters theme music to the opening / closing credits and the menu screen. ...or even better, had JC himself as a consultant to create the gloomy hopeless feeling he did to his movie.

title: Connects to the Xbox just like any other external drive
text:
I'm giving this 3 out of 5 stars for it's usefulness/practicality. All this device does is act as enclosure for a 3.5" HDD. It uses the USB 3.0 for connection to the Xbox just like any other external drive. With external drives becoming pretty cheap like the 4TB WD MyBook (goes b/w$100-$120) it doesn't make this a very attractive option when it costs $40 and then another ~$120-150 (possibly more) for a 4TB drive. If you're looking to go smaller, you could do that but it's probably a waste.

It still gets 3 stars because it works well and there is a convenience factor for the drive sitting on top of the console nice and neat. Would have gotten 4 stars if there had been a passthrough for the power into the console. Instead it requires it's own power brick, again making it's usefulness even less appealing.

title: “Multiplayer” feature BREAKS THE GAME for Console Sharers
text:
The gameplay itself is great and so relaxing.

The problem is this: if you share a console with ANYONE else, only 1 person really gets to play the full game.

With only 1 ISLAND PER CONSOLE, if there are multiple people that share one console who want to make their own island, they can’t. Whoever the first person is to play the game is the only one who can advance the ‘story’ and build up the town. The rest of the ‘players’ can have a tent on the island (the location of which the 1st player chooses) but cannot do basically anything else except fish and catch bugs. You can’t donate to the museum, you can’t invite other residents to the island, and if you are playing simultaneously, you can’t even be on different areas of the island at the same time.
Not to mention that on an island with limited resources, the second or third player on a given day only has access to whatever resources the first player is kind enough to leave there.

This ends up not only creating conflict between players (I thought this game was supposed to be light, relaxing, and fun) but also breaks the game for anyone but the first (main) player. If you have more than 1 kid (or want to play the game too, for that matter) or share a console with your roommate, sibling, significant other etc., just know that while the main player can play the full game as intended, any subsequent player is only able to do a fraction of what this game has to offer, which really defeats the purpose of even having multiplayer at all.

title: Better off with an eSATA enclosure
text:
Attempted to use the Nyko Data Bank with a 6TB WD Green drive. Installation went fine. Restore from a 2TB external drive went fast and smooth. I knew the PS4's "rest mode" wouldn't work correctly but I am willing to live with that for the extra space.

However, after everything was completed I can't actually play any games larger than a few hundred MB. The PS4 shows the loading image with the dashboard music. After 30 seconds it shows an error. I've seen a few different error numbers but the most common is CE-38612-0.

Mine did shut off randomly once when left downloading overnight. The drive was physically hot. It's not clear what the cause was but it didn't do that before the Nyko.

I tried restoring the firmware from safe mode, rebuilding the PS4 database, re-initializing the PS4, and re-downloading. In every case the same problem occurs. No response from Nyko support via email after 36 hours.

No one who has done this mod with eSATA enclosures has had issues with the 6TB drives. So I've ordered a good external eSATA enclosure and cable. Hopefully I can use the 6TB drive successfully with the PS4 that way since I can no longer return it. Plenty of people have done so successfully.

========================= Update June 19 2015 =========================
Today the external eSATA drive enclosure and cables to connect my WD Green 6TB drive to the PS4 arrived. After performing a re-initialize and re-install of the system software from the PS4's safe boot menu I restored a backup to my PS4. After downloading Witcher 3 I'm happy to report the error I received above did not occur.

It's certainly possible that the Nyko Data Bank I received is defective. I'm not going to take the chance of overheating the $250 6TB drive just to save $40 on the enclosure. Admittedly the external enclosure doesn't look as nice as the Data Bank... but it actually works!

title: Adventures Ahead of Other Core Aspects of The Sims games
text:
I like Adventures though I had misgivings before I bought it. The problem for me is not this expansion pack, it is with not having some core aspects that make the game far more enjoyable and playable...like being able to buy clothes and change your wardrobe. To live your life living in a safari type outfit is just not fun. It detracted from the Adventures expansion for that reason. And there were all the clothes EA added to the game; but no place to change your outfit to suit the occasion.
The challenges in the game were varied and made for a nice change of pace to the game. (It isn't just tomb after tomb after tomb.) The puzzles are easy enough for most all players; and they didn't really try to make that the issue for the game, as much as the interaction with the culture and people.
My other major concern is the "Indiana Jones" image of the "American" adventure going to other countries to take their priceless history home to OUR museums. The game as it is set up and hinted at all over is I believe insensitive to the cultures we get to visit. Egypt has most of its history scattered through out the world's museums in real life. China has lost many of their artifacts,also, to the "Black Market" and private collectors. I wish there was a disclaimer or an addition to the games manual that shed light on the history of these three countries and people. It is a game; but people from those countries are playing Sims 3, too. I wonder how they feel about taking the artifacts home and participating by the game in what once was a whoesale stripping of their historys. I see this as a serious issue for a world class game not being sensitive to the world class people who buy their game.

title: One island per Switch is an infringement
text: One island per switch killed this game for us. My wife and I kick butt in real life together. We are a team and always will be when it comes to life. But we are also introverts and sometimes need to recharge separately and the greatest vehicle for this is gaming. We share a single Switch and love to watch each other play games, but we have separate accounts. Separate Zelda accounts. Separate Stardew Valley accounts. Why not the same for Animal Crossing? We didn't know this before so when I tried to play after my wife loaded up the game first, we were disappointed that we had to share the same island with the same layout and name. Now, I've missed out on the thrilling moments of choosing an island, its fruit, and naming it as well as placing my tent in just the right spot. title: Do not buy this without knowing this information!
text:
Know this: the game is great for single player, but multiplayer on a single Switch system has issues.
Do I love this game? Yes. Do I have a complicated relationship with this game? Yes.
I have not stopped playing this since I got it. I have poured so many hours into it, just like everyone else that is playing it right now. It's great for adults and single children. Yes SINGLE children. I do not recommend this game for families with one Nintendo Switch and multiple children. At all.

Things you need to know about this game:
1. The first person to start an island is deemed the "Island representative" which means they control almost everything, even getting a smoother experience, leaving other players trying to figure out things that the first player was hand-fed. Some Crafting recipes are not given to secondary players at all. Some you can buy, but others you cannot.
2. First player starts tasks, and is the only one that can really work on them. This makes it so that secondary players are stuck in progression until the first player starts a task to move the game along. But even then, the first player is sometimes the only one that can help advance that task as well because only they are given the important crafting recipes for that task. The other person could collect the items, but then they need to give them all to the first player so they can craft the items, and there is no good "give other player these items" option. You have to just throw it on the ground, or collect them into the "recycle box" which is a place where the main character can pick them up later. So far, to my knowledge, these are the tasks that the second player (btw, you can never change who the second player is. If someone starts the game first, they are the first player forever and always) can only do include: -Creating new houses for residents. -Creating bridges. -Creating Slopes so you can go up a cliff without a ladder. -Change locations of buildings. -Get certain shops to move to your island. -Start the task to let KK Slider play at the island. -Place a campsite. -and probably more restrictions to be discovered as we keep progressing.
3. Playing at the same time is very frustrating. The Second character is basically along for the ride and cannot do much at all. They can pick up items, but it takes a lot longer than normal, and they are sent directly into the "recycle box".
4. One island per switch. This was reported before hand, but you don't understand how limiting this actually is. If you are playing with anyone in your family at all, this will drive you crazy in so many ways. The second person to boot up the game will simply be told they are moving to the island the other player created, and they will have a shortened introduction to the island, without tasks like telling some residents where they will live.
5. Resources are just as limited as if only one person is playing. If you harvest a tree, that tree will not give any resources to the next player later that day. Same with rocks. Shells do not seem to be impacted by this. Also worth noting is that message bottles and special glowing "money holes" spawn for both characters once a day on the main island.

If you are playing this game single player, it's a great experience. It is a beautiful game, but if you want to play with someone in your household, you should pass over this one without a second thought unless they update it. (Review originally written March 28, updated so far on April 6). My wife was the first player to start an island, but I play more often. I cannot imagine two younger children sharing this game. It would be a nightmare and I do not envy all the parents out there that are in this situation. I'll say it again, PARENTS DO NOT BUY THIS FOR MULTIPLE CHILDREN.
If you think you'll just spend a few more bucks to have a second switch for two islands (I seriously considered doing this), then look at the prices first. As of this post, the prices have skyrocketed because everyone wants their own island, and switches are sold out everywhere.
I really wish I had done some research before hand about this. All I heard were positive reviews on YouTube.

title: <READ THIS>
text:
I bought this game recently and I love it. It is much better than the Two Towers game, for you can play as 9 characters, including Aragorn, Legolas, Gimli, Frodo, Sam, Gandalf, Merry, Pippin, and Faramir. The upgrades that you can buy with experience points are fantastic and much much better than the Two Towers upgrades. Also, this game has a sort of "choose your own ending" theme, for you can either play the Path of the King levels as Aragorn, Legolas, or Gimli, the Path of the Ring, playing as any of the hobbits (only Sam and Frodo at first; you unlock Merry and Pippin as you progress), and the Path of the Wizard as Gandalf. Once you beat the game, you unlock interviews with the actors who play Merry, Pippin, Faramir, and the actor Andy Serkis (who plays Gollum). Also, you unlock a bonus level "Palantir of Saruman." There is twenty floors in which you battle the dead warriors, archers, many other foes. After you beat this level, there is one more level that you have not unlocked yet. There is only one way to get this level, and that is to get Sam, Gandalf, and either Legolas, Aragorn, or Gimli to level 10. Once you do that, the "Palantir of Sauron" level will be playable. This is my favorite level because it gives your character tons and tons of experience points. If you want to get a TON of "perfects," all you have to do is build Legolas up to level 10. Then, you get arrows that penetrate enemies, and the Elven Bow Mastery skill. This allows you to fire two arrows at two different targets at the same time. Also, Gandalf is very powerful once you get him to level 10, along with Farimir. All of the other characters are mediocre, but that is my opinion. I would reccomend this game, not because the single player function, but for the online and co-op gameplay modes. Although the single player aspect of the game may become frustrating (on such levels as Osgiliath, Pelennor Fields, and Minas Tirith; The Top of the Wall), it gives you a great sense of satisfaction after you beat the levels. OK, here's a level summary:
Helm's Deep: This is a tutorial level in which you play as Gandalf. You pretty much can't die, so try your best. Once you beat this, you unlock Paths of the Dead.
PATH OF THE KING
Paths of the Dead: Like most of the levels in this game, this one is unique and difficult. It takes place in the Dead Mountain and doesn't give you much experience points (EXP).
King of the Dead: This level throws you in right off the bat fighting the King of the Dead. He is mostly easy on co-op mode, but can be challenging on single player. Once you defeat him, you must run out of the mountain with the ground collapsing behind you. If you fall, you either (A) in single player, start out after defeating the King of the Dead, or (B) in co-op, start the whole level over again. Once you make it out, you beat the level.
They supply endless hours of fun and excitement.

title: Active?  Only if you think getting on and off the couch is active...
text:
Wow... I bought this for my wife and we both set it up and tried to work out with this. First of all, I think that the reviews giving it 5 stars had to be planted from either EA or Bob Greene. There is no way that anyone looking for a workout could consider this anything other than a joke. Ok, if you're never worked out in your life, you might consider this as a starting point, but even then you'd be better off just going outside or to the mall and walking a mile or so.

Do yourself a favor and save your money. Go buy some dumbbells or some serious resistance bands and create your own workout... just not with the software/game.

I even bought the Step attachment for the Wii Balance Board to add some intensity (hopefully) to the workouts. Not that the description implies that you should buy this accessory... it doesn't. But that didn't even help. The fastest dance routine still felt a bit like walking up a flight of steps in slow motion. This was the fastest... really? Buy Dance Dance Revolution instead.

And honestly... lifting your left leg or right leg to balance while supposedly Rollerblading is supposed to be ACTIVE? Come on...

I was disappointed by the original Wii Fit, but had high hopes for this after seeing all the positive reviews and having it made/endorsed by EA Sports. I felt like it was maybe a half star better than the original Fit software and I would give that zero stars if possible.

Buyer Beware!!!

title: Great home workout for the rest of us!
text:
I love this program. It is a great way to get a total body workout for those of us who (a) are not in the best of shape and (b) are not disciplined enough go beyond their favorite exercises and work both upper and lower body. Of course, within about two weeks, as many others have said, you won't want or need the commentary anymore, so I just switched to listening to my own music with headphones to make the workout more enjoyable.

The reasons it doesn't get 5 stars: (1) As others have noted, response can be poor on a few exercises utilizing the leg strap, particularly high kick ups (fast). (Note: One tip on this - make sure your batteries are NEW. If they get weak AT ALL, the delays in response will drive you nuts and your trainer will start criticizing!) (2) I am guessing some would find the program not challenging enough. It is fine for me. I have done a lot of exercising in my time, so am not a novice, but I am also not young, not in the best of shape and have a bad knee. Even with that, I was on medium intensity within a week and already thinking of moving up. (3) The band is adequate, but not the best. It doesn't really give a hard workout unless you remove a lot of slack, and then it feels like it is about to snap (although, admittedly, it hasn't done it yet). Eventually, I am sure I will replace it with another strap as others have suggested.

Overall, I still highly recommend this program. The flaws are very minor and it is great for most of us. For the rest -- If you are a serious exercise addict in great shape, I doubt you would be working out on a wii at home anyway!

title: Great workout...with kinks
text:
I've had Active for about six weeks now. I've completed one 30-day challenge at medium intensity and am working on a second at high intensity. I purposely waited to write a review so that I could speak to all facets of the video game. I'm "severely obese" as far as BMI goes, but I'm also moderately active, hiking and kayaking when I get the chance. I needed something that would encourage me to get moving and stay moving. I wanted something more than Wii Fit Plus to make me sweat and feel the burn.

The Good:
You will workout and you will sweat. On medium intensity, I was regularly burning 150-175 calories per workout. On high intensity, I seem to be breaking 200 consistently.
I have not experienced the issue that others seem to have had with the leg band slipping. I'm not a huge girl, but I'm not a slim girl, either. I wear lycra-based yoga pants when I work out and it just isn't a problem for me. It fits snug and stays in place.
After just one challenge, I could feel the difference. I could also see the difference. My triceps are actually starting to cut in and my abs really, really want to come out and play, but there's still some pesky fat in the way. My quads are also showing a nice definition. It's reinforcement to keep me going.

The Bad:
The sensitivity of the Wiimote and Nunchuck leave a little to be desired. If you're even slightly shaking out of exhaustion, it can sometimes register as "movement" and hang up the exercise. On the flip side, it fails to register correctly when completing certain movements (the dancing comes to mind). I echo what has been said about working your left side harder than your right on lower body exercises. It was terrible design by EA in that respect. You WILL hold a left side lunge longer by at least 1-2 seconds. Be sure to keep the room between you and the sensors clear. Even a pet laying on the floor in front of the sensor can affect how or if motion is registered.
The length of the cable for the Nunchuck also wasn't considered in the design. If doing standing crunches, you can easily get tangled in the cable if you don't pay attention. However, if doing squat jumps, you'll want to be careful that you don't yank the Nunchuck out of the leg strap. Unfortunately, both of these actions can interrupt the exercise.
When playing any of the sports, how you hold the controls seems to dictate how well you perform, volleyball and tennis in particular. If they're slightly rotated or too close together, the action does not register.
When a workout says it will take 30 minutes (including videos), tack on at least 5-10 minutes. By the time you account for the forced delay between exercises, it adds up. Give yourself ample time.
The "band" they ship with the game is simply terrible. It's cheap and practically worthless. I found myself buying actual exercise bands and cutting off the plastic handles so that I could get real resistance without popping myself after a knotted end of the cheap rubber came loose.

The Ugly:
I really, really want to facepunch the female avatar. The feedback given is often inappropriate or ill-timed. You can be doing everything correctly and the comments are about correcting your form and not giving up. Similarly, you can complete only 1 rep of an exercise and the comments will be about having a great tempo. The designers failed to consider when an exercise might occur in the workout or when to use certain comments. For example, when finishing the last two reps of an exercise, the comments will involve "setting" a great pace. Feedback is also inconsistent when you are working out and hear positive reinforcement comments that are immediately followed by negative comments regarding improving your performance, yet nothing has changed.

The Bottom Line:
If you can deal with the Bad and the Ugly, as I have, buy it. Better yet, buy it used. It's been a great kickstart for me and I look forward to continuing to use it after I complete my second challenge. After using the challenge in conjunction with a 1400-calorie diet of 5-6 small meals a day, I lost 10lbs.

title: Heart Rate Mon Confirms it's a good workout
text:
First, thanks to all of the other reviewers -- they were right on target. After getting burned by the pitiful, and embarassing, Jillian Michaels game I was hesitant to shell out $ on another one. But so glad I did! I'd say the game actually follows your movements w/ accuracy about 99% of the time. I am currently obese although I do workout at least 3x/week. (Was always fit until I quit smoking and packed on 80 lbs. a couple of yrs ago.) Currently, I've had the game about 25 days and have it set to "Easy" which gives me a good workout. I stay in my target heart rate (low end of the range for right now) on average about 10 mins. of the 20 min workouts. For those who think it isn't a good workout, try setting it to "Hard". I've created my own workouts w/ several set on Hard and there really is a difference!

That's another great thing about this game. It has several excercise sessions to choose from, each w/ a Easy, Moderate, and Hard setting so, basically, multiply the # of sessions by 3. You can also edit the indiv. exercises w/in the preset sessions. Then, on top of that, once you figure out the individual exercises you like, you can create custom workouts. You can set an overall level on the custom, or set each exercise w/in the workout to the level you want. I think this is an excellent value for the $.

The only "negative" (which is a very slight one) is that the resistance band has minimal resistance. They show you how to increase it but I still feel like it's a little too easy. Because of the way you have to hold the controllers, it's difficult to use another band w/out the handles included w/ the game. Still trying to work around that one. Maybe using wrist weights would work. But that shouldn't keep anyone from purchasing it. It really is worth the $. Now I'm off to read reviews on Gold's Gym...

title: Classic Fighting Game
text:
If you're looking for what started the whole fighting genre, this game is pretty close.
The premise is very simple: You are "karate man in white suit," and you must defeat "karate man in red suit"--over and over and over again. And, well, that's pretty much it. It's one of those old, neverending Nintendo or arcade-style games that you never actually finish.
The graphics are just basic NES fare, although quite primitive since it was an early NES title. Can't really comment much on the music, since there are really only 3 songs in the whole game: the opening theme, the victory song, and the game over song. The sound effects aren't much either--just generic swinging and hit sounds, the sound of points scrolling on the score, and the voice of the old referee saying "Begin!" "Point!" "Stop!" or "Judge!" All of them were pretty cool though.
Like the whole premise, the rules are simple: You fight round by round, and each hit scores either a full point or a half point, depending on how impressive of a move you used. The first one to reach two full points, or the one with the most points at the end of the time limit, wins. If you win, you get to play a bonus round in which you are trying to hit objects that are being thrown at you. The game ends when you get hit (which will probably be by the first object, until you get used to it).
The gameplay is what really stands out here. You wouldn't think so by just looking at it, but upon playing this game, I can see that there is more depth in this game's simple fighting engine than in many of the 3D fighters out there today. It's like this: Every different combination of a button and a direction results in a different move. Each different move is useful for any given situation. Certain moves will counter other moves. A sweep, for example, will counter a roundhouse, and a roundhouse, in turn, will knock a jumping opponent right out of the air. There are attacks that strike low, and some that strike high. Some strike in front of you and some strike backwards. There are some attacks which let you quickly whirl around and attack behind you. You can also jump horizontally to lunge toward your opponent, slip behind your opponent, or get away from the opponent. You can also jump vertically to dodge an opponent's low attacks, such as sweeps and low kicks. Some attacks will score more points than others, depending on the situation. For example, striking your opponent from behind or knocking them down with a counterattack will usually get you more points.
Ok, let me take a breath after all that... When you get down to it, it's an impressively deep fighting engine for such an old game, and that's what amazes me about it. It's also rather addictive.
If you just happen to be checking out really old games, or want a quick little diversion from Tekken and the like, check this one out.

title: Fun For All
text:
Let me preface this with I have been a Sims player since its origional incarnation with Maxis. Since EA took over I've been sorely disapointed. The relevance here is I am by no means an EA fan.

Origionally I wanted to get Wii Fit Plus, but did not have the 90$ for for the board and everything. My daughter and I enjoy playing the Sports game that came with the Wii. However, I bought the Wii for its exercise aspects and the Sports game wasn't cutting it for me.

So, I looked around and decided to try EA Sports Active: More Workouts. The Wii board is optional, but I do reccomend getting the EA active accessory pack if you don't have the leg band.

I have been pleasantly surprised. The controls are very well designed and easy to use. I really like that for the sports activities (i.e. water skiing) there is a video tutorial with a real person going through how to use the Wii-mote and engage in the activity. The second time through it gives you an option to review the tutorial or go right into the activity. Which is nice since you arn't stuck waiting for the tutorial to finish. Also, the next time you do the workout you can view the tutorial or skip it. If like me, you have physiological issues which make some activites difficult or impossible you can skip them without some kind of 'penalty'. You can create your own workout or select one of a wide variety of preset workouts to do.

Now, I mentioned my daughter. She turns six in March. The video tutorial was super helpful for her. She was able to participate with minimual fustration at learning the Wii-mote and how to engage in the sports activities. She thuroughly enjoyed the island workout we did. Anybody with a younger child knows how difficult it can be keeping them actively engaged. The island workout combined exercise techniques and a variety of sports in a way that kept her interested for the entire 35 minutes we worked out.

We both liked the journal and its various atributes. Specifically she liked watching the graph populate and was tickled to get a trophy. I liked the calander and its customizability.

When we finished our initial workout my daughter looked at me and said 'Mommy, can we do another one?'

I would definately reccomend this product to anyone looking for an exercise game for thier Wii, whether it be for themselves or as a family activity. As a matter of fact, I already have reccomended it, lol. I was telling my best friend about it and she asked me where I got it and to e-mail her the links!

title: Great Graphics, seamless movie/game integration
text:
I bought this game the day it was released and have loved every minute of playing it. I enjoyed "The Two Towers," but "Return of the King" is a far superior game. I really like that is has checkpoints. I hated that in TT you would get almost to the end of a level and then have to re-do it all when your character kicked the bucket, so this is a nice addition. I also like that you follow the path of each contingent of the Fellowship on its journey towards the destruction of the One Ring. The transitions from the movie clips to the game graphics is much more seamless than other games and does not leave you wishing they would just keep running clips. I have not had a chance to try the Co-op mode yet, but that is something that was really missing from the TT.
Another feature of the game I like is that it is not as linear as the TT. While you are basically going to the same place at the end of the level, you have different paths on each level to get you there. Some of them have more XP power ups, or more enemies to dispatch to get more XP, but you do not have to go the one path like in TT.
The voice acting is great. Like TT, they used the actual actors from the movie to do the voice acting and it adds so much to the game. the original score from the movie is also the music in the game, so of course it is great.
This game is a good purchase. Even though it seems like it is short, I think it has lots of replay value with unlockable charcters and each character having unique abilities. If you are a real fan of the books and movies, you will enjoy playing ROTK.

title: The worst game in the history of games (if a little hyperbolic)
text: A career gamer, I purchased this game to try to enjoy a more recent college basketball game than College Hoops 2K8. Unfortunately, it was a disaster. The gameplay is completely unrealistic. Even on the hardest difficulty levels, players can rack up 10 steals or blocks per game easily. There is no natural feel for where a player is on the court. Players pass to other players (CPU controlled mind you) that are running the sidelines out of bounds. Want to go back to the basket 5 feet from the hole? There is no way to ensure you're big man won't drive the lane, and be tackled by an opposing player (no foul is ever called on this animation by the way) and turn the ball over, even if you have pushed the pass or shoot button prior to this animation. Want to rebound under the basket? Just hope that the CPU doesn't plan on doing this too, as you have no control over whether the other guy gets in there, or if your player will ignore commands completely (something very prevalent, especially in rebounding). The tackling/strip of the ball move, and the blocking foul in the lane call are called so differently on opposite ends of the floor, you'll wonder if you're playing a rigged arcade game from the early 1990's. It is that bad and mortifyingly inconsistent. It's just a terrible game, and that EA decided this was okay to put out to the public is telling for a company who has twice pulled it's sister NBA game from the market for similar reasons. If you want a maddening, unrealistic, unnatural and completely inconsistent basketball experience, shell out $30 (depends, sometimes it's more) on this piece of garbage. If you have a brain, play 2K games, and 2K8 for college basketball. Despite being almost 3 years older than this game, it is 100 times as good, and has such a fan base that gamers are still posting yearly roster updates.

title: Terrific, except when it isn't
text:
I've been using the Wii Active for a couple of weeks, and apart from a few serious drawbacks, it's a superior addition to the Wii universe.

First the good:
* The exercises are intense and challenging
* The variety helps keep it interesting.
* It exercises the whole body.
* In short, I feel like I'm making real progress, and getting fitter and stronger, and that's what I use it for, after all.

Tne not-so-good:
* Maybe it's just me, but I get very frustrated when the Wii doesn't recognize my movements. Especially with upper body exercises like bicep curls and shoulder presses, it often stops and "scolds" me for doing it right. It takes a few moments for it to figure out I've done it right. Very frustrating.
* Similarly, I'm periodically told I have the nunchuck in the leg strap the wrong way -- though it isn't -- which seems like some kind of programming glitch.
* The leg strap doesn't always stay up. Not sure what can be done about it, but it's very disruptive to have to pause a run or other strenuous exercise to put the leg band back on.
* The resistance strap offers very little resistance, I have to really shorten it in order to get any value.

All that said, it's mostly fun and I feel like I'm getting fit.

title: C'mon Nintendo!
text:
This game lets you have one island per console. That means that everyone in my real-life house hangs out on one in-game island. That could be fun! But it's not.

The first person to power up the game becomes the Resident Representative. They get to do the cool stuff like name the island, decide where people's houses go, and gather materials to build stores. Player 1 gets lots of fun recipes and things to do. Everyone else is a second-class citizen who only has control over their own house. If player 1 doesn't build a store, then you're never getting a store. Player 1 gets the $60 game, and the rest of us get some pathetic lite version. One of my kids is having an awesome time, and the rest of us are primarily NPCs. Player 1 kid runs around taking all of the resources to build her projects, and by the end of the day the rest of us are looking at tree-stumps and can't find any fossils.

I had no idea that this is what the experience would be like, and if I had known, I wouldn't have bought the game. The glowing reviews are from people who are the sole players on their console. I would really like to play the game that they're playing! C'mon, Nintendo, I've been with you since the SNES, and am really disappointed in you today. Let each account have its own island, and let us visit each other in local multiplayer.

title: I ignored the reviews and wasted 40 bucks...
text: Honestly, this is not good. The triggers feel squishy, the C left sticks are a bit off, and dead zone for the left stick is wonky as hell. DON'T Try to play competitive smash with this. Examples from experience: perfect pivots will turn you back around, and if you dash one direction by flicking it, it will turn you around, because the left stick is flimsy and flicks in the other direction for a frame or two. I've tried to dash and end up doing a Perfect pivot for the same reason. Just get a proCube controller or something for sm4sh, those are pretty good. I don't know if it's just mine, but I've read forum posts about the same exact issues. title: NON-UPGRADEABLE
text:
BUY WITH CAUTION. This stick does NOT use microswitches, it uses plungers on a pressed circuitboard. This will cost you accuracy and "button-feel" in arcade style games. There are also issues with the compatibility of the board and its claims to be "universal".
While the case is nice and simple with a good weight (thanks to a steel plate bottom), and I do like the button layout, modding this stick will be an ABSOLUTE HEADACHE for anyone who isn't an expert. The button slots are non-standard and will need to be expanded with a cutting tool in order to fit industry standard parts. I believe the stick is replaceable, but the original is of no usable quality for gaming.
It could, theoretically, benefit from extensive modification, for example a Toodles Cthulhu board and Sanwa/Seimitsu parts, but you would need something like a Dremmel tool to expand the button slots.
If you want ONLY A CASE and are an EXPERT MODDER, I would actually recommend it because I like the simplicity and weight, but otherwise, STAY AWAY.

title: Just a way to play games
text:
The WII Active gives you a nice alternative to walking, running and jumping, but the resistance bands are a problem. The bands that come with the package aren't adequate for a taller or more fit person. The suggestion is to buy bands that fit your height and resistance need. The problem is that the WII controllers don't pick up the signal as well, so the trainer gets "stuck," and you are unable to go forward without bumping out of the exercise. After bumping out of all of the resistance band training exercises, there is no reason to have WII Active unless you need a running companion or the same sports you get on other WII games.

Don't buy this product until the resistance band problem is resolved (or at least noticed by EA Sports)

title: Great Game
text:
I wanted a game that would give me a workout and EA Active does that. Wii Fit is fun, but my heart rate never really went up using it.

response to negative reviews:
- controller response - the game requires correct hand position, but provides a lot of instruction. After a couple of reps it is easy to get the hand position right.
- no weigh-in - I have found that the scale on the balance board is inaccurate. My scale, the scale at my doctor's office and the weight watcher's scale I use each provide the same weight. The balance board weight is generally 3-4 pounds off (in either direction) so there is really no reason to use it as a scale.
- leg strap falling off - You have to put the leg strap on high or it falls, but it stays on if you put it on right.

pros:
- leg strap allows for lower body work without the restrictions of the Wii board (it is not possible to do proper form squats on the wii balance board because of the size of the board)
- large variety of exercises at many different intensity levels
- the game really works the muscle groups.

my cons:
- the calorie counter is WAY off. I used my heart rate monitor to count my calories and came up with a completely different number.
- the ab workout is lacking. I do core training on the [[ASIN:B001H0RZX2 My Fitness Coach]] program or do pilates and I think I will continue to supplement with Pilates and My fitness coach.
- The band is not great, so I use the bands I already own. If you don't currently own fitness bands, a good set could add another $45 to the cost.

Even with the cons, I give it a 5, the game is well designed and it is a great workout.

title: HORI Nearly Perfected the Feeling of a GameCube Controller
text:
First off, this is an excellent controller. I might even like it a little more than the official Nintendo GameCube controller and I absolutely love the GameCube controller. This is "pretty much" wireless and the GameCube controller is not with the GameCube adapter to the Wii U. Unless, you have a Wavebird controller, which is completely wireless but was discontinued in production.

Overall: It feels exactly like a GameCube controller when you hold it in your hands. Same size and feeling on the palms of your hands. The HORI Battle Pad feels a little "cheaper" because of the plastic and the lightness of it without a rumble motor. However, it is a durable controller that feels like it will last, this is just a first impression anyone will have that has used a GameCube controller.

Triggers: The triggers are better, in my opinion, than the triggers on the GameCube controller. Why? The GameCube controller triggers go too deep and feel too springy for my preference and I feel like it negatively impacts my performance in Super Smash Bros. for Wii U because it feels awkward to press so deep on a fast-paced game. The triggers are better than the triggers on the Pro controller because the Pro controller triggers feel flimsy and too shallow. These triggers feel great and there are two on each side instead of the single "Z" button on the GameCube controller, which feels too sticky.

Buttons: One thing I like about the GameCube controller more, is the button pressing. The buttons on GameCube controller feel like they have more stability than on the HORI Battle Pad. This is definitely not a deal breaker, the HORI buttons still feel great, I just prefer the buttons on the GameCube controller.

Analog stick and C-stick: The sticks feel like they have more "resistance" on the GameCube controller than the HORI Battle Pad, which makes it a little better for most games (such as FPS) than the HORI Battle Pad...except Super Smash Bros. in my opinion. The sticks also feel just very slightly raised more on the HORI. These are such small details that someone can only barely notice. The grips on both of the sticks feel the same as on the GameCube controller as well.

D-Pad: The D-Pad is SO much better on the HORI than the GameCube controller. Why? It's bigger. I was afraid this would affect the overall feeling of the controller because I wanted something just like the GameCube controller. It doesn't though, at all. Feels just like a GameCube controller, but you can actually use the D-Pad in all directions easily.

Home, Start, Select buttons: These buttons don't really matter to me, but they feel similar to the GameCube controller with them being slightly "sticker" when you press them down.

Turbo: I don't use turbo, but it has this option.

How does it work?: You plug it into a Wii remote, so it is "pretty much" wireless. It works extremely well. When you start up your Wii U, all you have to do is press a button on either the HORI controller or the Wii Remote and it connects immediately and you can use it on the home menu and throughout game menus. This is of course, after you have synced your Wii Remote with your console by pressing the tiny red button next to the batteries on the Wii Remote and the red button on the console near the power button.

Colors: I initially wanted a red one because red is my favorite color and I prefer Mario. However, I chose the Luigi version and I really think the green goes better with the blue on the underside of the controller.

Doesn't have: Motion control or rumble motor.

What games can use this game?: Any game that uses the "Classic Controller" or "Classic Controller Pro." A list of games with these types of controller support on Wikipedia (Wii U games is #3): http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_games_that_use_the_Classic_Controller

Conclusion: Now, you may think I am "picky," but I'm really not. I just wanted to give a picky review to those who want every little detail about this controller. The cons I speak of are so slightly negative, I just wanted to give my impression being as articulate as possible. I love the GameCube controller, I would give it 5 stars as well even though my review sounds picky of it also. Both controllers are excellent and you cannot go wrong with either, but I prefer this controller for Super Smash Bros. for Wii U. This is a cheaper option versus if you are paying for an adapter and a new GameCube controller.

title: A True Expansion Pack
text:
I bought World Adventures along with The Sims 3 Collector's Edition for my birthday 2 years ago. I had a good feeling about it and knew it would be a nice little expansion pack--but I especially was sold on their decision to include Egypt as a travel destination (I'm biased because I love shawarmas in real life). I will start with the pros:

-Destinations: I love how they chose a destination which represented a distinctive culture and continent. France represents Europe and the west, Egypt the middle east, and China (the largest country in Asia) to symbolize the east/far-east. The cultures have been very well thought out--in furniture, food, music, and clothes, and hairstyles. Each destination has tourist spots inspired from real life (The Forbidden City in China, The Great Sphinx in Egypt) along with the city market where vendors will sell items like food or books. The General Store will sell "survival" and touristy items like Shower-in-a-Can, sleeping tents, dried food, and cameras.

-Adventures: When your Sim first arrives at each of these destinations, there will be an "Adventure Board" near the lodge (the look of the lodge differs from destination to destination). Here, jobs are posted by the locals asking for help to seek out things--these can range from collecting information from other Sims, to fetching objects buried in tombs. I have read some reviews where adventures get repetitive very quickly. I think that any aspect of The Sims (heck, even a Sim going to work) can be redundant. Lucky for us that there are incentives for our Sims to complete these adventures which are in the form of relics (that can be collected or sold for a tidy sum), and ancient coins (special currency that a Special Merchant in the vicinity can exchange for special items to enhance future adventures). Each destination has its own backstory regarding the main adventure. Also, an adventure can have a side-quest needed to fulfill and complete the adventure in its entirety. Sometimes, this could involve your Sim going to another destination (a special axe found in China can break the boulders that block the entrances of some tombs in Egypt and France). And so, this forces us to interact with all the destinations that has been put in for us.

-Culture: Sims can now keep in touch with local Sims by "long-distance chats", and also learn songs. If your Sim is pursuing the Photography skill, collections of pictures can be shot in each of these destinations. Also, I think you can create sims to live in one of these destinations (but I'm not too sure?).

-Passport and Visa: The more your sims help out the locals by doing what is asked of them, the longer your stay is extended. The default number of days that a Sim can stay is 3 days. Gradually, this can be extended from 3 to 5 to 8 to 12 days. There is even a special extension sold by the Special Merchant. However, if a sim were to just arrive at the destination and start exploring the tombs, the duration of your stay is not extended (I think your sims have to help out the local sims).

-Journal: A travel journal or adventure journal is set up when you sim travels for the first time. This documents statistics like how many tombs they have explored, how many relics they have found and the worth of these relics, how many adventures completed, how many left to go, and how many are still in progress.

-Sim needs: I have noticed that when my sims are in the tombs, their bladder bar is essentially put on hold. This makes things so much easier because no merchant sells a portapotty.

-Time: Time back in your Sim's neighborhood, be it Sunset Valley or Riverview or Bridgeport or any other world, is paused. If you Sim leaves on a Sunday morning (before their spouse has work in an hour), and spends 5 days in France--they will return on a Sunday morning (before their spouse has work in an hour), if that made sense. All activity in the home lot and neighborhood is paused when the sim leaves. This is the same with Adventures--if your Sim has to leave in the process of completing an adventure opportunity, it is left unfinished until then they can return the next time they travel. The only con I have with this is that once your Sim returns home after traveling, they cannot travel for 2 days. I think this number stays the same regardless of visa status.

Cons:

-Traveling restrictions: Pregnant sims and toddlers cannot travel. This is to ensure that they are not at risk or at harm should they set off a trap in any of the tombs.

-Adventure Board: I don't think this game is programmed to tell you that it's out of adventures even if your Sim has finished all of them. They start to literally repeat after a certain point.

-Glitches: I have a GTX 280 with 12 GB or RAM, and occasionally when my sim was traveling (especially China), my sim's actions would be delayed for 30 seconds, almost as if on pause--but the surrounding animation (the swaying of plants, the position of the sun) would play. This is because each travel destination is essentially one massive lot and somewhere on this lot, another sim is stuck (usually NPCs). It took many "resetsim*" cheats to make the game snap out of this habit--but make sure your Sim is at the lodge, or else the Sim will teleport to the lodge. Also, most digital copies of the Sims games are especially buggy. I recommend buying retail as I did and I have never experienced sims losing items from their inventory or families getting lost.

-Loading time: The loading time can take a while, especially if yours graphics are on high regardless if your RAM can handle it. I usually turn my graphic settings down a bit, to speed the loading but it makes a marginal amount of difference.

Final Verdict: I preferred World Adventures over Ambitions because it adds a whole new world (no pun intended) to the sims' lives, and also gives them something extra to do and look forward to. I highly recommend getting this Expansion Pack, you can't go wrong with it.

title: Like many who are here to read about this controller
text:
Like many who are here to read about this controller, you've probably been searching for a controller that you can use for smash 4. And like many probably have owned a gamecube and a wii for Melee and Brawl and also probably used a gc controller for those games as well. If you are not one of those people, well I'm sorry but I'm reviewing for the narrative of someone who would want this for that game in particular as I am one of those people who didn't preorder and would not think to shell out $100+ for a piece of equipment that lets me link my old gc controllers.

I actually bought the Luigi controller from another site that was selling them for 24 bucks a pop. I only bought one initially only later find that that $24 price wasn't going to be found due to it's apparent popularity (the makers, Hori even raised the price to $44 from the original 20 something bucks). This controller is pretty much a replica of a gamecube controller. Its feel it very reminiscent of one besides the fact that there are two Z buttons and you won't find the large L and R triggers anymore (personally I can live without those triggers. I was actually never a fan of them). Depending on the person might find this more favorable as it gives more of ps2 controller top feel which is my preferred layout on the shoulders.

Some nice things is that it is wireless, in a sense. You need to plug it in to a wiimote for it to work and it feels as if there is no lag input that I can tell when playing smash. That can be seen as a good thing or a bad thing. Sucks a little because now you'll have to keep your wiimote charged with batteries and the such. Wired controllers is usually a standard for fighting game tournaments offline and are just more preferred mainly due to no lag input problems and other various reasons. However, like I said above, their doesn't appear to be any lag and if you're going to use this for smash, history has shown that you probably wouldn't be the only one with a wireless in a smash tourney (brawl had nunchucks and wiimotes). There are extra buttons for turbo which I don't even use but if you're into that thing I guess it's pretty cool. As far as the build, it's sort of light. I'm hearing it's because of the fact their is no rumble which might be preferred for some.

I'd like to see how long the controller will hold up over the test of time. Perhaps my opinion will change down the line but at the moment I would recommend this product to anyone that wants a feel for a gc controller that could not get a gc adapter for their wiiu.

title: For the price point...
text:
At the price point it is fair to say there is going to be an element of getting what you paid for with this stick. I like to think that I typically can keep a product's price point in mind when evaluating it. With that in mind I think there are some positives that can be said for the stick.

The size seems reasonable, and is comfortable in the lap. The housing feels reasonably solid and that it is better than what you might expect from a product 1/3 to 1/4 the cost of a higher quality device.

The buttons are one area where we start to feel the low cost. I didn't have any problem with pressing buttons or with having them detect a press. I do get the feeling that sustaining a button press without firm pressure could be an issue for some buttons from time to time, so if you play a game or a character that needs long presses, you may want to weigh that in. I don't think would be a big issue for most users, and think it is one of those things you can over look for the price.

One (unsubstantiated) concern I have with the buttons is their basic design has a lot of side to side play in them. I can see how some wear could allow for them to rock and lock when pressed on the sides instead of the middle. Again, I have not had this happen, but it is something I've seen in the past and can envision happening here. IF I am right, that would be something that occurred with use and that is something that should be largely forgiven for the price point. The product should be expected to have a shorter lifespan when compared to the higher end products. However, it should also be expected to work for a time, which brings me to my final point and reason for my review score.

My main issue with the stick comes down to my particular one being dysfunctional from the start. Everything works fine outside of the downward direction. Down kind of works. Sometimes it does, just not always. That's a pretty big problem for a stick to have. A bum button I could probably work around or repair, but directional input failure is the point where you have stick death. It's most certainly not where you want to start. I don't know how often this happens, or what that means for the general longevity of the part, I just know mine never worked. If it only lasted 6 months I could say I got what I paid for, as it is now I paid and got nothing at all.

This is a singular instance of one bad stick, so if others are getting working units it still may be worth trying as long as one keeps in mind it is not the equal of a $200 unit. All things considered, I still think a working unit could be a good buy for someone on a budget.

title: NC in WY
text:
I purchased EA Sports Active to add to my workout options. Those options being: Leslie Sansone dvds and Wii Fit.

I purchased EA Sports Active 3 weeks ago and have used every day since then.

Positives:

I like the fact that with EA Sports Active I can select the exercises I want to do. This is important as I have back problems that make it so I can not do all of the exercises in the pre-programmed portion of EA Sports Active.

I enjoy the tennis, but wish there was a 'random' feature that would allow for the option of the ball to come towards you for either backhand or forehand rather than set patterns. It would make it an even better workout with the tennis.

The upper and lower body exercises also allow me to set up my own workouts to strengthen legs and arms more so than Wii Fit does.

Negatives:

I quickly replaced the resistance band it comes with and use one with more resistance. I already had some from my Leslie Sansone dvds. It would be nice if it came with say 3 resistance bands: light (like it comes with), medium, and high resistance.

As others have mentioned...the system has glitches. The biggest one for me being that while I do not feel I'm holding the nunchuk and remote wrong I get the message that I am or that I am not standing still. This can last for seconds, to minutes, and sometimes requires restarting the software.

I could also do without the 'awards' the makers of this type of software feel necessary to put in. I simply want to workout. I am competitive enough though that with those there I want to achieve them, but with my back problems there are some that I simply will not be able to achieve.

I have given 2 stars to EA Sports Active because it really has helped tone my legs and arms, but do not feel it's worth more than $15-$20 with the glitches it has. I purchased it for far less than the almost $50 listed here. So, for the price I paid and the results I've gotten from it, I feel I got my money's worth. I will continue to use it - my own way.

title: Terrible game, do not buy!!
text: My husband and I bought a copy of this game and he started playing. After a few days of watching him enjoy it I decided to try, and learned that you can’t set up more than one game per Switch. Not per player, not per game purchased, but per Switch. The first player has all sorts of interesting tasks they can do but any later characters are incredibly limited. You can only set up on the same island, you can’t build or move buildings, you can’t advance beyond what player 1 has done,.... If multiple players can’t agree on how they want to run things they can run around destroying each other’s games, but can’t share their things. Either the game designers are incompetent beyond belief, or they are expecting everyone to buy a separate $300 Switch for each player in order to play the game, making the total game cost $360. Sorry, Nintendo, for $360 I would expect a hell of a lot more game than this. (And what on earth would we do with a second Switch anyway besides this ONE game?) Terrible for families with multiple children. Don’t waste your money; play something else.

title: Good start for beginners
text:
I bought this game with the ideas of supplementing my gym workouts and introducing fitness to my 10 year old, since he is too young to go to the gym with me. He loves it!!! He actually will race to finish chores and homework so he can "work out". We both work up quite a sweat and the 'work out with a friend' option has become a family activity.
There are a few drawbacks. First, there is no ab or core body work. I would suggest some pilates in future generation games.
Second, the work outs are a mix of low and high-impact. People with joint issues (me), and upper floor apartment dwellers, cannot effectively perform the high impact jump squats, jump lunges, side to side jumps and the in-line skating jumps. Sure, you can tailor the workouts and eliminate those activities, but you are left with half of a work out and half the calorie burn.
My third concern is the inability to 'work out with a friend' for the 30-day fitness challenge.I have to perform a '30-day challenge workout' and log it into my journal and then my son has to perform his own '30-day challenge workout' and log it into his journal. It would save a lot (up to an hour) of time if you could work out with a friend for the 30-day fitness challenge. What better motivator than a workout buddy?
Overall, a fabulous product and a great way to introduce kids to the benefits of an active lifestyle. I will keep my gym membership though.

title: A fantastic game!  Maxis has redeemed themselves
text:
I have been eagerly anticipating this game for some time. I have loved playing the Sims in the past as well as enjoyed all of the older versions of SimCity. I fondly remember laboriously playing it on all of my old machines "back in the day".
However, after playing the hideously bad "Sims Online" I was wondering if there really was any hope anymore for Maxis and Electronic Arts.
Lo and behold... there is. This game is simply everything a SimCity fan could have ever expected and more. Not only is the gameplay divine, but the musical score is top notch, ethereal, even catchy... but it isn't intrusive, which is a bonus.
The game play itself has been cleaned up, simplified a bit and the overall appearance should make fans of The Sims right at home. The feature to import your sims characters is pretty neat, too, although there seems to be a bug that lets you import PETS from Unleashed as though they were human players! It certainly gave me and my girlfiend a chuckle to see Waggles Kat going off to work.
In all, I think this is a fantastic game. Even the tutorials are great, and I hate tutorials.
Thankfully, I picked this game up TODAY retail at an Electronics Boutique (computer software retailer) at the Mall. They weren't SUPPOSED to have sold it, but they did because some other franchise owner was selling it as well. Lucky me!
Please oh please purchase this game. You will not be disappointed!

title: best Sim City series game this far
text:

If you are new to Sim City you should be aware this game is not for everyone and you might not find it "fast" enough. For the rest of us, this game far surpasses all of its predecessors.

title: One of the best games I'd already played
text:
Sim City 4 (and its expansion pack Rush Hour) are very cool! Simply amazing. I was also a Sim City 3000 fanatic and I was expecting much about the new release. Well, it was better than I thought it would be. The graphics are astonishing and the entertaiment given by hours planning and developing your cities are incredible.
This game also offers a much higher challenge, one of the main problems in SC3000 was already solver, that was that it was relatively easy to build a city and develop. Nope, in SC4 you must have complete control over the budget.
I see some small problems, like the size of your cities (why we not have the option to size the cities in a region in a new region?), the high price of the game, some things could be added to the game and, mainly, the necessity of a super-computer to play the game (512mb RAM recommended if you are playing in a big city with more than 300 thousand inhabitants), but sure the game its worth all these problems.
Having patience and caution in planning your city, you won't regret the fact that you spent hours, days, weeks, even months to do a big and nice city.
