title: A little disappointed
text:
Sim City 4
A Great, and the only, city simulation game for the computer. This latest installment boasts the best graphics and special effects in the series, as well as more detail in the area of micromanagement.
The Good:
Graphics, sound, music, dynamic visualizations, disasters
The Bad:
Awful terrain editing machine, railroads do not operate properly, streets and railroad tracks cannot bridge over each other or cross at odd angles on the city grid (although this problem should be corrected in Rush Hour), seaports and rail connections are a pain to get working properly, city areas are much smaller than in previous versions.
Overall a great game, but not much better than Sim City 3.

title: High Requirements!!!
text:
The game is absolutely fantastic! The graphic design, the transportation simulation and the animations all add up to a very nice city constructing game. The experience from the previous games had a good effect.
Unfortunately, the game is hungry for memory. I bought a new PC some weeks ago. A 2.4GHz CPU with a GeForce4 4400 128MB grafic card and 512MB of DDR (333MHz) RAM and guess what!? I get an annoying slowmotion-show as soon as the city is big enough (approx. 100000 people). It looks to me as the RAM memory is too small! I hear and see that the HD is constantly being used, so it smells like swapping in and out the content of these rather big maps. So I guess I will buy another chunk of 512MB DDR RAM to try to finally play fluently Sim City 4 with a total 1GB of RAM!!!

title: Worth Every Penny
text:
Wow........ Just got done playing SimCity 4 for the 5th hour straight......... LoL........ This game has everything. Zoom all the way in on you city and see little Sims swimming in their pools. High School students smoking on the side of the buildings. Homeless Sims wandering the neihborhoods. SimCops laying down the law. Kids on their skateboards. EVERYTHING IS INCLUDED!!! This game is also BEAUTIFUL graphically, and night time brings a whole new look to you city. Each little building has a set of lights, and street lamps come included on your roads and streets. Another COOL thing is in the morning you see all your little Sims heading off to work, and in the night time they return. This can become even greater in the region play when you can build one town with residential, one with commercial, and one with industrial, connecting them with highways and railways. In the morning, you can see your Sims speeding off to work in your different towns, and seeing them return at night. It is amazing. Another sweet feature is the God mode. You can create a world you've always wanted, and fine tune it in every detail. Form mountains, carve valleys....... make that giant bride over that canyon and then blow it out with the meteor while it has cars on it.......... And that leads me to my favorite: The disasters. Amazing. The lightning is my favorite, but you can bring reign of fire down on your Sims with the meteorite, or totally destroy it with a volcano. And a new disaster, obliterate, destroys every trace of your city and returns it to its natural state. The way they did it reminded me of those movies with the end of civilization..... simply great. Well, ok...... I want to get back to playing my game =)
P.S. Whats this about bugs? It worked perfect for me, only zooming all the way in slowed down my computer, But I can live without this feature easily. Thank For Reading. Hope This Helped.

title: If you have the power
text:
The game is as great as any previous SimCity version, and with more features, and amazing graphics. Unfortunately, to run all that, you need one heck of a computer. My P4 1.3 MHz with 256MB RAM can barely handle a medium size city. I'm buying more RAM because it's definitely worth it.
The new region feature isn't bad, the only noticeable problem is the size of the individual cities are smaller now, so you cannot build that city with a million people. You are, however, now able to build a completely industrial city, a rich suburb, a commercial center, etc, all in the same region. It isn't a revolutionary change, but it's a somewhat welcome one.
The graphics are great, what is to be expected of a new SC. The street level detail is unbelievable, with children playing, dogs walking, cars going to actual specific destinations, and other crazy things.
I've had the game for two weeks and it has only crashed on me once. That's still too many times, and Maxis needs a patch. We don't expect anything less.

title: SimCity 4 is GREAT!
text:
SimCity 4 is great! I admit, it's been a bit more difficult for me to start off compared to the previous games in the series, but that just makes the game more interesting.
I was disappointed about there not being auto-disasters in the game. There are mini-disasters which kind of make up for it, but it just seems strange not having an earthquake or something which used to happen occassionally. The fires happen and destroy things if you let them go long enough, but the mass destruction is no longer a chaotic force - it's you! Good for the people who wanted more control over disasters; Bad for people who liked random disasters. I dreamed of having a city built at the foot of a volcano, but there is no option to have it randomly active... it's dormant until you tell it to erupt.
If you're looking for micromanagement... this is the game to have. 9 different tax categories; local adjustments available for each individual service building; more building types to plan for; different kinds of airports and train stations; and the list goes on.
Overall... I'd highly recommend this game to anyone who has enjoyed SimCity in the past or any similar development/strategy games.

I also "tested" SC4 on a 700 MHz P3 with 256 meg of RAM. It was unplayable. Taking the RAM up to 512 meg helped. 1 gig of RAM seems to be the point at which the game actually starts working decently.

title: This game is why there's no clock near my PC
text:
The improvements are apparent from the moment you start up. As a graduate of SimCity, 2000 and 3000 Unlimited, I was expecting a similar jump in gameplay and graphics for this one. SimCity 4 is a quantum leap ahead, however.
The graphics are photo-realisically awesome. So much so, that they will tax anything less than a 2 year-old or older PC. The game can be played on a 800-900MHz/ 128K machine, but it will be slow at times...be warned.
The scenery and buildings are very realistic. No more 20-story apartment buildings in cities of only 1500 inhabitants, either. Plus, once something's built, it tends to last for a long time, making the bulldozer tool a necessity for growth.
This game is much more difficult. It's taken me several tries to get a city of 10,000 with a balanced budget, without going broke. Watch your expenses carefully and don't build schools or police until you absolutely have to. Keep your budget constantly in mind. Accounting happens monthly, so deficit spending wipes you out fast.
A few quips -- the roads are less real-looking here. You almost have to establish a grid, where they seemed more natural in SC3000. Now, though, they can traverse the topography much easier. It's a trade-off.
There seems to be little benefit to linking to the region unless you've developed other areas. This means you're on an island and development even to a small town of 5,000 to 7,000 can take hours and lots of money. This may not be a bad thing.
Also, editing the terrain is tricky business. On the regional level, it seems almost impossible. Could we please have a God mode for the region view, instead of only at the city level?
Be patient and this one will ruin your career, mariage, etc. Awesome.

title: The Almost Perfect City Simulator
text:
Once you get the hang of this game, it becomes a lot of fun! More fun than any previous version, and not just because of the cute graphics. At first, it feels the same as SimCity 3000, but you eventually discover that there are important differences behind the scenes: The internal algorithms that drive the city's development have been reworked to run more realistically. (SC 3000 was more "fantasy-based", in my opinion.) But, you never have to delve into too many complicated details to enjoy it! Once you understand a few zoning concepts, the game is very intuitive.
My computer is fast enough to handle it, most of the time, but those who attempt to run the game at its minimum requirements might suffer. There are also some visual bugs to work out, but none have been detrimental: Sometimes cars, trains and pedestrians run over each other. Sometimes traffic signals and train crossing arms do not sync properly, but these are purely visual anomalies, and do not really affect the game. Sometimes, ugly dark bars appear in the middle of large cities, but they seem to go away soon enough.
Some important new features include controllable disasters, true agriculture zones, improved terraforming tools, distinction of streets from roads, and better visual feedback with props and "zots".
The most annoying thing about SimCity 4 is that it forces a new "Region" system on you. This makes it more difficult to load cities from other sources, and it lacks a "Save As" feature. I also wish they had more starter towns.
Overall I am very pleased with the product. But, I guess you just can't have everything.

title: Perfect for casual play, don't buy for tournaments.
text:
This review is from the perspective of a competitive Smash Bros. player.

An almost flawless controller. The only thing holding it back from being a 5 star controller is with the control stick. It occasionally will "flick" an input in the opposite direction with the left stick. The chance of this raises when you are doing fast inputs and letting go of the stick. Such a flaw is unacceptable for playing competitive Smash Bros.

On the positive side, this has a lot of nice features. All the buttons, including the shoulder buttons, are mapped exactly like a gamecube controller. This is as opposed to the PDP wired controller and Nintendo pro controller which have the shoulder buttons reversed from a standard gamecube controller layout.

This controller is also very light, which I consider a positive quality. The plastic doesn't feel cheap. It's not quite the same as a gamecube controller, but I don't mind it. Overall, the controller feels very similar to holding a gamecube controller.

A final note, this controller does not use analog springs for the shoulder L and R buttons. This is a HUGE advantage since the analog inputs aren't used in the new Smash 4. This allows you to input your shield quicker than a standard gamecube controller since you don't have to push through the spring.

If someone knows a way to fix the "flick" inputs on the left stick please respond. With that flaw fixed this controller is easily 5 stars.

2- Lack of options. The story was precise, but you were gauranteed to follow it in the same order every time you played it, wich made it dull after a while.
But I have little, if anything bad to say about ROTK. The graphics were much better, as were the scene transitions. I did have my memory card by the time I got the game, but even still, saving wasn't much of an issue, since I played it constantly like a stupified zombie. The new horde of playable characters, more levels, new moves, and the fact that you can use any of the characters in any level makes this game magnificent; 5 for 5, and well done Tolkien.

title: Product Information Incomplete and Trainers not Very Encouraging.
text:
I did sweat and get a good workout using this product. However, by the end of the workout I was ready to punch a hole in the tv set.

First, the highest weight limit one can put into your fitness profile is 300. I was mildly annoyed but let it pass.

Next, the strap on the leg band is not long enough to go around my upper thigh so I had to strap it just above my knee. This did not bother me. It was just further evidence that I needed to lose some weight. However, moving my leg during the exercises caused the band to loosen and and fall down my leg. I then strapped it very tightly and it caused my leg to become very sore.

However, all that was minor inconveniences. After all, I figured, most people who use this product aren't as obese as I am and it works just fine for them.

No, the aspect that made me angry was being scolded by an inanimate object. Whenever I had trouble getting the machine to register my movements during lunges, inline skating, and even running (when my leg strap began to fall) the trainer would scold me and inform me that I needed to commit myself more and show more passion. I have never taken well to being scolded and it was especially frustrating when I was trying my best and it was their stupid equipment which wouldn't register my movements. The first time I did inline skating the machine did register me squating and standing up. Also, the first time it had me run it thought I did a great job. The second times on these exercises, it didn't work so well, and that's when the trainer informed me that I wasn't putting myself into it enough.

Yes, it's silly but it did make me very angry. Why would the developers and the trainers think that scolding works?

I will continue to use this product but I plan on muting it next time.

(The reason I put product information is incomplete is because nowhere do I see that the fitness profile only goes up to 300 pounds nor the measurements of the leg strap.)

title: A Creative and Enjoyable Game
text: I recieved RPG Maker II for my birthday and have not been able to put it down.  Well, let me make a correction, I have not been able to put it down ever since I planned out on paper in detail the entire first section.  This is not the kind of the game you can just go into without a plan.  Therefore, if you don't have hours to dedicate to the game without even playing the game, don't get this.  When you do start playing, there are insanely many controls so it takes a while to learn how to use them, but they make sense once you do learn.  The largest problem I've found is that there are many controls that are very important but are not mentioned at all in the instruction manual (which is 52 pages!)  Really, to be seriously able to play this game, you NEED the Prima strategy guide.  I tried to make a game before I got it but failed miserably, but now that I have it, I've successfully made a town and multiple events in it!  I'm not at all trying to advertise for Prima: It's just that the instruction manual only teaches you how to make circular pieces of land and it doesn't explain well how to register anything (a very important aspect of the process) along with other things.  The color illustrations also are extremely helpful.  The game itself is really free in what you can do!  There are over 250 preset items and a great choice of characters and villians.  Nearly any plot you can think of can be created (provided you have the time).  It's a wonderful game for anyone who wants to make their own RPG!

title: Video Games just don't get any better than this!
text:
Based on the John Carpenter Movie, the game starts out right where the movie left off. You're the leader of a rescue mission at the demolished site in Antarctica.
The significant reason to like this game is the COMPLEXITY of it. The game can be completely different ever time you play it.
There are so many options, from what weapons you give to your crew, what weapons you take away, who will trust you, who won't trust you, or why they will trust you, and who might just lose it, and go postal on ya and start shooting everyone in sight! It's an amazing conglomeration of leadership choices, survival skills, and quick reflexes. And the possibilities are just endless. The story line is great, including bits and pieces from the original film(although, they are the voice-over actors for the game and not from the Carpenter movie). But it's very intense, and creepy to the max. It really keeps you on your toes.
The only negative I have noticed about it, involves the "controller". On one of the controller configurations, it involves the "left stick" of the dual shock controller. To "crouch" you have to depress the left stick. Unfortunately, that button is ALWAYS the one to break first on playstation controllers. So be careful when useing it. I have been through 3 controllers already, just because of that "crouch" button. So if you are a first time player to the game, go to your options screen and choose the "TYPE B" configuration for your controller, so you won't have to use the "left stick" to crouch, and you should be A-OK!
Otherwise, the game itself is without a doubt, the most fun I have had staring at a television screen since The Thing DVD was released.

text:
This game is, overall, pretty cool.

I must make a point though-- if you don't have a good graphics card, you're not going to enjoy this game at all. This is a very detailed game, and if you don't get the detail, then you're missing out on more then half of the game.

Overall:
The Tombs are my favorite. You explore these new tombs that have different puzzles (they're very VERY simple puzzles, yet fun to have your characterized sim go through them), defeat mummies (or run from them), and even find numerous of simones. Traveling CAN be a career for your sim because of how much money you gain within the short amount of time that you travel.

The Bad:
The "adventures" are lame. Unless someone needs something from a tomb, they're lame. It's normally someone asking another person something through you, you finding a treasure for someone, or you running around town for them doing stupid things that take wayy to much time then they deserve. I hate that the only way to boost your Visa (which are the points that you get, and the more, the longer your next stay can be) and get money (besides going into tombs). They were all pretty pointless and pretty frustrating.
Also, careful how you act towards the villagers in the different countries. It's EASY to offend them. Be as polite as possible, or else you're not going to have much help when coming to getting short cuts for those lame adventures that you have to go on.

The Good:
Detail, detail, detail! Everything is detailed to an amazing level. I love the menus when you go to the different places. You get the cultural dishes, such as frog legs and cheese plates in France, to dim sung in China, and unpronounceable dishes in Egypt. The clothes are accurate, and there are even a few outfits that have been modernized. AMAZING extras for your sim, as well. Including new hair styles and clothes, the furniture is great. All of the addtions are useful. Espeically if you're into landscaping, there are tons of new flowers to choose from.

Pretty good game. I would reconmend it to anyone who's a Sims 3 fan. Overall, I think it's good. =)

title: Good modding platform for beginners, average overall stick
text:
I bought this stick because it was a low cost multi-platform controller that offered pretty accessible modding potential with Sanwa/Semitsu/Happ parts. I haven't yet modded it but I have been playing shooters and fighters with it on multiple platforms and my impression is that it's a good stick, not exceptional due to the buttons, but good overall.

The buttons are a plunger contact type setup like is found in game pads. The button presses the plunger directly onto the contact pad on the PCB which completes the circuit and registers as a button press. This is good enough if you want a general use stick but its not nearly sensitive or precise enough if you're looking to really hone your skill at fighting games. There's just no comparison between mechanical micro-switches and game pad type switches which this setup uses. I'm getting a little far afield with the mod talk though..

Overall I'd say get it if you can score it for around 30 or so. The joystick itself is really nice and responsive, it just fails at the buttons.

I gave it 4 stars because as a first mod stick, it just can't be beat.

title: The Harvest Moon series have just been kicked up a notch
text:
When I first heard that a new Harvest Moon game was coming to the DS, I was determined to buy it. After buying this game, I have not regret for one moment buying it.

This is definetly the most advanced HM game on the market, with specific "water points" and "sun points" for not only crops, but grains and trees too! There are even more animals involved this time too with cat, pig, badgers, sparrows, rabbits, ducks, mice and monkeys to name some of them.

The tool upgrade is a bit of a pain since you need to use "wonderfuls" which are very rare, and can only be won in festivals, and after many (game) years of work, made by yourself.

The romantic prospects are a plenty in this game, both for female and male players.

For those who liked the mining system in previous HM games will love this one with lots of challenging floors (255 floors to be exact) to explore.

A huge tips for players, both experienced and newbies: BUY THE STRATEGY GUIDE. I will pretty much say it is a "must have" to manage to play this game, and have fun with it (sadly, but true)

This game is without doubt a 5 out of 5 in my book, and a must buy for HM lovers and time managment / simulation fans!

Good luck, and happy farming!

This game is fun to play, but if you are an average skilled player or more I would only suggest renting this game for 3-5 days instead of spending $50 on it because it only takes a few days to defeat. Also most of the footage of the movie on the game come from The Two Towers movie or the previews of the Return of the King movie that you can see on the Two Towers DVD special features. I was disappointed because I expected to see footage from the upcoming movie but I had already seen the footage that I did see on the game.
So save yourself some money and go rent this game from your local video store and go and decide the fate of Middle Earth.

title: Blocks my WiFi
text:
It works as advertised. The cabling inside it is somewhat cramped. I was barely able to get the adapter to connect and close the cover.

I am using it with a 4TB SSHD which works fine except for rest mode. Whenever I enter rest mode the ps4 crashes and I have to manually turn it on by pressing the button on the system, then re-sync the controller. So, I just simply don't use rest mode any more. This isn't Nyko's fault, but still relevant.

My more annoying problem is that the ps4 wifi antenna seems to be easily blocked by any metal placed above it. The Nyko Data Bank places the HDD directly above the wifi antenna. This caused my internet speeds to drop from 9 Mbps down to about 1 Mbps. I might have taken off two stars, but this is partly sony's fault for having a crappy antenna.

title: Gives a good workout
text: I decided to try this after reading the reviews on Amazon.  It is so much better than the Wii Fit workout.  Wii Fit is boring and doesn't make me feel like I have worked out quite hard enough.  I am completely out of shape, and I feel confident that I will be able to start a successful new fitness routine wtih the Sports Active 30 day challenge. Today was my first day. My heart was pumping, and I worked up a good sweat by the time it was over.  The exercise band is a beginner band, so I think I'll try to find one with a little more resistance.  The boxing workout is fun, and it doesn't make me feel completely uncoordinated like I did on the Wii Fit.  My only real complaints are that the nunchuck pouch kept sliding off my leg during the boxing kicks, and the Wii didn't recognize my movements on the side lunges. title: Really great purchase
text:
I am so pleased with this purchase. I've used Wii Fit for a good amount of time, but I never saw any real results physically. I always thought that game was just cute and fun, but not really the apparatus to add to my workout regiment.

EA Active, on the other hand, provides me with a real work out. I do the 'high intensity' workout, and I definitely break into a sweat and feel the workout in my muscles. It gives you great instruction on how to complete the exercises, and reminds you to isolate the muscles you are working on. The trainer is constantly encouraging you to keep going, and the exercises are pretty fun as well.

I am an active guy in my mid twenties, so this program is right for me. This is a higher intensity workout than anything on Wii Fit, so if you are a beginner at working out, be sure to not strain yourself and use the low intensity workout.

Overall, I think this is an amazing program to supplement your exercise program with. If you can't make it to the gym everyday, then bring the gym to your living room. 5 stars!

title: Wii Active
text: I was looking for something that would help me exercise. This one really helps you keep track and gives you a work out that is fantastic!

title: Good in theory.
text:
The first problem with this game is the equipment. The resistance band is a thin sheet of plastic that has the resistance of a wet noodle. I had to go out and buy one that could give me an adequate amount of resistance, but the problem is that you can't hold the Wii remote and nunchuck with the large handles of the ones sold separately. The leg strap fits well, but the velcro strap ends right between your legs causing it to constantly scrape against your other leg, slightly opening it and creating distracting sounds.

The workouts featured in the program are solid making you break a good sweat, but the exercises are redundant. There are only slight variations of the same exercises, and the pace even on the hardest settings is completely out of whack. It would be great if they had an option that allowed you to do the exercises at your own pace while still recording it in your log, but unfortunately the feature doesn't exist.

My biggest complaint about the game is that it isn't properly calibrated to the Wii remote. Some exercises like the inline skating don't even register no matter how hard or high you jump, and it can be quite frustrating. Side lunges are horribly timed, taking about 2 seconds to complete a rep to the right, but then 4 seconds when you do a rep to the left. I noticed this throughout most of the exercises. There are small timing issues everywhere you look, and it is unbelievably distracting as you work out. Worst of all, these timing issues causes the workout to pause until you reposition yourself "properly" and the voice instructions constantly nag you throughout the ordeal.

The game would be great if it weren't for these issues. I also purchased Wii Fit Plus and My Fitness Coach, so hopefully one of those will be better.

That definitely takes away some of the fun for me.  Doing things as a right handed doesn't feel natural and I do find it harder to concentrate on whatever activity I'm doing because I keep wanting to adjust the remote in my right hand or switch to my left altogether. title: So Worth It!
text: I really love this product!  I hate to call it a game because I don't feel that it is.  I am doing the 30 day challenge and I feel like I just got out of a class at the gym when I get done. Cons: if you can call this a con, you have to have the controllers precisely how they say to have them or the Wii won't register that you've done the exercise.  It can be frustrating when it doesn't register right away and you have to wait, but if you do the exercise correctly things progress in a timely fashion. title: Great for lazy people (like me)!
text:
I bought Wii Fit to spur myself to exercise and lose a few pounds. In the beginning it was fun and I was always excited to unlock new exercises. After a while the novelty wore off and I would go days (weeks!) without exercising. When I did decide to exercise, my laziness got in the way and I found myself choosing the easy activities like hula-hooping and balance game.

This is my second day with EA Active Sports and I love it. Yes, there are some issues with the synchronization and holding the controls just right (and the leg strap slipping down), but what I love is the 30-day challenge. It chooses the activities for you, so unless you go to the trouble of customizing the routine, you're pushed to stick it out. So, yes, I grumble a little when I see the next tough exercise coming up on the screen when I'd really prefer to quit and get back on the couch, but this is just what I needed to keep me motivated. I'm using the lowest intensity level, but I'm panting and soaking wet at the end of each workout. This is just what I needed!

title: Love it! It works! . . . But with modifications . . .
text:
Let me start by saying that I agree with others when saying this is a much better work out than the Wii Fit. I own both and find EA Sports Active much more challenging and have gotten actual results from using it consistently for the past six weeks. I'm a fitness novice and I've lost 11 pounds and inches from my waist, hips, thighs and arms in 6 weeks with this and some small diet adjustments. I would like to address some issues some other users have been having that have caused negative reviews. Here are my findings. Take them or leave them. :)

1. Difficult to set up and use - Really? Using the controller and nunchuk with some of the exercises (mostly the upper body ones) can be awkward as many have reported, but there is a simple solution to this problem - PUT THE CONTROLLER AND NUNCHUK DOWN. Really, you can. It's alright. Put them down, do the exercise without them (because honestly, you can't do them properly when you're holding all that stuff) and then press the + button, choose 'skip exercise' and go on to the next one. Ok, some people are saying "But it won't register that I did my lateral shoulder raises and I won't get my trophy!" - Which is more important - a trophy that pops up on a TV screen or definition in your arms? . . . That's what I thought.
2. The music is lame - No kidding! I'm with ya there. It's like bad porn music (not that I would know!) My solution: iPod, baby. Get some sports earbuds that won't keep popping out of your ears when you jump around and you're good to go with a customized playlist of your own. Or if the sound barrier isn't a problem at your place, just put the TV on mute, put your favorite CD in the stereo and crank it.
3. The instructor's comments are annoying - see #2. Problem solved. If a virtual instructor is annoying but you can't hear her - is she still making a sound?
4. The leg strap keeps falling off/feels like it's cutting off circulation - I don't have this problem, and I'm a full figured gal. Not sure what's up there.
5. The resistance band lacks resistance - yep. Buy a new one. I know you shouldn't have to, but I did. It was $10 at Target for a Reebok one.
6. No left hand option for baseball/no left hand options period - ok, this one cracked me up. I use the batting to work on my waistline and surprisingly it's been dwindling. Here's what I do - you may want to take notes . . . I swing and lead with my right leg for 20 swings and then switch to the other side and swing and lead with my left leg for 20. I know your character on the screen doesn't move, but that doesn't seem to be an issue for me. For the record, I'm right handed, and maybe I'm missing the point here, but I seem to work out both sides doing this. . . by switching sides. . .I'm just sayin' it works. Give it a go.
7. No cardio - Umm - anyone ever heard of running? It's new. Look it up. There is also dancing, and I will go along with anyone who wants to say that the dancing on here is a bit lame. But come on - who amoung us doesn't want to bust out and 'raise the roof' and 'churn some butter' every now and then? I get an extra cardio work out from laughing while I'm doing this one.
8. Takes several minutes to set up a customized work out - not so. My 11 year old set one up faster than I did. It's really user friendly with a drag and drop method.
9. Movements aren't registering - I have found that this is always operator/equipment error. Either your legstrap isn't in the right position, which is an easy fix, or your batteries in your remote are running low. Sometimes it can help to reset exercises, too. I know it's a pain in the butt, but it just takes a second to check these things.
10. No ab specific work outs - thanks to a great follow-up comment, this turns out to not be true! See below for some great info!
11. The 30-Day Challenge is impossible - Amen! Which is why you can create your own work out. And did I mention that was easy to do? A friend of mine actually completed the 30-Day Challenge and - Spoiler Alert! - all that happens is Bob Green pops up and tells you to do it again. If you can live without that, just create your own.
Summary - are there better exercise games out there for the Wii? Probably, depending on your appetite, but I'm perfectly happy with EA Sports Active. Is it for the hard-core fitness enthusiast? Probably not. I think a real fitness freak would be bored with this, and maybe that's the problem with some people. I'm your average overweight middle-aged working mother trying to get healthy. I've seen real results with it in a short amount of time. And after a few modifications I've come to love it. I start every day with it - and my iPod. :)

I checked out the Active website and see a new version is coming out this fall that will have ab specific exercises. I intend to purchase.  Overall, very good excercise "game". title: ea sport active

title: I think it is great, but Jeremyna huffs and puffs...
text:

Poor little winded Jeremyna.

title: Any overweight people using this??
text:
Reason why I ask this... I am overweight and want to get in shape. I have been using the Wii Fit, and have gotten bored as I have reached certain levels and played all the aerobic games. When this came out, I was super excited! Hubby even pre-ordered it for me.

The first thing I had to do was put the leg strap on. Again, being a heavier girl, my thighs are not exactly skinny. I am not the biggest girl in the world either, though. The leg strap is NOT made for overweight people. It is made for the skinny people you see in the Active commercial (IMHO!). After finally getting the leg strap attached (just barely), I was able to work out.

Frustrating at first, definitely. Trying to figure out where you need to hold the remote and nunchuck when doing strength exercises was not fun. I was running and the system thinks I am walking. Most frustrating are the squats, as sometimes I am nearly to the floor and then it says I am not bending down enough!! Also, the kick backs, I have watched the demo over and over and forget it, when I do it the way the trainer shows, it doesn't register on the program.

So, those are all the cons (or some of them!). I CAN get a good workout, when I am able to pick which ones I like and know I can do the proper form so it will register on the system. I am still using it, still swearing at it when it does not register a squat. I will keep using it for awhile, and hope that I can eventually slim down enough so the leg strap is more comfy. I just wish the makers of this game had done more testing, especially with overweight people that do want to work out with this.

title: Frustrated Fitness Enthusiast
text:
I was so excited to get this game, however, I'm in agreement with many who have purchased the game and have given it low ratings. Though the workout regimes are structured well, the system would freeze alot and fail to pick up the remote signal. title: Great workout, a few snags
text:
I am very glad I purchased this .. it was well worth the money. I noticed several reviews didn't like the resistance band. Eventually, I will probably upgrade to a stronger one, but right now I just double layer it on the floor (they show this in the pamphlet, pg 7. I'm also having issues with the nunchuck cord ... particularly when I'm running. It keeps getting snagged on the end of the strap for the leg band.

The one irritation that I didn't see in any of the other reviews has to do with the balance board. During my 1st workout using the 30 day challenge I let the machine know that I had a balance board. Okay, fine. I did some exercises without the board. The trainer was wearing shoes, so I wore shoes. Then we switched to the board. You're not supposed to wear shoes on the board, and the trainer wasn't wearing shoes in the video. I take my shoes off. Next exercise, we're not on the board anymore and the shoes are back on. Repeat this insanity several times. I was cussing about 15-20 minutes into the workout but, I did keep going. I did workout some off of the board without wearing shoes, but then next thing I know I'm supposed to run and I just can't do that on laminate flooring without being in pain pretty quickly.

Luckily, it's pretty easy to just change the setting ... so on the next workout out I told it not to use the board. I will keep it that way for the 30 day challenge. I designed a customized workout that has all of the board work together, but I've decided to wait until I've seen all of the exercises before bringing in my own design.

Despite all of the complaining above - I love this game. Today is rest day (thank goodness) and I'm a little sore, but it's a good sore. I would recommend stretching before doing the workouts, especially if you have been inactive for awhile and are using this to bring fitness back to your life.

title: Good balanced workout
text:
EA Sports Active offers a good balanced workout that follows along in the spirit of the immensely popular wii fit.

Unlike wii fit, this game gives you preset workouts designed to focus on different areas each day and also gives you the ability to customize your workout to your personal taste without a lot of waiting and selecting between exercises. The only waiting you will need to do between exercises is during first time you do a new exercise. In these cases, the game will allow you to view a video of how to perform the exercise properly. It is important to pay attention to these videos, because there are occasions where, if you do not hold the wii remote or nunchuk exactly the way the trainer demonstrates in the video, the game will end up not recognizing your movement properly.

This game allows you to (optionally) use the wii balance board as well as it's own resistance bands and leg strap in order to give more variety of exercises. The leg strap simply holds the nunchuk to your leg for some of the exercises, so the game can track your lower body position. The resistant band is used for upper body workouts. However, the bands do not offer much in the way of resistance and cannot offer much in the way of strength building even at their highest setting. If strength training is what you are looking for, you'll need to supplement weight training into your workout plan or use weighted wrist bands along with the strength exercises.

The cardio exercises are effective and diverse. The running exercises combine a series of kick-up and leg-up exercises, there are a variety of cardio boxing exercises as well as dancing exercises.

Overall, this game is a great addition to your wii game library if you don't have time for the gym and if you want a good pre-built set of workout plans.

title: Almost perfect - but those with latex allergies should be careful
text:
There are some small glitches in the game or I would have given it five stars! Other reviews have done an excellent job in describing the game and its strengths and weaknesses. I have just a couple other observations.

First, it says it is balance board compatible. I was expecting that this would add an option to the journal area for it to capture your weight like Wii fit does. So far as I can tell, it does not use this ability at all.

Hopefully they will integrate this in future versions, as it already tracks items like how often you eat out in restaurants, how much water you drink, hours of sleep, etc. It allows you to set goals on how many workouts you want to do per week and how many calories you want to burn and then tracks progress towards the goals. Adding the weight would have been a really nice touch.

Overall, the balance board integration seems kind of an afterthought, and I found I liked many of the excercises better without the board.

Second, those with latex allergies should be very careful. The leg strap is backed with a rubberized material that contains latex, and the resistance band is latex. This was not noted anywhere in the product descriptions that I read. Those with latex allergies will need to find an alternate resistance band (Thera-band makes them and they are sold here on Amazon). The leg strap is a bigger problem to replace, but some folks in the [...] forums are using a stretchy sweat head band instead with good success.

Last, the resistance band is very light and does not provide much resistance. You can improve this by keeping more of it between your feet, but I will be purchasing new bands or tubes soon. I am extremely out of shape and I still find the resistance band too weak.

With all that, this game has me exercising (and enjoying it!!!!) for the first time in my life, and I absolutely love it.

I recommend users check out the forums at [..] as the users are wonderful with suggestions, support, lists of custom workouts, etc.

title: Loved it!  Only one gripe...
text:
So I got the new Wii Personal Trainer and got a really good workout. I started with the Low Intensity 30 Challenge and it really got me sweating. By the end my hamstrings were shaking, my left calf muscle was on the verge of cramping and yet I was so proud of myself and almost wanted to go another round. I would definitely recommend stretching before you start. The resistance band wasn't quite enough resistance for me so I will probably get a stronger one in the future.

My only gripe about this thing is that the leg strap is already TEARING! Seriously, I'm overweight but I'm not that fat. I had to keep trying to tighten it cause it slipped down to the floor twice while I was running and by the end my husband groaned that it was about to be completely ripped at the seams and I had only used it ONE TIME!!! Maybe I was wearing the wrong clothing (I was so excited that I worked out in my jean shorts) for the leg strap to stay on properly. Other than that I loved it. It even gave me a heads up on what we will be focusing on tomorrow and a new skill I'll be learning/working on. I can't wait to do it again tomorrow and see how my progress has come along after the 30 days.

title: Excellent Workout program -
text:
[...]
I have used the Wii Fit but after awhile was very bored as you could not flow through from one exercise to the next. With Active, it delivers a 30 day challenge and every day is different and it is easy to stay engaged. Also- it is very thought provoking if you use the Journal and quickly answer the questions of what you ate yesterday, did you eat out, how much water did you drink, etc. The only thing Active doesn't do is weigh you and do BMI like Fit, so I use the two to track all of the information on my progress...I have been faithfully at it for almost a month! I wish I could return this game. But Target would not take it back since its opened. It doesnt read your movements. (especially the arm curls) I did not break a sweat.
