title: E A Sports Active
text: I got this game a week ago & it is awesome.  I was using the Firm Body Sculpt system with the fanny lifter & its ok, but I'm feeling soreness in places playing this game that I haven't felt before.  The back of my calves & my glutes mainly.  I enjoy it because its not the same boring thing over & over, & I burn alot of calories in a short period of time, perfect for an early morning workout before work (doing 30 day challenge).  After just two workouts I felt my jean fitting as they should instead of being too snug.  I think I've found something I will stick with for the long run, then I'll try the "More Workouts".

title: Frustrating non-working technology
text: This software could be really good, but after 3 days of dealing with all the non-sense involved, I'm either going to trade it in or throw it away. The game has no idea what my movements are. It says to run on the track, so when I start running in place, the message on the screen constantly switches back and forth from "perfect" to "too slow" even though I'm running at the same pace for the entire exercise. The resistance band that comes with the game is not even challenging for my 7 year old daughter. I'm not sure if it's 2 lbs or 5 lbs, but it's useless. When performing curls, the game repeatedly told me to hold still and hold my arms like the person on the screen. I ended up doing about 30 curls and it only registered one of them. I have no reason to believe this is a Wii hardware problem as the family plays lots of other games on a regular basis.

title: OK, but misses the point
text:
The program itself is fine. Sadly, I think EA (and other producers of such titles) misses the point of exercise as a video GAME. Essentially, EA Active is like a workout DVD but more interactive. It tells you what to do, counts calories (bonus) and gives feedback much like an aerobics instructor.

THE DOWNSIDE:
The game isn't fun. The whole point of a VIDEO GAME is to be fun. If I wanted to use a workout video, I would just... get a workout video. There are tons and they are MUCH cheaper than what games go for these days.

Why is it so hard for publishers to create a GAME that requires you to work out??

In a way, this is the fitness version of the 'edu-tainment' that was the scourge of schools years back. Not really educational, not really entertainment. The goal is to do both so well it is seamless. EA Active falls short on this count.

The correct answer to the 'fitness game' thing is to make it a fun game FIRST and then have the exercise come naturally and always be fun. Wii Fit was OK at achieving this, better than EA active.

That said, EA active is rather polished, and well executed for what it is. I just think they executed the wrong thing.

title: Broke a sweat...
text:
I have never written a review before, and have to say that this game completely kicked my butt...I was in a full out sweat by the time it was over--and considering that it is 100 degrees outside, it is great to be able to get an effective workout indoors!

While it is great, here are a couple of changes that would make it even better!
- Support for us lefties! It is not a huge deal, but still an inconvenience!
- I am allergic to latex, and it would have been super if the band wasn't latex--I had to go out and buy a latex-free band!

title: Finally someone is figuring out how to do a workout game
text:
I was willing to put up with previous attempts at the workout "games" because they did motive me for a short time but now i think someone has finally figured it out. There are still plenty of opportunities for improvements but I think this game breaks through the barrier for getting real exercise.

I've only done one day on the ea sports active program but i think this is one that will keep me exercising and motivated for a while. They've done a good job. It is entertaining enough (i don't need much though) and yet it is a good workout. Finally!

There are enough different types of activities to give variety (and exercise different muscles). The exercises aren't "artificial" like the Jan Michael's game (where you had to keep trying to throw grenades until you got the motion right or space out your punches so the game could keep up with you). It really felt like i was exercising efficiently and enjoying it.

I'm surprised it doesn't track weight over the course of time because that would be so easy but that is a nit.

I haven't tried the multi-player mode yet - hope they did a good job on that too.

title: I really like the Gold's Gym Wii games
text:
I really like the Gold's Gym Wii games, but was looking for a little change of pace. I tried this game for just over 30 days, and I have to say I intensely dislike it. Every time I use it I end up wanting to throw my remote through the television.

My biggest problem is the "Stand Still" command at the end of a rep (mostly for the leg exercises). If I were standing any more still I would be dead. No matter how I readjust the remotes, change my stance etc. it still gets "stuck" on stand still, and won't let me move forward. Very frustrating, especially since I lose all momentum and end up having my heart rate drop.

In addition, I find it VERY hard on my knees. As I mentioned above I regularly do the Gold's Gym workouts (I would highly recommend both) and Zumba, neither of which are a problem. I have retired this game and won't be using it anymore.

title: Great Workout and Outstanding Results
text:
For those of you that own the Wii Fit and are looking for a more intense workout, look no further.

My wife and I received this game about 3 weeks ago and have logged about 12 workouts each during this time. I would say this game is geared to people who are very serious about increasing their fitness level. There are different difficulty level's, so it's good for beginners and the more advance. I do high intensity training at the gym and on the track - I could honestly say after the first week of using this game, it progressed to a level that pushed me physically and in a different way than what I'm used to at the gym. This is a perfect game to increase your physical performance and to throw into the mix of regular strength training. The only thng I do advice for those that have a high fitness level already is to go to Target or Sports Authority and buy stronger resistent cords.

title: Best workout game for the Wii!
text: I love this game. I absolutley love it! It's like having my own personal trainer in my living room and the workouts really make you sweat. I have a two year old and she loves watching me play eh rather workout to this game. I find the trainer to be very motivating and informative. The game is very futuristic and completely fun. Not to mention a great way to exercise. I would say this game is more like a personal and interactive workout video. I can't wait until November when they release additional workouts for this game.

title: Wii EA Sport Active Fitness
text: i love this Wii Fitness and i would definitely recommend it for anyone who is trying to get in shape and lose some weight or just to tone up or down in the right areas.  It targets the areas that you want to work on getting rid of.

title: Try Something Else
text: I was extremely disappointed in this product.  I was so looking forward to getting into some fun exercise, but this was more annoying than anywhere near exercise.  As others stated, the leg band kept falling down (and it's not because my thighs are skinny!), if I wasn't holding the controls perfectly, the exercise would stop and I would have to stand there for a long time until I figured it out. This happened over and over.  The competitions are not challenging at all.  Maybe, just maybe, this would work for someone who has NEVER worked out before.  They might find it fun.  But if you are looking for a workout that is challenging and enjoying, this is not for you.  I wish I would have listened to the critical comments instead of the great ones.  I learned a lesson!  I would have saved myself time and money.

title: Great workout!
text:
so far ive only 'played' about 4 times, but it seems like ill get a really good workout from this game. im doing the 30 day challenge and plan on adding this game to my regular workout that i do (which is just running and pushups haha!)

just to get it out there i am a 26 year old male, 5'10 and 3/4 and weight about 205lbs at the moment...

the first 2 times i played i tried the game on medium and got a good workout. i finished a little bit sweaty and could feel what i was working out the next day even a little bit! that impressed me. i took a few weeks off without the game and so i started a new 30 day challenge so that i wouldnt be cheating. when i went back to it i decided to try the high intense workout, and high intense it was! by the end of the workout i was dripping sweat! I felt it a lot in my legs the next day, i just wish they would add more upper body the same way they do with the legs. maybe they will though later on and i just didnt get that far yet. dont get me wrong, they do have arm workouts, but some of them are only 1 or 2 sets. I also have my own workout cables that i use rather than the one that came with the game because mine have a lot more resistance on them, but with more resistance i did find that its harder to do the correct movements that the game asks for in order to accept each rep. this got frustrating for me, but i will get used to it or just workout with a little bit less weight than i did on my last workout and work my way up a little bit more gradually.

all in all i think this is a great workout program and if you have been thinking about starting to workout or need more motivation to work out that this would be a great tool to use. i think if you stay with it you will DEFINATLEY lose weight, there is noway to deny that after i saw how much i was sweating on my last workout, and it only took about 30 minutes to complete all the excersizes, when i go to the gym im usually there for about 2 hours! what a difference!

title: I like it but wish there was more
text: I do like the Wii Active and feel that it does work.  The only thing I don't like is that you can't review the exercise before other than watching the "watch me".  For example, while making my own workout, there were 6 different icons for volleyball.  Sure they say, SET, HIT, BUMP, SERVE, ETC but it would be nice to see the whole thing first to decide if I can Volleyball #1, #2 or #3, etc.  The other thing is it seems as if they target mostly upper or lower body areas.  Being a typical middle aged woman that enjoys a good beer now and then, I need to target mostly my middle and there wasn't alot to choose from.  I do think it works.  I really like the 30 day challenge idea but again, seemed like it targeted upper & lower mostly.  But so far I've tried Gold's Gym (like for boxing)[[ASIN:B001KX504C Gold's Gym Cardio Workout]], Jillian's Fitness[[ASIN:B001DDBBSS Jillian Michaels Fitness Ultimatum 2009]]My Fitness Coach [[ASIN:B001H0RZX2 My Fitness Coach]] and Wii Fit [[ASIN:B002BSA3EM Wii Fit Plus with Balance Board]] and of them all I like Active the best.

title: Just what I needed
text: This game is just what I needed.  It is the trainer in the box!  The steps are all explained.  I am new to working out and Im glad I got something that is not boring.

title: Difficult
text: Tried it a couple of times, leg thing is a general pain in the ...  Stuck it in a drawer, won't find it for a couple of years.  Fine with me.

title: Definitely recommend this game!!!
text: Wow, I went into this with reserves thinking there was no way a Wii was going to give me a gym quality workout.  Boy was I wrong!  Ten minutes in, and I'm thinking, this is great...I can keep up and it's fun and easy to use...perfect.  Thirty minutes in and I was gaping huge gasps of cold air from my backdoor like a dying goldfish.  Forty minutes in...I'm a quivering heap of jello yelling obscenities at the TV (and I'm not in bad shape, been working out with gym equipment for seven months and not overweight, about 5'5" and 130 lbs).  I had to stop and catch my breath several times during my first workout (so many lunges...so, so many lunges), but I was using the "hard" setting so maybe I should have started off a bit easier.  Still, great workout, got me sweating, and seemed like something most people could use easily.  I had no trouble using any of the the accessories, leg band, etc all worked fine.  I'm trying to lose about 10-15 pounds more and I'm not sure that this burns a ton of calories so I don't know that this will be my one and only routine, thinking maybe 3-4 times a week would suffice for toning along with my usual cardio workout for weightloss but we'll see.  I do enjoy using the program and it has enough variety to keep me busy for a long, long time. Two thumbs up for sure!!

title: EA Sports Active - Post 30 day Challenge
text:
Like many reviewers, I thought this product was going to be a "game" vs a workout, but I was wrong. I'm trying to get back into shape after having a hip fracture finally heal, and bought this after comparing reviews of the Wii Fit and other fitness games. To be fair to the program, I didn't rush to post a review after the 1st workout, but waited until a full month has passed.

Since I'm not new to exercising, I did my 1st 30 day challenge on the medium intensity, and was sweating at the end of each session. I worked out with the program once, sometimes twice a day, and also added running, yoga, and aerobics to my fitness regimen. At the end of the 30 days, I am 12 pounds lighter, and have lost nearly 15 inches. I admit, I did cheat a bit and restart several of the exercises to increase the intensity and duration of the workout, which helped to burn a lot more calories than projected.

While I rated a 5 star in "fun-ness", I only am giving 4 stars for the overall rating due to the following reasons:

1) Continuity. After day 1 or 2, the user should be allowed to just move from one exercise into the next without having the video interruptions. This would allow heart rate to stay at a relatively high rate.

2) Weak resistance band. While mine didn't snap as other users reported, it was weak, so I went out and purchased a set of 3 different bands at a local sporting goods store to combat this. Even using the "easy" band, the challenge was 100% harder. The 3 bands were only $12.00, so I don't consider that exorbitant.

3) Constant changing of nunchuck/bands. During the pre-set workouts, the user is constantly putting nunchuck in/taking out of strap. Likewise, the use/non use of band. I wish the pre-set workouts would do all upper body exercises first, and then switch to lower, or vise versa. This con, too, can be overcome by creating personalized workouts.

4) Lack of proper warm up and cool down. Cool down typically is a few dance moves or 10 paces of walking. That's really not long enough. Perhaps the next version can have warm up and cool down exercises that you can choose before the workout.

5) Lack of consistency in the "trainer comments". For instance, I put in the journal entry my 30 minute run at a 7 intensity, and also indicated that I had 6 hrs of sleep. Even after these, the "trainer" recommended that I add yet another workout to my day, since the sleep increased my energy. The journal needs to take information from both parts: nutrition and other activity and then make comments overall.

6) Lack of focus on strengthening the core. Like many, I wish the program did have more exercises that focused on the midsection and lower back.

7) Nunchuck cord too short, or gets in the way. I am considering ordering an adaptor to make the nunchuck wireless; but haven't really read if that is worthwhile.

Regarding other comments re: interface problems: the only exercise that my system had a problem registering was kickups. The slow ones registered fine; fast ones, on the other hand, only registered about 1/2 the time. Unfortunately, this meant that it took me much longer to complete the exercise, especially considering that my pace didn't change once.

Unlike other reviewers, I didn't really see the problem with focusing on the left during the majority of basketball exercises, since it focused more on the right during tennis.

Also, I didn't ever have a problem with the leg strap falling down. I positioned it fairly high on my legs, and it was tight (but not cutting off circulation), and it stayed in position very well.

Bottom line: obviously, this is a video game. It does not, and will not, replace actually going to a gym, or working out on machines. Do I wish it was more challenging? Yes. Do I think that it is geared towards non-exercisers? Absolutely. Is it a total and complete waste of money? No. The program, like many of its kind, has a few hangups which make it a little difficult, but not impossible to use.

Lastly, I watched some of the videos on the EA Sports website that stated another edition will be coming out later this year in time for the holidays, and am looking forward to it. Some of the changes that are supposedly being implemented include more core workouts, different scenery, different music, and different exercises. Like a prior reviewer stated this edition seems to be the buggy one that will be fixed with subsequent editions.

title: Promising, but doesn't deliver well.
text:
So normally I don't comment about stuff like this, but this is somewhat ridiculous. Anytime you run (which is every day in the challenge mode), half the time you're fighting the thing registering how fast it thinks your moving. It only has 3 speeds: too slow, perfect, and really fast. Most of the exercises have some element that doesn't register perfectly, which is expected, but it feels like they didn't test with more than one body type.

The leg strap was too small, and I'm not an enormous guy. After 2 months of my wife and I using it, the strap is so worn we're going to have to buy a new one because this one's almost stretched out.

Looking online, there are a lot of people that have had these problems and have come up with their own solutions to "fix" these issues, but overall it reeks of EA selling this game to marketing before talking with any kind of programmer. Some of these issues could have been resolved by doing things like using 2 Wiimotes per person instead of the nunchuck. Some more of the issues could have been solved by some more testing. Some are just bad ideas.

All in all, this is a great idea, it's just very poorly executed.

title: More intensive than Wii Fit
text:
So I've been doing this for a few weeks now and I love it. The idea of doing all the exercises in a row, unlike WiiFit is great. Personally I love Wii Fit, lost almost 15 lbs playing it a few days a week, BUT one thing that always bugged me was 2 minute exercise, then you watch where you place then do i wanna do it again, then no then back to the menu click click click click click ok there's the next one in the line. It wasn't an issue that made me return it but when playing with my boyfriend we found it too almost an hour for us to switch back and forth on exercises and complete 15-20 minutes of play each.
With EA Active, I make a 60 minute work out it, there's a small delay in between activities but its not like I remember every time that this is the exercise where i need to tilt the wii-mote when I pull my arms up. I never had a problem with it not registering me and each move I do, actually doing a better job than the Wii Fit an noticing. I love bring in the balance board, adding kicks to boxing, I LOVE it. Be careful thought because you can fall if you don't pay attention to what you are doing.
Now I have had no problems with my red band, we have 2 his and hers, I am pretty short, one of the main reasons I have my own (the one with the box) I just did the loops for the handles at a height that suits me, took 2 attempts before I got it right, he's tall so he has it looped at the end (we did get the official multi player pack). Also, I thought I hated it the first workout because the leg strap kept falling off me, if you are having this problem, move it keep it at the top of your thigh and you're fine.
People seem to compare using a video game to going to the gym, of course having a personal trainer, and hitting the gym is better. It will always be better and no video game can replace that. Compare it instead to walking around the block each day or a jog, why would someone who is at the gym 5 days a week want to replace that with a video game. I personally hate the idea of joining a gym, having people see me work out, struggling in public, these things are not something I would want to deal with. Thats why I picked a game at home. Its more fun than walking, you can do it inside with the AC, you don't have to deal with working out in front of people, and it mixes things up giving you more options than a tape. This was a great investment especially for me. Not only because because of previous reasons, but I'm not watching TV during the weekends/afterwork. within 2 weeks we saved enough to cover the cost of the game from not going out AND its changed our outlook on what we eat for dinner and what we do going out, staying in etc.

title: Love, Love, Love it!!
text: I have been a gym rat for the last 20 years and consider myself to be in pretty good shape.  However, after using the Wii Active for the last 2 1/2 weeks, I am feeling a difference in my body.  I am using muscles I was not previously using at the gym.  I currently still workout at the gym but I also regularly use and enjoy the different workouts with the Wii Active.  I especially like the fact that I am able to customize my own workouts.  The track and sports exercises are my favorite, along with the squat exercises.  I do wish that abdominal exercises were included in the workouts.  I highly recommend the Wii Active regardless of your current activity level.  It will get you moving!

title: Best Workout Plan =]
text: This package is really good. I bought it today and am tryiing the 30 day challenge and I'm going to try to keep up with it because trust me you sweat alot while doing this. I had trouble sticking to a workout or going to the gym ebcause of laziness or embarassed of people seeing me workout but this can be done in the living room (like I do it) and you just work out. I recommend it fully!

title: A decent workout!
text: I was pleasantly surprised by this game -- I was actually sore after the first few workouts!  I definitely recommend it to anyone who has little time to fit in a fitness routine.  There is plenty of variety in the workouts.  I haven't finished the 30-day challenge yet, so I'll need to wait and see if there's some structure to the workout sequences after that.  A great game!

title: Overall a Good Purchase
text:
I am a 5'2", 110 lb, 27 yr old female. I grew up very active and played many sports, but like many, I now have a computer job and sit at my desk all day. I'm lucky in that I work from home, so I do my workout during my lunch break. I am by no means overweight, but I have just noticed my composition changing as I get older. I don't want to spend the $$ for a gym membership, and the convenience of doing it at home is worth it. Overall I am really happy with the game so far.

I have been doing the high intensity workouts, and they can be exhausting (especially all of the jumping!). I've seen some reviews about 20 min workouts taking 40-60 minutes because of the tutorials and trouble getting the remote sensors to read correctly. I haven't really had this problem. If you are familiar with basic exercises you don't really need to watch the tutorials, and once you've seen them they're easy to skip through. I can easily jump straight from one exercise to the next, only taking time to tuck in the nunchuck or grab the resistance band. I rarely have sensor problems, but I agree with another post on here that it always tells me I'm going too fast with the jump lunges.

I read reviews beforehand and didn't even bother using the resistance band that came with it and bought a separate one when I purchased the game. I definitely recommend attaching the straps that came with it to the new band though, as a band you buy likely has handles that are too bulky and awkward to hold at the same time as the controllers. It took me a few workouts to figure that out, and it has made a big difference.

title: NO left hand option!
text:
Buyer beware!! No left hand option! Makes playing baseball etc difficult.

Not a problem for regular exercises such as lunges, bicept curls, etc. though.

title: Nice fitness game
text: I like what I've seen of this game so far. It is a nice option for working out at home - but I'm definitely waiting for more intense workouts to come in the 30 day workout challenge (I've only done two workouts so far). My favorite exercise is boxing! There are lots of lunges, and squats so be ready for that!

title: Quality exercise at Home
text:
I was curious after hearing from coworkers aboutEA Sports Active. I have used it once since recently receiving it. I am a pretty devoted runner and exercise enthusiast and found the product to be a good workout. The program seems to be accurately sensing my movements and tracking my progress. It does depend on the user holding the sensors in hand while working out which is a bit difficult and may be discouraging over time.

Best to have a good space to totally engage in the workout. Don't have a TV in a room devoted to exercise and that is a disadvantage although it can be done in front of any TV. Would prefer a better quality of the resistance band supplied with the system and will replace it with one of my own.
Definitely could take the place of an aerobics class if done correctly.

title: Great Workout!
text:
I received EA Sports Active as a gift after owning a Wii Fit and loving it. The problem I had with the Fit was that it lacked vigorous cardio exercises, and the exercises did not flow together very well. The Active fixed both those problems. The exercises are intense, and the preset workouts have a quick flow to them, which keeps your heart rate up and really enhances your workout.

Being nitpicky, there are only a couple downsides. The first is the resistance band, which is fairly weak. I would shorten it in order to add more resistance to my exercises, which ended up causing some tears. I eventually replaced it with a stronger one. Secondly, in a few exercises (kickups, inline skating, and sometimes lunges) placing the nunchuck in the leg strap causes a lack of sensitivity. While it's not too bad, these tend to be the some of the tougher exercises, and it's extremely frustrating to be doing a killer exercise and have the game tell you it's incorrect.

All in all, this game is highly recommended for someone who wants to get in shape at home. Good luck!

title: Hope Next Version Will Be Better
text:
This product feels like it was rushed out before it was ready. The biggest issue is timing. Your avatar moves before or after you move. Some exercises (like lunges) have you hold the position for a second longer on one side than the other. The next rep is either rushed after the last one, or they make you wait too long (and then you get scolded for jumping the gun). The trainer's encouraging sound bites have no connection to what you are doing. (I got a "Right on!" for adjusting the leg strap.) One last irritation: on Bentover Rows With Triceps Kickbacks, they have your avatar look around helplessly at the end of every rep.

I suggest you wait for the next version and hope they've ironed out these glitches. Oh, and Bob Greene is creepy.

title: Fun and entertaining
text: I have tried EA Sports Active with and without the Wii Board and prefer not to use it.  It was too time consuming taking shoes on and off and the activities weren't as enjoyable.  I have also found that on a handful of times the game didn't always respond during the punching and kicking activity, but primarily during a track event like running.  I would maintain my pace but the game would seem to think I had slowed down.  Otherwise, it's been great fun and I like how you can earn medals and customize your playlist.  I just wish there was some way for the Wii Fit and EA Sports Active to communicate together.  I think having a product that combined both programs would be great.

title: Outstanding!!!
text:
The EA Active 30-day challenge is a very good workout for someone who is just starting an exercise plan. It keeps you challenged and motivated to continue on the program. I like that it has a video demonstrating the moves.

The only thing I dislike is that sometimes you don't get the right motion and the game freezes up until you get in synch. The hints are helpful but not always accurate in where the problem is regarding how the exercise is being done.

OVERALL RATING: A+

title: EA Active
text: Very good, it gets my heart going that is for sure. I like this one the best!!

title: EA Sports Active
text: I love this product because it's like having a personal trainer and it keeps me motivated. I can do the workouts at my own pace and for as much or as little as I choose. So even on a very hectic day, I can still fit in a short workout.

title: Awesome workout!
text: I recently bought the Wii Active because I was looking for a good workout that would be fun and convenient that I could do just in my home. After using this game for the first time I was amazed at how much it worked me! I started off with a 20 min exercise that worked almost every part of my body to the core! They make it easy for you to follow along! If anyone is looking for a good workout that cost less than going to the gym, this is the game to get! Love It!!

title: A little disappointed
text:
It seems that I am in the minority here, but overall I was disappointed in this game.

The good:
If you ignore all the pre-programmed training and go for cardio and the more-isometric based exercises, it is a very nice game. Creating a customized workout is easy, and you can make and save several. This is great for a 15-minute before work morning workout and a 30 minute cardio in the evening. The ability to have multiple custom workouts is a great improvement over Wii Fit Plus (Which I will use for all my comparisons).

The bad:
The exercises seem to lack the variety that Wii Fit Plus offers, and that's not saying much. How many different "activities" can they make out of hitting a volleyball, or going through the basketball free throw motion? Apparently a lot. The exercises are too similar and not varied enough for my taste. The typical workout in the 30-day challenge went jog,squat,do some strange exercise with the band, jump, squat, repeat.

The use of the band was awkward at best. Holding the band, and the controller, and doing the exercises that the "trainer" wanted was not pleasant. To get any benefit out of the band, I had to stand over it with doubled under my feet to shorten it, but then I was afraid I would break it.

The dancing could have been a lot better. The balance board integration was weak, and most dancing was pointing you hands in a random direction. And apparently no one told EA that disco was dead -- the lawn mower? the shopping cart? That said, I still enjoyed this activity to the point where I actually wish the dance activities were *longer*, which leads to...

The cardio activies (apart from the long run) were just way too short. By the time I finish the two minute exercise, and wait for the next one to load, I'm halfway cooled down (and I am not in that great of shape). Rhythm boxing, longer dance sequences, step aerobics, more scenic "runs"... any of these would greatly improve the game.

My nit-picky complaints:
The trainer went a painfully slow pace through many of the exercises. And the trainer expects you to stay in time, which is hard when there is no real rhythm.

Rollerblading? This was just dumb and ill-conceived. The balance board version version was even worse. I have to wonder if they tested some of these activities before they shipped, or if these were thrown in at the last minute.

There is no feature to weigh yourself with the balance board. ( Like Wii Fit )

The music is awful. Why can't I play a mp3 off the sd card? ( Like Excite Truck )

title: Great for advanced exercisers!
text:
So, I was a little worried when I purchased this game that it would be way too easy. I am pretty fit, working out 5-6 days a week for an hour at a time. Let me just say...I was not disappointed at all!

This game is amazing, the cardio workouts really get your heart rate up, and they are a lot of fun, such as the volleyball and inline skating intervals. It makes you feel like you're not exercising at all! I was so into the inline skating I didn't even realize how badly my thighs were burning until the very end...lol As well, I burned in one hour just as many calories as I would in an hour of running. (I checked with my Polar HR monitor)

Ok, now for the gripes, and they are minor. The bands suck. If you have any upper body strength at all they won't be challenging. I am going to see if I can use my hand weights or maybe buy some wrist weights to try out. Secondly, the calorie count is really inaccurate, but I think you should expect that from something that isn't tracking your heart rate throughout. In an hour, it told me I burned 230 calories and it was actually 560... but whatever. The last thing would be the Wii remote. Definitely invest in a wireless. I don't know how many times I accidentally whipped myself in the face with the cord while doing volleyball serves....lol

Other than that, awesome investment that will keep me interested for a long while. I may cancel my gym membership!

title: Not too impressed.
text: We bought this for our physical clinic and have been playing with it for a few days before giving exercises to patients.  I don't feel like it really works you that hard.  The exercises are easy and you barely break a sweat.  Maybe if you're a couch potato, this is a great program to get you off the couch but if you're in shape at all, skip it.  There is not a very large variety of exercises.  The basketball exercises don't work very well (the controllers don't transmit the twist to the left that you have to do to pick up the ball very well).  Each exercise has a duration of only 3 to 4 minutes at the most and then you rest a lot in between because they always show you the videos (even though you can skip them, it ends up giving you a 30 second rest between exercises that only last 4 minutes).  Also, there is too long of a rest between repetitions so you can't effectively fatigue your muscles.  Even on the hardest settings, the exercises seem too short/easy.  I wish there was a larger variety of exercises and more flexibility in setting the difficulty/duration/speed of the exercises.

title: EA Sports Active Review
text: Great workout program and I loved the fact you can customize your workout to suite your needs. You can also change the music which is a great feature.

title: excellent home workout by Melany
text: I have cp. I have been doing the 30 day challenge for 3wks. My balence is limited. I can not run so, I hold the nunchuck in my right hand ( instead of the leg strap)I don't use the exercise band either. I hold my 4lb. wieghts in my hands along with remotes and do it that way. It is much easier and faster for me this way.And I can feel it in my arms more this way. For me, it is simply just about moving as much as possible any way  I can. I also do a workout of just playing sports when I'm done doing the challenge of the day. My balence and stability have improved greatly. I can't wait to get the more workout game in Nov.This game allows me to kind of do things I may never do. I love it! It is wonderful to work up a good sweat and have a great time with a friend or all by yourself, at home!

title: EA Active - Excellent
text: I love my EA Active.  I have been using WiiFit for about 6 months and wanted more variety/challenge.  EA Active gives that and more.  I read about a lot of issues with the exercise band (breaking) and the leg strap (slipping).  I've not had any problems with either one.  I've been using it for a month now, 5 days a week.  Still love it and am I'm getting my daughter one for her birthday.

title: Motivating workout
text: I got the wii Active last week and love it! It makes working out fun. It gives a clear picture of how many calories each exercise burns and helps me realize that I need to work out more. I also have the wii fit plus. I like them both but the Active gives a better cardio workout. The fit is good for balance, yoga, etc. If you are looking for a good overall cardio workout, the Active is a good purchase.

title: Eh - used it once
text: Really not that engaging.  Maybe we are just bored with the Wii, but this was no "Wii Fit" or "Wii Sport."  Bending movements just didn't seem to make sense.  Honestly pretty frustrated with it.  I'd give it a 1 star, but feel if more effort was applied you could do SOMETHING with this.

title: Great product for me when I customized it...
text:
Well, after reading several positive and negative reviews about this product, I decided to purchase it and make up my own mind. Now, the REALITY...it's a product marketed to thousands of people of different ages, genders, sizes, and abilities. Knowing this allowed me to have a more open mind as to how I approached it. After opening it and reading all the literature, which isn't much, I spent a few hours watching the instructional videos, so when I started using it, i would have the correct form and know to use and place the remotes. I also went to the Wii set-up menu and made sure that the distance range for the remotes to the sensor bar were correctly adjusted as I was closer to the bar when exercising that i was when playing a standard game. The distance will affect how one's movements are perceived.
I started easy with a few standard workouts and found them challenging and I felt that after combining them with others I had a rather extensive workout. I then decided to do the 30 day challenge. I'm now at #15 and here are a few of my observations. First, the resistance band is too light for my preference...easy fix, I purchased a heavier one, no fuss. Just make sure that it doesn't have bulky hand holds as trying to use it with the remotes will be awkward. I still didn't feel I was getting enough of the upper body workout I desired, I purchased 6 lb wrist weights with thumb lock...done. Now, with the heavier band and the wrist weights I feel as though i get a terrific workout. Secondly, If one shakes, moves too fast, or has jerky movements, the game will stop and add precautionary statements. No biggy, just follow the directions.
Any negativity will come from the fact that it doesn't have a weigh in. OK, not that big of a deal. Secondly, it's too easy to "game" the system by not following the directions, knowing how to move the remotes to simulate proper movements, and finally not having a partner/coach to either yell at you to do it right or assist you in keeping proper position/posture. Well, there's the trade off with a club membership and personal trainer vs at-home exercising. I have no aspirations of being an olympic athlete, nor win the New York marathon. If that's the level that one is trying to attain, then this is NOT the product for you, but if one is striving to exercise more, be in the privacy of one's own home, and have a pretty fun time doing it, then by-all means consider this product.
This product is not the "be-all" of exercise videos/games. It does require one to be committed in their pursuit, honest in their expectations, and open to adding custom accessories. I get a great workout, losing nearly 10 lbs in the last 20 days, and I have heard comments from my family as to being in better shape. No product, right out of the box is going to be perfect for everyone, but with a little tweeking, I find this an absolute keeper in my daily routine.

title: Nice try EA but off mark.
text:
I really wish people would rate products after having used them more than once or twice, otherwise EA Sports Active wouldn't have as many positive reviews... on that note...

The workouts in EA Sports Active are for lack of a better word, boring. EA tries to make the program more interesting by throwing in activities like basketball, tennis, baseball etc, however most can't be considered workouts and they really aren't that fun. Detection for them is very crude and there is pretty much no skill involved, this is no Wii Sports.
At first glance it appears that there are a-lot of various workouts BUT after about 5 or 6 workouts you discover that it really only has a lot of different ways of working the same muscle groups. The program concentrates on quadriceps, biceps with some shoulder and triceps exercises and the occasional kickback which kind of exercises your glutes. Forget about anything that will isolate abs or back. As for the program being continuous it is not, there is a loading time between the exercises and you need to press the A button to continue which interrupts the flow a bit, this is minor but enough that I wouldn't call this a continuous workout. All in all I would have to say that the range of exercises is disappointing.

The thing that is supposed to make EA Sports Active worth more money as apposed to a ten dollar workout DVD is one of the things that ends up making it more frustrating. The detection of a few of the exercises is downright HORRIBLE, especially the bicep curl and upright rows. The program will sometimes get stuck and display a message stating that you need to hold the Wii nunchuck still, the message will not go away even if it's perfectly still (including if you set both the Wiimote and nunchuck on something) this forces you to play (read redo the exercise over and over) with the controllers until the program recovers (which is almost always more than a minute and once for us was greater than 5 minutes.) The designers for some reason decided not to include a timeout or continue in case this screw-up happens which is very dumb in my opinion. Also, because it attempts to "detect" everything, for which is does rather poorly, your exercise timing is always off and since it detects your right side better than your left you end up with an uneven workout. As an example if you are doing lunges (which you do a lot of) you will hold your left side lunge much longer than your right.

The balance board support is tacked on and really serves no purpose. I really don't understand what others mean by it adding "intensity" to the exercises because that claim is false. What do you get with the addition of the balance board? Stand on one leg or the other. Step off the board and on again, that's it. There is nothing you can't do without it, therefore I would say that it appears that this "feature" was more of a marketing ploy and really adds no value to the program. You will get the same (or better) experience without the balance board. We disabled the use of the balance board after about 4 workouts because it was more of a pain then it's usefulness to this program. I'm still waiting for an application from Nintendo or a 3rd party that will justify the money spent on my balance board, so far no luck.

The equipment included is pretty weak, as described by most people. The nunchuck band slips down. In fact you will probably get better use out of a pair of shorts with a side pocket to hold the nunchuck, the resistance band has very little resistance so having weights is probably a better way to go. Also, unlike most of the workout DVD's I've tried you can start EA Sports Active on HARD. I'm way out of shape and the HARD on this is less of a workout than the easy workout on many of our DVD collections. Do you sweat, yes. Is it that difficult NO. As an example there are many workout DVD's which I can not complete the beginners stages, however with EA Sports Active I've had no problems completing the HARD setting. The two hardest workouts are: 1. hold squat for 1 minute. 2. Four minutes of fast kickbacks. Other than those two it's really not all that difficult.

If you are expecting EA Sports Active to motivate you more than any other workout DVD then don't waste your money. Instead buy 6 workout DVD's for the price because it will add a lot more variety and you will get a more divers and well rounded workout. However If you really love squats and lunges then EA Sports Active is the ticket for you. If you want nice arms then I would suggest any other routine because EA Sports Active just doesn't do a good job and holding the Wiimote and nunchuck at the same time as weights or the resistance band makes doing the arm exercises awkward.

All in all even though there are a lot of positive feedback about EA Sports Active it's really not worth spending your hard earned money on and I truly believe that if most who give it a glowing review would change that review after having used it for sometime before writing their review.

title: Thoughts after Several Uses
text:
I wanted to update an early review (didn't know how) b/c I've now used it a few times. As I expected, I like the game and I'm using it (go me!) but it is getting too easy for me even though I'm out of shape now and put it on the hardest intensity. The 30 day challenge is good to get you going and makes you do exercises like squats/lunges that you would probably not do -- but it is not enough cardio, it's way too short and the repetitions take too long. So I did a regular challenge day, and then immediately followed with a custom workout (I kept jogging in place so as not to lower heart rate while clicking through menus - do this every time you switch exercises or you are coming to a standstill way too much). I set 35 mins. of running, mixed running (with kick ups and knee ups), running again, boxing (especially punching bag), some fast dance (mostly as a rest), boxing, knee ups and ended with volleyball for fun. Now that was cardio that got me seriously sweating.

Notes-- WEAR SHOES. My dr. warned me she's seeing lots of foot problems (esp. kids) b/c of using any active Wii game without shoes.

Also, leg strap stays on me if I wear workout pants only (no shorts) and strap cord through each slot.

Warm up and cool down yourself - game doesn't do it.

My toddler likes to play the sports with me - we just set up a "custom workout" with tennis, targets, volleyball etc. and then play them all through together.

All in all - definitely got this lazy runner off her butt at last.

title: Even better then the Two Towers! *shocker*
text:
Well as my title says, it is better! Not that I though it possible, but I've been proved wrong before.

A whole new side of Middle-earth is seen in this game and through new character's sides and through different paths. Play as Aragorn, Legolas, Gimli, Gandalf, Sam and Frodo as well as 3 other locked characters, gotta beat the game for them though and NO, the cheat codes won't free them until you've beat the game. I know, I tried. :-)

Just as in the Two Towers, this game had loads of nice extras like actor interviews, behinds the scenes, image boards and movie cut-ins. Along with the old actor voice overs, some new ones join in, such as Dominic Monaghan, Billy Boyd, Sean Astin, Andy Serkis and David Wenham. Can you guess who the locked characters might be?? :-)

You start the game with Gandalf at the end of Helm's Deep and then take your pick of 3 different paths. The Path of the Wizard, play as Gandalf but do it alone as he is alone on his route. The Path of the King takes Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli to the Paths of the Dead to face the dead army and on to face Mumakil and Trolls to Sauron's front door or the Paths of the (stout little) Hobbits as Sam and escape Osgiliath while hiding from the Ringwraiths, to Shelob's lair and fending off the enormous Spider (ew, bug) to finally facing off with Gollum as Frodo in the fight for the Ring.

Music from the movie, great special effects, actor voice-overs, atractive backgrounds and just a flat out good fight to stay alive make this a really good game. You almost feel like a part of it.

But before you go and buy something you might not like, rent it.

title: 2k fans show some RESPECT!!!
text:
Ok, first off let me say this....I am a long time fan of college basketball and EA Sports ever since NBA Live 95. With that being said, College Hoops 2k8 is the BEST NCAA B-Ball game ever made...BUT, NCAA Basketball 10 by EA is a close 2nd and has somethings that the 2k series doesn't and hasn't had that are great!

I LOVE THIS GAME.....I really do, I have been playing it for 2 years now, and it is very good. Being that EA already has over 10 sports titles, including Madden, Fifa, NBA Jam, etc, and 2k only has like what? 4 games to focus on? Give EA a break and to have their hands full...this game is DAMN GOOD!

The commentary is authentic, the courts are great. Unlike 2k the online mode is flawless, not much lag...and this game has never froze on me. The dynasty mode and player models are very well made and thought out. You can play up to a 30 year dynasty with any team of your choice. After the season there is also the McDonalds All American game....and the NIT. The ball handling is also better than any 2k bball game that I have ever played! You can also take over a smaller school and take them to the NCAA with other job offers along the way.

This game does have flaws and glitches, but what game doesn't? This is an overall FUN and GREAT game, there are even people that have done very good roster updates online for the 2010-2011 season that you can download for FREE! Sorry for you Xbox "brown nosers". If you dont have this game, get it.....and get it now! It is the last for a while by EA, but you can find it cheaper at a pawn shop Im sure. Is this the best b-ball game ever? NO, but you 2k punks quit hating until you play it for at least a week, ENJOY FOLKS!!!!!!

- A. Lindsay (Louisville, KY)

title: Bugs? Yes, but still fun!
text:
I love this expansion pack! The sets are gorgeous, with the open-world movement adding to the vacation experience that "The Sims 2: Bon Voyage" lacked. It's a little expensive to go on trips initially, but if you like to collect things (and who doesn't?) your Sim can come home richer than he/she left! Oh, and make sure you check out the new display cases for showing off your loot. The largest, two-shelved one is particularly interesting... ;)

The adventures themselves are interesting, fun and with varying degrees of challenge. The tomb exploration feature is delightful, with traps, clues (look in every nook and cranny, people!) and new discoveries around every corner! Some of the challenges will send your Sims to a different adventure destination altogether, leaving the remainder of their vacation time to explore on their own. There are new gems to find, new fish to catch, new recipes to learn and new friends to make, so your Sims will have lots of reasons to keep coming back!

There are a few bugs, true. One of my Sims came home with a new last name and a child by someone he'd never met. Rather than being an inconvenience, I had him go meet the family who was "fostering" his "son" and he walked away with 4 more friends. I did have another Sim reach the end of her elderhood, only to reset back to the beginning when I to her to the dresser to change her outfit. Easily avoidable. Other than that, I haven't yet experienced anything to make me regret purchasing this expansion pack (knocking on wood!).

title: NCAA Basketball by EA, are you kidding me?
text: Ladies and Gentlemen, if you are wondering why I hate EA basketball games, then take a look at this game and you will see for your self. Some people will give you a load of crap by comparing this game to games that are two, three years old if not older. Don't buy into this crap. This game I will grant you has a ton of options, and two different types of commentaters, on the one side you have the ESPN set, which gives you the ESPN Broadcasting team and they do avery good job. The other team of folks, well let's just say they do a lack luster job. If your team is even a one point difference in the ratings you will get blown out of the water. Your people make passes that even a first your freshman knows he shouldn't make. This game lacks a lot of things that hey, I could write all day about. This is why EA, went the extra mile to lock up the Colligate basketball license, as well as the NFL license, because the competition (2ksports) where rapidly over taken the sports game market, buy storm. Everyone that is a 2ksports fan, knows without a doubt that 2k would have produced a college basketball that would have been well worth the money. If you don't believe me, just go on youtube, and check out videos from their other sports games (NBA 2k10, Mlb 2k10, NHL 2k10), and see for yourself. That is what a game should look like, sound like, and play like. I will wait it out until 2k gives me a collegiate basketball game that I can enjoy and be proud to have in my library. Yes, I did buy this game, because I wanted to give them a chance to prove they had a quality product, and yes I was disappointed. No, I will not buy another basketball game from EA, and YES, I am selling my copy. Save your money, and go 2k.

title: it should be noted that this controller functions like a Wii Classic Controller (or Classic Controller Pro)
text:
The controller is a worthy replacement for the original GameCube controller. However, it should be noted that this controller functions like a Wii Classic Controller (or Classic Controller Pro), and is NOT specifically for the Wii U. Because of that, you will need to own a Wii Remote or Wii Remote Plus in order to use this controller, and the controller is only compatible with those Wii and Wii U games that function with the Classic Controller or Classic Controller Pro. Again, this does NOT function as a Wii U Pro Controller, which is the Xbox 360-esque wireless controller made specifically for the Wii U.

As for the controller itself, all the buttons and both thumbsticks are nice. The thumbsticks are neither too loose or tight, and are fairly close to the original GameCube controller in terms of the kind of pressure you will need to apply to each stick. The Control Pad is shaped slightly thinner than that found on the GameCube controller, but still functions well and is comfortable to use. The L and R triggers on the back of the controller are not analog as they are on the GameCube, and function instead as simple buttons like the two shoulder ZL and ZR buttons.

The controller also features a turbo function that is quite easy to set, although you have to keep up with which buttons have the turbo function activated and which do not. The turbo frequency can be set to 5, 10, and 20 button presses per second via a switch located on the front face of the controller. The controller also features the ability to completely reset and disable the turbo functionality by holding the turbo button down and pressing the Select button. Pressing the Home button will also disable the turbo functionality, however, so you will need to re-activate the turbo function on each button if you should enter and exit from the Home screen while using the controller.

Overall, the controller is very comfortable to use. The are only a few drawbacks: incompatibility with some Wii U games that utilize the Wii U Pro Controller, but not necessarily the Wii's Classic Controller or Classic Controller Pro, the fact that this controller does not function as an actual GameCube controller, and the fact that you must also have a Wii Remote (or Wii Remote Plus) with which to use the controller. If you are looking for analog L and R triggers, then that's another possible drawback. Otherwise, it's an excellent controller.

title: is it any good? Picture quality is decent
text:
A budget system that can be played in HD, but the question is, is it any good?

Picture quality is decent, colors are bright and vibrant, clarity is decent as well. Obviously, a High Def NES will look better, so don't expect anything overwhelming, granted, it's a huge step up from Composite. Though, I just can't confirm it's playing in true 720p, especially after seeing the Retrousb AVS in action.

Sound is fine when it actually gets it right, as I am running into more and more problems due to the system not reading the sound chip correctly. Music just seems off, especially from Castlevania 2 and Castlevania 3, and now in Batman, which is as common as an NES game as you can get. It's just a mixed bag and a toss up whether the music will play correctly, which is a deal breaker for some.

Compatibility is poor, I have to add that music is thrown in this category as well due to the game being fully functional. In addition, just ran into a problem playing Total Recall. The game just crashes on the first level and when trying it on a real front loader, the game works as it should. While most won't complain that a game like Total Recall won't work, you have to wonder what other games will not be compatible, especially when Total Recall is a very common game.

To conclude, at least you get good pack in controllers, they are good enough to use on a real NES. Another plus is that the 8 bitdo's dongle and controllers work just fine offering a wireless solution, which is awesome. In the end, I can't fully recommend this system, but for the money, it's good value, again just don't expect too much: 6.5/10

title: Violent, intense, puzzle-solving action!
text:
The Thing, if you don't already know, is based on the 1982 film by John Carpenter. The film has been dubbed the title of the goriest (if you will) movie ever made. The game, however not THE goriest game ever made (one example of a game gorier than The Thing is Resident Evil: Code Veronica X), this game is EXTREMELY violent. Take a true gamer's opinion: this game definitely earned its 'M' rating.
With the "Not for children w/ queasy stomachs" factor out of the way, lets get to the game:
1) Graphics-8.5
2) Gameplay-9.0
3) Controls-7.5
4) Story-(although unoriginal by today's standards)9.5
5) Overall-9.0
This game is an incredible one. From blowing off heads w/ a sniper rifle, to torching Thing beasts w/ a flamethrower, this game will provide you with a nonstop adrenaline rush. In addition, puzzles are added to balance the game a bit. Some require the simple resupply of power to a fuse box, while others require more strategic and complex thinking. Think of it like this: Resident Evil (any) with better controls, better weapons, and a lot more actual fighting (the RE series focuses more around puzzles than gunfights).
This game, although long, can be completed within 1 or 2 rentals. I would not recommend buying this game unless you are a diehard fan of The Thing, or you just need some variety in you game collection.

title: Rent It
text:
I don't own very many games. I could say it's because I'm very selective, but really it's because I don't have much money. Because of that I try to select games that have alot of replay value. Games that you can play and beat, then continue playing without just rehashing the same thing. I bought the game because the graphics were outstanding, the game play offered some new features, like the element of fear in dealing with the other characters. Also I am a big fan of the movie. The game reproduces the feeling of the movie really well, but the original elements of the character interaction could have been handled better and the game has very little replay value.
While the fear/trust elements are interesting, sometimes they are just cumbersome. As other reviewers have mentioned the ability to blood test your team members is sometimes useless, the tests are better spent testing yourself to gain the trust of the others. The movie relied more on mystery and suspense, not knowing where the Thing was going to strike. In the game there are hundreds of small things running around, coming seemingly out of nowhere. Some levels don't offer enough assistance/weapons and they don't give you any idea what you are supposed to do. You just end up repeating the levels again and again, until you practically memorize what is going to happen. That takes some of the fun out of the game.
The game is still fun. But it only takes a couple of days to beat, even with repeating some levels again and again. After you beat it, the game doesn't offer anything new. There's no difficulty levels, the only changeable options available is narrowing the auto-aim area. So you just end up playing again. Overall, I'm dissapointed with this game. It does NOT provide worthwhile entertainment. I recommend you rent it. If you fall in love with it, and you have money to burn, then by all means buy it.

title: EA = FAIL
text:
I've been a loyal follower of the Sims from the earliest of times. As the games progressed, tiny problems began popping up. I never really noticed them in The Sims. When The Sims 2 was released, these problems came roaring out of the gate. I don't need to list them all, but first, many of us suffered a violin issue that, once placed, made the "tile" unplayable. Then there was the constant disappearance of the head master for the private school. (EA did send out a patch for the violin. The head master was never fixed, at least for me)

Now comes The Sims 3. I'm so excited. It was great. The best one yet. And when they announced their first expansion pack, World Adventures, we're all thinking "great! This should be AWESOME." And it should be. But EA won't get their behinds in gear and FIX WHAT THEY'VE CREATED. This game came out 2 weeks ago. 2 WEEKS. Where is the patch for this? Most players are experiencing unbearable load times, crashes to the desktop, unable to save the game, families and neighborhoods disappearing, blue/black holes where houses or other items used to be, Sims' relationship panels completely turning red and removing ALL friends and family from the contact tab, ages drastically changing when wanting to change clothes or hair styles, babies and toddlers being deformed, sims magically having unexplained and unknown children with foreigners while on vacation (yet they never interacted in that way), and these are all from the top of my head.

For most people it's unplayable. I can actually play the game, but have quite a few of the "bugs" listed. When you're terrified to actually send your sim on a vacation or save your game, what on earth was the point on wasting money with this Expansion Pack?! I'm sure EA works hard, but they must have slept through testing this pack. And the thing that irritates most of the hardcore sim players: EA refuses to comment, respond, admit or FIX these issues. In fact, they seem to delight in deleting posts on their forum from people who complain, especially about THEIR COMPANY. God forbid someone wants to return the game! They're not listening to the millions of players on their own website, so be warned. This game is REALLY bad at the moment. Until EA wakes up from their Thanksgiving turkey slumber, we'll all have to suffer. And to be honest, no one knows when they'll return.

title: Much better than expected!!
text: Let me preface this review by saying I am a very hardcore Animal Crossing fan- I've played all of the games except the original GameCube and I'm pretty picky about the new games sticking to the original tone of Animal Crossing. So I will say that when the ads for this game came out I was kind of negative about the whole thing- it looked so different from the older games and I was wary of it. But let me say that I honestly think this is the best Animal Crossing game since City Folk and possibly even on par with it. First of all the art is incredible- it's a new twist on the old style but it's so amazing to watch (even just the way the wind is animated to blow) that you can't be anything but impressed. The new crafting features on the island lend so much more possibilities for the game- no more days of wandering around the town wondering what to do with your day because you've done so much fishing and bug catching there's kind of no point. It's honestly a bit like Minecraft and Animal Crossing had a cool superior baby of a game and it definitely gets you hooked. Blathers is back and there's the option for him to give his old speeches that old fans will remember from earlier games. All in all, it keeps to the old Animal Crossing tone much better than New Leaf (definitely better than Welcome Amibo or Campground) with lots of cool new features that really fit in well with the old spirit. I am a big fan!

title: If you've come to find another GameCube controller that doesn't take up a slot on your GC Adapter, look no further.
text:
I'm very consistently satisfied with what HORI does with their products, and the battle pad is no exception. The console recognizes it as a classic controller, so you can play it on most virtual console games as well. A large group of my friends play Smash Bros, and we're all used to the GameCube controller, so these battle pads are perfect for 8-player smash; all you have to do is use four controllers with the adapter, and four battle pads connected to Wii remotes and nobody is stuck with the GamePad or a Wii remote and Nunchuck.

Pros
-Feels almost exactly like an original Nintendo GameCube controller.
-Added turbo and Z shoulder buttons allow for more customizeable play.
-Connecting to the Wii remote allows for wireless play.
-Pikachu graphic (or whichever depending on the type of battle pad you buy) is visually appealing.

Cons
-The shoulder buttons don't have the springy feel that the original GameCube controller does. Not a problem for me, but others have listed it as a concern so I thought it should be said. It might at least take some getting used to.
-It has to be connected to the Wii remote, forcing you to have it in your lap or off to the side somewhere while you play.

Random Notes
-The controller is definitely lighter than my regular GameCube controller after having done a side by side test. Not really a pro or a con, but it's noticeable if you've had your hands on one a lot in your life.
-There are small gaps between the controller casing and the analog and c-sticks. They don't affect play at all, but it threw me off-guard when I inspected them.

title: Good For Beginners -- But You'll Eventually Want To Mod It
text:
Rating: 3.5/5

I purchased this product because for the last few weeks I have been hooked on Street Fighter IV. It's been years since I have been hooked on a fighting game. Everyone had their Street Fighter IV MadCatz Fight Sticks and I found them ridiculously over priced (especially the Tournament Edition), so I got this instead.

Now, I'm no expert by any means, but I've been to countless arcades, know the brands, and know how they work (i.e. wiring). This product is just "meh".

Here are the pros and cons so you don't get a headache reading a long review:

PROS:

- Excellent response time from the stick and buttons. There is no delay whatsoever and the response is flawless.

- Very nice weight and size. It fits perfectly on your lap and if you want to take it somewhere you can just put it in a bag and you're off.

- Pretty durable cable and the cable is a good length. The stick works with the PS3, PS2, and the PC.

Cons:

- The joystick I received was wobbly. I don't know if it's true for everyone, but the one I got was just okay. If you put your finger on the top of it you can move the stick with very little force. It feels like it has been used before. I had purchased it new, so I don't know what's up with that!

- The buttons seem to respond best when you press them directly in the middle, and it can get annoying if you're not pressing it RIGHT in the MIDDLE. This is not true for all the buttons, just a couple. You also have to tap them a little hard, but it's not that bad.

Overall the stick is just good for practice, which is what I got it for. I love Street Fighter IV and this stick is improving my fight stick game. It gets you the practice without a doubt, and that's what most people want, especially for a price like this. For the price it isn't that bad. I barely recommend it due to the buttons and joystick I got.

Eventually, however, you'll want to mod it. I think most people agree with this statement from the reviews I've been reading. This product is VERY good for modding. Just buy a Sanwa joystick and Sanwa buttons and then you'll definitely have a fight stick that will last for a long time. This stick will only last maybe a year or less unless you mod it. I'm looking forward to modding this, and I've only had it for one day.

Overall, get this if you're short on money and if you want some practice with fight sticks. I'm a beginner in terms of actually using a fight stick in a game at home and my game is improving, but like I said I'm dying to mod this because the product itself can only get you so far. There are products out there better than this one, but this is alright for the price.

title: A fantastic joystick that feels great
text:
Let me start off by stressing this as much as I can, there IS a home function. It is mapped to the 9 and 10 buttons and even mentions this in the instruction manual.

The stick has a nice square gate that takes some time to get used to if you've used the d-pad most of the time. The biggest and hardest transition was trying to do a dragon punch (because the proper way to do one isn't watered down to forward-down-forward like on d-pad controls).

As for PC functionality, it does wonders for those MAME games you've got. The package comes with a very generic CD that automatically installs the drivers you need to run the Auto (turbo to the best of my knowledge) and Clear.

Be warned, if you're running the controller adapting software "MotioninJoy", you'll want to remove it before attempting to use this stick. It commandeers your USB ports and installs the stick as one of its devices. Just remove it and delete the drivers, and you should be good to go.

All in all, this is a great stick for such a low price. If you get good at it, you could probably show up to a tournament with one of these.

I've added screen protectors to three different DS systems over the years and this is the first time I've had a problem with a screen protector. As much as I hate spending $10 for a single screen protector, I don't think these 3 for $6 protectors are worth the risk of having to scrap all of them.

title: It's a great controller. Almost exactly what you think it is.
text:
I've been playing with this for the last while, and I really like it. The buttons feel really nice, the springs on the sticks feel great, and the construction overall feels very solid. That said, if you're used to playing with a GameCube controller, you might find that it feels a bit light. It doesn't have any of the rumble hardware that the original had, which of course reduces its weight. It's much lighter than an original GameCube controller, and even a bit lighter than a Wavebird without the batteries. I don't mean any of this as a bad thing, but it's almost the only thing there is to talk about. If you've played with a GameCube controller before, you pretty much know what to expect. This is a really great replica of the original.

The only other thing that stands out are the "short stroke" trigger buttons. Like the weight, they aren't a bad thing, they're just different from what I'm used to. The GameCube controller had very deep trigger presses, but these behave like any other button. Go grab any game controller you have at hand and press one of the buttons--that's what you can expect from these triggers. They have zero play. It's either press or don't press. Once again, it's not at all a bad thing, just not the same as the original.

I suppose I should finish by talking about the turbo feature. I haven't really needed to use it yet, but it behaves like you'd expect. Hold the turbo button, and press the button you want turbo'd. That button now presses itself over and over very quickly. There's a switch to the right that lets you select how quickly you want the turbo to go. It's a feature that does what it says on the tin, but I don't know how much use I'll get out of it.

Overall, I'm very, very happy with this purchase. It feels like this is going to last me a long time.

The fact that this game forces households to buy multiple systems to properly enjoy the full game experience since it locks down an Island per CONSOLE (not per user or profile) clearly categorizes as a "bundling (antitrust law)" and it is an obvious subject for a class action lawsuit.

I understand that playing in local coop mode with multiple islands can be used to abuse the in-game economy, bot nothing stops Nintendo to issue a simple update where each profile can choose between having it's own Island and not be able to coop locally or join the other profile's island to coop.

This is a very simple feature to be added in a patch and if Nintendo don't do it quickly, besides the review/score bombing this game is having because of just that simple issue, someone (or a group of people) will have a lot of material to sue Nintendo very soon. It is just a very stupid and dangerous business decision.

title: Good Beginning Arcade Stick
text:
Works fine on PC, PS2, PS3, Gamecube, Wii, and Xbox 360. The Gamecube, Wii, and Xbox 360 require adapters.

Gamecube - [[ASIN:B000F7B516 Wii/GameCube Converter PS/PS2 to Wii/GameCube w/ Dance Pad Support]]
Note: Works on the Wii Gamecube ports (GC games on Wii and any Wii game that supports the GC controller).

This will limit you on games that do not support the GC controller. Also, be aware that buttons 5, 8, and 9 on the joystick register as the same input on the GC controller for the Wii. This will limit you on button placement if you are picky about which specific button you want a specific action performed on. I cannot speak for other adapters. I also do not know if it has this limitation on an actual Gamecube (I assume so).

Wii - [[ASIN:B002OJ8S7C PS2 Controller Adapter for Wii Remote]]
Note: Just think of it as substituting a PS2 controller in place of the Wii classic controller.

Xbox 360 - [...]
Note: Ps2 controller adapter to Xbox 360 (remember the joystick has PS2 AND PS3 extensions

I have yet to find a quality adapter converting PS3 USB to Xbox 360 USB

Comments:

The device could be a little wider for armresting, but oh well. The black is nice because you can mod whatever cover or art designs you want all over this thing. You will have to get your own adapters, but most are pretty cheap. This is a pretty good deal for those starting out in fighting games and want to invest their time in new/old games. It's a bit loud when using so keep that in mind if you live with other people in close proximity.

The reason people are saying some PS2 fighting games don't work with the joystick portion is because the joystick defaults as the analog and not the directional pad. Its not the joystick, its the game (one example: Tekken 5) that does not support the analog directional input (even with a regular PS2 controller, Tekken 5 will not allow you to use the analog stick). For some games (one example: Guilty Gear XX Accent Core+) the game allows you to designate whether to toggle analog input on/off. It would have to be toggled to "on" to be able to use the directional stick. Again, this is not necessarily the "stick's" fault, just that particular games don't support the ps2 controller analog feature. It would have been nice to have a toggle feature on the stick. All the buttons work though for these games.

title: Exactly what I paid for
text:
As a warning, I've only gotten 4 hours of game time so far, so these are still first impressions.

The CAS content is slightly disappointing, as I had expected from negative reviews, however, what they do have is decent. The creators could have done a lot more, but they did produce some nice content.

The Build/Buy content is nice so far. There isn't enough to do pure themes in each room but, with mixing and matching with base game content, a lot can be done.

I really liked my first vacation. The price of the vacations don't bother me. I use the "kaching" and "motherlode" cheats frequently when I'm trying out a new game. If that isn't your style, you could be saving up quite a while before you get to travel.

The exploration felt a little like Runescape, but not in a bad way. I had a little trouble finding one of the switches but the rest was very easy to figure out. I hope they get more difficult as I go on. The rest of my (3 day) vacation was shopping and looking at all the places that allowed visitors. I'm looking forward to longer vacations.

Since I got into the Sims 3 late (plenty of updates have come along since World Adventures was released), I didn't have too many of the loading troubles others seemed to have when they played. I play on a Mac, and recently I've been having some speed issues. It's hard to be sure, but I've only been having slight issues with speed, usually when I set the time speed to 4.

With what I've played so far, it's worth the $20 I paid.

ADDITION: I played some more and found a few minor issues.

1. When I was exploring a tomb and rotating the viewpoint, the camera would jump up a few floors to the ground level. This may have been because the tomb was set into a mountain, but it was, nonetheless, quite the annoyance.

2. I tried to marry a sim from China. Everything worked out but silly goals popped up, like "Woohoo for the first time" even though they were about to have a baby, and "move in with ____ " when they were already married. It isn't a huge deal to me, but it was odd.

3. When I went traveling with another sim, sometimes the sim wouldn't complete an action if I had the other sim selected. I basically had to guide them step by step for them to complete the task. This was annoying, but not something I'd uninstall the game for.

title: Challenging Yet Fun
text:
"Harvest Moon: Sunshine Islands" is much more challenging than the former "Island of Happiness" game. This is because I sense a lot of structure in the game. The game's weather patterns are set a week ahead, so it's hard to cheat, making it fair to others.
Still, there's not a whole lot of tedious work, since your crops don't need a lot of water. Although you will have to work up to a higher experience level in which to obtain better quality items to make more money, so it's not as easy and random as "Island of Happiness."
The game forces you to work in all areas of the game mining, fishing, cooking, farming, and gathering to be able to move on in other areas. For example, you will need minerals in the mining area to make a machine that converts milk into cheese(which you can sell for more money)! The game's different aspects all mesh together in this way, creating a feeling of accomplishment. Besides that, you'll be trying new things in the game!
This game is extremely enjoyable for a mellow player like me, but is not recommended for people who demand action from video games.
